Chapter 37: A Visitor's Guide to Brockton Bay - Experience Your Heroes Up Close and Personal​


The man facing down Jaune swung the katana with all his strength. The weapon belonged more on a mantelpiece than in conflict (Jaune would know what he was talking about there), but that wasn't the true issue. Sharp pointy object was sharp pointy object—deadly in the right hands.

No, the problem was that the man had no form, no balance. Like an amateur that had picked up the ancestral blade he didn't know how to use.

Or, a civilian press-ganged into a war he didn't sign up for, a bomb implanted in his head as a fail-safe to force compliance. His manic rictus did not speak of a warrior lost in the sheer rush of battle, hot blood pumping through his veins. It better resembled the false face of a clown.

Laughing at the absurdity of the world, while screaming on the inside.

Jaune sidestepped the blade, and with hardly a pause stepped in close to grab the man's hand, crushing it within his grip to render him incapable of holding the katana. He then seized the now screaming man, and swung him around.

The speedster Velocity raced by in a red blur, dropping a canister on the road which broke open to spew forth white foam that hardened in seconds to immobilize the man. Thus ended the skirmish, all members of the ABB squad strewn about the road in various states of incapacitation.

He gave them a cursory scan before sprinting back inside the auto shop.

Thousands of blinking lights lit up the interior space, thickest in front of Armsmaster, who squatted facing the wall. The entire place had been rigged to blow once the ABB depleted the cache of bombs Bakuda left out for them, which would be some time tomorrow morning going by Tattletale. Wires crisscrossed the room in a tangled network that made Jaune's eyes spin, resembling the hairball Escha coughed up the other day. To him, it looked impossible to decipher.

Armsmaster had spotted the pattern, and narrowed the trigger down to one central cluster.

"Are you done yet?" He hadn't quite spat the words, but it'd be a lie to say they were spoken kindly.

The hero answered blandly, "This is a delicate task."

"And we're on a schedule. Miss Militia's team is probably almost done ahead." He placed a hand on the phone dangling around his neck, steadying it. "Tattletale. How is it on your end?"

"Just took care of another bomb. Bakuda tried to get clever, but it was child's play to figure out. Moving on now."

He returned his attention to Armsmaster. "See? Tattletale is faster than you! C'mon, we can't let her win!"

Of course, her success may have something to do with the fact that she chose for herself places she had previously encountered in another Brockton Bay, while foisting the rest on her local version and Faultline. The bet had paid off, with the explosives she disarms thus far being very similar, if not identical, to ones she knew. He kept that part from Armsmaster, letting the implicit suggestion that the hero was inferior to a villain light a fire under the man.

Sure enough, Armsmaster took the news personally. To the sound of grinding teeth, his hands moved in a blur, deftly cutting three wires in quick succession. He beckoned to Jaune.

"Put this in your pocket dimension," the man said, standing up and clearing the path to the trigger explosive.

Now that was unusual. Jaune's offer to employ the Pocket in these situations had been met with disregard by the hero since the formation of their group.

With a shrug, he squeezed past Armsmaster to touch the bomb. It vanished from the wall, and he then experienced the oddest sensation of warmth as he directed his thought to the new item in his Pocket. He mulled on the phenomenon and what it may indicate, before whirling on the hero.

"Wait a damn minute." He pointed an accusing finger. "This thing is still active!"

Armsmaster had severed its connections to the rest of the network, but neglected to disarm the bomb. From what Jaune learned of Bakuda and her penchant for nastiness over the last hour, the hero might have even hastened the countdown, and only his time-locked Pocket prevented it from blowing up in their faces.

An unrepentant Armsmaster grinned. "You wanted faster. So, there you go. There's seven seconds left on the timer."

Jaune couldn't help baring his teeth right back. Nestled among the man's many qualities for which he justly deserved hate, Armsmaster turned out to have a spark of that JNPR mentality in him. The Nora approach to problem solving, some call it.

"You crazy bastard. Let's keep going."

They exited the auto shop, with Jaune lingering a couple of paces behind so he could in passing brush his hand unseen against a cache of bombs , ste—requisitioning a few. Outside, Velocity was in the midst of securing the scene, handcuffing or spraying more of that hardening foam. An armored PRT truck meant for transport had pulled up, not to make arrests as that would come later, but to disgorge Clockblocker and Panacea from the back. The pair of teenage heroes served as the medic team, Panacea for obvious reasons and Clockblocker… Jaune would guess his purpose was to either ensure a patient lives long enough to see the healer, or to protect Panacea from a surprise attack by freezing her in time. On paper, they made quite a potent duo.

Their presence signaled that his part here was over. Handling the aftermath laid outside his purview, which was to assault the enemy's defenses and gain access to the workshops. The hideouts and barracks, too. Anywhere that the ABB had resources, whether arms or manpower.

A second PRT truck stopped in front of Jaune and Armsmaster. Rather than waste time getting in, they leapt onto the side of the vehicle, grabbing the hand- and foot-holds built into the metal. Armsmaster pounded a fist against the truck, and along with a screech of tires, they shot forward down the street. Velocity soon joined them, taking position on the rear bumpers.

Releasing a hand so he could swing over the road, Jaune leaned back his head and took a moment to enjoy the cool wind blowing through his hair.

This night was not a quiet one. Even now, he could hear the staccato of gunfire, and the occasional explosion lighting the sky briefly aglow. At turns and intersections, it's not uncommon to catch a glimpse of one of the patrol teams—a mix of New Wave and teenage members of the Protectorate like Shadow Stalker, Gallant, Browbeat—fending off ABB reinforcements. Somebody, somewhere, had started a fire, and its smoke rose in a column to block the moon from his sight.

At one point, he saw what he thought was a shooting star, burning white and flying low across the city. His eyes tracked it as it passed behind an office building, yet failed to come out the other side, leaving him to wonder if he had imagined that.

The truck rolled by another of their targets, a sewing shop used as a front for ABB activities. There, the driver lingered to let them survey the scene. A quick look was enough to decide that they could continue the push forward, as the battle seemed almost over. Concluding, of course, in favor of the Protectorate.

Assault and Battery—what a set of names for superheroes—were tag-teaming the remnants of the ABB contingent posted here, zipping around at high speed to avoid harm. Behind them, the big display window to the store had shattered into a million fragments, and Jaune noted that Miss Militia, the leader of this team, stood past the window alongside a kid dressed in green—Vista.

A muffled boom came from further inside, startling him and prompting a second glance. He soon relaxed as the blast radius was far smaller than it should be. Minuscule, really, and the building hadn't gone sky high as he feared.

Vista could alter distances, he recalled. That tidbit shone a light on the tactic he was witnessing, a remote detonation. The kid had brought her space-bending powers into play, warping the area around the bomb to form a spot where the world appeared to swirl, the colors bleeding together in ways that stung the eyes to see. It must have translated to the equivalent of an open space measuring in miles.

All in all, a very effective approach. Using one child, this team was setting off explosives at a proximity where the blast failed to even scratch the nearest shelf, let alone themselves. He somewhat envied Miss Militia for having such a great setup going. Quick, simple, none of these nerve-wracking games of cutting wires and guessing passwords.

"The sewing shop on Maple Avenue is cleared out," he reported into his phone. "Dauntless hasn't called in yet, so my group is headed for that apartment you mentioned."

Tattletale's chirpy voice came over the line. "Good to hear. My side had a rough spot with Squealer, but that's being taken care of. I'm on my way to the next place, too."

"What happened over there? Are you okay?"

He heard her groan.

"No matter how much she insists she's a Tinker, Squealer just isn't cut out for this. It's nowhere close to her field of expertise, and the idiot's too strung out from the drugs she takes to figure out all the details. Half the street is covered in acid as a result. If it wasn't for Trickster swapping her out with a mailbox, we'd be down a cape right now."

Her tone indicated that any sadness at the possibility would last a whole two seconds instead of one, the girl concerned only insofar it meant a reduction in their forces.

"Why don't you stay far away from that disaster case, Tattletale? I'd hate to find that you or Escha got hurt."

Admittedly, he shared her sentiment on the matter. If Squealer screwed up on a job she insisted she could accomplish, the fault was on her own head. Were he absent to save her from the resulting catastrophe, oops. He placed far more importance on his team's well-being than some random villain.

"Who else was present? Are they all fine?" he asked very carefully, thinking of nobody in particular, of course. Could be the local Tattletale. Could be the capes he met from Faultline's crew.

"Sundancer was. She's gone."

His hand slipped. He would have fallen off the truck if not for Armsmaster hooking the halberd under his arm and pulling him back on the vehicle.

"What!?" he squeaked into the phone.

"Haha! I knew that's how you'd react!" Her laughter rang loud, but not louder than his thundering heartbeat. "She's gone… in the sense that I saw the signs coming a mile away and ordered everybody to evacuate."

"Don't scare me like that!"

"Oh, please, it wouldn't be any big loss. Not like she should matter to you. Wrong version, remember?"

He grimaced. "I get your point, I do, but we should still watch out for our allies. They're on our side." Sure, maybe he reserved those thoughts more for certain people than others. That didn't make the notion worthless.

"Yeah, yeah. Whatever."

He sensed that she was reading him like an open book, [Blank] or not, and she didn't care much for his priorities.

"I'm coming up on my destination now, so I'll be out of contact for a bit."

His own vehicle slowed down, taking a turn that put them on the street they were headed for. He glanced back, finding the medical truck chugging along at a safe distance, ready to lend aid. Miss Militia's team must not have left much work for Panacea.

"Good luck, Tattletale. I mean it about you staying safe. Aura might not last long against some of these bombs." The acid one sounded nasty. The first bomb Armsmaster deactivated that was supposed to turn a person inside-out sounded just as bad.

"...'Kay. I'll probably do some reassignments of the teams. Move Squealer where she can't cause trouble. Jaune?"

"Yes?"

"Go easy?"

"Don't worry. I am," he said as he jumped off the truck.

Light touches on the rockets helped him achieve a soft landing, sword and shield out. Meanwhile, Armsmaster and Velocity opted for the safer approach of remaining aboard and waiting until the truck turned aside, which created a cover for them from the band of gun-toting ABB gangsters ahead. This place should be one of the barracks, which explained why he was seeing a significantly bigger force compared to the previous raid.

A quick eyeball estimate, and Jaune broke into a run straight at their formation. These were rookie numbers. Baby numbers!

Bullets pinged off his shield and the road, the volume of firepower the gangsters could output undercut by their awful accuracy—he doubted they ever learned proper aiming, simply shooting just to shoot. What they did have in spades was enthusiasm, yelling and whooping in an eagerness to watch him die. It pointed to their status as willing participants of the ABB, and he interpreted that attitude as their enthusiastic consent to an ass-kicking.

Activating his boots, he blasted across the final intervening distance to crash into, then through their ranks.

They parted before him, thrown aside by the impact, slamming into their allies and knocking each other off their feet. In the resulting pandemonium, the smarter ones still standing traded guns for knives and baseball bats with nails in them. The dumb, or inexperienced, gangsters swept their firearms in his direction.

As Tattletale (constantly throughout the night) asked, he went easy. Returning his shield to scabbard form, he stowed his sword and in the same motion cracked it against the hand of the closest gunman. A backswing slapped the same person across the face, and he collapsed in a boneless heap. And that, was three or four people Jaune just saved from friendly fire.

With another swing of Crocea Mors, at least two of those were taken out of the fight, teeth bashed in and nose broken.

A gangster opened fire with his handgun, the rounds finding flesh… but missing Jaune as he had ducked low. A tackle folded the man in half, and on recovery Jaune stomped his face for good measure, simultaneously sweeping his sword to catch an ambusher on the side. The sound of snapping rib bones was accompanied by a screech, cut short as he punched out the gangster.

The ones he bowled over were climbing back to their feet now, which put them in the way of those trying to reach him. The messy situation suited him fine, and he took the opportunity to lay into them. They didn't last for much longer, and he soon stood above a mound of defeated foes.

As he considered going to help the others deal with their own pack of attackers, the doors to the nearby apartment building crashed open. More members of the ABB spilled out onto the road, wielding various dangerous implements in their hands. Very few guns among them, and soon to be fewer still as he marked the people holding those to take down first.

Mixed in with the gangsters were a number of people who had the look of civilians terrified out of their wits. Jaune took a short moment to address them, offering an out.

"Do any of you want to surrender?" He waited for a beat. "No?"

Repeating his earlier success, Jaune cannonballed into the newcomers. Shouts of 'He's a cape!' arose as it fully dawned for them that his mundane outfit hid unordinary powers, along with 'Brute!' which he thought was rather rude. Some tried to back off here, pushed forward by those pressing forward from behind.

Amidst the thick of bodies, he eluded their attempts to hit him with a speed they cannot hope to match. Each well-placed swing of Crocea Mors brought with it a satisfying crack to denote another downed opponent. Definite civilians like the older folks and crying housewives received firm shoves to move them out of the fray, broken hands deterring those that proved more persistent. The iffier ones, he plucked from the disorganized mob to simply toss them over his shoulder, the height of their falls ensuring they wouldn't return to the fight.

A gangster who thought himself clever was using other people as cover to strike at him. Jaune showed the same courtesy, seizing him for use as a club to strike at his allies, the impromptu flail rendered unconscious by the fifth collision or so. He threw the person aside, and eyed the crowd for his next potential weapon. A bulky man his age, face scarred by a blade, saw fit to dive at him. Seconds later, he was screaming like a scared child as Jaune swung him by a leg.

Once he had cleared some space, Jaune swept the gangster in an overhead arc then slammed him down into the concrete curb, letting go to let the man flop on the ground.

He looked around. Collectively, the ABB shrank back. They refused to run, though, so with a twirl of his sword, he advanced on them.

Then, everybody was behind him.

Jaune spun on his heels, staring in utter confusion at the ongoing battle before his eyes. The ABB were mounting a desperate counterattack, throwing bodies at the fray. Armsmaster stood within the crowd, dispatching people left and right. Velocity skirted the periphery, tossing out containment foam canisters. A squad of PRT troopers supported them, in danger of being dog-piled by sheer numbers—Jaune recognized the vehicle at their backs, the medical transport.

Nobody paid him any mind.

"What just happened?"

It's a question that could be left for later. He had spotted Clockblocker near the troopers, and like them, the boy wasn't faring well, near overrun.

Racing past the hero, he raised Crocea Mors high.

All of the ABB were on the ground.

"—hear me? What's your situation? Jaune, answer me!" Tattletale's voice came through the phone, sounding upset.

Now quite lost, he lowered his sword while scanning the area. The Protectorate forces were moving between the ABB members and handcuffing them to each other, displaying a calmness that juxtaposed the hot-blooded intensity of an instant earlier. Armsmaster and Velocity chatted, standing a good few yards from where he last saw them. Two figures in white—Panacea and Clockblocker—stooped over one of the captives.

"Jaune!"

Numbly, he grabbed the phone, and said, "Tattletale, I… I think I just lost minutes of my life." His voice cracked near the end. Whatever happened to him, he didn't understand it and didn't like it.

Tattletale only needed a split second to surmise the cause. "Has to be Clockblocker. He used his time-stop power on you? But why would he…"

"We're going to find out." Jaune narrowed his eyes. "He's coming over."

"He is? Good. Hey! Hey, blue balls! Is this a declaration of war? What the fuck do you think you're doing?" Tattletale yelled for the hero to hear.

Far from cowed, Clockblocker stomped right up to Jaune, yelling back at the phone.

"What am I doing? Ask your boytoy that." He raised his head, the blank expanse of glass that formed the mask an inch from Jaune's face. "Buddy, what's your damage?"

This was not the attitude Jaune expected to find.

"Hah?" he said with unsurpassed eloquence.

"Did the ABB do something to you? Or are you some kind of psycho?" Clockblocker swept a hand behind him. "We have a bunch of people in critical condition because of you, and that's not counting the ones Panacea saved!"

Jaune leaned to the side to look behind Clockblocker, where he took in the scene of Panacea running back and forth, tending to the ABB gunmen that he subdued. His eyes trailed over the splatters of blood and the twisted limbs.

Their necks were still screwed on at the right angle, and their chests rose and fell. It could have been a lot worse. Jaune returned his gaze to Clockblocker.

"Aaand your point is? They're alive, aren't they?"

"..."

"..."

Both Tattletale and Clockblocker fell quiet in response, the latter seeming to choke on his spit as he gawked.

Slowly, Clockblocker came to grips with what he had heard. "You don't see how thinking 'they're still barely breathing so it's okay' is a problem? Holy shit." He stepped back, a hand going up to rub his temples before he remembered he was wearing a helmet. Instead, he jabbed a finger at Jaune's face. "Our job might be to bust heads, but not to the level of them cracking open like an egg! Seriously, dude, Glory Girl vouched for you, then I see you go and pull this. What the hell?"

"Boo hoo hoo," Tattletale piped up in snide mockery. "A bunch of gangbangers-turned-terrorists got manhandled by the guy they tried to kill. Oh, the humanity." She gave a bitter chuckle. "Where was this mercy at the bank when Kid Win tried to shoot us with a cannon, huh? Jaune didn't kill anybody." Boy, did she sound relieved there. "You acted like he committed murder. Overreacting much?"

"Tattles or whatever you're called, I know you can't be all there since you're on the same team as the creepy bug girl, but this kind of brutality—"

"I know what I'm doing," Jaune said, cutting off Clockblocker. He held up his sword. "I've trained to use this, and by now I've got a pretty good handle on what it takes to kill someone." His mind conjured images of Hound Dogs sliced apart in a careless swing. Mostly, he amended to himself.

"Uh, yeah, I call bull. I had to freeze people that were bleeding out. They might not have been dead, but they were actively dying."

He shrugged. "You have Panacea." A snap of his fingers, superfluous yet satisfyingly dramatic, summoned a stimpak to hand. "And I have this little doohickey to heal them up. It would have been fine."

"Oh my god, why is this so hard for you to comprehend?" said Clockblocker as he slapped a palm to his facemask. "I'm telling you we aren't supposed to let it get to the point where that's needed in the first place. Use handcuffs! That's what they're there for!" He glanced back at the downed ABB. "As it is, half of them aren't waking up because of you."

Jaune reviewed his memory, wondering if maybe the squishiness of Earth people were worse than he thought, but calmed down as Tattletale gave a loud, pondering hum.

"What's the diagnosis? And don't lie. Panacea can at least see the causes even if she 'can't heal brains'."

"Blunt force trauma leading to brain damage. Real pretty," said Clockblocker.

"Yeah… somehow, that doesn't sound like the whole truth. Did Panacea say something else?" She waited, needing no answer as the silence itself was a confession. "Yes. You don't want to admit it. It undermines your point. Ha! It's obvious, then. They'll recover."

Jaune pumped a fist. It looked like he got that control down pat, after all.

The other boy didn't share the same cheery outlook. Clockblocker scoffed, and was about to speak when a new voice joined the conversation.

"Clockblocker, enough."

Both boys turned their heads toward the approaching Armsmaster. Grim-faced, he marched in even strides that were quieter than one would expect. Jaune hadn't heard him until he spoke up.

"But, sir!" Clockblocker straightened up, prepared to argue.

"What did I say? We are on a timetable, if you recall. Bickering among ourselves will solve nothing right now."

Jaune nodded along in agreement.

"Be useful. Get back to your tasks."

Jaune stopped nodding, and cringed, sending Clockblocker a glance. The other boy had taken it as well as he thought, flinching under the older hero's rebuke. Clockblocker hurried to obey the order, rushing off with a last look—no doubt scathing behind the mask—over his shoulder.

"That was a little harsh," Jaune said. Clockblocker might have been oversensitive about matters, but the guy was putting in solid effort considering that he left the safety of the armored truck to join the front line.

Armsmaster looked to Jaune. "Was it? I advised him to focus on what he can do."

It took him a moment to realize that, yes, the man was serious. Armsmaster had intended his words to Clockblocker as a statement of fact rather than criticism.

"Don't ever take on work as a motivational speaker," he said, shaking his head as he walked past the hero.

An armored hand clamped down on his shoulder, squeezing until his Aura flared.

"Understand that any fatalities on your part will be investigated," Armsmaster warned, his jaw set in a hard line, "And are grounds for reconsideration of your status as an independent hero. My Protectorate will not work with a villain. Got it?"

The man didn't wait for an answer, releasing the grip before leaving for the transport truck.

Jaune stared after his back, then turned to survey the battlefield. From heroes to troopers, everyone angled their helmets so they could watch him out of their periphery while carrying on their duties.

"I really was holding back," he explained himself to the only person left to listen, and heard her exhale a long breath.

"I know, but they're worried. I think you might have killed someone, Jaune, and they're just keeping news of it from the kiddies." She paused, before continuing, "Do you understand why I asked you to go easy on the ABB?"

He nodded even though she wouldn't see it. "Because the Protectorate gets leery of murder, you've said. Their reaction seems kind of overboard, though, don't you think? It's not like I wasn't aware there are regular people mixed in with the gang. They didn't want to turn on the city, they were forced into it, and I did my best to separate them."

"...Try a little more? Please?"

Well, he couldn't say no to that, could he?

At the next location, he hung back, forgoing earlier tactics to adopt a careful approach of skirting the edges like the others. His opponents would come within range in ones and twos. To the approval of the Protectorate, he blocked or parried them, seeking a chance to disarm where he could have powered through the exchange in a single blow.

It did become somewhat of a slog for everyone involved, because now he was no longer grabbing the attention of the ABB. The heroes had to take the brunt of it since their costumes were much more recognizable to the locals than his, and thus registered as the bigger threat. They handled it well, if slower than the pace he was used to.

He had to admit, the new restrictions chafed on him. The praises Tattletale would give him about what a good job he was doing were pretty nice, though.


Author's Notes: Jaune meets his new mortal enemies, proper procedures and reasonable force.

#1,855
Chapter 38: A Visitor's Guide to Brockton Bay - We Have Ninjas, Dragons, and Explosions​


The sky lit up in red and green. Oni Lee was on the scene.

Jaune caught a glimpse of his demonic mask, before the man exploded into ash. One would think that was the end, yet the villain returned again.

An ambush on New Wave had started it all, catching the heroes when they were patrolling the next street over from Jaune's group. Those that could fly—Lady Photon, Laserdream, Shielder, Glory Girl—now chased the villain in a cat-and-mouse game that rattled windows and rained down fire, accompanied by a scattered boom, boom, boom rhythm to shake the night.

Hanging off the moving PRT truck, Jaune watched as Oni Lee would appear in mid-air, trying to grab onto one of the New Wave heroes and detonating them both with a tinkertech bomb. The shields that the Pelhams could conjure saved them here, forming walls or bubbles that rebuffed the villain, often stacking on top of each other to help mitigate the blasts.

As he possessed no means to stay aloft, Oni Lee took the moments in between attacks to recover by landing on the rooftops, at which point the tables turned and lasers—or a flying blonde—would attempt to clip him before his next teleport. An odd quirk of his power was that Oni Lee would always leave a copy, one capable of independent action. It fooled the eye, on multiple occasions making Jaune think that New Wave had succeeded in striking the villain only for the copy to burst into a dust cloud upon receiving a strong blow.

"He's good," Jaune said with a grimace. It was becoming clear after the repeated exchanges that the villain exhibited top-notch combat awareness.

From his phone, Tattletale replied, "Who?" A loud boom answered her question. "Oni Lee. Careful, Jaune. He survived for years without capture by being a complete sociopath. He goes for the lethal option right off the bat, and never shows mercy."

"An accurate summation," Armsmaster said from his spot on the vehicle. The man did not hide his distaste of Tattletale, though that may apply to all villains in general. "It's curious that his power can copy Bakuda's tinkertech—"

Tattletale cut in. "She must have simplified the ones she gave to him. They're barely tinkertech, which probably means limited range and limited effects." Reveling in a mind unrestrained, the girl continued to rattle off conjectures that better resembled firsthand observations with how they seem to narrate the scene before Jaune's eyes.

His inclination was to join the aerial battle, but he resisted that urge. Despite the wanton destruction he could inflict with his new arsenal, Oni Lee ranked far lower as a priority to the true threat facing Brockton Bay, Bakuda. The plan simply called for him to remain occupied, and New Wave's combination of shields, laser, and flight had the matter well in hand even if it looked like they might not achieve victory. His presence added very little to the equation that they didn't already have, and might be better utilized elsewhere.

For example, up ahead.

"Tattletale, I think Lung's here."

"You sure?"

"Unless they have another guy running around in a mask on their side, that's probably him."

A newcomer to Brockton Bay's cape scene—say, a certain Jaune Arc—might expect the dragon man of the ABB to make an entrance that involved roars and fires and flapping wings, the villain either swooping in like a hawk or slowly descending from the sky in a dramatic fashion. With boss music.

Instead, a sedan careened down the road at breakneck speed. The car had its roof ripped away, allowing a view of the people inside. Of the driver, there's not much to note. A mook in ABB colors. The one in the back, though…

With one hand gripping the driver's headrest, the man half-stood in the backseat of the car. A suit jacket hung off his shoulders like a cape, billowing in the wind. On his face, a stylized mask depicting a snarling beast—a dragon.

"Oh, you are just catching all the luck tonight, aren't you?"

He chuckled. "A little less sass, you. I'm going to need those reinforcements as fast as you can bring them."

"On it. I'm disarming a bomb at the moment so I won't be there, but I'll pass the word to the teams and get some people out to you in… let's put it at ten minutes, since I can still hear fighting outside. Think you can stall him that long?"

"I'll make do. Should you really be talking to me right now?"

"Psh. Bakuda's work is no big deal. She's a child playing at being clever. Don't worry about me."

A few blocks away, the driver of the sedan slammed on the brakes, swerving to a dead stop. With casual ease, Lung jumped a good ten feet in the air to land lightly on the asphalt road. That prompted the PRT truck to also slow to a halt with Jaune hopping off first, Armsmaster and Velocity following suit.

In near perfect sync, the two vehicles pulled in reverse, neither drivers inclined to remain in the vicinity of a battle among superpowered people.

With a flex of his shoulders, Lung shrugged off his jacket, letting it fall to the ground. He had eschewed a shirt beneath, and indicated no discomfort at standing bare-chested in the cool chill. Sinuous dragons tattoos covered almost every inch of his skin. They rippled as he advanced down the center of the street in languid strides.

"So," Jaune began, turning to address Armsmaster. "Lung. He gets stronger the more time he spends in a fight, right?"

Gaze locked onto the villain, Armsmaster said, "A bit simplified, but yes. The exact mechanism for Lung's transformation is a mixed bag. His baseline begins at enhanced physical strength and pyrokinesis, scaling up from there. Analysis draws a high correlation with the presence of parahumans." He adjusted his grip on his halberd. "Visual awareness of a threat may contribute to his growth, albeit it is unclear to what extent that factors."

"That matches up with the briefing I got. Okay, game plan. I'll need Vista, Gallant, and I guess Clockblocker here for this. Call them over for me?"

The first two numbered among the names Tattletale suggested as ideal options for this phase. The last one, he added just now, and it had surprisingly little to do with their earlier encounter.

He didn't necessarily need Lung dead, and he definitely didn't need Lung exploding in size to become a giant lizard. A space-warper, an emotion-controller, and a time-stopper fit well within that purpose. Someone to keep Lung at a distance, someone to sap his drive to fight, and someone to put him in timeout. It seemed, to him, a combo that should give the villain quite a lot of grief, distracting him from providing aid to Bakuda.

"Denied. I will not send the Wards into a battle with Lung, of all people."

Which was why he so very much wanted to slap Armsmaster right about now.

"Of fucking course," Tattletale muttered on her end.

He decided to offer more tact than that. "What's the big deal? They knew the danger they're getting into, fighting the ABB."

"There's danger, and then there's Lung," said Armsmaster, refusing to bend.

An answer that, in all honesty, evoked no surprise; Tattletale had warned him of the possibility. The Protectorate were a strange lot in regards to their teenage heroes, preferring that they avoid conflict altogether. Thus, he had been hoping to spring the decision on Armsmaster, so as to force a snap judgment call under pressure. No dice.

Granted, Vista's circumstance was a little ridiculous, and near impossible to overlook. The kid was, like, twelve years old and didn't belong anywhere close to the battlefield. If her superpower wasn't to functionally put infinite distance between her and a threat, he would have had strong misgivings on including her in his plan. (Gallant and Clockblocker were his age, and as a result clearly possessed the wisdom and maturity to take care of themselves.)

"I've sent an request for assistance through my comms to the other members of the Protectorate," Armsmaster informed him. "You, Velocity, and I will distract Lung in the meantime."

Jaune thought about it for almost one whole second. "Wait wait wait… I heard from Tattletale you tried that a few years ago, and the entire neighborhood burned to the ground."

Eheh. Someone looked unhappy at the reminder.

The point stood, nevertheless. Until the villains got here, they had to maintain the situation at a level that denied Lung the energy to fuel his transformation. Gradually adding capes to the fight benefited him to an enormous degree, playing to the core mechanism of his ability. For a strategy of numbers to truly succeed, it required a quick and overwhelming response from the start without any option to resist, a dozen superpowers working in concert to crash over Lung like a tidal wave.

"Let's maybe give my Plan B a shot," he suggested.

"What does that entail?" asked a curious Velocity.

He gestured at the two heroes. "Well, you'd stay right here in this spot so you don't provoke Lung." He proceeded to point at Lung. "While I stroll on over there to beat him up."

A brief silence ensued as the heroes parsed the statement. Afterward, Armsmaster spoke up, "Are you a fool, or are you just that arrogant? Do you think you're the first person to believe they can go toe-to-toe with Lung? If it were that easy, I would have captured him long ago." He shook his head. "Prior simulations put my odds against him at 44.475%, the highest of any single Protectorate hero in Brockton Bay."

"Sounds kind of low," Jaune commented.

"The number assumes no other capes are in the area, and holds true for close to seven minutes, at which point Lung's rate of improvement would advance beyond my capabilities. Either I subdue him before then, or I lose. You? You'll die."

Jaune raised a finger to stop him there.

"Hang on, now. You're missing one important detail." He skipped away from the heroes, placing himself ahead of them and looking from one to the other. "See, I have an advantage you don't."

"Which is?" Armsmaster asked. With his warning given, the man seemed content to let events play out, no doubt having seen this exact sort of attitude in the past from other capes.

Jaune spun on his heels to face Lung. "Wouldn't you like to know?"

Before they could inquire further, he strode forward on a direct course for the leader of the ABB. The villain was only a block away now. The mask hid his thoughts, but the way he clenched his fists spoke of a rising temper. It's possible he saw Jaune's bold action as a sign of disrespect.

He would not be the only person taking umbrage with that decision.

"Jaaaune," Tattletale hissed dangerously. "You didn't tell me about this. What's going on, silly man?"

"You know I fought Leviathan?"

"You never shut up about it," she grumbled.

"It's a story that bears repeating. Anyway, there was something I noticed during that fight."

"Let me guess. A certain someone's rear end?"

"Ha. No. I noticed that I should have died five times over, if not for Leviathan's own mistake. It doesn't just rely on its eyes. It can detect superpowers."

In a split second, she pinpointed the connection. "Like Lung."

"Like Lung," he confirmed. "Leviathan had no trouble killing the people it focuses on, but didn't know what to do once it got to me. It tried to hit me as if I was a normal person at first. Only when I survived did it escalate to a harder attack."

It's a simple thing, his advantage. Armsmaster could never imitate the strategy in a million years.

After all, the man couldn't lose his powers.

"So, basically, you look weak."

"Super weak. Scrawny, even."

"And you think Lung's ability operates on the same principles, meaning one of his senses—maybe the most important one—won't register you as a threat, which would gimp his rate of growth."

"Exactly. To his powers, I'll appear as ferocious as a housecat."

"If it works."

Jaune rocketed forward, ducked under a reflexive punch, and with a full body spin both summoned then smashed a gunlance against Lung's midriff to launch him away with the force of a cannon shot. The villain flew in a straight line across the street and struck the brick wall of a building, the impact kicking up a cloud of dust and debris.

"It works," Jaune said with a carefree grin.

He lifted the Red Rook gunlance to rest it on a shoulder. Gone were the jeans and poncho, replaced by the armor of a Monster Hunter. The red scales of an otherworldly beast gleamed in the night, and heat thrummed within the chamber of the lance, primed to roar with the might of Rathalos.

As Jaune watched the spot where Lung landed from behind his helmet visor, his mind raced. That opening shot had told him a few things. One, he was faster. The punch Lung directed at him moved at a speed he could follow and react to. Two, Lung shared the same weird Earth quirk as most people in this world where they had a hard time resisting impact. One little hit and they just fly off, no gritting their teeth and bearing it with their legs. Three…

"He didn't look much like a dragon. I feel cheated."

Twin jets of flames blasted out of the dust cloud. One missed him, while he summoned the paired shield for Red Rook to block the other. The flames spread atop the metal and scales, washing over his form.

Jaune stood there, and enjoyed the sensation of a summer breeze.

The dust cleared to reveal Lung, breathing hard with arms outstretched. Small patches of silver scales had broken through his skin, most notably over his belly. His eyes behind the mask now glowed orange, vertical pupils sending forth a baleful glare.

"Ooh. There it is."

The transformation proceeded in spurts, it seemed. Faster in areas that Lung suffered injury, and rather random elsewhere. Still, Jaune couldn't see how the man would go from this to a twenty-foot tall dragon with wings in a reasonable length of time, so his theory might be panning out.

A part of him contemplated stabbing Lung with the lance and firing off a shell. The villain might be famous for his regeneration factor, but a big gaping hole in the chest should prove quite debilitating. And say what you want, nobody comes back from a missing head.

"Tattletale, would anyone mind if I kill him?"

"You really think you can?" Her voice was muffled due to the phone being tucked under the armor chestplate, but the skepticism carried across just fine.

"His body is tough, but not to the extent where it's invincible. He felt kind of squishy when I hit him."

"I wonder how wise that'd be," Tattletale mused, ignoring the last part. "The PRT is wary of you. Killing Lung will turn you into a person they can't ignore."

"So? We're on the same side."

"That doesn't mean much with the Director of this PRT branch, or with Armsmaster. They'll reprioritize, and—"

Her explanation was drowned out by a stream of words in a language Jaune somewhat recognized—Japanese. Lung had gotten to his feet, and seemed to have overheard him talking despite the distance between them. Evidently, the man disagreed with Jaune's proposal that he pretty please shuffle off this mortal coil, spewing what Jaune suspected were curses and insults. That became a shout as Lung leapt at him, traversing the intervening space in a single bound.

And then Lung exploded. Fire roiled from the villain to create a ball of flames, one with weight behind it that knocked Jaune back before he could take another swing at his foe.

Briefly airborne, his boots found purchase on the asphalt, scraping to a stop a few steps from his previous place.

Lung rushed out of the smoke, fire burning on his skin and clothes. His form followed a loose boxer's guard, but with fingers shaped into claws instead of fists. With a gesture, he summoned more flames, swiping to create an obscuring curtain.

A moment later, his other hand pierced the flames only to meet the tip of Red Rook. The Rathalos tailspike punctured the center of Lung's palm, drawing a shriek from the villain.

Jaune twisted the lance to worsen the wound, and pulled the trigger. A spark ignited within the chamber, and a gunlance shell shot out of the barrel to pulverize the trapped hand altogether. It then traveled along a path that seared the flesh off of Lung's arm, passing by his face and ripping away his ear, splattering blood across the steel mask.

The screams bounced off the buildings, carrying with it a touch of a bestial roar. Lung's transformation continued on, even now.

Following the force of the recoil, Jaune pivoted, sweeping the gunlance in a wide circle and slamming it into Lung again. Once more, the man went flying. This time, Jaune chased him. [Third Arm] grabbed onto a street light, pulling him up high. He reversed his grip on his weapon, angling it to strike the villain from above.

Another spontaneous explosion occurred, diverting the lance tip so that it drilled into the road instead of Lung's face. Jaune landed on unsteady feet, and Lung used the opening to scramble upright. The torn side of his face had staunched its bleeding, and his missing hand had regrown as a singular metal claw, resembling a sword. Lung brandished his new blade, surging forward in the hope of reaching Jaune before he could free his weapon.

Red Rook simply vanished, then reappeared in Jaune's grip. He cradled the lance on his shoulder as he ducked the first swipe, and backpedaled to avoid the second. The subsequent series of slashes found similar success, never striking true; ineffectual flames licked over near impervious armor.

"Too slow! Too slow!" Jaune mocked. All the while, he watched for an opportunity.

"How are you doing this!?" howled Lung.

Jaune doubted he was referring to the evasive maneuvers. The villain meant the delay in his transformation. Perhaps years of experience informed Lung that his current state did not match up with the injuries he had taken, because at this point he still appeared more human than beast, giving the title of dragon a bad name.

Of course, Jaune refused to shed any light on the matter. The time was not ripe for a heroic monologue.

"Wouldn't you like to know?" was his answer for yet a second time.

"Raaahhh!"

The screech contained a shrill note that no human should be able to make. Frustrated, and no less confused, Lung whipped his arm-blade across Jaune's throat.

Despite being backed by such incandescent rage, the blade whiffed empty air.

Jaune laughed, straightening up. "It's useless! You're still too slow!"

Bam!

Jaune stumbled back, "Ow…"

That jab had been a blur, fast enough that he couldn't easily dodge and augmented by scales that were akin to a gauntlet. Lung pressed the advantage, kicking out.

Jaune caught it on his lance, and grunted at the power behind the attack.

"Careful! I don't think you're mitigating all of his growth!"

Jaune blocked a fiery punch with his shield, and tilted his chin down to mutter at the phone. "I can tell, thanks. Because, you know, it's happening right in front of my face. What's his next piece of transformation? When will he eclipse me?"

"Ugh, you act like that's so easy to figure out."

He could practically imagine her rolling her eyes at that moment.

"Whatever. You're hopeless. Leave it to me." Tattletale gave a hum. "Let's see, let's think, since he took…uh, how many seconds was it… wait…"

The tip of the lance got Lung on the chin, twisting his neck right around, back to front.

Now, that should have decided it, Jaune rather thought. Instead, with a series of sickening cracks, Lung reoriented his face to the correct angle. His neck was several inches longer, becoming somewhat serpentine.

"Aha. That's new," Jaune said weakly. "Tattletale, you still there? This guy's getting kind of weird."

When he received no response, he craned his ear. At the very edge of his hearing, there came a soft murmuring.

"...oh god… oh god…"

That didn't sound good.

"What's wrong?" He waited for an answer while dancing around Lung's claws. "Hey, Tattletale, say some-ack!"

He doubled over, eyes stinging with tears due to the low blow struck with superhuman strength. A follow-up knee smashed into his helm, throwing his head back. Keenly aware he was wide open, he set the rockets to full blast and launched himself out of range, landing half a block away on the sidewalk. It bought him a reprieve of mere seconds, and he was soon back to fending off a flurry of claws and flames. Every couple of strikes registered as a little faster, a little stronger. Lung loomed above him, measuring near eight feet tall.

"Jaune…"

"Tattletale, are you hurt?"

"No. No. It's all good. It's nothing." Her bright tone contrasted the earlier despair, but listen close, and a warble could be detected beneath the blithe facade the girl was putting up. She took a deep breath. "Okay. Business. Lung. Clearly his active recognition of a threat can have a bigger effect on his whole dragonification shtick than we thought."

He still wanted to know what was going on with her, but she wasn't letting him get a word in edgewise.

"It's also possibly due to him realizing on an instinctual level that he's losing."

"I NEVER LOSE!" Lung screamed through what seemed like a mouth full of fangs.

"And he can now hear me. Hi, Lung!"

If she could joke, she has to be okay, right? Relatively?

With the knowledge that their enemy was listening in, they couldn't reveal too much. Tattletale tried her best to advise him, anyway.

"You're damaging him to the extent that it's forcing his body to adapt to survive." In other words, slow down. "What's he looking like? Are there spikes behind his shoulders yet?"

That was difficult to tell, as the villain kept angling his body to stay centered on Jaune. A gunlance shell pulped his shoulder and twirled him around.

"Nope. I see nothing."

"Good. That means he's not too far along. Those would have been the beginning of wings, and is usually a sign he's ramping up to unmanageable levels. Watch his mouth if the mask falls off. He bites. Oh, and his fires get hotter. You might be able to endure it at the moment, but at a certain point, it could be a problem."

"You're rambling. I already heard most of that stuff from you a couple hours ago."

"Less snarking, more fighting!"

[Third Arm] shot out to grab Lung by the ankle, yanking his leg from under him. Jaune stayed defensive on Tattletale's advice, unwilling to push the transformation too fast. As a diversion, he fired a shell at the ground to startle the villain, then waited for him to recover.

When Lung charged back in, swinging his arm-blade, he deflected it with his shield and snapped out a kick at a shin—a light attack that taunted rather than cause actual harm.

Well, sort of.

Lung hissed as the bone shattered and mended. Anticipating a follow-up, he bought room by exploding again, something that Jaune was content to let happen as all it did was waste time.

It couldn't last. The villain wasn't stupid. After a couple of exchanges continued in that vein, Lung finally caught on that Jaune would pass on obvious chances to hurt him, and shifted his style to suit. He leaned into attacks, trying to stoke his transformation by receiving injuries as he came to understand that a drawn-out battle was for once benefiting his opponent rather than himself.

And when that still wasn't enough, Lung seemed to decide a big move would bring things to a close. Both hands, one whole and one warped, came together to summon a huge fireball.

Jaune thought nothing of it, jumping as Lung launched the attack in his direction. He had to activate his boots to further gain height when, manipulated by its master, the fireball ballooned to an enormous size in midair.

Except, after vaulting over, he couldn't see Lung anywhere. That was, until an arm extended from within the inferno to clamp tight around his leg.

Wham!

He struck the ground. A foot stomped on his back to trap him, followed by a conflagration to cover his form.

The heat didn't present an issue. Lung had a ways to go yet to even ping his Aura in this armor, and Jaune could have just laid there for the duration if not for the fire consuming oxygen as fuel, robbing his breath in the process. Suffocation would be a terrible way to die.

With that thought at the forefront of his mind, he braced his arms beneath him, and shoved. Lung might have gained another fifty pounds with his transformation, but he still lacked the leverage to keep a person pinned in place. The sudden movement threw him briefly off-balance.

Then a stop sign smacked him in the face, knocking Lung on his rear.

Jaune turned his head, and saw a welcome sight. The villains have arrived.

Ballistic was the one to have sent that attack, standing at a street corner alongside the rest of the Travelers. Newter, Gregor, Grue, and Skitter joined them there, with some of Coil's mercenaries stationed further back.

The Protectorate heroes provided their own support in the form of Miss Militia, Velocity, Triumph. Manpower and Flashbang of New Wave were present, too. Their group assembled on the opposite side of the street, looking at the villains with complicated frowns.

"Tattletale. The backup's here," he reported as he climbed back to his feet.

"Nice! Who did the do-gooders sacrifice to the slaughter?" Tattletale changed her tune as he named them, blowing a raspberry. "Half of those are bad matchups against Lung! What were they thinking? Man, they're going to have a bad time."

"You sent Skitter, so I don't think you have room to talk. What good are bug powers here?"

A laugh came over the line. "She almost killed him a few weeks ago with those bug powers."

That piece of news made him take a second look at said villain, happening to catch the yellow insect eyes of her mask staring back at him. He shivered.

It seemed, in any universe, one thing remained constant about Skitter: she's nuts.

Also, was he imagining it, or was Sundancer squeeing like a fangirl while looking at him?

He checked over himself to see what he was doing right. His armor and gunlance stood out as the one big difference between past him and present him.

Lung sat up, silver scales covering the majority of his body. Purely for showing off, Jaune swung his gunlance to point at the villain, and fired a shell that hit him with the sound of a gong. Down Lung went, as he observed Sundancer's reaction.

Yes, definitely his gear. He filed a mental note to wear this outfit more often.

"Time to swap, Jaune. Let's let the others handle it." Tattletale suggested, having heard the shot and mistaking it as his eagerness to continue fighting.

"I'm heading out now. That was just a little gift I'm leaving for Lung. Do we meet at Bakuda's hideout, or should I swing by to pick you up?"

"Um. I'm… actually going to be busy, so you'll have to handle this on your own. Sorry."

"You're not in trouble are you?" He asked suspiciously. She was never one to enjoy sudden changes in the plan, so he couldn't see her sounding this neutral about it.

"I wouldn't put it that way. I'm fine."

Save him from sulky Annoying Blondes. It's always 'I'm fine' and 'don't bother me' as if that would magically dispel his worries.

The steps to his immediate future lined up in order. Defuse Bakuda. Avoid death by explosion. Defuse Tattletale. Avoid social death by humiliation. Celebrate.

"Okay. If you need me, just shout."

"Uh huh, I will. Good luck, Jaune." And with that, Tattletale hung up on him, the call cutting off as she started to address Escha.

He disengaged from Lung and made his way up the road. That signaled for the villains and heroes to begin moving, and they surged forward while granting their counterpart a wide berth. The two sides threw constant glances at each other, alert for signs of any tricks. One by one, they passed by him and took up positions at ranges that suit their powers to establish a loose formation.

"COWARD!" Lung's guttural roar followed his departure, soon drowned out by Miss Militia opening fire and the buzzing of a million insects. Jaune flipped the bird at him over a shoulder as a parting shot. Anybody with eyes would see that he had won this bout. No coward, was Jaune Arc.

Passing by Sundancer, who he was glad would be staying far at the back, he gave her a nod. She shyly waved her hand in kind to send his mood soaring. Who would have guessed that the key to a good impression was to show off the dragon you skinned and wore as clothes?

A couple of steps later, he experienced a most familiar sensation of heat at his back, and the light of the daytime sun illuminating the dark. It rather left him with a lingering feeling that he was going the wrong way.

Armsmaster was waiting for him by the PRT transport. After giving the driver an address, Jaune hopped onto the truck in a practiced motion alongside the man. They hung on as the truck turned down a side street. With a final glimpse of Lung, covered in bees and raging against a burning star, they set off deeper into the neighborhood.

After a few minutes of comfortable silence, Armsmaster spoke up.

"That was… impressive," he said. "You show a formidable level of combat experience for your age. Where did you learn that?"

"Here, there, everywhere." He shrugged and made a vague hand gesture, indicating the world in general. "I travel a lot."

"What alloy did you incorporate within your armor? Was the manufacturing someone else's work? The heat-resistant properties it exhibited would suggest the use of tinkertech materials. I'm interested in sourcing some for my own equipment."

The conversation remained on that topic for the whole length of the journey, a mind-numbing interrogation in which Armsmaster grilled him for inane technical details that he wasn't inclined to reveal even if he knew the answers.

Jaune might have been more cooperative had the man not sneered at the gunlance, calling it quaint while comparing it to his high-tech halberd. As it was, he breathed a sigh of relief upon receiving an alert from the driver that they were approaching Bakuda's hideout. One could only withstand so much subtle boasting of 'streamlined' Tinkering processes and 'efficient' tradeoffs, the latter very often boiling down to a disdain of aesthetics deemed superfluous. Armsmaster had something to prove, and he did it by putting down other people's craft.

As a precaution, the truck dropped them off at the point where residential homes butted against the sea of warehouses populating the eastern side of the neighborhood, a few blocks from their target. A quick trip through an alley, and the two of them were peeking around the corner, observing the path forward.

News of ongoing events must have reached Bakuda, because she had forsaken stealth for safety, gathering a veritable army to guard what could only be her hideout. It practically lit a beacon for those looking for her. The nondescript warehouse would have passed under the radar otherwise, identical to the ones surrounding it down to the graffitied exterior and general atmosphere of abandonment.

"What's the plan, then?" Jaune asked. "Frontal charge, push our way in?"

"If that was my intention, I would have brought my colleagues. No. Bakuda can detonate the bombs implanted in her victims, and I do not put it past her to use all of them in a desperate attack if she believes we might pose a threat to her." Armsmaster pointed at the top of the warehouse. "Can you get up there with your flight unit?"

Flight unit. How needlessly technical. Why not call a pair of rocket boots, a pair of rocket boots.

"Sure, I can do that. You want to go in through the roof?"

"You are going in through the roof, and will locate this bomb you've told us about. I'll draw Bakuda outside in the meantime to allow you an opening to neutralize it."

A simple plan. Too simple, perhaps. The crux of it depended on Bakuda deciding that she'd leave a fortified position to face a veteran superhero out in the open. What a laughable notion that told him Armsmaster didn't really understand basic tactics.

Five minutes later, squatting on a warehouse roof, Jaune facepalmed as he revised his opinion. Below, Bakuda, a woman donning grimy jeans and t-shirt with a gas mask her sole nod to a cape costume, stood at the entrance of the building and ranted insults into a megaphone at Armsmaster. Said man held a megaphone of his own that he had previously stowed inside a tiny compartment on his armor, and as he kept the crowd of ABB conscripts at bay, he hurled a slew of insults right back at Bakuda.

Well, 'insults'. They probably sounded far more devastating to a Tinker, but to Jaune, it resembled a scene of a teacher marking a student's papers—calling out a corner taken here, a better solution there, that kind of nitpicky stuff. The nastiest Armsmaster got was when he inquired about her IQ, intimating that it measured a few points lower than the number she proudly yelled out. Bakuda had gone ballistic upon hearing that bit. (Might have been crying, too.)

All told, the ploy was working like a charm. Somehow.

Then, Bakuda brought out her grenade launcher, and all hell broke loose.

As the building shook and smoke rose to the sky, Jaune followed along the ridge of the curved metal roof, on the lookout for a way in. His first instinct was one of the skylight windows dotting the area. Getting near the closest window dissuaded him of that possibility—the wires and blinking lights boded ill. He should have seen that coming. In a world of superheroes, blocking every entry point no matter their elevation was simply good sense.

That said, he had to raise a weakness in that assumption: in a world of superheroes, why assume people will use doors?

The gunlance slammed against the metal roof, blowing a hole in the aluminum sheet through the force of the blow. The blank stretch of the ceiling had no footholds or ladders with which one could climb, no spot for a bomb Tinker to stand as she set a trap.

No place to keep a person from falling to their death, either, unless they had a means of flight.

Before he dropped through the hole, he peered inside to search for his objective. The place was a mess, filled with all manners of bits and bobs. Piles of scraps laid beside tables and benches, atop which Bakuda had spread her unfinished projects, dozens in total. One corner appeared to have seen use as a testing range/torture chamber. Another corner, a surgeon table/torture chamber. That spot near the back, a makeshift bedroom/torture—

Basically, Bakuda was nuts.

On the second level of the warehouse, a bulky, beeping device sat pride of place surrounded by tools and notes. The plate of food placed on the table beside it, partially eaten, hinted that Bakuda had been spending time there prior to all the commotion.

He snapped a picture of the device with his phone, sending it to Tattletale along with a text.

Jaune: Is this it​

Annoying Blonde N.8: Could you maybe step away from the edge?

Jaune: I did. Is that the bomb​

Annoying Blonde N.8: Did you really? Send a pic.

Jaune rolled his eyes and took a step back, then snapped a second photo to send over.

Jaune: There now can you please just tell me​

Annoying Blonde N.8: Yeah. Matches the one they show on the news in my world.

Tucking the phone away, he hopped forward to drop inside the building. After a short free fall, he rocket-stepped to slow his descent, traversing the warehouse without touching the floor because a person would have to have a screw loose to booby-trap the place they're living in.

Hovering above an empty spot of floor, he threw out a shadowy hand as a test, only landing after a smack against it didn't result in an explosion. A turn on his heels, and there his goal laid.

For a device capable of wiping out every piece of electronics in a few hundred miles, the EMP bomb was tiny. A waist-high cylinder that, to him, looked a bit ramshackled due to its haphazard construction comprising whatever material was available. Walking over, he rested a hand on its side, and willed it to enter his Pocket.

Nothing happened.

Jaune sighed, and summoned his gunlance to the other hand. That still wasn't enough, so assorted tools and knickknacks began to spill out at his feet. He bumped his hip against the nearby table, and bombs rolled onto the surface. The 7-second bomb became a 5-second bomb before he managed to grab it again. A couple of healing potions replaced it.

He let out a loud cheer as the EMP bomb was finally whisked into his Pocket, and pumped his fist in victory. The world (technically the local area, but the world sounded more impressive) had been saved and it was thanks to him!

…He then spent the next ten minutes scrounging up a sack to shove all his stuff in, because he worked hard to hoard them and wasn't about to let that go to waste.

With the heavy gunlance on his shoulder, a trip back up through the hole in the roof seemed a little iffy. He wasn't that great at controlling the thing yet to deal with the increased weight and balance issues.

The front entrance was open, though, and Bakuda left through it without blowing up. It's likely safe as an exit.

Going across was a lot easier than going up. He blasted through the doors to the outside, sliding to a stop at the same spot the bomb Tinker stood earlier.

The battle appeared to be over, judging by the absence of further explosions, though the whole area was undergoing various states of catastrophe. On fire, frozen, melted, and a host of other effects. He winced upon catching sight of a leg fused into a warehouse wall, still twitching. A pile of ashes that reminded him of Oni Lee's power denoted a few more victims of Bakuda's careless aiming.

The majority of the ABB conscripts survived, so there's at least a silver lining. They cowered on the periphery, torn between fleeing and breaking down to cry.

As for Bakuda, she laid at the feet of Armsmaster.

"Oh, wow, did we just win?" Jaune wondered aloud. He flicked his helmet visor up for a better look.

Bakuda faintly stirred. Armsmaster jabbed the butt of his halberd to her neck, deploying a sedative of some kind. She ceased moving.

Welp. That was confirmation enough for him.

"We won!" Throwing back his head, Jaune laughed. He strode over to Armsmaster, tucking the sack of his possessions under his arm and stretching out a hand for a high-five.

The butt of the halberd pointed in his direction, and a cloudy puff of something shot at him. He inhaled a whiff and immediately felt a spreading numbness.

A vial of Antidote materialized in his hand. He upended the entire dose down his throat.

Escha said it was effective for poison. This felt like poison. Ergo…

The numbness faded, and he whooped in joy before realizing that, oh, this wasn't the time to celebrate.

"Hey, what the hell!?"

"Bakuda has been subdued. Oni Lee is in custody. Lung has fled," the hero rattled out, and leveled the bladed end of his halberd at Jaune. "You are under arrest."

…

…

"Wait."

He held up a hand.

"Wait."

He pinched the bridge of his nose.

"Wait."

He pointed at Armsmaster, and asked one question.

"Are you turning on me?"
