#2,126
Chapter 39: A Visitor's Guide to Brockton Bay - We Play Cops and Robbers After Dark (Pt. 1)​


The question was somewhat meant to be rhetorical.

Are you turning on me? How dare you! Raaah!

That sort of thing.

Armsmaster saw it as his own chance to attack, charging in with his halberd at the ready.

Which, Jaune supposed, rather answered the question. Any hesitation he had melted away, and he slammed his helmet visor shut. With a roar of effort, he swung the gunlance over his head.

In another life, Armsmaster would face Leviathan, and for a decent length of time matched the beast blow for blow. A normal human, augmented by the technology he built, had become superhuman. He jumped higher, punched harder, fought longer than any normal man could. Above everything else, his ingenuity shone through in the myriad tools he brought to hand, hidden within his halberd.

All that to say, if someone wanted to hit him, then they had better hit him hard.

Red Rook shattered the pavement, missing Armsmaster by the narrowest of margins. The man tried to seize the opening, but with a pivot and another roar, Jaune brought the gunlance back up on a course for the hero traitor.

Armsmaster angled his halberd to redirect the force of the lance, letting it pass by. With a twirl, the butt of the weapon struck Jaune under the chin, snapping his head back.

Recalling a certain mimic and its enviable acrobatics, Jaune activated his rockets to ride the momentum, kicking up to catch Armsmaster on the chest, scorching a line on the armor. He let go of the gunlance, and summoned Crocea Mors to hand, chopping down as he dropped back to the ground.

Armsmaster braced to deflect again. This time, Jaune was ready and his sword sliced through the metal shaft with the barest whisper of a sound, forcing Armsmaster to quickly backpedal before his head got split in half. A low, mechanical whine accompanied his steps, motors and gears boosting the strength of each leap to carry him out of range.

Having bought himself a reprieve, the man slammed the two broken ends of the halberd together, and twisted. Tiny hooks sprang out of the smooth metal to reconnect the parts, with some kind of adhesive spilling into the gap before hardening to a metal-like consistency. In seconds, the weapon became whole again.

Jaune, meanwhile, used the moment to stow Crocea Mors and retrieve Red Rook, then unlatched a clasp to open the gun chamber. A wave of his hand over the empty slots filled them with new shells. A flick of his wrist snapped the gunlance back into place.

Both fighters set into their stances, the tip of their weapons pointed at each other. In the periphery of their battle, the remnants of the ABB—press-ganged or otherwise—were scrambling to vacate the area.

His phone rang. Jaune couldn't spare the attention to answer the call.

"Why'd you do it?" he asked, glaring. "We won. Why ruin a good thing?"

For a while, the man said nothing. The silence dragged on until Jaune was about to give up on waiting, before Armsmaster spoke.

"For years, Brockton Bay hung in a delicate balance." The man paused, finding his words. "The ABB, the E88, Coil. My team could defeat any one gang. It would exhaust us, sap our numbers, occupy our full attention, but we could do it… were it not for the simple fact that the others would pounce upon the chance to tear us to pieces."

Jaune cocked his head. "What's that have to do with—no, no, I'm game. Why didn't you call reinforcements? Someone told me that you guys are the biggest parahuman organization in the world."

He seemed to have struck a sore point, because Armsmaster growled under his breath.

"Do you think my branch hasn't requested help?" the man snapped. "What we're given is never enough! Each move we make, we lose more resources, more people. Any reinforcements we receive, we spend shoring up our defenses to keep the parahuman gangs from gaining sway over another neighborhood. Most nights, a single crime we intercept means two more where the villains escape without consequences. That is the state of Brockton Bay."

Armsmaster shifted his weight, and Jaune moved the gunlance to keep covering him, finger on the trigger to blast a shell at the first sign of aggression.

"But, finally, I have a chance to turn it around and retake the whole city!"

Bang!

A nozzle extruded from the halberd, and spat a glob of acid that splashed against the gunlance shell Jaune fired. It didn't stop the projectile, instead eating through enough of the casing to destabilize its course, sending the round careening past Armsmaster to explode on a brick wall. An instant later, Jaune was in range, leading with the tip of his lance.

Armsmaster ducked low to sweep out Jaune's leg. Uncaring, Jaune stomped down on the foot with his full strength, only to slip as it failed to pin Armsmaster down.

The armor was the key to that. He would estimate the man compared on par with a Huntsman in physical prowess right now, mimicking the enhancements of Aura with whatever tech was hiding beneath the armor panels.

As he landed on his side, a boot met his helm to disorient him. A hand clamped over his own, and attempted to pry the gunlance from his grasp.

A canister appeared in Jaune's free hand. He tossed it up. "Bomb. Think fast."

Armsmaster reared back, letting go of him. The man realized his mistake as the canister spewed out a dark cloud, blinding yet harmless. Rather than any sort of tinkertech, it had been a regular smoke grenade acquired in Academy City.

Jaune escaped to the other side of the smoke, and called out, "Alright, I kind of get your frustrations. Hard not to after seeing what Bakuda's done. Still, you haven't really answered my question. Why did you stab me in the back, traitor? I gave you a solution to defeat the ABB, and passed the names of the E88 capes to you guys. I fought alongside you this entire way. I was on your side!"

"Out of the goodness of your heart?" Armsmaster said, and Jaune could just imagine the man sneering from somewhere beyond the cloud. "No. You are doing this because of what you stand to gain. Territory, influence, businesses that you can extort, people that you can rob or push your drugs on to… it's always the same old pattern." Heavy footfalls warned of his coming arrival. "But this time your greed would bring about your very demise. The ABB is defunct after tonight. The E88 will follow them soon. What a victory it'd be, if I get the rest of you villains."

The rest.

Bright hot anger turned cold.

"It's not just me you're trying to arrest," he stated rather than asked. His thoughts ran a mile a minute.

Tattletale had said that the heroes sent against Lung were a bad matchup for him. But what if they had a different opponent in mind?

Miss Militia possessed an arsenal of firearms at her fingertips, yet she used rubber bullets for them; great for ramping up Lung, devastating to squishier capes. Triumph had a shout that won't do much to a dragon, but could subdue many baseline humans at once. Velocity, with the speed to reach capes stationed at the backline like Skitter and Sundancer before they could run. Flashbang formed and threw concussive blasts, again a problem for those that cannot heal from a hard blow. Manpower… there's strength in strength, simple as that.

They had been getting ready to fight everybody except Lung.

Armsmaster strode through the smoke, and he had never looked so proud.

"Once it's over, thirty seven villains will be behind bars because of my team."

Let's see. ABB's got three. E88 has fifteen. Undersiders, Faultline's group, Merchants, Travelers...

They wouldn't know about a second Tattletale, so that number included him and Escha. Even a cat wasn't spared the name of villain.

"I can't help but feel you're labeling a lot of people as hostile when you don't have to. Of course, that's a moot point."

Because Jaune can definitely be considered an enemy now.

Pushing against the ground, he shot forward. The rockets compensated for the weight of the gunlance, letting him close the distance in a blink.

Two wires darted for him, blocked by his shield. Electricity arced along the length of the wires, the resulting shock sending a tingle up his arm until he threw the shield in his Pocket and slammed Red Rook down on Armsmaster, the man crossing his arms to catch the lance on his gauntlets.

Surprisingly, Armsmaster managed it despite his knees almost buckling—the revving motors inside his armor had gone from a soft whine to a shriek at the moment of impact. A deft twist angled the head of his halberd at Jaune's face, the blade replaced by a nozzle. More of that knockout dust blew out, forcing him to disengage before he breathed it in.

Skipping back outside range, he swung the gunlance barrel at Armsmaster, the threat of an imminent shelling round turning the man's pursuit into an evasive flip.

It had been a bluff. He wouldn't have fired, as the open doors of Bakuda's workshop was behind Armsmaster, and he'd prefer to not find out what a gunlance shell combined with a bomb warehouse resulted in.

Slowly, he started to circle Armsmaster, repositioning to a better spot. The man shifted his stance to face him, weaving his body to stay out of the direct path of the gun barrel. Neither rushed in.

The situation reminded Jaune of bygone days, sparring in a ring. In the past month, he had fought mortal men and invincible espers, along with beasts of all stripes. Yet, rarely did he meet this, a person he could overcome that might defeat him in turn. A battle of skill and weaponry where it could go either way.

Which sucked, because he really, really wanted to skip to the part where he beat Armsmaster to a pulp for his crimes, past and present.

"The Merchants, I get," he spat. "The Undersiders are small-time thieves, though. Faultline's a mercenary that you can buy off. The Travelers, I don't know much about, but at least one of their members would give up the life of a villain in a heartbeat. None of them have intentions to wreck the city or murder its people. They're—"

"What, harmless?" Armsmaster finished for him, and gave a derisive snort.

"Aren't they? Compared to what else is out there?"

Armsmaster quietly regarded him for a short time.

"You're serious, aren't you?" he said. With an intrigued hum, he began twirling his halberd, making gentle revolutions. "Then again, you have been in contact with Tattletale, a Thinker. She could well have poisoned your mind. They do that, you know."

"She spends most of her time being an annoying brat. I assure you, that isn't a superpower. Do you not have sisters?"

"She performs actions that remind you of your family? And you see nothing unnatural there?"

Jaune shrugged behind his shield. "Weird way to put it, but that's just how she is." He couldn't imagine her behaving otherwise, and didn't care to; life would become far too peaceful. "You'd know this if you ever bothered to give her a chance, but I guess it's beyond someone as heartless as you."

The blade of the halberd kept passing within a hair of the ground, never quite touching.

"In my experience, villainy is insidious," said Armsmaster. "It likes to cover itself in a romantic veneer, always ready with a sob story or a supposed code, some reason for why we should treat it with a softer touch than the 'true monsters.' It then digs its way in, little by little, until one day it becomes entrenched, at which point the pretense comes off and now we must expend unimaginable effort and sacrifice to drive it out." His voice hardened. "Well, not again. Not today."

Jaune found his eyes blurring out of focus, and noticed too late that he had been following the halberd as it spun around and around, picking up speed.

A metal ball on a chain cracked against the side of his head, throwing wide his aim with the gunlance. Armsmaster closed the gap in quick strides, eager to press the opportunity.

Shadows clamped onto the man's visor. A swing of the halberd—now back to bladed form—dispersed the ghostly arm. Armsmaster cursed as his vision returned to the sight of red scales. The gunlance knocked him off his feet.

Armsmaster hit the ground, rolled. He came up swinging his halberd to clear some room, expecting Jaune to have followed. He had been correct.

The weapon passed just under Jaune, whose knee met the one unarmored part of Armsmaster, his lower face, smashing against his chin to snap his head back. Two rows of teeth slammed together, cracking with the force.

Pushing through the pain, Armsmaster rolled with the impact. The taser wires shot out again as they had proven effective the first time, a deterrent for Jaune should he think of chasing, or a reversal had he actually been dumb enough to try.

Rather than striking their target, the wires landed on a bulky device of haphazard make that wasn't there before, and Jaune would have believed it if Armsmaster's heart stopped for a moment.

Its purpose served, the EMP bomb vanished as the gunlance crashed down on the distracted Armsmaster, driving him into the ground. His grip loosened on the halberd, and Jaune kicked it out of range before taking a half-step forward, pressing the gunlance barrel down to hear a click.

He flicked a catch, and the gun barrel shifted in response, panels sliding aside. He then drew hard on the trigger to release the remaining rounds in the chamber all at once.

Boomboomboomboom!

The gunlance's fullburst barrage caught Armsmaster with nowhere to run and nowhere to hide. His armor had to bear the full brunt of a point-blank explosion that would have gotten Jaune an approving nod from Bakuda. The rebound force threw the gunlance behind Jaune, dragging him along for a full body's length, his boots scraping two lines on the asphalt. A tremor originating from the lance shook his entire arm.

He'd take that minor discomfort any day just for the sight in front of him.

Ahead, Armsmaster laid flat on his back, twitching. The suit of armor bore a new color to go with blue and silver, a scorched black. Internal parts peeked through the broken outer shell, shooting off sparks.

His helmet had closed up, likely after Jaune wrecked those damnable perfect teeth. As he watched on, the mouth section slid apart again to let Armsmaster spit a glob of bloody vomit to the side, afterward gasping for breath.

Jaune studied him in anticipation of a trick, but he relaxed as Armsmaster tried to move his arms and merely managed with great effort to somewhat lift them before the weight proved too much to bear. Swinging the gunlance to cradle it on his shoulder, he strode over to his defeated foe.

"My win, I think," he said, drawing a grimace from Armsmaster.

"K-Knew that fucking thing had m-more tricks. Knew you were d-dangerous. Fucking dumb k-kid running"—the man groaned—"running around treating t-tinkertech like they're toys. You don't deserve it," he spat, his voice finally steadying.

Jaune squatted down next to the man. A snap of his fingers and a stimpak appeared between them, held between the index finger and thumb.

"Talk like that and I'd just leave you in this state."

He stabbed the needle into the exposed cheek, and administered a portion of the healing concoction. Not all, as he didn't trust Armsmaster to stay peaceful. (It's why his foot was grinding down on the man's dominant hand.)

"Illegal testing of unauthorized tinkertech…"

Jaune paused, and shot Armsmaster an odd look. Realization soon dawned on his face.

"Seriously?" he deadpanned. "I'm a criminal for taking pity on you? If this is your definition of villainy, then I kind of get why everybody's on that list."

Armsmaster did his best approximation of a sneer, blood staining his teeth red. "You had your chance. Dauntless thought you were just reckless and misguided. That you could be taught. Fool. You fight like an animal, brutalizing the weak…killing them. Your actions speak louder than words, murderer."

"Oh, no, no, you don't get to say that." Jaune waggled his finger in reproach. "I grabbed their attention. Took on all the risks. I cleared the way for you, and you waited until after I was done to call me out. You know, once you've reaped the benefits of it."

"Excuses. You lay the blame at the feet of everyone but yourself—"

Jaune shot back, "Who did I kill? Someone press-ganged into the ABB?"

He waited for an answer. The hesitation gave it away.

"...Yes."

"Liar."

Getting up, he looked around. The place was deserted by now, with Bakuda the sole other person in sight, still out of it. The PRT was sure to move in once they thought it's safe to do so, in order to secure the scene. They could handle her arrest.

He nudged the suit of armor with one foot, and withdrew it as more sparks flew. Armsmaster should have been blown to smithereens by the fullburst, testifying to the superb defensive properties of the suit. The whole thing was useless now, its value barely worth mentioning. Such a shame.

There hadn't been a method to strip it off Armsmaster during the fight, though. Not like the halberd that he kicked out of reach.

Which he had now retrieved. And was his.

Checking it over from end to end, the weapon seemed in good shape. The panel of buttons near the grip lacked markings to tell him their functions, and an experimental press ended with him pressing them all to try and change it back to the basic halberd form. He tested the heft, and swung it a couple of times to see how well a fit it was for him.

Not very. He decided then and there that the halberd was destined to be sold. Hawking the prized, state-of-the-art possession of his enemy on the market like a fresh-picked vegetable sounded like a wonderful idea.

"I'm keeping this," he said as he walked back to Armsmaster, detouring to grab the sack filled with his stuff.

The man did not look happy about that, but couldn't do anything but breathe out a sigh. "Do you think that'd hurt me? Go ahead. It doesn't matter. After tonight, I'll have the budget to craft ten more. One of you rats getting away is nothing. This day is still a resounding victory."

Jaune stared at him for a long time, mulling over those words. They bothered him something fierce. Not the idea that Armsmaster was declaring it his win, though that rankled, too.

"Hey, quick question."

Armsmaster stirred, but stayed silent.

"If you, oh, I don't know, defeated an Endbringer, what would your budget look like?" Jaune watched Armsmaster as he spoke, noting how the man stiffened up at the mention of an Endbringer. "By any chance, is it high enough that you'd kill people on your side for the opportunity?"

The man scoffed. "I never would."

Jaune looked down at himself, then at Armsmaster. He cocked an eyebrow.

"You would have had your day in court," Armsmaster said, pausing to take a breath. Just talking was tiring him. "Even a chance to turn your life around, away from the scum you associate with. I'm not a murderer."

"...I don't believe you."

First-hand eyewitness speaking, slightly scarred for life in the aftermath. He knew what he was talking about.

"But then," he added, squatting down next to Armsmaster again, "it's possible you really won't do that this time around." He set the halberd and sack aside. "Not because I trust your strength of character or whatever. It'll just be very, very difficult for you, is all."

With one hand free to work, he proceeded to administer the rest of the stimpak. Once done, it was discarded, dropped atop Armsmaster as a bit of color returned to the man. Besides all the red, he meant.

Jaune then summoned a small object.

If one were to describe the object, they might say it was a cylinder colored yellow with an empty light at the end and buttons along one side.

It sort of looked like a bomb.

"You know, I couldn't quite believe it when this ended up in my Pocket. Goes to show that I should perform battlefield requisitions whenever I can. It's apt, don't 'you' think?"

Armsmaster's mouth fell open.

"You wouldn't. There are rules!"

"Pret-ty sure we broke most of them between the two of us."

Jaune placed the bomb beside the recovering man, inches from his grasp. A moment of further thought, and he stabbed another stimpak into Armsmaster, leaving the syringe sticking out of him. Maybe it'd make the difference, a courtesy never given to Sundancer.

The buttons were numbered. 1, 5, 10. Seconds, he presumed, and he pressed the last option. The bomb started beeping. The light lit up, blinking.

Jaune began backing away, picking up his stuff in the process.

"Put in this situation, I can kind of understand Corvo a little better now," he admitted. "If I had to guess, he let them live and didn't care if they died, while they wished he had killed them. It's not a kind thing, but there's a… a fairness to it, if that makes sense. Anyway, bright side? You might survive." His eyes darted to the side, a tell for one of his lies. "Might. I still get nightmares about her."

Armsmaster tried to move. The suit refused to budge.

Gunlance on a shoulder, Jaune spun around and booked it.

Behind him, the timer hit zero.


-o-​


His phone rang and rang. This time around, it was the other side refusing to answer. Given little to go on, Jaune made for the only spot he could expect to find the heroes and villains, the place where he fought Lung.

He didn't have much of a plan, more of a goal. The Protectorate sought to put three dozen people in custody. He, however, thought that the number needed some trimming.

The villains stepped forward to stand upon the line when this city called on them, and the reward for their deed was a jail cell? No, that didn't sound fair at all, and he rejected the notion of being yet another person to turn his back on those guys tonight.

He covered most of the distance through a series of long glides, the gunlance tip sometimes scraping the road below. Any higher risked a bad fall with what he was carrying, and though he had the presence of mind to swap the bombs in the sack with other items in his Pocket, that still meant healing potions and various useful things breaking should the boots overheat and he drops out of the sky.

The rockets did, eventually, shut off to leave him traveling along the ground. Weighed down by his armor and weapons, his pace slowed down to a jog, and he ran somewhat blindly through the unfamiliar streets. It didn't matter too much, as a glimpse of glowing figures zipping around high above the buildings provided a good indication of his heading.

He ducked into an alley, and a ways down found himself experiencing the strangest sense of deja vu. Up ahead in the gloom, there grew a great din of overlapping shouts, the clashing of steel, explosions, and other tell-tale signs of conflict. He hurried his pace, soon bursting out of the alley with his weapons drawn.

There were no Endbringers on this occasion, but the number of capes present, locked in battle, reminded him quite vividly of that time. They—

Wait a damn minute.

What was the E88 doing here?

Pandemonium reigned amidst the three-way battle, as everybody fought everybody. Lady Photon and Purity, the latter shining bright as a star, shot laser blasts at each other high above the street, while Dauntless maneuvered to try and hit Purity with his glowing lance. One of Coil's mercenaries was engaged in a sniper duel with an unseen person on the rooftops. Below them, the duo of Assault and Battery contended against Krieg, who in turn was trying to get in range of Faultline to strike her down, who in turn cut into the asphalt, walls, and street lights with a mere touch, causing the terrain to trip up or topple onto the Protectorate heroes. Oddly, the woman never used her power on her opponents, fending them off through indirect means whenever she could and employing martial arts when it came to close quarters. She was holding her own but her focus seemed elsewhere, and it's no mystery why.

Labyrinth hunched against a storefront with Spitfire standing in front of her teammate, spraying down lines of lava-like substances on the road to keep Clockblocker at bay. Geometric crystals sprout around them to block the electrical zaps Kid Win fired from atop his hoverboard. Nearby, a teenage hero whose name Jaune had forgotten struck a knockout blow to a strange man, one completely white from head to toe, only for the man to flicker and appear upright in his previous spot, none the worse for wear.

A fog rolled across the ground, the sound of claws scrabbling within, advancing on a PRT truck and the troopers there. Shadow Stalker knelt atop the vehicle, firing bolts into the cloud in the hope of hitting whatever was lurking inside.

And far, far down the street, the Merchants were running away, leaving their allies behind to save their own hide.

Jaune narrowed his eyes at that. This wasn't the time, but he'd remember it. For the time being, his first order of business was to punch Clockblocker help Spitfire and Labyrinth.

"The fuck is that samurai armor? When did the ABB get another cape?"

Jaune turned towards the speaker, meeting the eyes of a shirtless man wearing a steel tiger mask, an appearance that reminded him of that Hookwolf from the meeting at Somer's Rock.

That was the furthest he got before the air exploded in front of him, throwing him back into the alley.

Screeching to a halt a few yards in, he moved the person firmly into the 'Enemy' column. The halberd and sack were placed to the side, and he drew his shield, advancing again. Another blast occurred, weaker than the first, and ensconced behind his defenses Jaune saw that it was just plain air doing this, shimmering claws forming around the cape's fists before he threw them with a swing of his arm. The blades of wind whistled as they crossed the intervening space, exploding on impact.

It made for slow going, each blast stopping Jaune in his tracks. The cape used a tactic of aiming at different angles—the head here, the leg there—to buffet him from one side of the alley to the other, shaking him to the point of nausea.

Unwilling to keep playing that game, Jaune swung his gunlance forward, finger on the trigger.

He didn't get the chance to fire. A ball of purple energy slapped the cape in the face, and for reasons unknown the man immediately doubled over in laughter. A person crashed into him a moment later, knocking him off his feet. A brief scuffle ensued that ended with the disoriented E88 cape in handcuffs and a suit of high-tech silver armor standing in front of the alley.

Jaune stared at the scene for a bit, then shrugged and shifted his gunlance to the newcomer.

"Whoa! Whoa!" cried the armored cape, Gallant, as he waved his arms in a panic. "No need for that, I don't mean you any harm!"

Carefully, and with great suspicion, Jaune lowered his weapon. Gallant heaved a sigh of relief.

"You're HuntsMan, right? Jaune Arc? I was hoping to run into you. Clock mentioned that you switched to wearing red medieval armor when you fought Lung."

The helm vanished into the little space left in his Pocket, showing his face. "Yeah, you found me. Why did you help me out, anyway?"

"Uh, well." Gallant seemed to not know what to do with his hands, fidgeting about. The boyish uncertainty contrasted his knightly appearance; it rather lent him an air of honesty. Finally, he mumbled, "You're a relative of Glory Girl…"

Jaune resisted the urge to facepalm.

"I'm not—nevermind. What's your point?"

"I didn't want my girlfriend to hear that a family member died because of the E88, it'd devastate her."

He cocked his head to the side, brows furrowed as he parsed that statement. "Sooo, you helped me because you don't want her to be sad? That's your reason?"

Gallant nodded.

Huh. Should have expected that of the guy who chose the old-fashioned donut (simple tastes, let's others pick first, sometimes exactly what it said on the tin).

Jaune adopted a less aggressive stance. "Alright, how do you want to proceed? Telling you now, I'm not surrendering. You guys screwed us over."

"I-I know, and I'm not here to fight you," said Gallant. One of Purity's lasers shot out the street light above him, and the boy ducked his head, speaking quickly, "Look, I don't agree with what's going on, either. Things have gotten a little too crazy with the E88 showing up, and at this rate I'm worried a lot of people will end up dead, yours and mine."

Jaune hummed in thought, finding himself concurring with the assessment. Whatever hope the Protectorate had of an easy victory went out the window with a third faction added to the mix. The chaos around them was intensifying over time, capes like Spitfire and Purity growing desperate to stave off their opponents. It'd take only a single move to start the dominoes, with people dropping like flies.

The presence of the E88 also begged the question of why they've come. They're a hostile force to the other villains, that was plain to see with Krieg's attacks on Faultline.

"What are you suggesting, then?" he asked.

"A truce," Gallant offered, and his breath hitched as the gunlance rose a touch higher. "I understand you don't trust me since the Protectorate was the one to break the last deal, but I'm serious. A truce, so that we can de-escalate and pull back our forces."

It sounded nice. Problem was, he didn't believe Gallant had the authority to make that stick, and he said so.

Today he learned it was possible for a faceless suit of armor to express sadness. Sighing, he racked his brain for a solution. It…wasn't impossible.

"We can't rely on your superiors," he warned. As far as he knew, they were all complicit in the decision to turn on the villains. Also, one of them might be dead, but let's not mention that. "I need to get my people out, and they probably want nothing more than to bail, too. Since your Protectorate isn't letting it happen, we'll have to stage an escape for them." Jaune glared at the other boy. "We," he stressed the word.

Gallant gulped, but nodded. "Most of them would be a few blocks over by now. My group was supposed to take down the villains that didn't go fight Lung—"

"Where's Tattletale?" Jaune cut in. "And did you see a cat?"

"I, uh, I might have? Sorry, it all became a little muddled once the Empire arrived. They hadn't expected to see us, but then Hookwolf tried to attack Assault and it snowballed from there. During that, I overheard somebody shouting to the other villains to head for their teammates. It was Tattletale, I think…one of them, at least." That last part was spoken with a measure of confusion and, perhaps, fear.

"To mount a rescue, I'll bet," Jaune said, and despite the grim situation, he couldn't help a smile. She had read his mind.

Well, that, or she was banking on causing a huge commotion that'd keep everybody busy while she slipped away with Escha.

…Yeah, that seemed more likely.

"She broke through our encirclement along with the Undersiders and Coil's guys," Gallant confirmed. "A bunch of the nazis chased after them. I got the impression that your…friend?... might be one of their targets."

Jaune swore under his breath. That explained the unanswered calls. She had her hands full.

"I don't know what happened to them," Gallant admitted.

"We'll get to that," Jaune said, hiding his worry. He pointed at the altercation between Spitfire, Labyrinth, and the teenage heroes. "Right now, it's time to prove your conviction. Get your teammates to back off, or I'll do it."

He nudged his stuff deeper into the shadow of the alley with his foot for later retrieval, and broke into a run. Gallant rushed to follow, then overtook him in order to reach his friends before Jaune could make good on his warning.

"Clock, Kid! Stop!" Gallant chanced a glance behind him, getting another good, long look at the giant cannon on Jaune's shoulder. "Guys!" he cried, a little shrilly.

That drew their attention, and Clockblocker almost tripped over his feet on catching sight of who was next to his teammate. He scrambled to the side, away from both Jaune and Spitfire, his hands stretched out to freeze anybody that came near. Kid Win, the more trigger-happy of the two, fired a shot of his pistol at Jaune, the electrical zap smacked aside with a casual swipe of his shield.

Gallant jumped in front of Jaune to ward off a second attack.

"Stop! Stop! He's friendly!"

"No, he's not!" Clockblocker called over.

Spitfire looked from the Wards to Jaune, having no idea of what was happening. At her back, Labyrinth looked from the Wards to Jaune to a spot of empty air and now Jaune's extremely paranoid about the possibility of invisible people floating around them. For his peace of mind, he won't question it.

"He's willing to listen," Gallant amended. While keeping an eye on the various fights, alert for any stray shots heading their way, he explained, "HuntsMan is going to take charge of the unaffiliated villains and lead them in a retreat. We're letting him."

Kid Win balked, "What!?"

"Fuck that!" Clockblocker added.

If Gallant hadn't been sweating, he was now. "Please, guys, just listen to me. We need to focus on what matters. Vista and Aegis pursued the other group, where Hookwolf went. These guys aren't important. Our friends are."

Jaune nodded along, and gave Gallant a thumbs-up in support. That was a sentiment he could get behind.

He also shifted the gunlance to make a statement. Clockblocker and Kid Win got the message, falling quiet.

Unaware of the byplay, Gallant continued, "All they want is to go home."

"Oh god, please," Spitfire agreed, nodding rapidly.

"See? The E88 is so much higher of a priority, it's not even funny, and we're here fighting a battle we don't have to."

"But, Gallant, Armsmaster said—"

Gallant cut off Kid Win. "Armsmaster isn't here, and we can't contact him."

Guilty~

It's like they couldn't connect the fact that him being present meant he kicked the stuffing out of the older man, and left him for dead. That's some confidence they hold for their leader. Had they but asked… he would have lied through his teeth.

"And he was wrong, Kid. He assured us it won't end in another Boston Games." Gallant pointed at the ongoing melee. "Instead, we kicked it off early."

Kid Win grimaced, as did Clockblocker. Jaune had no clue what they're talking about, and so did the obvious thing, and acted like he completely understood the point.

"Armsmaster isn't here," Gallant repeated. He waved a hand at the older heroes, embroiled in combat. "Miss Militia, Dauntless, Velocity, Battery, Assault, Aegis, none of them are. That puts me in charge of the Wards, and I say we're needed elsewhere."

Jaune walked up next to him. "Your friend there could use your time-stopping power," he said to Clockblocker, indicating the scene further down the street where the nameless Ward was still beating up the pale man. "His opponent just won't go down."

"And Kid, I need you to support Shadow Stalker," Gallant added. "Think of a way to hurt Fog in that form."

"What will you be doing?" Kid Win asked.

"I'm accompanying HuntsMan to make sure he keeps to his word." Neither of his teammates looked happy at that prospect. "Trust me."

"...Fine." Kid Win was the first to give in, zooming away on his hoverboard.

Clockblocker took a slower path, maintaining a watch on them lest they ambush Gallant. Soon, though, he turned and raced for his other teammate.

Gallant released the breath he was holding. "Oh my god, I can't believe they listened."

Jaune patted him on the back. "Hey now, you did a good job. Real leader material, from what I saw." He turned to the two villains. "Spitfire, Labyrinth, are you good to make a run for it? This opening won't last. The other heroes will notice us standing around."

"We are," Spitfire said, helping Labyrinth get to her feet. "Which way? I'll signal Faultline."

He indicated an alley, one that should take their group in the direction of Tattletale and Escha, and they began moving. As they entered the alley mouth, Spitfire gave a piercing whistle and kept going without pause. A short moment later, a second whistle answered her.

"She heard," Spitfire explained.

Jaune had to admit he found their professionalism very impressive. His team didn't have signals, just a lot of shouting and him relying on Tattletale to understand what he was thinking. It's all rather haphazard, really.

A steady beeping emanated from Gallant's armor. He fiddled with the side of his helmet, and the beeping stopped. A call, Jaune realized. One that the other boy had ignored.

"I can't see your teammates being very happy with you tomorrow," he commented, and gave an amused huff. "And all this because of a girl."

"I'm thinking of asking her to marry me. Don't tell her that."

Spitfire awwwed, to Gallant's embarrassment. She and Labyrinth soon split off down a side alley, no doubt to rejoin Faultline. Hopefully, they'd stay in the fight, and not run out on them all.

Jaune and Gallant raced on into the night.

Author's Notes:
