Chapter 40: A Visitor's Guide to Brockton Bay - We Play Cops and Robbers After Dark (Pt.2)​


Two clanking suits of armor journeyed through the alleyways and side streets of Brockton Bay. One called to mind a futuristic knight, the other red as the sky at sunrise. Their frantic dash had brought them about a block away from their destination.

The ground began rumbling beneath their feet, and they slowed their pace.

As Jaune peered into the dark alley ahead with great suspicion, shapes grew out of the gloom accompanied by monstrous growls and barks—and, curiously, human voices. The figures soon coalesced into a pack of massive beasts, all muscles and spikes to remind him of the Grimm. Sharp canines jutted from their jaws, and they appeared capable of eating him whole, measuring the size of cars.

Were these creatures hostile? They sure looked it, and Jaune braced his lance to stab the one in the front, stopping just short as he recognized the people sitting on its back.

Leaping aside, he pressed his back to the brick wall as the creatures, Bitch's dogs transformed through her power, thundered on by. Bitch glared at him, whereas Grue kept his steady gaze ahead. Regent was hanging onto the next dog, a fatter one that almost clipped Jaune in passing. Skitter rode the last mount, and she turned her head to look at him with those unnerving yellow eyes of hers.

Just behind Skitter sat Tattletale, and on instinct he opened his mouth to call to her, until the differences—the less healthy cast to her face, the weaker arms—leapt out to inform him this was the local version. The girl he knew yet did not know spared a look over her shoulder. Their eyes met, and she fluttered her fingers while showing him a vicious grin.

Then, the Undersiders were gone, through the alley and around the corner to leave him and Gallant in the dust.

"They…" He tried to find the right words, as the ones springing to his mind had to be wrong.

Gallant, with no such qualms, said it for him. "Are they running away? I guess once they rescued their teammates, they didn't see a reason to stick around."

"Can't be," Jaune replied, shaking his head in denial. "Maybe they managed to rescue everyone, and Tattletale sounded the retreat." Because the other possibility, that the Undersiders bailed on their allies like the Merchants did, was one he did not want to think about. He'd have to see this for himself. "Come on, let's hurry."

They resumed their previous brisk pace. At this distance, the two boys could catch snippets of the ongoing clash. It sounded downright nasty, full of shouts and screams. Taking a turn, Jaune sprinted the last stretch of the alley to arrive at the battle.

And if he thought the other place was chaotic… well, it didn't have two giant, well-endowed women in armor running around, he'd say that.

Of course, in terms of danger the pair ranked a fair bit lower than the giant metal wolf formed from an amalgamation of hooks and blades, currently running amok on the wide avenue with an oversized sword that it had gotten from somewhere—Kaiser can summon metal, couldn't he?—grasped in its maw. The blood splattering its body indicated that Hookwolf wasn't much concerned with holding back. The E88 had gone big, and they weren't going home.

Miss Militia led the offensive against Hookwolf, commanding Aegis and Vista along with a squad of PRT troopers, while Flashbang threw in his support. Together, they were barely containing the rampage, hampered further by the fields of sharpened blades that dotted the ground at their feet. Attempts to use containment foam led to Hookwolf casting off affected areas, growing new mass to replace them. Gaining his attention meant a desperate chase as allies poured down covering fire to allow his chosen target time to escape. Nobody was using rubber bullets anymore on him, though that changed little of the result.

Jaune tore his gaze from that scene, and began scanning the area, grimacing as he confirmed that, no, his allies hadn't won their freedom. There was Gregor spraying out glue-like fluids to slow down Manpower. Genesis clashing with Velocity. People switching places as Trickster, one eye blinded by a bleeding cut, kept ahead of capture. Ballistic going ballistic and shooting objects at the speed of bullets, sending entire cars crashing through second-floor windows. (Seriously, what the hell was he even doing?)

All of them occupied a place on his priority list, but none of them were the people he was looking for right now.

"Dammit, where's Tattletale? Where's Escha?"

A gauntleted hand grabbed his shoulder. Gallant pointed. "Is Escha the cat? I see it."

Indeed, it was her. Further down the street, where the PRT left their fleet of vehicles, the felyne fought alone against a dozen troopers trying to subdue her. Yowling her battle-meow, she swung her boomerang, knocking batons out of hands and cracking shins, darting between her opponents to avoid their retaliation.

One of them took her down with a tackle, and almost lost his grip as he found the cat far stronger than she appeared. His shout for help led to the others dogpiling Escha to keep her trapped.

Gallant said something. He didn't hear it, already off like a shot as [Third Arm] flung him across the ground. It compensated for the weapon weighing him down, letting him slip through the various battles without impediment. Most of the participants were too busy to notice him, anyhow, though he had to dodge a couple of errant shots that Laserdream fired off during her aerial battle with an E88 cape, at one point passing by Triumph and a woman with a cage over her face laying opposite each other, both out of the fight with their ears bleeding.

Approaching the PRT squad, he released the gunlance to leave his hands free as he crashed against the troopers at an angle that toppled the pile, throwing them into disarray. In the aftermath, he laid into them with his fists, men and women thrown every which way as he made short work of the group; the martial arts they learned weren't designed to match bones that refuse to break, and a strength beyond the human limits.

Escha, meanwhile, pulled free. She scrambled to her feet and looked up at him.

"Jaune! You're back!" she cried, beaming.

He stomped on the last trooper, the one that had tackled Escha, then knelt down to the felyne's level. "I am. Sorry that it took a while. Are you alright?"

She flexed her arms to show how hearty and hale she was, causing him to smile.

"Would you happen to know where Tattletale went?" he asked.

Escha gasped in sudden recollection, and darted around him towards the open rear of a PRT truck. Turning back, she beckoned for him to follow before clambering onto the vehicle.

"She's here! She's here!" her voice called from within.

Jaune entered the darkened interiors of the truck expecting to see cushy seats and racks of equipment to match the vehicle he traveled around on earlier. Instead, he found a space built so barren that it was little more than a box with two benches. The purpose of this design became apparent to him as he looked at the occupants. The PRT vehicle, despite sharing a similar exterior to its brethren, served to transport prisoners like the two blondes laying on the floor before him, squirming in their restraints.

His head tilted to the side.

"Huh."

Tattletale, who wore a gag in addition to other bindings, began to make growling noises at him, signaling to Jaune that he should probably get a move on before she loses her patience (or catch an inkling of what he was thinking). Kneeling down by her side, he checked over the cuffs securing her wrists and ankles.

"Daaamn, they mean business," he remarked. "What even are these?"

"I-I think they're meant for Brutes, because she snapped the normal pair they put on her," Sundancer helpfully piped up from her spot. Unlike the blocks of steel strapped to Tattletale, the cuffs on her were of a lighter construction, albeit attached to a bar on the bench to limit her mobility. Also, no gag, presumably because she's polite.

"Yeah, no, I can't break this. Escha, can you check those people outside and see if they have keys on them?"

Escha nodded, and scampered off. In the meantime, he assisted Tattletale to a sitting position, and worked on loosening the knots for the gag. Once that was done, he pulled the cloth away.

Rather than a thank you, the first words out of her mouth were, "Jaune, what the fuck is going on? The heroes just started attacking us all! What did you say to them?"

"It had nothing to do with me, thank you very much," he snarked. "Turns out they want to capture all the villains in the city, big and small."

"They what!?"

"Yeah. That was pretty much my first reaction, too." Jaune shook his head, disgusted. "If Armsmaster told the truth, they were setting things up to backstab us from the start."

"Again, what!?"

"Hang on a minute, why are you so surprised? Shouldn't you be the one telling me this stuff?"

Tattletale flinched. Her eyes darted around, anywhere but at him."I-I… Shut up!" She glared, finally looking at him. "I was handling my side, and all the heroes were on yours. How am I supposed to know stuff that was happening over on your end? You should have noticed something!" she spat.

Jaune leaned back from the unexpected outburst, hands raised in placating motions. " Alright, alright, my bad. I wasn't trying to blame you, I swear. We were both caught by surprise."

Tattletale drew in a shuddering breath, and it occurred to Jaune that under the dim lights of their surroundings her eyes seemed to be rimmed with red.

"Hey, Tattletale? Is something wrong?"

"No," she replied, quickly. "Look, Escha's back. Help me get out of these cuffs. They're killing my blood circulation."

Escha scurried over to them, jingling with each movement, and offered up her bounty, a pile of keys for cars, houses, lockers, and many other purposes. The daunting task of discerning which keys would fit the cuffs became fairly easy after Jaune discovered the matching dots color-coded for the different types of restraints—red for Brute cuffs.

"How did they catch you?" he asked as he finished releasing her wrists, and moved on to her legs.

"It was Tattletale, that bitch!" hissed Tattletale, growing angry at the reminder.

He glanced up at her. "Uh… she's you."

"Yeah, so? That means I can call her a bitch if I want to. I helped her get Grue and Skitter back, and the first thing she did was hightail it out of there to leave me surrounded on all sides by the PRT. Somebody tackled me from a blindspot"—she spread her arms—"and now here I am. God, I hate her."

"Did you see who it was that brought you down?"

He made a mental note to teach her the basics of fighting on the ground. With Aura, elbows and knees can do nasty things to an opponent lacking its protection.

Tattletale bit her lips, thinking. "Miss Militia, maybe?" she guessed. "They all piled on too fast, but she certainly seems the type that wouldn't hesitate to sucker punch a sweet, delicate girl like myself. Gal gets downright nasty with how she fights, let me tell you…"

He left her to grumble, listening with half an ear as he padded over to Sundancer. Her cuffs bore a purple dot on the underside, and lucky for her, that matched with a few of the keys he had.

"Thanks for that," she said afterward, rubbing her sore wrists.

"You're welcome. Are you hurt anywhere?"

"A few bruises, nothing that bad." She gave a rueful laugh. "I should have paid attention better. I think I might have been the first to go down—got decked in the face before I knew it."

Tattletale shot her an unfriendly look. "Yeah, well, maybe you should have called up a sun to keep Velocity away." What began as a mild snark grew bitter. "You know, like you could have to get us out of here ten minutes ago, instead of wasting time?"

"I told you, it was too risky," Sundancer said, shaking her head. "I could have killed you at this range trying to melt my handcuffs."

"It would have been fine."

"Say that after I hit the gas tank and blow up the whole car!" Sundancer argued with a bit of heat. Jaune got the sense that the two girls' time together in the back of this PRT truck hadn't been a quiet one, despite Tattletale's inability to talk throughout the whole experience.

Tattletale gave a scoff, crossing her arms and turning her head to the side. "Always with an excuse. What good even are you without your powers?"

"Hey, cut it out," Jaune chided. As Tattletale whirled towards him, displaying a sullen glower, he softened his tone and said in admonishment, "Would you like it if I made you do your Thinker thing all hours of the day, and have you live with a perpetual migraine?" He pointed at Sundancer. "She might not suffer the same blowback, but she does have better reasons to not use her power than other people have to use theirs, so let's not rag on her too much, alright?"

As best as he could understand it, parahumans acquired powers through a luck outside their control. They didn't get to have an initiation test, a moment where they could choose between a normal existence and the life of a Huntsman. For someone thrown headlong into this situation, to fear killing a fellow person wasn't wrong. Unwise and very unrecommended, but not wrong. Given a cause—people to protect and a monster to be slain—he knew firsthand that Sundancer would fight with all her heart.

That sentiment didn't quite click with Tattletale. She gave a derisive snort, puffing herself up to continue sniping at the other girl.

Changing tack, Jaune patted her on the shoulder, adding, "Just watch her fry Leviathan sometimes, then you'd change your tune. Everyone has their specialty."

"Excuse me, watch me do what?" squeaked Sundancer.

He blanked for a bit, then smacked his forehead. "Oh, shoot. We still haven't told you all about that yet. Yeah, so, Leviathan's dropping by in around a month."

"Three weeks," Tattletale helpfully corrected, cheering up a little as she watched Sundancer's rather polite and quiet freakout at the new information.

"T-That was a joke, right? Please say it's a joke," the other girl managed to choke out.

"You'll see soon."

Jaune interjected, "Or don't. Honestly, I'd suggest skipping. If you need a quick exit—"

Tattletale clamped a hand over his mouth.

"Quiet down, Jaune. Don't go making decisions like that on your own."

They began to bicker, except the world wouldn't let them hit their strides before sending a reminder of the ongoing troubles taking place outside this box.

Tock, tock, tock.

The knocking came from the open doors of the vehicle, where Gallant now stood with knuckles poised to rap on on the wall again. How long he had been present was unclear, and the boy tried to dispel the wariness of everyone there beside Jaune by waving his hand.

"Hi, all! I apologize for the interruption, but there's still a big fight going on out here."

Tattletale jabbed a finger at him. "And you're on the other side. Escha, attack!"

Heeding her, Escha pounced at once. She landed on the suit of armor, where she proceeded to unleash her mighty claws upon Gallant, swiping furiously.

Good enthusiasm. Not that effective. Gallant plucked her off of his scratched-up armor, and held the hissing felyne at arm's length.

"He's a friendly, actually," Jaune said, to calm Escha.

The cat ceased her struggling. Looking from Gallant to Jaune, she scratched her ear with a paw.

"Really?"

Jaune nodded. "Uh-huh. We worked out a deal. He'll help me get everybody on our side away from this mess."

"And I need your help beating back Hookwolf," Gallant blurted out, to make Jaune frown.

"That wasn't part of the deal. Why?"

"He's escalating. All of the Empire capes are, but he's the worst of them. So far, it's just Aegis that he's tearing to shreds, but that won't last."

Poor Aegis. He's 'just' facing grievous injuries, no reason to worry. Jaune dreaded to hear how they treat the guy in the day-to-day.

"Sounds like a good distraction for us to slip away," Tattletale remarked.

Gallant turned to Jaune with what was probably a pleading gaze behind that helmet. "Come on, man. Let me go home with all my people. Please."

Put on the spot, Jaune dithered, trying to find a reason to agree that was compelling enough to convince his own self. A part of him loudly supported the idea of hunting a giant wolf to keep people safe—it's pretty much the first line in a Huntsman's job description. The rest of him admitted that Tattletale had raised a stellar observation. A busy hero was a hero that lacked the time to chase them.

"I… guess I'd have to travel that way anyhow," he said slowly, his eyes flicking up and down the street to pick out the individuals he came here to get, evaluating their situations. "The Travelers and Faultline's team are scattered all over the place. If we happen to get within range of Hookwolf, I can pitch in. Otherwise, every hero freed up is one that you can send at him instead of at us."

"That's a better plan than anything else I can hope for. Let's do it!" Gallant agreed without missing a beat. The boy stepped aside for Jaune to exit the transport truck, eager to move things forward lest he changed his mind.

Before following, Jaune turned to the other people within the vehicle. While Escha had seemed fine with whatever he decided, Tattletale didn't look very happy and Sundancer was downright fretting.

"We could use a couple of getaway cars," he said, passing the pile of keys into Tattletale's hands. Seeing her hesitate, he leaned down, peering eye-to-eye with her. "We don't have to be like the other Tattletale. A quick in and out, and I can have everyone ready for you to rescue. Push comes to shove, and the heroes object to that? I'll give them a good reason to back off."

"This is just more stupid risks for no payoff," she complained. Idly, she began sifting through the keys.

"Story of our lives, Tattletale. It'd get better." Leaning to the side, he looked past her shoulder at Sundancer. "Can you drive, too?"

Sundancer shot to attention upon being addressed. "Y-Yes! I took my driver test a couple years back. Um, my license might not…" She trailed off, no doubt recognizing that driving with an expired license would be the least of their offenses tonight. Fidgeting in embarrassment, she settled for a firm nod of her head.

"That will work," he assured her, glossing over the slip-up. "You and Tattletale can stay here to figure out which cars we're taking. Check for those guys that worked for Coil, too, because I don't see them anywhere. Escha, I want you standing guard to keep people off their backs."

The felyne wriggled out of Gallant's grasp, and after landing on the ground she gave him a salute.

Jaune returned it, and hopped down from the truck. "Alright, gang. Plan is a go. Good luck, I'll see you in a bit aaaand of course it's not going to be that simple," he grumbled under his breath, gaze directed upward.

Cape fluttering in the night breeze, Glory Girl descended from the sky bearing a wrath worthy of a storm god (Misaka Mikoto). Hers was the kind of face that said she had long chosen violence, and was here to make good on it. Uncaring of the gunshots and lasers going off behind her, she hovered above them, casting a judging glare from face to face until it returned to him, where she stared with a hard intent.

"You."

He ventured a joke. "Whatever happened to 'cousin'?" The cheeky grin was more of a grimace; his audience wasn't laughing.

Slowly, she shook her head.

"I really thought I was doing the right thing, going to bat for you," she said in a voice that seemed barely-restrained from becoming a shout. "I thought we were connecting. Hell, you could have straight up joined our family and nobody would even blink with how well you fit in. I offered you a place to belong. I opened a path for you to get away from villainy."

Jaune raised his hands before him, motioning for her to calm as he spoke quickly, "Look, that was nice of you and I appreciate it. Thing is, the situation isn't that simple. There's—"

"I tried so hard," she continued, giving no indication she heard him. "But you had to stick with scum in the end." Glory Girl jerked her chin at Tattletale, half-hidden inside the truck. "Is she that good a fuck? Was that what I had to do to get you on side?"

"Glory Girl!" Gallant rebuked, only to stiffen as she whirled to face him.

"And you! What the hell are you doing with them?"

The poor guy looked ready to bolt. "I, um. With how tonight has gone sideways, I figured if I could reduce the number of moving parts, it'd swing things in our favor again."

"Oh, really? How were you going to do that, hm?" asked Glory Girl.

For Jaune, the alarm bells began to ring. He had often heard that tone of voice in the past. Gallant missed it, to his detriment, and gave an earnest reply with little thought.

"Okay, so the smaller gangs like the Travelers and Faultline aren't as dangerous as the Empire. Without them in the picture, the Protectorate can focus on the real danger. I was—"

"You were what?" Glory Girl snapped. "Letting them go? The Protectorate dragged my family into this mess, and now you want to back out? No. You and I are arresting them, starting with the ones right here."

"Give it a rest, will ya, Glory Hole?" a new voice joined the conversation. Tattletale stepped off the truck, and planted her hands on her hips, looking at Glory Girl with a fearless grin. "Your boytoy there is the only person among you heroes making any headway in stopping the E88. What's your plan? Punch harder? That didn't go very well for you the last time, as I recall."

Greeeat. She's in that kind of 'helping' mood. Jaune sidled closer to Tattletale, maneuvering his frame in front of her. She elbowed him in the ribs, sliding forward to continue her spiel.

"Did you get all the bugs out of your hair yet? I doubt you've fixed that weakness in your forcefield, so we can have a repeat act, if you want." She turned to him. "Get this, Jaune. Girl goes around pretending she's the top dog, except one good hit shatters her shield to make her human again. We scream that from the rooftops, and she'd be dead within the week."

Glory Girl gave a derisive scoff. "Wooow, that's literally the same crap you spouted off before," she said in mock praise. "Why don't you get some new material? Because I remember smacking you so hard you cried. I don't back down to threats. Gallant?" She tilted her head, her expectation clear.

A flash of hurt then passed on her face as Gallant stepped between her and the pair of Jaune and Tattletale.

"Hahaha! Look at that, even your man can't stand by you," Tattletale taunted. "I wonder what he'll think if he hears the truth about your sister. You know what? Let's find out, unless you back off right now."

Glory Girl's eyes widened.

Tattletale caught the look, and she deepened her grin. "I'll be nice and give you a count of five to think it over, then the PRT gets to—mmph!"

She looked down at the fingers placed over her lips, then turned her head slightly to glance up at Jaune.

"Now, now, Gossip Girl," he said as he wrapped an arm around her waist, pulling the girl back. "As much as I like to hear you talk, it's doing more harm than good in this situation. We're not here to hurt her or her family, so how about everybody just chill." He directed the last part to all parties present, receiving a grateful nod from Gallant.

Tattletale tried to say something behind his hand. When he wouldn't relent, she bumped her hips against him and pouted.

They had an observer. Jaune gazed upward, and saw Glory Girl watching their byplay with an uncertain air. For one who divided the world into simple terms of villains and heroes, it must be quite a strange sight. Before her were a pair of criminals, dastardly and nefarious. Yet, he rather suspected that she had not many chances to encounter a villain taking part in this kind of casual, affectionate scene, such goodness being the domain of heroes. His actions ran counter to her worldview, and it stayed her hand.

Within that short reprieve, he considered how best to proceed. Now that he was aware of her weakness, Glory Girl presented less of an issue for him—it just took two hits to bring her down. That said, he'd prefer a peaceful outcome, because she was right on one thing. She had tried to be kind to him.

So, he leaned into the act, resting his chin atop Tattletale's head and smiling at Glory Girl to project a carefree—playful, even—image. With his hands full, he held no weapon, evoked no threat. As for Tattletale, her greatest weapon, that mile-a-minute mouth of hers, had been neutralized. Clearly, they weren't here to fight.

The ball had been passed into Glory Girl's court. She could try to arrest them, sure. On the other hand, any reasonable person must agree that launching an attack on them would be a bit much. Whatever she decided would speak volumes, and she knew it.

Gallant did, also, and he threw his weight onto the scale, speaking soothingly, "I don't like Tattletale."

"Mmph, mmph!" retorted Tattletale, rolling her eyes.

"I was at the bank, too. I don't like Tattletale," repeated Gallant, his focus on Glory Girl. "That goes for pretty much every villain. But this plan to stab them in the back? It doesn't sit right with me." he pointed behind him, at them. "They came here trusting us, and they were willing to help. They still are, that's the strange thing. You talked about giving HuntsMan chances, and he was doing the same!"

"But he—"

The two heroes started to argue back and forth, warming up to a furious row. On the sideline, Jaune felt a tug on his sleeve, and he looked away from the pair to see what Tattletale wanted. She was pointing at his hand, once more requesting he move it. He sent her a tepid gaze to convey his doubts of how wise a course of action that would be.

She pouted harder in response.

With a sigh, he took his hand away. In a surprising turn of event, Tattletale didn't immediately begin with snark, but peered up at him through her eyelashes.

"...You like hearing me talk?"

"To a point," he qualified.

She pouted at the comment, scrunching her nose. "Give me a better nickname," she demanded.

"Nope. You're Gossip Girl. What else would you call that thing you do all the time to people?" He tilted his head in Glory Girl's direction. "It's what you deserve, and way better than what you called her."

Tattletale clicked her tongue. It seemed to him more for appearance's sake than true annoyance.

They both fell quiet as Glory Girl drifted lower, touching down on the ground so that she was level with them. The hero studied them with careful suspicion, alert for a sudden and surprise blow. When none came, she looked Jaune in the eye.

"You'll really help?" she asked warily.

"Of course I'm going to help, what are you, dumb?" he replied with a scowl, which then flickered to reveal an amused expression.

Glory Girl snorted. She had remembered his words earlier in the day.

"I'll hold you to that. I'm gonna be up in the air, with a view of everything you do. A step out of line, and you're in for a world of hurt, got it?" She waited for him to nod in agreement. "And if you try to do anything to Gallant, I'll snap your spine in half. He's putting his job on the line for you."

With that warning, she shot into the air, heading off to assist her cousin. A quick twirl emphasized her point, that she would be watching.

"We could've taken her," Tattletale declared, squawking as Jaune ruffled her hair.

"Yeah, yeah. Go find us a ride."

He nodded to Gallant, and after picking up his gunlance, the pair set off.

Amidst a forest of steel and giants, it was easy to miss Crusader, who dressed like a knight and fought like an assassin. Ghostly copies of his form, long spears in hands, took to the field while the man remained out of sight. Jaune stabbed a few, and his lance went through them to little effect. He was left dancing between the ghosts, too quick for them to follow yet unable to strike a blow.

Gallant broke that stalemate. His powers dealt in emotions, and manifested in more ways than just the energy bolts he fires. He could see happiness. Grief. Worry. Anger. The full spectrum of the human heart. The man lurking in an alley thought the dark would hide him. Under Gallant's direction, Jaune launched a shadowy arm to drag him kicking and screaming out into the light.

The man shouted a lot of words Jaune didn't understand. Going by the way Gallant condensed and blasted a ball of pure frustration to the side of his head to shut Crusader up, they weren't nice words to say—Crusader smashed his own face against the concrete until loss of consciousness to escape the sensation.

With a villain subdued, a hero faced them next, and they enjoyed an easier time by far. The donuts had counted for something, with Manpower holding good opinions of Gallant and Jaune both. Talking him down from beating Gregor to a pulp was an amicable affair decided by the suggestion that he go assist his children.

Unfortunately, he chose to help Shielder with Ballistic rather than his daughter fighting the E88 cape Rune. Eh heh.

…He concluded that Ballistic could handle the extra pressure, and after sending his well wishes, put the matter out of mind to move on.

Trickster proved trickiest, annoyingly enough. Jaune hadn't realized how paranoid the guy was. His attempts to approach the cape ended in various states of failure: running the wrong way, appearing in the midst of a PRT squad, on one occasion standing inside a clothing store's display sans his gunlance.

One particular attempt put him clear on the other side of the wide avenue, switching places with Velocity just as his punch was about to connect with Genesis. The hero proceeded to deck Gallant with that punch. Oops.

And broke his fingers on the armor. Oops, again.

Meanwhile, Genesis, to her credit, hesitated from leaping for his throat after his sudden appearance—she had recognized his face. They struck up conversation, and she became his messenger notifying Trickster to stand down as Gallant pleaded with Velocity to turn a blind eye.

Which brought them to…

"What's our answer to this?" Gallant asked, a hint of a tremble in his voice as he stared up at the giant woman wielding a spear heading straight for them.

Jaune scratched his head, wondering the same. "Beats the hell out of me. How tough is that enhanced durability of hers? You think a bomb would work?" He summoned one, showing the device to Gallant, who took a big step to make some distance.

"That was made by Bakuda, wasn't it? What does it do?"

"No idea!" he cheerily replied, and wound back an arm, aiming for the ground near the woman's feet where the blast might leave her alive afterward. His ally ducked low, covering his head in a panic.

"...eal."

Jaune never got the chance to throw the bomb. The cape, Menja, tripped mid-stride, and he watched as she went from vertical to horizontal in a manner reminiscent of a felled tree, faceplanting on the street with an impact that shook their surroundings. The entire battle paused as a great cloud of dust and debris covered the area, blocking the sight of enemies and allies alike.

Within that cloud, he caught a glimpse of silver. A blink, and it was gone.

Soon, the dust cleared to reveal Menja lying completely straight and flat inside a deep furrow. There seemed not a blemish on her, leading many to wonder how she had been toppled in a single blow. One of her high-heel boots was missing, raising further questions.

"Did you just throw a bomb that swipes people's footwear?" Gallant asked incredulously.

Jaune shook his head. "I still have it right here. Wasn't me that did this."

"Oh…" The ground began to shake. "I guess that means you wouldn't be able to repeat it with her twin, then."

Fenja, who differed from Menja in that she wielded a sword and shield, made a beeline for her sister, calling out in worry with a booming voice befitting her size. Lacking any indication of who had defeated the other woman, she zeroed in on the person closest to the scene of the crime—Jaune. What he could see of her face twisted into a snarl.

He considered his options, lightly tossing up the explosive he was holding and catching it as it fell. He looked down at the device.

"Welp. Bombs away."

Except, the duo of Faultline and Spitfire chose that moment to burst out of a storefront, shattering the window. A spray of fire caused Fenja to yelp, hopping away from the superheated ground beneath her feet. The distraction allowed Faultline time to apply her power onto the surface of the building they exited from, forming strategic gouges that collapsed the whole brick front onto the giant.

Elated as Jaune was that they hadn't simply run off into the night, he must admit to a small measure of dismay.

"I'm never going to get to use this bomb, am I?"

Newter came out from within the ruined building, leading Labyrinth. He looked in bad shape, cuts criss-crossing his body. Jaune tossed him a stimpak at once, instructing him on its use.

"Thanks, man," Newter said, observing the fading wounds in delight. "You wouldn't happen to have seen Gregor, would you?"

Nodding, Jaune quickly explained, "Rescued him from a spot of trouble a few minutes ago. He should be with our getaway car further down the road."

"Huh. You're pretty alright, you know that? Watch this girl for me."

Leaving Labyrinth under Jaune's care, Neuter fearlessly raced into battle and jumped on Fenja to attach himself like a limpet to her bare thigh.

…In what was no surprise to anyone present, the giant gave an indignant shriek and tried to smack the orange man. Only, her hand missed. She gave another attempt. That missed, too. The hallucinogenic properties that the Case 53 imparted on skin contact could bring down an elephant. Or, in this case, a woman the size of an elephant.

Fenja landed on top of her sister just as Menja was getting up to send them both crashing to the ground, planking flat on their fronts. She was content to lay there, tripping out on visions of pretty butterflies and muttering about tasting colors, while Menja struggled to shove her off.

The group of mercenaries weren't staying idle. Spitfire must have relayed to her leader the plan, because after receiving news of Gregor, Faultline set her team on a course for Ballistic instead of bailing from the scene. The mercenary leader gave Jaune a curt nod in parting, which he returned with a grin and a wave.

Okay, that's Ballistic, Trickster, Genesis, Gregor and Newter accounted for, leaving…

Gallant tapped his shoulder, and pointed ahead.

"Ah," Jaune said, looking at the giant metal wolf. "Technically, my business here is done. Just so you know."

Since he last paid attention to this end of the street, the battle had taken a decidedly lethal turn with Hookwolf carving a path through his opponents. Jaune got a front row view of the process when Hookwolf rammed into a PRT trooper who had been a touch too slow, and the metal parts forming his shape shifted to draw the man in. What happened next started out gradual, cuts and tears ripped from the protective gear. Then, the hooks struck flesh.

The trooper was torn apart piece by piece, limb from limb, screaming the entire way. His remains left Hookwolf in a spray, rendered into tiny chunks.

"But I can make room in my schedule," Jaune added.

A monster was a monster, and his adventurer card didn't have Huntsman written on it for show. Also, he had a bomb.

The resulting explosion bloomed in total silence. A gray bubble grew in midair, suspending in defiance of gravity. It enveloped near a half of Hookwolf, and with an errant movement by the cape, a mere step forward, it ripped him in two. One part was locked in place, while the rest of him collapsed to the ground. Unlike the cast-off shedding he performed to recover from damage, this loss of mass included something important, for his keening wails reverberated across the area, sounding more animal than man. New growths warped in strange patterns as they took shape, crumbling as Hookwolf thrashed about. More bits and pieces detached as time passed, shrinking his form until flesh began to emerge. Soon, a person remained, panting for breath and crying as he laid in a shivering heap.

"Done~," Jaune said, buffing his nails on his armor. "See, this is why I like to start with overkill and scale down from there when facing big, nasty beasts with sharp teeth. If we mess up, we mess up on the side of 'I win,' meaning we still get to go home afterward."

"That's… not what I expected you to do," Gallant said, perturbed by the sight.

Jaune gave an awkward chuckle, raising a hand to rub the back of his head. "Well, it's what you got. I don't think I could have matched him in brute force."

Still, that bomb was scarier than he envisioned, with him almost preferring fires and shrapnel. At least there, a person stood a chance. This was just an instant death field for anybody caught inside. In another life, it—or one like it—would claim a number of capes, Dauntless and Miss Militia among them.

The pumping of a shotgun right beside him warned Jaune of the imminent danger, and he slapped the gun off course before it could fire. With the culprit within reach, he only had to swing his lance to catch them.

Miss Militia rolled with the momentum and came up on a knee, aiming down the sights of an assault rifle. She didn't shoot, waiting with her finger on the trigger as others moved into formation. Jaune grew keenly aware that he was surrounded by the heroes at this moment.

"Stand down, HuntsMan," Miss Militia ordered.

"Hah?" was his eloquent repartee.

Jaune looked to his left, then his right. He noted the chilly reception by most of the faces in attendance. Gallant might be the sole representative of those happy to have him here… except the other boy had also skipped back to stand alongside the Protectorate forces arrayed behind him.

"Not this again," he murmured, striving hard to not blow his top.

"Stand down," Miss Militia repeated. "Drop your weapon, and put your hands on your head. Any further actions of that level and we will resort to lethal means."

Jaune did neither. "Are you… are you mad that I went too hard on him? Seriously?"

"No kill order has been issued for Hookwolf. You did not have the authority to employ such measures," she snapped right back. "With your past actions, we're not taking chances."

"He killed, like, ten of your guys that I saw, and would have done the same to all of you," Jaune argued, pointing at the bloodstains. "It was pretty damn justified if you ask me."

That sentiment struck a chord with a number of people, none of whom spoke up in his favor, though they did look to Miss Militia for her answers.

"The necessity of that decision rested with the commander on the field, not with the rank and file, and certainly not with you," she replied in a tone that brook no disagreement. "For your sake, please surrender. We can sort it out at HQ."

Tension notched higher as the heroes saw Jaune tightening his grip on the gunlance.

"I'm not even asking you to leave us alone. Can't you just let us have a headstart?" he tried, one last time.

Miss Militia seemed to consider it, but…

"This isn't a game of cops and robbers, HuntsMan."

And that was that. Jaune braced for a fight.

A little ball of energy zoomed past him, missing by a hair to hit Miss Militia instead.

"Gallant! What are you doing?" yelled Vista.

"Oh no! I'm so sorry, I thought I could get him with a surprise shot!" No great actor, was Gallant.

The rumbling of car engines reached their ears. Two PRT transport trucks were barreling down the road, avoiding the capes still locked in battle and the various debris scattered around. A few heroes and troopers sent curious glances toward the vehicles, but nothing more, making the assumption that some of their own were operating them. They missed the trucks slowing down near Faultline's team and the Travelers.

Aegis dove for him. Jaune twirled aside, manifesting his shield to block a salvo of rubber bullets from the troopers. He charged at them, thinking to buy time by raising mayhem.

The world around him began to twist and bend. Distances stretched further than should be possible.

Gallant, again, sprang into action. He grabbed Vista, lifting her and moving her away while shouting that it was 'for her safety'—a poor excuse that he will likely pay for, later on. With her power interrupted, the road flattened out.

The trucks came roaring into range. The one in the lead diverted toward the group, prompting people to dive out of its path. Jaune did the opposite, running at the truck which hit the brakes long enough for him to leap onto its side, before it floored the accelerator to shoot past the Protectorate.

The look on the heroes' faces was one he'd remember; they hadn't realized until it's too late that the villains have hijacked the trucks, trusting in the logos stenciled on its sides. As he hung off the hand- and footholds, he stuck out his tongue at them.

Token potshots followed the convoy. Flashbang lobbed one of his energy blasts, Miss Militia fired a couple of rounds. They faced a choice, though. A chase through the city streets, or mopping the remaining Empire capes—Kaiser, Rune, Menja. Miss Militia made the call, ordering her subordinates to assist their colleagues.

Among them, Gallant kept looking in his direction. His knightly costume covered his whole face, so Jaune had no clue what the boy must be thinking.

Gallant's helm featured a glowing slit over the eyes. Very quickly, half of it blinked off then on again.

A wink.

Jaune grinned, and turned away. He climbed along the side of the truck to reach the driver door.

The window rolled down. Tattletale sat at the wheel, and the wind whipped at her hair to send it every which way. On the other side sat Escha, who waved to him.

"Did we get everybody?" he asked Tattletale, leaning in.

Green eyes flicked between the road and him. She nodded her head. "Our team. Faultline's. Travelers. Even those mercenaries from Coil—they were in a different prisoner transport."

"A full house," he said with a satisfied hum.

"Uh-huh. Time to make like trees and leave, I think."

"Yeah—wait! We have to go grab my stuff!"

"What?"

"It's a few blocks over. Make a turn here, make a turn here!"

"Goddamnit, Jaune!"

The truck pulled into a sharp turn far above the speed limits, with Jaune barely hanging on. In the back of the car came the sound of many voices cursing and shouting, mirrored by the second truck as a frantic Sundancer followed their lead.


-o-​


There had been talks of a party bandied about. Nobody was in quite the right celebratory mood. His face would soon be plastered on the news, and with how they've stuck a foot in it tonight, hard times were a-coming for supervillainy around these parts.

The doors to the PRT transport slid shut. Jaune waved to Faultline's little group of misfits, who, after the ordeal they've been through, bade farewell to him as if he were a friend. Then with a screech of tires, they departed to destinations unknown, leaving the tired trio of him, Tattletale, and Escha standing in front of a nondescript alleyway. Deep within, strange energies stirred to life. A gap through the universe began to unfold.

The others drudged over to the space between the buildings, but Jaune stayed where he was. He turned his head to and fro, searching the street for the other truck.

It was a fruitless endeavor. The Travelers had taken off on their own somewhere along the way.

Jaune heaved a great sigh.

"Were you really going to offer her a spot with us?"

He looked towards Tattletale, whose face was set in an unhappy frown. A halberd rested on her shoulder, lightly spinning as she played with it.

"It was a possibility," he admitted.

"You mean a lot less to her than she does to you. You know that, right? She would have said no."

He got the feeling she wasn't just talking about this world's Sundancer.

"Maybe," he said with a slight smile, willing to let the comment pass. Tattletale was right, and Tattletale was wrong. She hadn't stood where he stood, hadn't fought by that girl's side. He had become Sundancer's friend, by the end.

"Why even ask, then?"

In thought, Jaune turned his gaze to the sky. A thin sliver of the moon shone upon the city.

"I suppose… because it would grant her the freedom to go find what she's looking for."

One thing held true in this world and the last. Sundancer was deeply unhappy where she was.

But a step outside, and her life could have truly begun.

"What about 'you'?" he said.

He hadn't meant her. Tattletale understood anyway.

"I might have made some insinuations to my dear little sister. Told her she could improve her outlook if she would just skip out on this godforsaken town, whether with us or on a bus." Tattletale rolled her eyes. "She sees a future in it, better than what she could get elsewhere."

"Would she?" He'd readily admit that their lifestyle was not what most would consider ideal, and rife with risks. It's already a wonder that Tattletale stuck with him.

She gave him a little smile. "I had friends, back then. Money, swanky clothes, a place of my own. And yet the best thing that happened to me in Brockton Bay, was the day I left it behind. I don't remember being happy here, even if I thought I did in the moment. This city, this… this hole that I've dug, and wallowed in, and dressed up like a life… I must have fooled myself into believing it was healthy for me."

"And the other Tattletale is going to stay in that situation."

"Partly my fault. She seemed to have figure that, without Coil, she'll get an easy ride to the top. Probably why she wanted to remove me from the picture, too. Heh."

"I know that sound. I know that look. You do that when you've gotten up to mischief."

"Hmmm. It wouldn't hurt to tell you, I guess."

"Don't lie. You're downright eager to brag about it, aren't you?"

"No. Maybe. Anyway, this wasn't really my intention at the time, but… in a certain room of a certain place, behind a door with a code I've set that only she could guess at, I left her a present, tied up nice and tight. He should be awake by now. Girl's gonna face the choices she'd have to make. Learn what it really takes. "

"So, you dropped a whole heap of trouble onto her lap, is what I'm hearing."

"Oodles and oodles worth of it, Jaune. Just what 'I' deserve."

With that, she strode into the alley, Escha sleepily following on her heels. They stopped by a crate that hadn't been there yesterday to study the contents stored within.

Before he joined them, Jaune spared a moment to look back, taking in the sight of Brockton Bay.

For the second time, he had entered this world to find a mess, only to leave it little better than before. He couldn't solve its troubles, then and now.

Because… he still wasn't the person they needed. Still someone for whom the right choices didn't come easy, and the easy choices feel all too right.

Heroes. Villains. Whatever lies in between. Their world was bigger than he knew, each action bearing consequences that spread far and wide. Setting out to save it, a fool's errand.

All he could do was try. Just like everybody else living their lives.

Jaune turned on his heels and walked to the portal, heading home.

It has been a long day.


-o-​


Jaune woke up to the howling winds, and an endless void.

He raised his head from the table, blinking his bleary eyes in weariness. The wooden chair beneath him creaked as he sat back to cast a gaze over the surroundings, getting his bearing. Worn and dirty floor, grimy bottles on the shelves, Somer's Rock looked just as ugly on the second visit. If anything, the missing walls and biting chill improved the ambience.

Around the table sat familiar faces, frozen in time. Tattletale, with Escha in her lap. Grue. Faultline. Trickster. Coil. Kaiser.

The Outsider.

"Hello, Jaune," was his mild greeting, the man leaning forward from his spot—comfortable and with room to spare—between Grue and Faultline.

Jaune searched his memory, and wondered how come nobody commented on that empty gap the night before last.

"Hello again," he said in kind.

"Tough day?"

"I've had worse."

He grabbed the armrest of the chair, pushing to sit straighter in his seat as he checked the area. Tables spread out across the small island, reenacting the scene. At a booth, the Undersiders watched the proceedings, Tattletale's counterpart singularly focused on her. Opposite them, the Travelers. Sundancer fidgeted under the attention of her teammates.

The girl seemed to be looking his way, expression inscrutable behind her—

"Masks. Interesting things, are they not?" the Outsider said.

Jaune turned back to the other man, who had stood up at some point and was peering curiously at the skull pattern on Grue's motorcycle helmet.

"They're pretty fun," Jaune agreed. Putting on a mask and cape, playing at superhero? That's the dream. "A little hard to tell what a person's thinking sometimes, though."

"That is rather the point in their mind, I find." The Outsider tapped the helmet. "They believe they can hide who they are each time they put it on. Of course, the opposite holds true more often than not. A mask reveals."

The Outsider vanished from sight.

Jaune twisted in his seat to see the Outsider, chin in hand, standing over Tattletale and observing her. The girl was in the middle of a laugh with her grin stretched wide, the stopped time causing it to appear spiteful instead of playful. The Outsider reached out a hand to pet the statue of Escha, before lightly spinning on his heels to lean on the table, addressing Jaune again.

"Curious, that a thin piece of cloth is all it takes for what lurks beneath to surface." He swept his gaze around the room, from Kaiser and the people behind him to the three from the Merchants to Coil. "Every thought that was bottled up. Every crude word never given voice. Every desire, base and animal. All that you are inside, just more so." The Outsider placed his hands on either side of his face, and pushed his cheeks up into the tiniest almost-smile. He then pulled it down to form a semblance of a frown. Upon release, his visage returned to a blank expression. "How freeing it must be, to let the world see one's true face. I envy them."

Jaune went to respond, but caught a slight movement at the corner of his eyes. He tried to overlook it at first, as objects tend to drift through the void. The sound of a mug sliding over a wooden surface, however, wasn't normal. He whipped his head in that direction.

"Hey, quick question. Who's that?" he asked, very much disturbed by the hooded figure sitting in one of the booths, the black robes hugging their skinny frame. A beer sat before them on the table. (Jaune blinked blankly at that innocuous detail, then resumed his surreptitious scan for a scythe and a skeletal horse.)

"A guest," said the Outsider, his voice achieving an unsurpassed blandness in its inflection. "One far too meddling for my taste."

The figure raised one of their voluminous sleeves, moving it in what Jaune would swear was a friendly wave. He glimpsed a hint of silvery white under the hood, and shivered as it implied everything he was dreading.

"Ignore them. I do. Care for a change of scenery?"

Jaune still had many questions regarding this second entity, but refrained from asking because he wasn't sure he'd like the answer. Keeping a wary eye on that booth, he pushed away from the table. A staircase made from the same dark rocks as the floating islands had quietly materialized some time during their conversation, and he stepped on them, strolling alongside the Outsider to a higher platform.

Halfway up, he addressed the Outsider, "Aren't you going to… you know." Jaune wiggled his fingers while making a 'whoosh' noise to denote the other man's usual disappearing act.

"I was told that walking beside mortals offers a new perspective."

By who, Death back there?

"And how is that working out for you? Learned anything new yet?" He assumed that emotions were the goal here.

"You walk with little steps."

Jaune gasped, offended. "I do not!"

Humor drained out of him at the sight that greeted their duo after they ascended the staircase. He stopped a few paces in, but the Outsider walked all the way to the other side of the figure laying on the ground, taking care to avoid the bomb sitting at the center of the island.

"This feels familiar, Jaune. I'm sensing a pattern." The Outsider squatted down beside the body. "I could say many things about this 'Armsmaster'—his secrets, his fears, his hopes. But we're not here for him." He looked up at Jaune. "Why did you do it?"

Jaune crossed his arms, defiant. "Because he's the same as ever. Exactly like he will be a month from now."

"A beast, as you once called him?"

The man knew. Of his doubts. Of his unease, buried deep. What he tried to justify.

"No," Jaune said—confessed. He tapped his heel on the stone ground, dithering for a while as he collected his thoughts. "I had the chance to fight by his side, and he wasn't the horrible monster I've built up in my head. The guy can do jokes, you know that? Stopped me from stepping on a few bombs, too. His people trusted him."

"A human, then."

Jaune nodded, after a second. "Yes, that's it. He's just a human. But…"

"Go on," the Outsider pressed.

"But that doesn't change what he did. A human can do bad things. I've seen that before, and so have you. Calling himself a hero doesn't make his actions right."

The Outsider tilted his head, staring intently. "No cause too great that the evils of man can slip on by?"

The sentiment gave him pause. Jaune considered it, this lofty ideal. He imagined himself an avenging angel who, having learned from his experiences with Kihara, Crowley, and Armsmaster, hunted down those that may consider the suffering of one girl a worthy trade for their grand ambitions.

It sounded wrong, the image better resembling a caricature. That gave him his answer.

"My reason was nothing so great. The simple answer is that I did it because it was Armsmaster."

The brief burst of satisfaction in his chest confirmed it as the truth.

It mattered not one bit what the man was truly like. Maybe he's a saint. Maybe he visits schools to read storybooks to children. Placed on a scale, it might be that Armsmaster was more good than evil.

Jaune would have brought about the same ending. It was that kind of selfishness. The morals and logic of the world bowed to something which dwelled wholly on a personal level, and the conclusion he arrived to was this: if Armsmaster was going to retread the same old road, where he had hurt and will hurt again a person Jaune held dear, that meant he deserves a terrible fate.

The Outsider hummed. "They call that revenge."

"Then, that's what I did."

Irritably, kindly, the young man with black eyes said no more of it.

They stood upon the island for a long time in what he'd hesitate to call companionable silence. Peace did not exist in the Void, too cold and lonely was it for that sort of gentleness, but he found a similar flavor in emptiness, and he let the sensation of nothing wash away his worries.

What he has done, he could not take back, and won't. The future stretched out before him.

He broke the silence.

"What could it have been, do you know?"

The Outsider turned to him, and it seemed as if the man had been waiting for him to ask.

"Well, now. Would you like to see?"

The bomb went off, bursting not with pure physical force, but light.

It faded to show Armsmaster, again. The man looked rather livelier now, posing with chest puffed out and arms akimbo to the backdrop of a big, officious building—the city hall. The full roster of Protectorate ENE heroes were arrayed behind him, plus a few additions.

The sliver of sky, the building, the costumes, all shone bright. Jaune and the Outsider stood in between one moment and the next, amidst a group of cheering spectators that made not a sound.

"The game had been played before," the Outsider said. "In another time, in another place, the defenders of a city threw themselves at the fray, bleeding dry to drive out their hated foes." He laid a hand over his heart. "They proclaimed it a great victory for all of a week. Once new contenders came, they had not the strength to maintain the line, thus losing all grounds."

The Boston Games. That dreaded outcome which Gallant had spoken of as a calamity and a cautionary tale.

"Here, lessons are learned. The engineers of the plan tout it as a clean sweep. You choose to not interfere and an emperor sleeps in his bed; it goes off without a hitch. The defenders aim rats against rats, and as the battlefield falls quiet, they turn upon the survivors. No warning. No quarters. No chance to scurry back to their boltholes. No game of cat and mouse."

Jaune looked at the smile on Armsmaster's face. He saw no signs of regrets, or loss, or anger. Pure happiness suffused the man's being.

"In the aftermath, there would then follow raids within homes and ambushes at favored haunts. An emperor would be arrested like a common thug, and they drag him through the streets. All in a day."

A clean sweep. Jaune considered the method, and what reasons may lie behind it. "If done that way, the heroes would have conserved their strength."

"Fresh and in fighting shape to meet any hardship, whether challengers from afar or a monster from below," said the Outsider, bringing up a fist in victory to mirror the crowd around him. "The shining city has found its hero, and a new way forward. Goodness built upon betrayal and hands stained red."

Jaune closed his eyes and imagined the scene. He listened to the roaring adulation, the booming speech proclaiming a new era for Brockton Bay. He watched the procession of heroes walking forward to receive their medals, and Armsmaster accepting the keys to the city—tears were falling down the man's cheeks.

With a growl, Jaune turned his back on the stage. And abruptly stopped.

He now witnessed an altogether different future.

The heroes—broken, bleeding—were gathered around a meeting room table. Some of the seats went unfilled, the one at the head of the table among them.

The Outsider appeared next to him, an elbow propped on his shoulder.

"In this life, you left your mark. The defenders curse your name as they licked their wounds, all barring a quiet few. A knight would be cast out of his castle in disgrace, forced to find a new banner to fight under. And the rats…"

Another table faded into view, set at a remove and familiar to his eyes. Faultline's team and Travelers stood on one side. Opposite them, Tattletale grinned, the Undersiders spread out behind her.

"Well, they learn from your example. Trust and cooperation are the order of the day. Alliances are struck, an understanding reached. They lurk in the shadows as the city continues in stagnation, and it would seem as if nothing had changed. Of course, that will last about as long as it takes for the newcomers to arrive, eager to build a home."

Between the two divided groups, a dark corner spilled out shapes from within its depths. Teeth and knives and frost, and other strange things.

"It will be a bloody day in Brockton Bay, full of highs and lows, defeats and triumphs. I suppose, in the end, people would have to take the good with the bad."

Jaune looked from one future to the other. They were as stark a contrast as noon from night, stemming from a single choice.

"Oh, how the story goes," the Outsider said, observing him with unblinking eyes, "had you just stood aside. Would you have changed your mind, knowing what you do now?"

Was it wrong, the answer in his heart?

"I think… that I still would do it all the same way again."

"Truly?"

"Maybe the heroes weren't wrong, but I wasn't, either. So I'm going to follow my path, and they can follow theirs. We'll just have to live with where it leads us."

The Outsider took his elbow off Jaune's shoulder. The man began to pace to and fro, pondering that thought.

Jaune, having no desire to wait in judgement like some delinquent schoolboy, wandered over to the edge of the island and sat down. He let his legs dangle over the empty air, and made a game of discerning the features of the far-off islands within the Void.

The odd part was, he seemed to spot movements among them.

Behind him, the Outsider spoke up. "One last thing. One minor thing, that I am curious of."

"Shoot."

But not literally. He'd rather not fall off this cliff.

"Glory Girl."

"What about her?" he said, wary of a trap.

"She proclaimed you family, yet you spurn her at every turn. Strange, for one who is so quick to form bonds."

"There was too much going on," Jaune said, shrugging. "I've no desire to keep hearing her harp on about a misunderstanding."

The Outsider made a noise of understanding. "Ah. She was too small, in the course of events."

"I wouldn't put it that way."

He couldn't deny it, either. At a time in which he had many a concern occupying his thoughts, from Tattletale to Sundancer to the city he wished to save, she was simply one more issue stacked among the rest, and less important beside. Someone that Jaune had no spare moment for, no attention for, no care for.

Someone that wouldn't be there tomorrow, like so many faces that had come and gone.

"She'll think of you, you know. Sometimes, as she flies above the city. Wondering if you are still out there, and if you are well."

Jaune had nothing to say to that.


Universe: Worm. Event: ABB bombings.
Loot: Tinkertech explosives, doomsday device, tinkertech rifles (5x), Armsmaster's Halberd​
