He learned one interesting tidbit, talking with them. As it turned out, Club Peek-a-Boo wasn't the drinking club he thought it was. No, the members belonged to—

"A diving club," Chisa said with an emphatic nod.

Jaune looked at the table heaving and creaking under the sheer amount of alcohol stacked high atop it, then back at Chisa.

Clearly.

"I don't believe you."

She hid her face in her hands. "I don't blame you. Sometimes, I think even they get confused."

Still, the girl proved it using her camera, and it was with curious eyes that he peeked over her shoulder while she showed him the pictures she had taken from underwater. A whole world existed down there to steal his breath away. Beams of sunlight cutting through the empty sea, tropical fishes swimming among rainbow coral reefs… Being fifty feet below the surface and surrounded by water sounded akin to a nightmare, but it might be worth it for sights like the ones he was seeing on this screen.

Expressing the sentiment revealed that he was wrong about Chisa. She's as crazy as the rest of them.

"...certifying for an open water license typically spans three days but a dedicated two days can achieve the same result provided you demonstrated a true understanding of the material and even then the certification process involves actual dives which in Okinawa means you will go underwater in some of the most beautiful diving locations in Japan including the islands of the Kerama National Park and the Blue Cave and every step of the way is supervised for your safety so there is very little risk and if you are looking for something casual, a 'discover dive' in the shallows can give you a taste of what you can expect and if you want I have a number of pamphlets for what I believe are the best tours and programs for a beginner and…"

The diving nut soon remembered that humans need to breathe, and inhaled a big gulp of air. Her face regained some of its color.

"Did you get Chisa started on diving? That's brave of you."

Chisa shot a glare at the speaker, Iori, who had come over to join the conversation. Kohei, Iori's partner in crime according to most people Jaune talked to in the club, followed on his heels. They each held a cup of oolong tea in their hand, judging by the color of the liquid.

"Speaking as a beginner myself, diving is pretty fun," Iori continued, missing how Chisa's expression softened to a far kinder look. "If you ever have time, it's not a bad hobby."

"I'll keep it in mind," Jaune said in what he hoped was a diplomatic manner. His hobby in recent weeks ran along the lines of stabbing things that tried to stab him and liberating objects from other people's possession. The higher callings in life. "My schedule is a bit hectic, and I don't get access to the water much. That could change in the future, though, so we'll see how it goes…" Jaune trailed off as his phone rang. "Excuse me for a moment."

On the line, of course, was Lisa. She had finished changing into her swimsuit, and wanted directions to where he and Escha had made camp.

"Just follow the smell of alcohol," he told her.

Minutes later, Lisa emerged from the crowd.

Jaune gawked. "I was joking."

"Puh-lease, I'm not a hound. I followed the trail Escha left in the sand to your old spot, then your footprints led to here."

"Ah, that makes more sense. Some good old detective work, huh? Should have expected that from you," he said. Lisa preened at the praise. "And nice bikini, by the way. You look cute."

"Don't I just?" Ponytail swishing, she turned to one side then the other, striking a pose. "Lavender really is my color."

That, and the style suited her. Standing between Chisa with her sporty one-piece and Nanaka who wore a mature and rather risque number, Lisa struck the balance of casual and approachable in a halter neck design. The toothy grin lent her a mischievous air. She winked at him, no doubt picking up his thoughts through his body language.

"Kuhah!" Kohei, the blond guy, suddenly spat blood and fell to the ground. At once, his friend was there by his side.

"Kohei! What happened? Who hurt you?"

"No. No, it can't be," Kohei mumbled. His body was shivering like a leaf in the wind, and he clutched at his heart with both hands.

Jaune, meanwhile, experienced the oddest sense of déjà vu. Oh, and an icy sensation crawling up his spine. He scanned his surroundings in a search for incoming threats. It could be whatever had downed Kohei.

A shaking finger rose, pointing straight at him.

"Seven… Seven centimeters closer…"

What?

"C-Coy smile!"

No, seriously. What?

Iori understood those cryptic words, and the boy whirled toward Jaune. His gaze bounced between Jaune and… and Lisa.

"Say you didn't," Iori said, his voice dropping to a growl.

Jaune cocked an eyebrow. "I didn't."

"Liar!" the other boy yelled.

In Iori's arms, Kohei howled, "Why him? Why, of all people, him?" He pounded a fist against the sand. "It should have been me!"

At that point, Jaune recalled what he knew of Kohei—namely, his fetish—and slapped a hand over his face. Of all the ways for his lies to catch up to him, this was not one he ever thought possible. He peeked at the other people present, finding many awkward expressions and an ever-widening circle.

Beside him (a bit closer than usual, now that he thought about it), Lisa muttered, "Thank god, we're not staying here. I will not be saddled with that kind of reputation. Jaune, fix your mess, and do a better job this time."

"Fair enough," Jaune replied. He cleared his throat, and stepped forward. "Okay, everybody—"

Everybody took a step back. Hurtful.

He powered on through. "What I said yesterday was not the truth. It's entirely fabricated, intended to calm those two down." He jerked a thumb at Iori and Kohei. "Imagine my surprise when one of them took offense. I mean, what even, am I right?"

Kohei's interests seemed to be common knowledge, lending credence to the reason Jaune put forth. There were a few nods and hums of agreement. Shoulders released their tension. Beer cans were opened, though that might not have anything to do with the current situation.

"After that was pretty much a haze for me, and I guess in the process the misunderstanding never was resolved." Guilty shuffling now, as the members of Club Peek-a-Boo avoided his gaze. They knew who was responsible for drowning him in Spirytus and oolong tea.

"You're not related, then?" Chisa asked, wary. At her height, she had to look up to meet his eyes.

"Nope. We first met each other a little over a month ago, and I don't have a long-lost sister I don't know about." Or if he did, she would be a universe apart from Earth Bet. His father's good, but he's not that good.

Kohei sobbed bitter tears, and buried his face in Iori's chest.

"What's his deal?" Jaune asked. "Shouldn't he be happy hearing this?"

Iori patted his friend on the back. "He is, but I think you've also shattered his dream that something right out of his games could happen in real life."

"What a troublesome fellow."

"Haha, I'll say. Wait until he gets started on his favorite anime." Iori stopped laughing. "Of course, you wouldn't experience it, since we're going to kill you."

Jaune did a double-take. "Pardon?"

"Yeah? Putting the misunderstanding aside, you still committed a great sin. There's no other choice."

In sync, the two college students leapt to their feet. They took up fighting stances with Iori managing a decent guard, elbows in and body minimized, while Kohei appeared to be doing whatever he thought would look cool, making knife hands.

"You speak wise words, Iori! The heretic must be purged!"

""Death to fuckboys!"" they shouted together.

Great. Jealous engineering nerds were after him.

He then revised his opinion of engineering nerds, because, wait a minute, where did they just pull those shovels from? Did they have dimensional pockets, too? These guys shouldn't be underestimated. Next to him, Lisa's face was twitching, the girl beset by a sudden stab of headache pain as she tried to work out the oddity.

"Now, unless nothing happened between you two, you might want to beg for your life." Iori tapped the shovel against his palm for emphasis, a truly evil sneer on his face.

Jaune shrugged, and taunted them, "Oh, it totally did. And you know what?" He put up his fists. "Come get some. Nobody challenges Jaune Arc and gets away with it."

Well, besides Accelerator, Leviathan, the half of his class that he still hadn't managed to steal a win against, his sisters, the green-haired girl on a hoverboard that flew into him last month (the donuts she bought somewhat made up for it), those twins who mugged him that one time in Vale (the donuts they stole from him meant the grudge burrowed twice as deep), Lisa, Escha, the Halloween trick-or-treaters that swarmed his house for candy—okay, some people challenge Jaune Arc and get away with it. For now. The point was, he's not backing down.

Iori and Kohei spared no regard to his introspection. They seized the moment when he was distracted to lunge for him.

He slapped the shovels out of their hands, then gripped them by the throats to lift them off their feet. They kicked and scratched as he held them there, but settled down after a minute to hang limply with their legs swinging in the breeze.

"I… What was the plan?" Jaune asked, baffled. "Rushing at me failed the first time this guy"—he indicated Kohei with his chin—"tried it, why did you expect that to work on the second go-round?"

Their senior, Azusa, cut in. "And didn't we tell you time and again? This isn't how Peek-a-Boo does things!" she scolded.

"B-but he—!"

"That bastard, he—!"

Azusa motioned for Jaune to put the two boys down, and he obliged. She placed her hands on her hips, fixing them with a gaze that brooked no arguments. "We use games to settle our differences, and drinks to wash away bad blood."

A soft smile broke through her hard demeanor.

"Give us a show, boys."

-o-​

Volleyball, the sport of summer. The rules may differ, the goal stayed the same. Get that ball over the net.

Club Peek-a-Boo had gathered around one of the free volleyball courts, in the process amassing a small audience of beach-goers seeking entertainment. Boundary markers drew boxes in the sand to denote the glorious arena upon which the battle shall wage. On one side of the net stood Iori and Kohei, muscles straining as they stretched to limber up. On the other side, Jaune and the only person he could trust in a contest like this.

Lisa scowled. "Jaune."

One word, no inflection. It sufficiently conveyed the point. She's not happy.

Jaune turned to the girl standing on the sidelines. "Look, we have to consider the optimal team configurations."

"And that means picking Escha over me?" Lisa seethed, pointing at the ball of fur running back and forth, chasing a butterfly. That people just rolled with it spoke well of how easygoing—or drunk, probably drunk—Club Peek-a-Boo was.

"The combat rankings support my decision," Jaune asserted. "Don't worry, it'll be fine. They can't beat me." The last part was voiced loud enough for his opponents to hear.

They weren't so easily intimidated, it seemed. Both of them were displaying smirks.

Up on the referee seat—looking like she'd rather be anywhere but here—Chisa heaved a sigh before calling out, "Let's get this over with. The team that reaches 21 points, leading by at least two, wins. First serve goes to whichever team doesn't have an Iori on it."

"But, Chisa, that disqualifies my team by default."

Chisa hmph-ed, and refused to dignify that with an answer.

A PAB club member tossed the ball into the court. Jaune caught it, and lightly spun the ball in his hand as he waited for everyone to get into position.

"Final chance to bow out," he offered.

"Kuhehe." Iori threw his head back. "Hahaha! I should say the same, because you've fallen into my trap!"

"Oh? How so?" Jaune asked mildly.

"It's simple. I knew from last night that you're a tough one, but volleyball is not like arms wrestling or a race. It is a sport, and in a sport, skill matters." Iori pointed at his own head. "Intellect matters. No matter how strong and fast you are, you can't—"

*BOOM!*

Iori looked down at the crater next to him. Three feet deep, a volleyball laid at the center half-buried in the sand. He, and Kohei, jerkily turned their heads back toward Jaune. Sweat broke out on their brows.

"Point for me," Jaune said, teeth bared in a bloodthirsty grin. He was not the person that should be worried here.

House rules required the losers to drink. Two cups of Spirytus were brought forth for his opponents, chugged to the last drop without much trouble as it was simply the first of many to come. 21 points equated to 21 cups of hard liquor, an amount that blinded the eyes and made livers cry.

Of course, that presented no issue for Jaune, because in beach volleyball…

*BOOM!*

The winner of a rally controlled the ball, even if they had just performed a serve.

In subsequent plays, it dawned on Iori and Kohei how screwed they were. All delusions of scoring points vanished from their minds, replaced with survival. The two ran pell-mell to avoid Jaune's serves as their side of the court grew pockmarked with craters to resemble the surface of the moon.

The score had reached 6-0 by the time they came to grips with their situation. A future awash in alcohol loomed before them, promising the mother of all hangovers, not helped in the least as the bystanders from their club started placing bottle after bottle on a table in preparation, stacked tall in a pyramid. That prospect caused a shift in their priorities.

In between serves, Iori shouted to his partner, "Kohei! There's no choice, we need to pull a sacrifice play!"

"Are you serious?" Kohei balked, his gaze drawn to a crater and no doubt imagining it were their faces that the ball struck. Jaune had to admit that in the general excitement, he's shown a bit too much of his otherworldly strength. Silver lining, the spectators oohed and aahed but did not question it further. Perhaps this world had more in common with Remnant than its Earth analogues, if such feats existed within the realm of possibility.

Iori nodded. "We have to receive the serve, no matter what it takes. Don't worry, my friend. I will handle this," he said, showing a thumbs-up that was contrasted by his bittersweet smile. The boy knew the cost of his plan, and so did his partner.

"I understand." Kohei saluted him. "Good luck… my friend."

"How touching," Jaune drawled. He experienced a strange urge to cackle and twirl his nonexistent mustache, but ignored it. His expression then grew sharp. "Pheh. Go act out your drama elsewhere, this is volleyball!"

Jumping high, he spiked the ball. It shot like a cannon, blasting over the net on course for dead center of the opposing box. He harbored no fear of reprisal, for what could they do?

In an act of great courage, Iori grabbed Kohei and shoved him under the ball. A loud *BOOM!* rang out across the beach, and for the first time, the ball remained in play past the serve. It flew high above the corpse buried under the sand, and Iori jumped after it to slap the ball back to the other side.

Unprepared, Jaune and Escha failed to stop it from hitting the ground. The ball bounced one, bounced twice, and rolled out of the box, accompanied by dead silence.

"Good," Iori declared, a satisfied look on his face.

No, no it's not.

The audience held a different opinion. A roar went up, and Kitahara Iori basked in the cheers of the crowd. What was once a one-sided beatdown had reached the turnaround. A comeback was in the making.

Hardly anyone paid attention to the hand bursting out of the ground, followed by the rest of a flailing Kohei. The boy spat mouthfuls of sand as he crawled out of the crater. His gimlet eyes bore a hole in his partner's back.

"I. O. RIIIII!" A spear-tackle took the hero of the hour off his feet.

As the two boys fell to infighting, Jaune felt a tap on his shoulder. Turning around, he found the beautiful Azusa. With a lump in his throat, his gaze drifted lower… to the cups she was holding out.

"Here we are! One Spirytus for you, and a special apple juice-water cocktail for the darling Escha," Azusa cooed as the cat ran up to her. She tilted the cup for Escha to lap at the watered-down juice, giving her belly scritches all the while. "Wow, you are so smart and well-behaved! It's like you can understand my words!"

Jaune tried to hide his jealousy at the cat receiving such lavish care, and also being spared the poison that everyone else must suffer. Holding his nose, he choked down the contents of the cup, gagging as the alcohol burned his throat. Afterward, the drink left a weird, dry sensation on his tongue that he just couldn't get used to.

The ball changed hands, and the next rally began. Iori was up to serve, and though he seemed athletic, his unsteady sway suggested that a stiff breeze would blow him over. Experience allowed him to function through the haze, and he tossed the ball high, leaping after it.

Before striking the ball, Iori's head suddenly turned. "Lisa's topless!"

Ha! Who did they think he was?

Jaune whirled around, gaze darting every which way. They settled on red-faced Lisa, who after a moment fluttered her fingers at him. Her bikini was still on, tied securely. The ball landed inside the boundaries with a soft *pomf!* to inform him he had been tricked.

"Point!"

Sneaky, sneaky. It won't work twice.

It worked twice.

The score narrowed to 6-3.

Jaune rapidly blinked, the sun a touch too harsh on his eyes as he tracked the next serve. A nice thing about two extra cups of Spirytus, he couldn't focus on the words Iori shouted, and thus in a paradoxical manner succeeded in keeping his attention on the ball. And drunk or no, his reaction speed outpaced the capabilities of his opponents. Before the ball even passed the net, he was there to slam it down. The terrified screams of Iori and Kohei was sweet music to his ears.

"Uh, Jaune?" Lisa called over. "You're taking things a little too seriously there. Might want to cool it."

She was referring, obliquely, to the fact that he had moved way faster than a normal human around these parts could. More and more, he stretched the credulity of the spectators, and ran the risk of questions being raised.

A squishy paw tapped him on the back of the leg. He looked down.

"Go get them!" said Escha.

Jaune sniffed, and wiped a tear from the corner of his eye. The cat got it.

Sure, it's a game. Pride was still on the line, and victory beckoned. He wanted to win, simple as that.

Walking to the corner, he readied for the serve.

"Wait!" Iori threw out his hand, face set in panic. "When one side regain control of the ball, you have to rotate! That's the rule!"

Jaune stared at him in askance. "You expect Escha to—How is that supposed to work? Also, I'm already giving you an advantage by having her as my teammate, and you're demanding more. That's not very good sportsmanship."

Iori shut his mouth. His teeth ground together as he mulled on a response.

"I have to admit," said Kohei, looking pained, "he has a point. The crowd isn't on our side in this."

Unwilling to give up, Iori spun toward Chisa. "Ref, what's your call?"

Jaune hummed in appreciation for the fast-thinking. Not a bad gambit, to move the decision out of the players' hands.

Chisa fanned herself to stave off the heat as she deliberated on the situation. On one hand, the rules of the game were stated in plain language. On the other…

"Allowed."

"What?" Iori staggered over to the referee chair, grabbing hold and looking up at Chisa. "Why!?"

"Iori, I agree that you're making sense… but it's a cat."

A beautiful argument, there was nothing anyone could dispute about that. The addition of a cat to the match already threw out the rulebook. Nobody could demand in all reasonable seriousness that a cat perform a volleyball serve. The species was not known for its ability to play sports.

Only Jaune and Lisa noticed Escha giggling under her breath. From the perspective of a felyne, humans must appear so silly and entertaining.

"Bunch of cheaters, the lot of you," Lisa concluded with a sigh. Jaune couldn't hear her over the sound of him winning.

*BOOM!*

That's the one.

Through the twists and turns, the match advanced forward. Iori brought to the fore his full underhanded slyness, revealing himself as the sort of man who would make any sacrifice, throwing Kohei into the line of fire again and again to stop Jaune's tyrannical displays of power. On his part, Jaune stuck to the tried and true method of spiking the ball whenever he could, his skill at the game starting and ending with that one move. The scoreboard ticked upward as the hour went by without a decisive lead.

Until, it came down to the wire.

Jaune rolled the ball in his hand, barely managing to not drop it during such a complicated maneuver. His team led 23-22, meaning they once more had the chance to break the stalemate for good. It hadn't gone so well on the previous attempts, and he didn't think he could survive another drop of Spirytus. 192-proof vodka had put the three boys on their last legs.

"No fair," Iori slurred, pointing at Jaune. "Beach volleyball is pairs only!"

"That's right! You can't bring reinforcement!" Kohei added.

All of them, including Jaune, have been seeing doubles for a while now. That's the crux of his final gambit. Where most would consider it a detriment, Jaune sensed opportunity.

Throwing the ball in the air, he jumped off the ground. His arm wound back, and at the apex of his ascent, he gave the volleyball a slap to send it sailing across the court. Immediately, a murmur spread through the crowd, because in a departure from his normal serves, the blow had been slow and weak. It's an easy return if the other team could get to the ball.

"It's going left!" Kohei warned.

"It's going right!" retorted Iori.

Still seeing doubles, they ran to the net and leapt side by side to block both positions. On their faces bloomed vicious grins. They thought they had him.

Jaune mirrored the look. He spun in place to build momentum, and launched his secret weapon. Where the drunkards once saw doubles, they now found quadruples.

"Four balls? How are you doing this!?"

Unable to discern which of the round, white objects was their target, Iori and Kohei frantically waved their arms to cover as much space as possible. Relief was found as the objects drew nearer, coming into focus to leave two shapes before their eyes.

The ball, and Escha.

The felyne uncurled from the position she had tucked herself in, extending her paws. With a boop, the volleyball bounced over the heads of the defenders, tracing a gentle trajectory that put it behind them on the sand.

"Game and match, to Jaune Arc and Escha," Chisa declared. Jaune pumped a fist in victory.

Iori and Kohei dropped back on the ground, and fell to their knees before the cat. They stared at it in disbelief.

"You've got to be kidding."

"I knew we should have gone for the Charpy Impact Test."

-o-​

Charpy Impact Test
A standardized high strain-rate test utilizing a pendulum apparatus that measures the amount of energy absorbed by a material during fracture, thereby allowing a person to determine its toughness.

It does not often involve smashing a heavy weight into one's nether regions.

-o-​

In Club Peek-a-Boo, there was not so much a reward for the winner as there was punishment for the loser. Escaping with one's life and dignity was the prize.

And so it was that Jaune stood tall over his defeated foes lying buried up to their necks in the sand, their sickly-green faces a testament to the frankly insane amount of alcohol they've further consumed following the conclusion of the match. There had been a lot of debate on whether the punishment should involve drinking or humiliation, which ended when it was put to a vote. By unanimous decision and in true college fashion, the pair would suffer both.

The drinking part was done. Now, the club had opened the floor for Jaune to enact whatever payback he deemed appropriate. He's having a hard time thinking of something, however.

Jaune squatted down, and looked the two boys in the eye.

"Are you guys willing to let bygones be bygones?"

They shared a look, sighed, and nodded at him.

"Alright," he said. "In that case, we're cool."

A beat, and the two boys brightened, grinning as they looked up at Jaune. Around them, the club members gazed at the scene with approving expressions. The mood swung from tense to festive in an instant, and Jaune almost fell over as Azusa slapped him on the back.

"Finally, it's over," Lisa grumbled, and grabbed him by the arm. "Jaune, come over here? I need someone to rub more sunscreen on my back~"

Looking at the pair, Azusa laughed. "That settles it. I can't believe anybody would think you're siblings."

Chisa tilted her head to the side, seeming puzzled. "I don't know. He sometimes give off the same air as big sis." She addressed him. "You really don't have a little sister?"

"Ehhh. Not a little sister."

He had multiple.

The merriment came to a screeching halt as everyone caught the subtext. Nervously, they glanced at Kohei to find the boy crying blood. The ground rumbled around him, his form pushing free.

Here they go again...

Chapter 44: A War in May​


Refreshed from his break, Jaune set out once more toward his goal. Another day, another try at ultimate power.

(Or, at least, gently-used/reasonably-priced power to see his enemies crushed beneath his heel and hear the lamentation of their loved ones, except in the fire lady's case since given what he imagined of her she probably already took care of that praying mantis-style.)

He slotted a final explosive round into the chamber of Red Rook, and with a flick of his arm, the gunlance snapped back in place, reloaded and ready for battle. It then vanished into his Pocket, and that was his preparations done.

"Lisa, Escha," he called out, getting up. "Are you two ready to go?"

"Almost!" Escha answered from over by her garden. She hurried to the next flowerpot, jabbing a weird doohickey into the dirt. They're supposed to water the plants over time according to Lisa who bought them. He'd take her word on it; the herbs and mushrooms had that Astera vitality to keep them alive far longer than regular plants, but some insurance was always good. They were growing in nicely, and the first harvest should come any day now to provide their team with a number of useful items. The bugs have started breeding, too. A process that would be even faster going forward, if the feeder they've put into the terrarium did its job.

Escha performed a final check of the garden, then scrambled over to Jaune. She slapped her paw to her head in an adorable salute.

That left Lisa, and right on cue the music from the bathroom shut off. She exited a few moments later. Her Tattletale costume was back on, her makeup fixed. She sent him a halfhearted glare before walking over, snagging her camouflage cloak in passing.

"Try and stay professional, Jaune," she admonished as she threw the cloak over her shoulders.

"Try to be less you, Lisa," he said.

That got her to crack a smile, and she bumped him with her hips. He poked her in the ribs as retaliation.

Soon, they settled down and returned their focus to the apartment wall in front of them. A tap on the Company scroll, and the blank stretch of gray swirled into every color. Jaune peered through the shimmering half-clarity of the portal, studying what details were visible.

"Another alley. The portal has a type," he said.

He was only half-joking there, because he still suspected the device of sentience for suggesting [Blank] to him as a purchase—nominally benign for the same reason. As per usual, he took the foremost position, stepping through to another universe with his shield up.

The world came alive just past the threshold, filling with noise. The brick walls now surrounding him in three directions muffled most of it, but the footsteps of hundreds at a distance was an altogether different sort of quiet than the utter isolation of the apartment. It was a sensation that had caused him no end of grief his first month in Vale, and one he had been experiencing more as of late.

Jaune stood still, his head cocked to the side as he listened to the hustle and bustle of the city, finding in it an unhurried rhythm punctuated by the occasional blaring car horn that spoke of people going about a normal day. After a moment's deliberation, he deemed the area safe enough for him to dial back from a state of alert. His shield and sword went back inside the Pocket, just in time for him to sneeze from the cocktail scent of smoke and refuse. He missed Okinawa already.

Meanwhile, Tattletale was also hard at work scrutinizing their surroundings, albeit with a different perspective than him. The brick walls received nothing beside a cursory glance, but she paid special attention to the mouth of the alley where people strode back and forth.

"Hmmm. The style of dress is from the mid-industrial era. 1910's, 1920's? They sure did love their hats back then." She removed her mask, then began adjusting the cloak to better hide her costume.

Jaune had no reference for most of the words coming out of her mouth, but he sort of understood it nevertheless. The clothes, from his viewpoint, were rather dated. Hardy, simple outfits for working in the factories, and fancy frocks or stately suits for the wealthier folks. And, yes, there were hats galore. It all reminded him of photos taken in the decades following the Great War, comparable in a sense to Dunwall. An old-timey car resembling a box on wheels rumbled by to cement the image.

"Are we on Earth, do you think?" he asked. A part of him was really starting to wonder what was up with that world for it to appear so often during their travels. Where were all the different versions of Remnant?

"I assume so," Tattletale replied, furrowing her brows. "Never heard of a city named Yuell, though. Maybe it's in Europe." She mulled on it further, before shaking her head. "I'll have a better picture out on a main road. Let's go."

"Meow!" Escha said, getting in character for the planet they're on.

Outside the alley, they found a wide cobblestone avenue, well-maintained as much of the city appeared to be. The buildings featured that old Valean style of stone facades and sloped roofs, a balcony at every window, that had Jaune doing a double-take at first until he noted the one big incongruity—the city lacked a wall. In fact, it looked as if the architects of Yuell intended a design that evoked openness, with fountain squares dotting the gentle slope of the street and the taller buildings set far apart from each other.

Flower trees lined the road. Coupled with the humid air, it suggested that they arrived near the tail end of spring, and beneath an overcast sky people went about their business, sometimes sparing their party a glance for their colorful ensembles before moving on. One young man stopped as he glimpsed Tattletale's costume under the silvery-white cloak she had donned, but hurried away after receiving her scathing glare. She then scanned the area, particularly the street signs and the lettering on storefronts.

"I'm seeing English words, but not typical English names," she remarked, tapping her chin with a curious air. "Coalhearth Clinic, Idio Bibliotheque, Vera's Books and Stationery—lots of bookstores, now that I think about it." She turned her head, looking up the street to a grand edifice of marble and bell towers. "We're in a university town, is my bet. And that's the campus."

"They must be doing well for themselves with a big, fancy building like that," Jaune said, before pulling the conversation back on track. "Should we ask somebody for details?"

"No need for that. It'd just make them suspicious if we say the wrong thing. The bookstores would have newspapers and history books for me to get a good idea of where, or when, we might have ended up."

"Alright, check it out and let us know. I'll scout the area in the meantime."

Tattletale nodded, and was halfway to leaving when she paused in her tracks. Turning back around, she squinted at him.

"Wait a minute, that sounds like you're going to goof off while I do all the work. Does this 'scouting' involve buying ice cream for you and Escha, and sitting at a park?"

He averted his gaze. "I want to get a feel for the place, maybe listen in on people talking to see if we can catch a hint on what's happening in this world. It wouldn't be a bad idea to browse for items we can sell, either."

She stared at him a little longer.

"And okay, yeah, I'm totally buying snacks assuming the currency situation works out. I'll keep a share for you, if that helps."

"You had better," Tattletale jokingly warned him, and broke out in a snicker. "Get me popcorn if you find it." Waving a hand in dismissal, she left on her own task, crossing the street to head for a chic bookstore that saw brisk traffic.

"Looks like it's you and me, Escha," Jaune said afterward. "Which way should we go?"

Escha sniffed the air, and peered up and down the street on the lookout for interesting sights.

"Let's go there!" She indicated a clockmaker's shop with her nose. Jaune thought it an odd choice, but obliged, and they padded over to the store.

As it turned out, the felyne simply enjoyed the tick-tock sound of a dozen clocks going at once. For a few minutes, she sat outside the display window, her tail flicking in time with the devices as she watched the gears click and whirr with the sense of fascination one would get from a child. Jaune considered telling her that this did not count as productive work of any kind. Her contented smile convinced him to give a little leeway.

"Do you have these in Astera?" Jaune asked as he studied a cuckoo clock. The workmanship was quite excellent.

Escha checked for people before she shook her head. "Some of the researchers have those neat time-pieces they put in their pockets, but we mostly use the sun." She perked up, and turned to him. "Oh! But it's different back in the Old World. The Guild headquarters in Dundorma had a big clocktower and monsters kept trying to use it as a perch. The guildmaster got sick of it so he stuffed the thing full of bombs to make a trap." Escha smiled. "It blew up."

"That's, ah… innovative?" Other, less complimentary words flashed through his mind. He kept quiet on that.

Escha nodded. "He put fireworks inside, too. They were really pretty when they went off." A line of drool trailed down her chin. "And a ton of grilled meat fell from the sky. That part was nice."

In recent days, he had come to wonder if Nora Valkyrie didn't wander in from the Monster Hunters' world during her childhood. They were clearly her people.

Much like a child, Escha's attention changed at the drop of a hat. She soon lost interest in the clocks and darted off along the sidewalk with Jaune in pursuit. The two of them wandered from storefront to storefront, plastering their faces to the display windows. Over the course of the stroll, he learned the local currency was called a ducat, or DCT. Of course, he didn't have ducats, he had gold. To an enterprising fellow working in a general goods store, that presented no issue, and mentioning that he's from overseas excused Jaune from having to answer too many questions.

It's a fair bet that he got cheated on the exchange rate, but not unduly so. He followed Tattletale's advice of demanding double for any offers given, which did end up netting him better terms than otherwise.

With local money jingling in his hand, Jaune began to pay closer attention to goods and prices. Here, a problem arose.

There's no ice cream.

Ha. No, that's not the actual problem.

There's a whooole lot more food missing than that. Entire store shelves sat empty, the selection reduced to a scant few basic products whose original prices had been crossed out and marked up twice thus far. The huge baskets at market stalls, meant to hold mountains of fruits, carried a small, pitiful pile of bruised wares. A second glance at the avenue revealed a number of restaurants closed for the day.

Well, that boded nothing good.

"Jaune, Jaune!" came a whisper below. Jaune looked down as Escha nudged his leg.

"What is it?"

"Everyone looks so serious. It's weird."

Once she mentioned it, he found the comment impossible to refute. The people of Yuell lived under a pall of gloom. Faces were pinched and drawn, not quite at the level of widespread famine but certainly spoke of missed meals. At a cafe, conversations took place amongst grim customers gathered around a radio. He entered a bakery, walking past shoppers counting their coins outside the entrance, and exited with a bag of pastries to see them shaking their heads and moving on. More than one person chafed at his carefree demeanor.

Only the children gave honest smiles, while the adults faked theirs.

Jaune craned his ears to eavesdrop on other pedestrians. They talked of supply line interruptions, of food and blankets moved to one place or another, or lost altogether. An older woman muttered to her friend about news of her daughter 'from the front'. Above all, he heard one word on everybody's lips.

War.

Boy, oh boy, he had an idea of what this Instance entailed now.

"M-Mister?"

The voice came from the alley located next to the bakery. High and squeaky, it sounded nervous. Jaune assumed the person was addressing someone else, and continued past until a small hand tugged on his poncho.

That hand belonged to a kid no taller than his waist, who looked like he was regretting life right about now. The boy quickly let go of Jaune, shrinking back to stand next to a girl hugging a doll in her arms—a hand-sewn thing with buttons for eyes and a green dress. The similar shade of brown hair suggested they were family. A brief moment ensued as the two kids jostled position, each hoping to hide behind the other.

The girl lost and had to step forward. Her knees were knocking together, and she gulped air in an effort to muster her nerves.

Before she could manage a word, two rumbling stomachs made the case in her stead.

"Are you hungry?" Jaune asked.

The pair nodded their heads, eyes riveted on the bag he held.

Tattletale later rejoined him, guided by Escha, at a courtyard tucked behind the main avenue. Beneath the purple flowers of a myrtle tree, Jaune lounged on an ornate iron bench as the bells of the university rang in the new hour. On either side of him, the two kids sat eating a second helping of pastries with gusto. They've lost their earlier reticence, and were happily yammering in his ears about their week.

…Around the group were another dozen or so children, all chowing down on bread.

"Jaune, what's going on?" Tattletale asked, her voice flat. She had caught sight of the empty bag in his lap, likely drawing the correct conclusion from there.

Jaune indicated the siblings. "I met Hans and Greta earlier. They haven't had anything to eat since yesterday."

"And the rest of the tykes?"

"They sort of crawled out of the woodwork and it didn't feel right turning them away when I'm giving food to these two."

Greta looked up with a beaming smile. "Thank you, Jaune!"

The cry was picked up by various other squeaky voices.

Tattletale pinched the bridge of her nose. "Jaune, did you get scammed?"

"Most of them don't seem to know each other, so I doubt it." Although, he was feeling a tad uncertain now that she brought up the possibility. "They were just hungry. If anything, I blame Escha."

Escha tripped over her feet, flopping to the ground. She stared at him from that position, and pointed a paw at herself as if to ask 'Me!?'

"Yeah, you—" He coughed, and turned to address Tattletale instead. "She was playing around with the kids earlier, and the noise drew in the rest."

In the Yuell of recent time, the unreserved laughter as Hans and Greta chased Escha around the courtyard would have been a rare event, and a beacon for other children desperately seeking a sense of normality. Some had family, others were from the orphanage. A common thread connected them—they didn't have enough to eat. Reading between the lines, the city was starting to teeter.

Tattletale seemed like she had a lot to say to him. A glance at the assembled group, and she chose to leave it alone. Walking over to the bench, she made shooing motions at Greta.

"Right, well, you kiddies budge over and you can keep stuffing your faces. I have business with the big guy."

Greta nodded and scooted to the side. She's a good-natured sort, albeit shy. Her older brother was the one with the impulsive streak.

Tattletale settled beside Jaune, and after making sure the kids were occupied with their meal, she leaned closer to murmur in his ear. "The bookstore had what I was looking for. I skimmed a whole bunch of texts in the last hour and have a pretty good idea of the situation now. To start with, we're in a country named—"

"Gallia."

She stopped short, blinking at him in blank surprise. After a moment, she continued. "Uh, yeah, that's right. Anyway, we're not exactly on Earth. This is some kind of weird close cousin where the landmasses are almost the same but aren't identical, the continent is called Europa instead of Europe, and Gallia sounds similar to Gaul which is, like, an old word for France or something. People don't use oil, or Dust, but—"

"Ragnite, right?" he chimed in. "They're these blue crystals that power most of the technology in the city. Hans mentioned that they're volatile stuff. Apparently, the radio reports on explosions at the mines and refineries every couple of weeks."

Glowy crystals that produce energy, with the risk of blowing up? He's still convinced that it's just Dust under a different name.

His attention returned to Tattletale as the girl started growling.

"What year is it here?" she spat.

"1935."

"What's the biggest news of the last few months?" was her next rapid-fire question.

"The Empire declared war on the Federation at the start of the year, then two months ago they invaded Gallia."

"Gallia is known for what chief exports?"

"Ragnite is the big one, along with cheeses, fish, and clockworks plus other precision instruments in general. They're also famous for their bread."

"A game of football in the Europa International League is played with how many players on each side?"

"Trick question. It's the same as Remnant and Earth. Eleven players."

"How the fuuuudge!?" hissed Tatttletale, amending the word just in time for delicate ears (though having once been a kid, Jaune would call it a futile effort). She had a tight grip on his collars, and did not look at all happy.

"I asked Hans and Greta," Jaune answered with a light shrug. "They do well in school, and their dad was on the national team when Gallia won the tournament four years back."

Him being a willing listener had led to the siblings breaking out of their shell, and he managed to learn a lot in a short time. They hadn't cared much about why he was asking inane questions, simply seeing it as a chance to show off their knowledge.

Tattletale buried her face in her hands, and gave a long groan.

"What was even the point of me doing research?"

He placed a hand on her back, rubbing in soothing motions as he put on a kind smile. "Hey now, don't say that. There's a limit to the things I can find out from random people. You definitely know more than me, so I'm relying on you. Alright, partner?"

On Tattletale's other side, Greta copied him. She didn't seem to understand the situation, only wishing to help. The honest concern brought a slight smile to the older girl, and Tattletale raised her head.

"Right…" She straightened her back, confidence blooming again. "That's right! What would you do without me?" she declared, more to persuade herself than others.

"Nothing," he said, indulging her.

"Exactly. You'd be dead in a ditch." She grinned. "Useless."

Without a change to his smile, Jaune pinched her cheek.

"Ow ow ow, stahp!" Tattletale whined.


-o-​


With a single word, the day took a turn.

"Imps!"

The news traveled like a telephone game, that cry taken up and spreading inward from the outskirts of Yuell until it hit the courtyard, then passed over them to travel all the way to the university sitting at the center of the city. In its wake, pandemonium.

[Imperial forces are coming from the east! Noncombatants, seek shelter immediately! All militiamen, to arms!]

The speakers mounted overhead continued to blare instructions as parents grabbed their children and ran. Shopkeepers shuttered their doors, or stood on the threshold to pull people inside. Cars were left abandoned on the street, belongings strewn on the cobblestone. A distant boom resounded across the air to push it all into a fever pitch.

Some amongst the populace headed in the opposite direction of everyone else, men and women spanning a wide range of ages from their teens to their fifties. The fear on their faces was apparent, but so was the determination. After ushering the kids into the bakery where he bought their bread, Jaune followed these people with Tattletale and Escha on his heels. More joined them along the way until there were dozens.

As they poured into a building, an armory, Jaune left them behind to race ahead. He used the sound of gunfire and explosions as his heading, and reached the edge of Yuell to find a battle in full swing.

Imperial forces had penetrated the first line of defense to enter the city. There were no walls to stop them. Parts of the area had been reduced to rubble, the fountain at the center of the square flattened, fires catching. Smoke and dust clogged the air. Clad in uniforms bolstered by plate armor, the invaders somewhat resembled knights with their closed-face steel helms. They wielded clunky firearms straight out of the history books, though that did not detract from the deadly storm of bullets raining down on their foes, and followed that strange flow of combat he saw in Academy City of seeking cover and running in short bursts—warfare for an Auraless age.

Fighting them were the Yuell militia. Caught by surprise, they could only muster a ragtag band thus far to stall the assault, hiding behind corners or makeshift barricades as they returned fire in desperation. Their primary arms consisted of bolt-action rifles that failed to match the machine guns of the other side, and their uniforms consisted of nothing more substantial than fabric. The Imperial soldiers kept them pinned down, preventing the militia members from forming up in a cohesive unit. Outclassed in weapons and tactics, the opening moments of the battle had already plunged Yuell into dire straits.

"This is it!" Jaune called over his shoulder. "Tattletale, this is the Event. I'm going!"

He hadn't been sure on taking part an hour earlier, because details from the scroll were too sparse to inform him of the situation. After talking to Hans and Greta, hearing about how their father left home and joined the army to push back the invaders of Gallia? Seeing the rubble in front of him that used to be houses, bodies lying in the streets? Jaune was ready to rock.

Tattletale threw out a hand to stop him, pulling him around the corner of a print shop. "Jaune, wait, don't just rush in."

"There's no time—"

"Something knocked those houses down!" she cut in. "They have more than footsoldiers. Explosions… this time period…" Her eyes flicked to the sky. "Not aircrafts." The ground shook beneath their feet. "Tanks!"

Through the smoke, three looming shapes emerged, each running on two big strips of tread that crushed the ground they rolled over. They shared more of a resemblance to the new Atlas mechs than vehicles, armored to the gills in red-tinted steel and sporting cannons atop turrets along with built-in machine gun emplacements.

Jaune thought of the tanks of Remnant, that failed project that stood as one of the most unnecessary developments to come out of the Kingdoms' history fighting against the Grimm, mobile fortresses that had turned into veritable deathtraps consigning their operators to final moments of waiting for Ursas to rip their way in, and then compared them to this.

Tanks didn't look so useless anymore. Turns out, they were great if the enemy was human.

"Those are the real killers in this battle," Tattletale warned. "The soldiers are really just there to provide them support. A round of that cannon will do a number on your Aura, maybe even crack it."

"I think I can survive one."

The lead tank, twice as big as its brethren, swiveled its cannon barrel toward a barricade. The squad of militia taking cover there scrambled to get out of the way. With a loud boom, the stacked sandbags and armor plates were blown to smithereens. Half the squad were wiped out along with it, and the building behind them now carried a gaping hole.

"Not two," Jaune added. "But if I stay on the move, I can probably avoid being in the line of fire. What are their weaknesses? I'll aim for that and take them out."

"I'm not familiar with the nitty-gritty of them. Give me a minute." She picked apart the scene. "There are subtle differences in design between these and the Earth iterations. They've put more armor plating at the front and sides. The rear part… that's where the engine goes, I think? It could make for a weakpoint. The tracks, too." She leaned further out. "Honestly, your best bet might be to cut in from above, where the hatch—" *Bang!*

The girl flipped head over heels, slamming into the ground with a cry.

"Tattletale!" Jaune was by her side an instant later, his shield covering her. A healing potion materialized in thin air, caught by Escha who hurriedly unstoppered the jar. It proved unnecessary.

Tattletale held her head in her arms, voice a choked rasp as she moaned and thrashed in pain. She was encased in the apple-green glow of her Aura, the bullet that struck her failing to pierce her defenses.

"Sniper!" she managed to croak out.

Dead man, Jaune corrected within his mind. "Escha, take care of her. Keep her safe."

"I will!" promised the cat.

With a nod, he stood up. His sword appeared to hand. Bracing his shield, Jaune charged out of hiding.

A bullet cracked the cobblestone next to his foot, its shooter unable to account for his speed. The shot revealed the sniper's location camped up on the second floor window of a home. A not-so-nice smile grew on Jaune's face.

The Imperial soldiers soon noticed his entry into the battle, unsubtle frontal rush that it was. The nearest squad of soldiers pointed their guns in his direction. A barrage of bullets struck his shield, and they promptly returned their focus to the militia, having assumed him dead.

Imagine their surprise when he dropped into the middle of the squad, laying into them with his blade. A radio held in a severed hand barked questions as he made short work of the soldiers. Once he was done, he resumed his run at the sniper.

The man had witnessed the defeat of his comrades, and didn't take it well. His arms shook as he peered through the scope.

One moment, Jaune ran along the street. The next, [Third Arm] latched onto the windowsill to slingshot him forward, and he now bared his teeth inches away from the scope. In panic, the soldier pulled the trigger. A sharp *bang*, and the bullet hit the shield, ricocheting straight back at the sniper to punch a hole in his chest.

"Gah—!" The sniper slumped to the floor, his rifle slipping from his grip to clatter on the wood. "What… How…"

Jaune ignored the man. He snagged the rifle, and dropped it in his Pocket for later. With a cold glare at the dying sniper, he jumped out the window.

He landed on the ground, greeted by dead silence. Miltia and Imperial forces alike had paused mid-battle to stare at him, bewildered by what had just occurred. He supposed that's proof enough that magic did not exist in this world.

Would rocket boots?

Activating them, Jaune blasted off across the square.

To their credit, the soldiers adapted to the situation. A detachment sallied forth to intercept him while the battle resumed around them. One of the smaller tanks joined in to bolster their side, driving on a course to crash into him.

A quick adjustment of his flight, and Jaune flipped over the tank, landing atop the exit hatch where he proceeded to slam his sword into the hinges. He worked the blade to saw through the steel.

A bullet hit him in the back to throw him forward, putting a stop to that. His grip on Crocea Mors prevented him from falling in the dirt, and as he hung off the side, a scan of the surroundings showed the soldiers in position and tracking him with their guns. With a curse, he kicked off the tank and hurried behind a nearby pile of rubble. Bullets bounced off the spot he vacated.

He took a few seconds to catch his breath, reviewing the plan. Breaking into the tank was viable, but slow. He's a sitting duck for the duration. Beating down the soldiers might be advisable before he tried again. Except, that would grant the tanks free reign to wrought destruction.

A bullet buried in the dirt in front of him, missing wide. Jaune whirled toward the culprit, stopping short—completely flummoxed—as it turned out to be a civilian.

Well, a civilian fighting on the side of the militia, but that didn't help her case any. She immediately pointed her rifle away from him, and signaled with her free hand, trying to communicate past the noise of the battlefield.

Despite his wariness, Jaune flicked his gaze to where the young woman indicated, spotting a squad of Imperial soldiers moving on her group's position while their allies kept the group pinned down with gunfire.

Ah. The bullet was to get his attention, never intended to land.

Jaune plucked the front-most soldier with a shadowy arm, clotheslining him in passing as he charged into the squad faster than they could respond. Blood flew in the air, and in seconds he had carved his way through their ranks. Grabbing the last person, he threw the man at his allies located further back as a distraction then booked it for the militia group. His boots scraped along the ground as he slid behind cover to join the five people squeezed in there.

"Holy shit, kid—" one man began, but the woman who signaled Jaune cut in.

"Not the time, Walter." She brushed her bangs out of her eyes, and pointed. "This is our best chance to take out that tank."

The man, baker's apron peeking from beneath hastily-donned armor, nodded his head. "Got it. Sorry."

He passed his rifle to an ally, and turned around to heave a massive stick off the ground. Wait, no, it's a lance.

Jaune felt an immediate kinship with this guy.

The man held the weapon in an odd manner, propped above his shoulder instead of under it. Grunting at the heavy weight, he aimed the tip at one of the tanks. His hand moved to a trigger set on the side of the lance.

Oh.

A pull of the trigger, and the tip detached from the weapon to fly off.

That's no lance, it's just a rocket launcher!

White smoke trailed the rocket as it drew a line straight for the tank. The projectile hit home at the rear of the vehicle, and the ensuing explosion did not so much stop the tank as it blasted the thing to smithereens. A fireball bloomed from the wreckage, and metal bits rained over the area, some of the chunks bigger than a person's head. A shout of dismay went up from the Imperial side of the conflict at the destruction.

"Whoo! Ain't that a fine shot!" crowed the militiaman while his comrades slapped him on the back in celebration. "I'll bet you never hunted anything as big as this, huh, Marina?"

The young woman allowed the joke to pass, the narrowing of her eyes the sole indication of ire in her aloof facade. She turned to Jaune.

"You. Can you use that ability of yours again?" she said curtly.

He'd guess she was referring to his rockets and arm, and took heart in that she wasn't calling for him to be drowned in a lake for foul witchery. Some people understood priorities. He nodded.

"We don't have people on the other side of the square," the woman continued. Her voice had a scratchy timbre, as if she didn't use it often. "You're the only one that can move in position to catch the tanks in the radiators."

"The what?" Jaune asked, cocking an eyebrow. "Sorry, I don't know much about tanks."

The young woman shifted closer, grabbing his shoulder and pointing at the biggest tank. Jaune followed her finger.

"That blue box at the back. Tanks need it to regulate the ragnite heat. Hit that, and the whole thing blows."

He perked up hearing that bit of news, and looked closer at his new target. The angle wasn't great from this spot, but he could make out the intense blue glow at the place she indicated. There were a pair of soldiers stationed near it to provide a light guard, a perfunctory task given the lack of militia presence on that front.

The woman let go of him. "Here, Walter, give him your lance."

"No need," Jaune said, setting into a runner's stance. "I've already got one."

Two steps, and [Third Arm] flung him into the sky. The rockets then activated, angling him downward as he traveled faster than a car.

The soldiers noticed his approach. Their training likely hadn't taught them to defend against an attack of this sort, but they gave their best attempt, rifles pointed upward. The sun peeking through the clouds at his back kept them from drawing a bead on him.

A well-placed shot took one of the soldiers between the eyes. A shade under a second later, his partner fell to an identical wound. Jaune glanced in the direction he came from, and found the young woman aiming down her sights.

He touched down to a free and clear shot. The tank's radiator hummed with power, the heat able to be felt even from his spot a distance apart. Glowing blue fluid—refined ragnite—coursed through the device.

His sword disappeared, replaced by the gunlance. The weapon swung around, too quick for anyone to prevent what came next. Red Rook fired, its roar drowned out by the resulting inferno as the tank went up in flames.

He pivoted on his heels. The lance aligned with his next target, almost snapping into place without his input. The soldiers have started pouring gunfire on his position, now playing the part of the hopeless resistance struggling against defeat. A second fireball erupted to shatter their spirits.

The destruction of the third tank signaled the end. Morale crushed and advantage stolen, the Imperial forces shifted to a fighting retreat. Bodies fell one by one as the militia seized the momentum, rolling over their enemy.

In mere minutes, the battle was won. Yuell was won.

Jaune stood at the center of the battlefield, breathing hard as adrenaline coursed through his veins. He startled as a great shout arose from all directions. Turning his head this way and that, he saw militia and townsmen alike punching the air, roaring in unbridled victory.

It was him they cheered for.

His heart fluttered with an odd feeling. Hesitantly, he returned their smiles, and gave them a small wave of his hand.

That's when the artillery shelling began.


Universe: Valkyria Chronicles. Location: Yuell. Event: Imperial Advance​


Author's Notes: The bells are a-ringing, spring is in the air~ Bullets shattering the morning, breaking up the fair~

In Valkyria Chronicles 1, Yuell was but a footnote. It features more prominently in VC2 and VC3, except one was exclusive on the PSP and the other never made it out of Japan, so I'm assuming the people aware of the story elsewhere can be counted on one hand. We're veering off the canon rails for this one, and there's a reason for that. Guesses on why?
