The roads they were aiming toward would allow them to beeline for Yuell ahead of the Imperial troops.

As the ambush teams pulled back, Lieutenant Faldio Landzaat said, "That leaves us with just a frontal defense. Our lances aren't suited for that kind of engagement. They will definitely reach the city at this rate."

"No choice, Faldio," said Welkin. "We don't have enough armor of our own to fight on the open plains, and their formation spreads them too wide for a flanking force to do anything other than catch the edges. The wall is where we will hold them."

"No go. Like I said, my dear friend. The Batomys is a fortress-breaker. It will plow a hole right past our defenses."

"In one spot," Tattletale chimed in. "That limits the number of troops they can move through." She glanced up at him. "We should let it happen."

She then blinked as instead of agreeing with her, Jaune reared back.

"We should what!?" he cried.

Allow that thing to come in? Let it tear down the wall?

"I have a plan." That stopped short the growing panic in his mind, visions of settlements aflame pulling back. Tattletale grinned. "The tank will get in the city no matter what, except we can make it do that on our terms." Faldio Landzaat tried to get a word in, but she shushed him and continued. "The urban environment works to our advantage."

Welkin Gunther spoke up, and Tattletale shushed him, too. The man powered on through. "A tank's narrow field of vision renders it essentially blind in close quarters. If we put our people in the alleyways or the rooftops, we can fire on them from multiple angles. That forces the tanks to a supporting role, and this will become a contest between the soldiers. She's right."

Tattletale preened at that. Not for long, though. Withdrawing from the conversation, she placed the radio on the windowsill and hovered close to Jaune's ear.

"Hah?" A question was on his lips when the comment filtered into his head, its implication abruptly turning crystal clear. "You want me in there," he stated.

"…We can sell that tank."

"We can sell that fucking tank," Tattletale agreed, the grin now wide and wild. "Good luck to those idiots, invading this place without it."

It was a risk. A heavy risk, although also a rather inevitable one. The Empire designed the Batomys with city defenses in mind and the halfway measures protecting Yuell presented a poor matchup against the superweapon. They could complain about the problem, or account for it in their solution. The idea earned a tentative nod from him; the tank breaking through did not spell the end of the world.

The pair rejoined the ongoing discussion between the Militia commanders. Thereafter, the battle plan began to take shape in the limited timetable they had. Their forces would shift their defenses from the wall to further inward, preparing a killzone for their guests. Ideally, they would catch the enemy in a pincer movement. Two platoons, Squad 3 and Squad 1, would stay at the rear, ready to respond should the Imperials split up to attack elsewhere.

As for Jaune and the Yuell garrison, they had the job of welcoming the Empire. Bait, to draw them in.

He landed on the ground below without anybody batting an eye. The wide avenue had become a staging ground, with the Militia platoons unloading equipment and ammunition in preparations. The Edelweiss sat off to the side, engine rumbling. Taking cue from him, Welkin Gunther climbed out a second-story window to drop onto the hull of the tank. Isara was at the tank hatch, and the girl wiggled her fingers in a subtle wave before returning to attention.

"What are your orders, Jaune?" asked Walter, who stood at the forefront of the group. Next to him, Marina hugged Escha to her chest and sent Jaune a reproachful glare for bringing the cat onto a battlefield.

"Grab your lances and climb the rubble," Jaune commanded. "We're going to engage them while they're outside the city and do whatever we can to weaken them. Ruin their cannons. Scatter their formation. Hell, let's see if we can send them packing before they hit the wall."

That one earned a roar of approval.

Walter adjusted the pair of shades he was wearing. "You talking lances, or lances?"

"Both. Take all we've got. Now, come on!"

The group set to work. Soon, they had a section of the wall to themselves, finding their footing amidst the uneven debris. Upon every shoulder rested a lance.

The first thing one might notice about the lances was that they in no way resembled the Gallian lance. Much like the armor worn by the Imperials, anti-tank weaponry in Europa had its roots within the traditions of an older era where knights roamed the land, in this case the jousting lance popular in tourneys. The shape of the implement lent itself to the technology in the early days of development.

These lances followed a simpler aesthetic. A short tube, in essence, with two grips near the front end. Plastics and alloys reduced the weight of the weapon so that even the slightest members of the garrison could wield one.

It was a weapon that should not exist in the current decade, acquired during his spending spree. A recoilless rocket launcher.

The Yuell militia had proven a quick study on its use, and they now aimed their strange lances with eagerness at the approaching line of tanks. Their fingers stayed off the triggers, however. Prior experience, relatively minor as they were, informed them that the vehicles had yet to enter range.

Kneeling on one knee, Jaune tilted his head down to speak into his phone. "Tattletale, tell us when."

Sure, he could learn the ins and outs of this thing, maybe master that range finder doohickey. It wouldn't take too long. But why, when he could rely on Tattletale's eyes and intuition? The girl was a dream when it came to serving as a spotter.

The Imperials maintained a pace that could not be called fast by any means. Yet, the Batomys carried within its bulk a sense of inexorable fate, plowing into and past a hill with barely a dip in speed. It loomed larger with the passing seconds, and all too soon, Jaune got a reply.

"Now!" Tattletale shouted.

His voice rang across the wall. "Fire!"

Computerized sights guided the gunners, and in the span of moments they unleashed a barrage of high-explosive ammunition upon the Imperial line. The tanks may have laid at the very edge of their range, but as blasts of flames and smoke jetted from the backend of the weapons, the warheads crossed that distance at a velocity no existing lance rocket could match. Not every single one struck true; those that did resulted in devastating effect. Designed to penetrate armor, the shaped charges punctured the thick steel at the front of the vehicles. Some 'merely' embedded in the metal to then crack open the hull like an egg when they explode. Others made it through to the very interior of the tanks, or slipped past the moving wall of armor to catch the troop transports behind them.

Deep within the city, loud booms could be heard. For once, it was Gallia that enjoyed artillery support. The air whistled as shells rained upon the attacking force. Fireballs bloomed over the meadow.

Jaune had shot at the giant tank, as did nearly a dozen other people with varying accuracy. Their combined assault set the Batomys along with the immediate area around it ablaze, gouging out the earth and throwing it in the air. Smoke washed over the tank.

For one good, long beat they watched on, holding their breath. Then, Tattletale gave her report.

"Crap."

The Batomys burst out of the smoke, its armor warped and blackened but the tank very much operable. The machine gun at the front was gone, ripped apart with its gunner never having a chance, but the hard steel shell at the rear of the compartment remained intact to keep the warheads from piercing into the mechanical vitals.

Shouts of dismay rang up and down the line. Still, Jaune took heart in that they had thrown the Imperial formation into chaos. Results were acceptable.

A shame about that hit to the resale value, but oh well. He would rather it blow up than lose Yuell.

"Don't rest now," Jaune ordered. "Hit them with the second verse. Backup arms!"

He dropped his rocket launcher, and the others followed suit. Perhaps they could have reloaded and squeezed in a salvo with the time they had left. Jaune didn't bank on it; the Imperials have cut down the distance by almost half. Which, as it happened, put them in perfect range for what came next.

The Yuell garrison grabbed at the standard lances by their side, or the lasguns for those with not the strength to lift those cumbersome sticks. He went the latter route, summoning a lasgun and cranking a dial on the side that regulates the power pack, setting it to the highest it can go. That had been a fun afternoon when they tested out the function.

Panic swept through the Empire forces. Tanks careened into one another in their bid to avoid damage. Burning hulks became deadly obstacles that led to crashes and pileups.

One tank, the crimson Lupus, revealed its capabilities here, zigzagging in a way no tanks of that size should in order to take cover behind the Batomys. The strategy was adopted by its nearest cohorts and soon formed a column with the giant tank at their head. The luckless crews further away formed their own columns, jostling for the coveted rearmost places as they pushed the sacrifices forward to serve as shields.

It began small. A… a ka-thunk was the best Jaune could describe it.

He had seen videos of Goliath Grimm attacking settlements, a required segment in Grimm Studies, and he recognized it. That moment when something shifted, a tiny bulge in an otherwise strong and defiant wall. That part was always so deceptive, a wound which seemed almost comical in its triviality. It gave people a split second to think "Maybe everything would be okay."

Then, the pinprick of a wound became larger. The damage widened, and the wall started to buckle inward. The ground quaked beneath their feet to herald the hell that would follow. Those who were to either side of Jaune could not help but flinch, and in every heart there burned a deep, desperate wish that the wall would hold, the plan be damned.

In aiming at Jaune and his troops, the supertank had ended up on the wide avenue rather than a scenario where it crashed against a building that held their people inside, squashing everyone. This also placed it right in front of the mine field, set at such a distance that momentum plunged the tank into the trap.

The cry of victory caught in Jaune's throat.

That slab of steel, the bulldozer blades attached to the front of the tank, had torn up the road ahead to grant the Batomys passage. Gallian soldiers stationed at the first set of barricades were forced to abandon the fortification as the Batomys crushed it underfoot. The supertank slowed not a single bit as it churned the dirt, cobblestone, and landmines before it in a roiling wave.

The Batomys sped past multiple layers of defenses and troops without a single by your leave. The Empire had failed again and again to put a foothold in the city, so they were putting in a fortress instead.

Behind it, the smaller tanks were funneling into the break in the wall. They rolled over the open ground with impunity, pair by pair pulling off to the side—angled outward—while their brethren continued on. The formation compelled the Gallians to back off lest they wanted to eat a tank shell.

Boy and cat deployed to these spots before the defenders could be overwhelmed, where their presence turned the momentum decidedly back in Yuell's favor. A quick hop relocated them among the Empire troops, and the thick concentration of enemy forces meant that a swing of the gunlance would knock half a dozen people away, while a shell resulted in a tank or truck going up in flames. Behind him, the Yuell militia steadily moved up the street to catch up with the Batomys.

The Imperials soon experienced a mysterious phenomenon. Ammunition caches vanished into thin air, heavy weaponry set to cut down swaths of defenders weren't where they left it, emptied-out trucks people used as cover blinked away to expose them to the Gallians' retaliation. The tight bulwark they established fell apart as Jaune brushed by the area.

A few blocks away at what passed for HQ, Tattletale would have the Company scroll in one hand, tapping away whenever she spied a new entry appear as she updated him on the situation. Because [Mobile Merchant] was less skill and more 'critical function locked behind a paywall', once bought it didn't require him there to press the button, merely that he was in contact with what needed to be sold. Tattletale had suggested he divert the split second decision over to her, saving him the distraction so that he could fight at his best.

The moving battle was especially fierce at the forefront. Squad 7 fought a constant retreat, relying on the dense urban environment and the tank's limited field of vision to launch attacks on the superweapon. Their efforts to delay the Batomys encountered stiff resistance from its supporting troops, however. The giant tank was staying near infantry squads, clearing a path for them yet ensuring that it never pulled too far ahead. The tank crew understood their weakness and minimized it to the best of their abilities.

A shadowy arm latched onto the Batomys's hull. In a blink, Jaune impacted against it, both feet planted on the sloping metal and his gaze scanning the soldiers below. He picked a spot, and dove.

Escha jumped off midway to harry the squad. Meanwhile, he landed on a soldier's back, bringing them both to the ground. Rolling upright, Red Rook reappeared in his grasp and he fired a shot that blasted through a group of gunmen preparing to fire on him.

A blue beam of light took out a sniper posted at the center of the soldiers, whose rifle was pointed in his direction. Jaune glanced up, catching a glimpse of Marina moving along the rooftops. Given the treacherous gaps between the buildings, she and other snipers seemed to be struggling to keep pace with the battle, the main portion of which had started to leave them behind.

The Imperial troops have recovered from his sudden entry. Entire firing lines established, machine guns aimed his way. Grabbing Escha by the scruff of her neck, he evacuated her to safety, landing on the sidewalk. They scrambled behind a low wall as bullets whizzed overhead.

Jaune tsked, and spoke into his phone. "Lisa, I don't think stealing the Batomys is going to work out. Our allies are barely hanging on. Is there anything we can buy from the Marketplace that you think can turn this around?"

"Just wait," was her curt reply.

"What do you mean, wait? Lisa?"

He could not hear her answer, if she did give one. The Batomys chose that moment to let loose a round, deafening the area with the sound of the cannon. People near the tank were knocked off their feet as the recoil transmitted through the tank and into the ground.

As the world stopped shaking, Jaune looked up to see Escha with the oddest expression on her face, the lips peeled back and fangs bared as she had her paws slapped over her ears.

"Not a fan of that?"

She shook her head, and shivered in discomfort. Jaune soothed her with a pat as he searched for the tank's target.

"Ah dammit," he cried. "That was my tower."

The university was now missing one of its belltowers, the structure collapsing due to the gaping hole near its base. A superficial wound on the building, all told. Nobody would be there.

Still, he liked that spot.

An Imp poked over the wall, machine gun pointed down at them. His sword sliced the gun in half, and Jaune jumped up to bash their helmets together, winning the exchange by dint of a harder head. The sword was traded for a lasgun, red light spraying across the enemy line. A boomerang joined the assault, whirling high and far to loop around and smack a soldier on the back of the head. Escha zipped along under the soldiers' feet to retrieve the tool, proceeding to lay into ankles and shins with ferocious abandon. Up top, Jaune swept through their ranks.

An explosion wracked a tall building further back along the road. Jaune did not pay it much mind until a second blast occurred inside, then a third one over at the building opposite. The two structures teetered, their walls leaning forward at a precarious angle. Then, with an almost audible snap, they fell one after the other onto the road, burying the unfortunate Imperials caught below. The soldiers assisting the Batomys suddenly found themselves separated from reinforcements.

"Yes!" Tattletale shouted. "Jaune, now is your chance. Get on that tank!"

He hurried to heed her advice. The whole time, his mind raced.

"Since when did you prepare this?" he asked.

"Had it set up when the Batomys breached the wall. What use are engineers if we don't put their expertise to work."

Huh. It went to show that the best thing to fight an army with, was an army of his own. He had no idea this was going on, as well as perhaps half a dozen efforts in places he could not see. And yet, help arrived at the most opportune time to open the way forward for him.

With a whoop, Jaune took flight. He scooped up Escha and beelined for the Batomys as Squad 7 performed an about-face. A few bullets dinged his armor, but entire teams of Gallian soldiers seemed to materialize from the side streets to unload on the Imps, pinning them down.

He reached out to grab a set of railings mounted atop of the supertank, swinging onto the platform. At this height, he was drawing level with some of the rooftops, and he shook his head at the mind-boggling size of the house on wheels.

A metal door, as Tattletale said, rested at the end of the platform. Escha tilted her head curiously once they got near it, and pressed her ear to the metal.

"I hear people on the other side."

Guarding against intruders, no doubt. A tank of such size can afford to house and spare the personnel for the task. Jaune raised his lasgun.

"Step back, Escha."

A laser beam crashed against the door. The sustained attack melted a hole in the steel, and they heard a shriek from inside, along with the clanging of boots. Jaune dragged the laser to cut the hinges and handle, then stepped back as the door tipped open. He seized the heavy sheet of metal and shoved it off the platform, belatedly realizing that he had just lowered the value of the supertank again. Shrugging, Jaune entered the Batomys.

He was immediately greeted by a team of soldiers grouped under a dim lightbulb set in the ceiling, one of whom suffered extensive burns. Terror-stricken, their hands holding guns trembled with nerves.

A shot went off, pinging his armor and doing little harm. Jaune did not even bother using weaponry in the confined space, barreling into them and relying on the Rathalos spikes on his armor to amplify his charge, smashing them into the wall. Afterward, he checked for a way forward. A small set of stairs allowed entry to the level below, and he and Escha jumped down without hesitation.

They emerged in a cramped corridor lined with pipes and cables. A steady hiss flowed through the pipes, possibly circulating fuel or water or some other fluid. It was dark here, but the weak sources of light illuminated enough for him to discern the gleam of red armor within the shadows.

"Intruders!" cried a soldier, and it was on.

Quick as a flash, Escha darted into range and bit the frontmost trooper on his ankle. The man thrashed about, getting in the way of his allies and giving Jaune time to close the distance. Crocea Mors deployed to slice apart metal and flesh. Gunfire erupted in response, bouncing around the corridor to present an unpredictable danger for anybody who happened to be present, including the soldiers themselves. A bullet clipped a pipe, which emitted a scalding steam.

This group fared no better than the previous one, and the last soldier ate steel as Jaune slammed his face against the wall.

Escha scampered ahead to another door, going up on tiptoes to grab the handwheel that would unlatch it. She then dangled there, body squirming as she tried to find leverage. Jaune helped her out, his height and weight a more appropriate fit for the handle.

The door opened to a platform overlooking a quite spacious room. A throne sat directly ahead of him, and that was no hyperbole. The ostentatious thing appeared gilded in gold, with—Jaune walked over to look at it from the front—plush red cushions that begged for someone to sit on it.

Which he promptly did, whereupon he cast an imperious gaze over the sweat-soaked peasants (tank crew) staring in shock below.

"Stop the tank," he said. "Surrender while you're at it. I was told you would be treated humanely."

Escha wanted a turn on the chair, too. She jumped into his lap, letting him pet her fur.

An officer stood up from his less grandiose, yet still way too rich chair to glare up at Jaune.

"Never! Never shall the Empire cave to the demands of inferiors, and never shall we surrender!"

"...Okay?"

Crocea Mors hurtled across the room to embed in the officer's chest. The man gave a choked rasp and fell to the floor.

Jaune stood up to lean over the railings. One by one, he met the gazes of the other people in the room. Next to him, a much more solemn Escha brandished her sword.

"I'm really not inclined to give a second warning. I know Lisa wants me to, but it doesn't make much sense to me. You're endangering this city. If you won't stop, then it's my job to make you."

The tank crew glanced at each other, and at the fallen officer. The desire to obey was there, they were just watching for someone to do it first. Finally, one man moved.

"H-He can't take on all of us!" the man stammered, drawing a handgun from its holster.

As far as rallying cries went, it was fine. It got people to take action. The tank crew pretty much regretted it instantly as Jaune and Escha leapt onto them. The tank fell into pandemonium, with gunfire and a steady shing, shing sound that dominated the fight and soon became the only noise left.

The last two crewmen flattened their backs against the wall, a sword and a gun pressed to their throats.

"Pull the brakes," Jaune commanded. This time, they fell over one another in their rush to comply.

The tank shook and rumbled as it screeched to a halt. The crewmen chanced a look at Jaune, nervous as they eyed his weapons still raised aloft.

He smiled at them. Crocea Mors and the lasgun vanished into his Pocket. The two people appeared torn between shock at his magic, and relief that they won't be disposed of now that their use has come to an end. That rather changed when he seized them by the neck and banged their heads together to render them unconscious.

"Welp, we're done here. Escha, let's head out."

"Okay!" Escha was all too eager to do so. The air in here did not agree with her, it seemed.

Jaune dragged the unconscious crewmen with them, and picked up other survivors along the way until he was lugging a stack of Imperial soldiers. Climbing up the stairs proved an ordeal and a half, but he managed it. They soon stood out in the fresh air where he threw the lot overboard, thus securing ownership of the Batomys for himself.

The action was not missed by those on the ground. The battle had stalled out with the cessation of operation of the Batomys, and a sea of faces greeted Jaune as he looked over the avenue.

The Gallian soldiers were struck dumb, not yet able to understand. They had been fighting a hopeless battle, with the situation changing in an instant. Imperial troops stared in a stupor. The superweapon should have been their invincible star of victory, and its loss shook them to the core.

From the roof across the way, Marina swept her bangs aside, gray eyes gazing at him unblinking. Walter braced against the wall of an alleyway, and shook his head while sporting a grin. Welkin Gunther peeked out the hatch of his tank in blank astonishment. His subordinates, Largo and Rosie, had their jaws meeting the floor.

Walls and fortresses could not stop the Batomys. Rockets and artillery could not stop the Batomys. A whole damn army fighting a war over the length of a street, a straight line of destruction leading from the edge of Yuell to near the city center, could not stop the Batomys. And yet, a single person succeeded where nothing else has. A man faced a superweapon, and the man won.

Plus a cat. But telling them that would make it less believable, not more.

Jaune looked over the avenue… and he noticed something odd stirring. Shouts arose among the people, calling up to him. Weapons were pointed his way. Gallians, to a one.

No, the guns were pointed past him.

Tock. Tock. Tock.

The clacking of heels on metal was followed by rustling fabric, the swoosh of a cape or similar.

"Jaune, behind you," Tattletale murmured.

He turned his head. Behind him rested the main cannon of the Batomys, and standing above it…

High heels, pretty face, she's the type girls love to hate. A dark uniform ornamented in gold, her legs went on and on.

She held a massive rifle, long and elegantly crafted, in a loose grip with one hand, the other on her hips. The light of the sun framed her silver hair, the angel's eyes as red as that of Grimm.

The beautiful woman leveled a dispassionate gaze at Jaune.

"To silence the Batomys, you are the one, then," she said. "The person who claims to be a Valkyria."

Jaune found his tongue. "That's what they call me. And you are?"

The woman tilted her chin and glanced to the sky in thought, considering a reply. She soon nodded, and looked at him once again.

"Selvaria Bles, the most trusted hand of His Highness, Prince Maximilian. My prince has developed an inordinate fascination with you. For his sake, I will judge whether you are telling the truth."

Wait a minute, he had heard of the Max guy before. That man was from the Empire. Which meant this woman was from the Empire. An enemy.

"Really," said Jaune, scoffing as he adopted a more guarded stance. "And what makes you think you're in a position to do that?"

The woman did not answer with words. Instead, she swung her rifle around and squeezed the trigger.

The barrage of bullets passed harmlessly above his head. He was already in motion. With one stride, he closed the distance between them, swiping a newly-resummoned Crocea Mors to take out her legs.

A light hop, and the sword passed through an empty space.

The woman's descent carried a weightless quality, her form seeming to float in the air. She snapped out a kick, and it turned out far stronger than he expected, launching him back. He hit the railings, going over.

As he fell, Jaune watched Selvaria Bles kick one long leg over the metal bar, then the other, crossing them to sit in an elegant pose as she spared a moment to regard him with a haughty gaze before jumping down after him.

A battle was beginning anew. War really couldn't be easy, huh?

Also… hot~.


Author's Notes: Tall, beautiful lady with the arm strength to lift a massive cannon that barely qualifies as a personal firearm. By Remnant standards, the dream.

Let's see if we can get a chapter out on Sunday next.

#3,486
Chapter 50: Real, and Fake​


As he fell, Jaune beheld the blue sky, and a vision of beauty whose curtain of long, silver hair streamed behind her in the wind. Rifle in her hand, a fencing saber on her hip, she belonged on a battlefield. What a memory this would be, he thought.

Rockets on, he went from dropping like a rock to flying sideways, touching down to skid along the ground until he came to a stop a short distance away, his shield up. The woman landed a moment later, high heels clicking on the cobblestone road.

A spark was lit to reignite the conflict between Gallians and Imperials. In the blink of an eye, gunfire once more engulfed the avenue, and Jaune joined them.

He pointed with an empty hand. A lasgun filled his grip, and he pulled the trigger. The woman was already twirling out of the way, the laser bolt passing by to sizzle on the hull of the Batomys. He readjusted his aim, trying again and again. His marksmanship ensured he fired at her with accuracy, but she was just never there for the shots to hit.

No ordinary soldier, was Selvaria Bles. At a glance, her reflexes ranked on par with the top of his class, the likes of Pyrrha and Jax and Ruby Rose. The type to be aware of the exact angle at which a gun was pointing.

One of her spins ended with her feet set wide for stability and her firearm braced on the ground. Without hesitation, she let loose a barrage of bullets aimed for center mass. The rifle barely wavered as it barked a rapid staccato, the shots grouped tight and slamming into his shield with enough force that it pushed him back, his shoes scraping on the road.

His arm numbed under the assault, yet the shield held solid. That outcome took Selvaria aback, Jaune could tell. The slightest trace of a frown shaped her icy gaze into something far less confident. She broke off the attack, and through a backbreaking hip twist maneuver she rolled upright to dash for cover behind the bulldozer blade of the Batomys. Her rifle then extruded from around the corner, along with a sliver of her face. The gun roared, and Jaune dove toward the tank threads, flattening against the metal panels to minimize his frame.

"Jaune, what's happening on your end?" Tattletale called out from over the phone. "How did you not win yet?"

"You make it sound so easy," Jaune replied as more bullets struck his shield. "But no, she's more skilled than the others. Dodged the laser bolts and everything."

"You said she dodge?"

"I did. Means she isn't bulletproof."

"Not the point I took from that. How can she be that fast—no, I'll have a better picture once I get to a better spot for a look. She's someone known to the Imps, I do know that. They started fighting like mad once they saw her kick you off the Batomys."

The message was clear. Take her down, and fast. The Empire soldiers drew courage from her presence.

He fired the lasgun to drive Selvaria out of sight, then traded it for his sword. For a foe armed with a big, big cannon like her, distance equaled options. The simple solution was to cut that short and bring the fight in close. The Outsider's Mark shimmered on his hand, and [Third Arm] latched onto a spot near the front of the tank. Jaune zipped through the intervening space, arriving as the woman peeked out of hiding. Her eyes widened in shock.

His sword sliced off locks of her hair, Selvaria ducking in the nick of time. Jaune swung around the corner and kicked at her, his foot diverted aside as she swept the rifle up to block him. The rocket under the boot activated to drive the foot right back at Selvaria, the metal sections crashing into her face. Her head snapped back. Anticipating the finishing blow coming for her, Selvaria flowed with the momentum, backflipping through the air, then again and a third time to end on a knee. She had not even a second to catch her breath before he was upon her.

This close, her gun was useless, and the woman unsheathed the fencing saber hanging on her hip. It snaked over and under his sword arm to trap it, and stabbed at the gap between helmet and breastplate, where one would think the armor thin. Imagine her astonishment as Jaune made no move to block or avoid the blow, and instead continue to close in. The steel blade scored along his throat, leaving not a scratch as he glowed with Aura's light. She couldn't see his reaction to the pain beneath the visor plate of his helmet. She mirrored it, however, when his sword—having mysteriously switched hands—pierced her side.

Quick as a flash, she pulled away from the blade before it could stab deeper, twirling to draw flush with his body where he could not easily angle his sword, her back to his chest. Saber and rifle fell to the ground, leaving her hands free to wind around his neck, tightening in a stranglehold.

Despite her bleeding wound, she lifted him, armor and all, and threw him over her shoulder.

Her prodigious strength tossed him a fair distance, except she found little reprieve from it. Jaune halted in midair, fires burning beneath his feet, and zoomed at her again. Selvaria hastily kicked her weapons up, grabbing them and taking a stance.

He barreled into her without a care. From the previous exchange, he had confirmed her capabilities. The conclusion he arrived at was that the advantage lay with him. She was good, but not good enough to prevail over the fact that when one side of the duel bled and the other stayed fresh as daisies, it could end only one way. Aura decided the match.

That said, Selvaria held up well, bending and twisting out of harm's way with a sense of serene detachment that spoke of skill honed over time as opposed to the mere animal instinct to not get hurt. She was better than anyone he had faced in this world, and worked with the weight of the gun in her hand like it was an extension of her body, a pendulum to speed up her movements and affect abrupt changes in direction.

"You… are very flexible," he said with surprising composure for one who was trying to lop off her arm at the moment.

"And you are a crude, boorish man," the woman replied as she leaned away from the slash, the dismissive air about her almost palpable. "Not an ounce of finesse or patience." Her face was splattered with mud from his shoe, a streak of blood where the metal edge sliced into her skin, yet she held herself with a sureness he found quite magnetic.

"Still dominating you, aren't I? Looks to me I'm coming out on top."

She scoffed. "We shall see how long you can keep it up. Try and impress me."

"What the hell are you two doing over there?" Tattletale piped up. She seemed to be on the move, her words punctuated by heavy breaths.

"Fighting?" said Jaune.

He spied a flash of purple on a rooftop, a ribbon tied around a blonde ponytail fluttering in the breeze.

"Huh. So you are." Her tone shifted. "Get her good, Jaune!" Tattletale cheered.

Selvaria's rifle worked best at a remove, and she attempted to create the necessary space by leaping high to land on the threads of the Batomys, then up onto a machine gun emplacement jutting outward. A final hop got her atop the hull, as Jaune flung himself after her with a shadowy arm.

"Whuh?" cried a flabbergasted Tattletale. "No human can jump like that!"

"Ahem."

"Shut up, there's something weird going on. Superpowers exist here!"

He left her to wonder the hows and whys. The enemy ahead occupied his attention.

Selvaria heard him coming, and turned back to meet him, her saber tracing a silvery arc through the air. His sword chopped the blade in half to leave her holding the hilt. For all her haughtiness, she wasn't above throwing that at his face as a distraction.

Jaune batted the broken saber aside and swiped at its owner, the woman jumping up to a higher spot on the tank to escape, then onto the base of the main cannon in order to clear some distance before bringing her rifle to bear. He followed, a rocket burst putting him on the same level, one foot in front of the other. He held his shield at the ready to counter her rifle, sword poised to strike.

To test her response, he swept Crocea Mors low. Selvaria retreated half a step, letting the sword pass harmlessly while retaining plenty of room to maneuver. A squeeze of the trigger, and a bullet slammed into the joint of his sword arm, bouncing off his Aura. His cry caused her eyes to narrow dangerously, her finger brushing the rifle trigger.

He couldn't have her thinking to seize the advantage. The next one was a lunge, aimed at her chest with the flat of his sword resting above the shield that was covering him to minimize his frame. She didn't even blink as she leaned aside, hips rolling to maintain balance. Still, it forced her another step back. Finding his rhythm, Jaune advanced step by step. His attacks pressed her to retreat a little further each time, the slow and careful approach denying her a suitable target to fire upon. It served her right for saying he had no patience. He could wait when the payoff was great enough.

Soon, they've crossed the base of the cannon, and onto the cannon barrel itself. When her high-heeled foot settled on the curved surface, Selvaria hesitated for a beat, then continued on. Jaune granted her not a single inch, pushing forward.

"You can try jumping," he suggested.

A delicate eyebrow rose. "And would you stab me if I tried?"

"Are you kidding? No way!"

He would totally stab her if she tried.

It seemed that Selvaria also suspected the same. She gave a slight shake of her head in reply.

"Well, then you can surrender," Jaune said. "I suppose I should at least offer you that chance."

At that, her eyes flicked past him. Jaune followed suit, chancing a quick look to make sure no danger was coming his way.

Up here, the two of them could observe far more of the battlefield, and the sights they saw drew a grimace from him.

Along the wide avenue, tanks spew smoke and flames. Trapped between the blue, a red line thinned to a sliver, pockets of Imperial resistance struggling to stem the Gallian tide. Defeat was a foregone thing. They were killing just to die. A complete, utter waste.

City garrison and Militia troops and even the civilians of Yuell fought side by side, covering for each other as they kept the Imperials pinned down. Where defenses proved resilient, grenades were employed to devastating effect. Lancers and snipers on rooftops rained death on the enemy below. Of the civilians, one particular man stood out, drunk on the carnage and moving so fast it almost looked like he teleported from place to place, firing on enemy soldiers with a gun from close range. On this side of the fallen buildings, the Edelweiss and Squad 7 were mopping up the remnants of the Batomys's supporting infantry, with Walter and others from the garrison covering their backs. Cut off from their allies, the soldiers in red armor shouted for reinforcements that never came.

"They'd listen if you tell them to stop, won't they?" Jaune said, growing somber. He returned her glare with a blank gaze. "I'm being serious here. What's the point of continuing? Your troops already lost, so what are you even fighting for? I mean, look at that." He indicated with his sword.

It seemed nothing could go in the invaders' favor, because a group of them was beset by rats, of all things. No cause was worth that fate.

Selvaria did not agree. "They move to the will of His Highness, and that is all the purpose they need. A sword, as I am, to enact his vision."

Were they? He saw soldiers curled in pain. He saw men sobbing as they lay dying, their knightly helmets cracked and fallen in the mud to reveal faces younger than his own. Theirs were not the cold, heartless steel of a blade.

He wondered what Selvaria saw through her eyes.

It hardly mattered, now. He had his answer.

Jaune shot forward, hands empty and armor suddenly gone to cut down on weight, advancing faster than he had done the entire fight—faster than Selvaria anticipated. Getting within range, he seized the woman by the arm, swinging her off her feet and throwing her into the sky.

The lasgun appeared in his hands, and he aimed it up high at his helpless foe.

Bam!

He was now holding a piece of junk, a bullet smashed into the center of the lasgun to render it useless scrap. His opponent hadn't been as helpless as he thought. With a stiff grin plastered on his face and one eye twitching, Jaune tossed the lasgun aside, and blasted off to follow Selvaria up into the air.

Bullets flew at him, Selvaria shooting as she fell, but he traced a winding course to avoid them. Once near, he retrieved his sword and swung it at the woman whose narrowed eyes watched him intently.

A midair twist at the last second, and she slapped the blade aside with her gloved palm. The muzzle of her rifle pointed in his direction. The shot was caught on a shield that appeared in a blink and vanished just as quickly, while Jaune rocket-stepped above her. Crocea Mors became Red Rook, and he slapped the massive gunlance down on Selvaria.

The rifle was torn from her grip, hitting the side of the Batomys with a clang. Selvaria struck the ground a moment later, and Jaune had to admit he was impressed when she bounced back up like some kind of crazed grasshopper to lunge after her gun. Even now, she intended to fight on.

Jaune squashed that hope by landing between them, his foot stomping on the rifle. He gave it a second to see if Tattletale had noticed the entry popping up on the Company scroll. When the rifle stayed in place, he deposited it inside his Pocket instead.

"And that's my win, I think," he said, playing off the brief period of silence.

Huffing for breath, Selvaria replied, "It is not you who will decide that."

"...Seriously? I'm amazed you can stand, and you believe you're in any shape to continue this?"

Apparently so, because with a final deep breath, she reasserted her composure. Her back straightened, and she planted a fist on her hip.

"Yes, I am," she said.

Her tone struck an odd note, prompting Jaune to study her with greater care. That hadn't been bravado at work. She sounded so certain.

He soon noticed what was wrong.

"Why aren't you bleeding anymore?"

Selvaria shifted her stance, running a hand above the tear in her uniform where he had stabbed her earlier. The open wound had knitted together at some point during their clash.

"A hundred cuts have been made on this body," she said, swiping a finger over the red stain and bringing it up before her eyes, "healed by morning so that a hundred more can take their place. For all your claims, your ignorance proves your lie. You are no Valkyria. You have not suffered for your power… because of your power." Her hand curled into a fist, and she gave Jaune an empty stare. "That is what it takes to reach this point. To awaken."

"Are you saying someone sliced you open to make you heal better?" he asked incredulously. "Was it that prince?"

She sighed a sweet sigh, shaking her head. "He saved me. For him, I was worthy as I am." The expression dimmed. "He is one of a kind. To the world, a Valkyria is a being of pain, born for destruction."

Jaune winced at that glimpse into a story he was not ready for, made worse by Tattletale whispering theories over the line about 'lab rat' and 'torture'. Still, a detail stood out, blaring in neon lights. If Selvaria was to be believed, then he stood in front of a Valkyria.

The word was one steeped in legend, shaping the creation myth of Europa. Warriors of nigh magical powers, they once ruled this land. Except, when asked, nobody seemed to have any consensus on what was possible for a Valkyria, or what they even looked like. Tattletale posited they weren't real in the first place as was wont with wizards, demigods, and other fantastical figures to be found in stories, hence why he slotted neatly into the role for the people of Yuell. Absent the real thing, who could say different?

One person, at this moment.

He wasn't about to let the lie come crashing down, now. The hope of too many people hinged on believing it as the truth. So, he put on a confident veneer, and scoffed at her.

"Oh, really?" he said, slapping a hand on the side of the Batomys. "Well then, do you see this tank? Want to know what I can do to it?"

With that, the entire Batomys—a two-story fortress on wheels—vanished from existence. For the second time, the battlefield fell to a hush. Nearby, the men and women of Squad 7 showed bug-eyed looks, with even the members of the Yuell garrison stock still in shock. Selvaria herself failed to stifle her reaction, lips parting in an open-mouthed stare at the deep groove left in the ground where the supertank once stood.

"Sure looks like destruction to me," Jaune remarked. Internally, he breathed a sigh of relief. Tattletale got the hint after all. He would have looked so stupid, otherwise.

Selvaria's mouth drew a thin line.

A whisper came from the phone. "Oh hey, want me to sell this rifle, too?"

"Nah, not yet," he said, matching Tattletale's volume and barely moving his lips. "I need a gun. Lost the last one." He returned his attention to Selvaria as she began to speak.

"The results appear inconclusive," she admitted, and the clinical way she said it raised the alarm bells in his head. Jaune swung his gunlance on his shoulder and summoned its accompanying shield. Bracing his weapons, he charged forward intent on ending the battle.

A resounding boom rang across the city that had him bringing up his shield, and his allies ducking on reflex. A long object then shot out of a side street, whistling through the air as it flew in an arc. The missile slammed into the road in front of Selvaria, impaling the earth. She displayed no surprise at its sudden appearance.

"Careful, that was launched by the Lupus," Tattletale warned. "Landzaat's flipping out. Something about a—"

Selvaria wrapped her fingers around a handle near the base of the rod-like object and, arm straining, pulled it out of the ground to brandish as a weapon. Comically large in her dainty hand, it bore a strange blue sheen, with grooves that ran along its length in a spiral pattern, flaring into a guard at the base and tapering to a point at the tip—it was a lance, no two ways about it. A circular disc covered one side of the hilt, its purpose growing clear as it detached and was wielded in her left hand as a shield.

"...Yeah, that," Tattletale finished. "Wowee, the thing's massive."

"Well, mine's bigger."

Tattletale spluttered, "I was providing you an analysis, silly man! She must have gorilla arms to lift that!"

Their bickering cut out as a glow overtook Selvaria Bles. Jaune's eyes widened as blue flames roiled from the woman, encasing her from head to toe in a sight which squeezed his heart tight for how it resembled something else so familiar to him. The lance that she struggled to hold aloft ceased to waver, the tip holding still. The weapon had taken on the same bright shine, bearing an otherworldly radiance.

"I called it! Dammit!" Tattletale appeared torn between smugness and concern. "She has superpowers. Enhanced strength to go with the self-healing. In fact, is that Aura? Do they make flames like that?"

"Not that I've heard of," Jaune said, warily eyeing this new development. "Unless it's an effect of her Semblance, but her eyes aren't glowing in that way."

Yet, what would he call that, beside Aura?

Selvaria strode forward, and swept the lance to the side. "Witness the flames of Valkyrur, a far cry from your pathetic imitation. I am Selvaria Bles, the one true Valkyria of this world. His Highness has no need of another!"

Boundless pride colored her tone, red eyes alight with conviction. The words reverberated with a supernatural timbre that carried over the distance. Wisps of blue fire flickered and danced upon her body, gravity defied as her hair adopted a life of their own to float on the wind. The rapturous sight of this angel of battle brought soldiers to their knees, prayers springing to their lips.

"…Pft. Daddy issues." Tattletale couldn't quite hide the shakiness of her voice beneath the attempt at humor.

"I think it's more complicated than that, Lisa. She's no joke."

He got the feeling that it was him, instead, who would be the punchline.

And when Selvaria zipped across the space between them, swinging the lance, Jaune learned how right he was. The lance smashed into his shield, and he might as well have done nothing at all. It blew him off the ground, sending him skipping across the road, leaving cracks on the pavement along the way until he hit a building. His back slammed against the wall, and Jaune saw stars.

"Holy crap, Jaune, are you okay!?" Tattletale yelped. Her head poked over the edge of the building.

Woozy, Jaune waved up to her.

"Aright, okay, this is a bit of a pickle, but you got this," Tattletale spoke at a fast pace. "She's a couple notches higher on the Brute scale than you. Aura on crack, basically, and we can add enhanced speed to that strength. That lance survived a launch that buried it in the ground without a scratch, the material isn't normal for the current level of industry here—harder than titanium. Uh… the more I think about it, the more it sounds like a bad idea to face her in a fight."

Tock. Tock. Tock.

Jaune raised his head at the sound, and sighed. "But I don't have a choice, do I?"

Tattletale didn't answer, which said enough. With what they knew now, the superweapon was never the Batomys, but this person before him. If he won't fight her, she could well turn that strength onto Yuell.

The woman was in no hurry, striding toward him with graceful steps.

"I do not know what you are," she said, a cold smile rising, "but you are not what he seeks. This world cannot change with your pitiful strength. Now begins your second test, although I hold no expectations."

Thwack!

A boomerang smacked her on the nose. In its wake, the world took a pause, with Selvaria and Jaune staring in confusion at the piece of wood clattering to the ground. Slowly, they turned their heads.

Escha, squatting on all fours, blinked innocently back at them. Selvaria scanned the area around the felyne, then peered at her in suspicion. A few seconds went by in silence.

Finally, Escha's facade cracked, and she stuck out her tongue. The felyne then dashed away to hide behind some rubble. It brought a smile to Jaune's face. With a groan, he pushed to stand upright.

If a cat could fight this 'Valkyria', then he could, too. Besides, for all that she received a power-up…

A blue beam of light slammed into Selvaria, fired from a roof.

…it was him who had help.

The Gauss rifle shot had struck Selvaria on her lance arm, eliciting a grimace from the woman but otherwise failing to dislodge her weapon. Next were Walter and his team of lancers, rockets blasting off their lances in a salvo that would have sent a tank sky high.

Turning on her heels, Selvaria let two of the rockets pass. It put her in the path of the rest. She caught the first on her shield, and the explosion couldn't even rock her back a single step. Her lance slapped the other rocket aside, directing it behind her where it detonated on the road.

Cries of disbelief passed along the Gallian line. Up on his tank, Welkin Gunther cut through the uproar with a sharp command, reasserting order. The soldiers, Militia and Yuell garrison, lifted their weapons, and peppered Selvaria with gunfire.

Selvaria hunched slightly behind her shield, and the bullets ricocheted off the glowing metal to no effect.

"Add bullet-resistant to the list!" Tattletale cursed. "Kinetic absorption on the shield? What kind of cheating bull—"

Jaune cut her off. "Give me something, Lisa. Anything."

"You make it sound so easy," Tattletale whined, mimicking his words earlier. She took a deep breath, and the uncertainty faded. "Buy me time."

"Got it~"

Jaune lifted his gunlance, and fired a shell. Red Rook was never meant for that distance, but his marksmanship made up the shortfall. Fire bloomed on Selvaria's shield.

Like the lance rockets, the shell did not manage much. It need not do more than distract her from the Gallian troops, and give him an opening. His boots carried him across the street, and as the smoke faded, Selvaria found him within her range. The gunlance traced an arc over his head, crashing down on her with all the strength he could muster.

It struck her shield, and stopped cold.

Jaune stared into red eyes. "Uh…"

This might have been a mistake.

Selvaria spun, dragging her lance in a circle and swinging for him. He caught it on his own shield. For a brief instant, he thought it would be okay. He could handle it, he could deal. Then, his arms buckled under the force of the blow, and Jaune was lifted off of his feet entirely. The Valkyria angled the weapon down to pound him into the ground. His Rathalos armor encased him just before impact.

Wham!

His face met the ground, and had barely raised his body when she slapped the lance down again. The pavement cracked beneath him, driving an imprint of him into the earth.

"This, is a taste of the power you lack."

No, it was dirt. Jaune spat out a mouthful through the gap in his visorplate.

Something furry and white entered his view, pressed against the road and shuffling stealthily along. Escha leapt for Selvaria from a blindspot, latching onto the woman's back with her claws, jaw clamped on a mouthful of the long, silver hair and pulling with all her might. The blue flames neither burned nor harmed, akin to Aura in how it lacked heat.

With a startled yelp that cracked her cool image, Selvaria shook her hair to try and dislodge the unseen thing on her back, then dropped her shield in order to reach around. Jaune dove for the shield, and Selvaria kicked him back. Seizing Escha by the scruff of her neck, the woman threw the yowling felyne away. Flipping end over end, Escha landed on her feet, drawing her boomerang.

Jaune coordinated with her, attacking from opposite sides. Pulling out Selvaria's rifle, Jaune aimed the gun at the woman, firing off a burst. The stream of bullets lacked the kick he expected, and he did not feel the pull of 'marksmanship' as hard as on other occasions—the shot maintained a tight grouping throughout, accurate to an astounding degree. A boomerang flew in an arc.

A shift of her stance, and the lance hid Selvaria's body behind its bulk, the bullets tinkling on the hard metal. At the same time, she hooked her foot under the shield and flicked it up to block the boomerang.

Jaune swapped for his gunlance, and Escha drew her sword. Roaring a battlecry, they rushed at their foe.

Selvaria smacked Escha down, then blocked Jaune's lance with her own. As Escha bounced off the cobblestone, the Valkyria caught her with a kick that sent her sailing down the street, before punching Jaune with her shield, snapping his head back. As he recovered, he saw her lance performing an overhead swing.

A premonition flashed across his mind. He really did not want to eat another mouthful of dirt.

Vanishing his weapons, Jaune threw out his hand, launching a shadowy arm that pulled him out of range. He rolled on the ground, catching his balance and springing up. He turned to face Selvaria.

Who was right there in front of him.

Cursing, he rearmed, stabbing his lance at her. It screeched off the shield, and her counterattack came screaming for his face.

A blast of his rocket boots propelled him above her. A blur passed him by, her red eyes meeting his blue. He turned his head, and she was the one above now.

Jaune twisted his foot, and a burst of rocket fire moved him to the side. The lance swept past his face, missing by inches. Instead, it was the shield that punched him in the gut, sending him slamming into the dirt again. Her knees collided with his chest bearing all her momentum, the force blanking his mind.

Disoriented, he looked through a haze at the woman above him. Her long hair draped down to cover up the world, leaving only them.

"I want that lance," Jaune breathed out.

"Yours is intriguing in its own way," she murmured. "I will take it from your corpse. A fitting end for the one to steal my Ruhm."

He searched his scrambled thoughts for what she could mean. "The rifle?"

By an unknown mechanism, her shield started to spin. Slow at first, then faster and faster until it revved like a sawblade.

"It was a gift to me from His Highness. A precious memento."

Uh-oh.

"Can I bribe you with it?" he asked hopefully.

Her head tilted as she looked at him. "To joke in these circumstances, you are a curious one. And the manner in which you fight… A false Valkyria you may be, but in your own way, it seems you too were born for this place."

Was that praise, or damning judgment? He was not happy to hear it, for what it implied.

A harsh voice cut into the conversation. "No, he was born for the kitchen, cooking up crepes. Say hello, bitch."

A tank shell impacted Selvaria on the side to throw her into the distance.

Jaune raised his head to watch her bounce on the cobblestone much like he did earlier. His heart swelled with warmth at the sight. It served her right for kicking his butt up and down the block. Gunfire poured down on her position from the Gallians.

Escha rushed over to him, an energy potion pulled out from who knew where. She offered it up for him to drink, revitalizing him.

"Good timing, Lisa," he spoke into the phone. "Thanks."

"Thank Gunther. He's got a good gunner in that tank. A little lower and it would have been you to get hit."

His face paled. "Tell him to let his sister know she did a good job, and for her to never do that again."

Tock. Tock. Tock.

That sound snuck past the roaring battlefield to reach Jaune's ears, and as if drawn by a spell, his head moved in a stiff, jerky motion to a point down the road.

Out of the fires and smoke left from the tank shell strode Selvaria, clothes ruffled and her pale skin scratched up but otherwise showing no signs of distress.

"Holy hell, I don't think even I could walk that off," Jaune said in a stupor.

"Blow this, you have to retreat," Tattletale decided without hesitation. "You, Escha, the entire Gallian force. Evacuate the city if you have to, and we'll figure a different avenue of attack. This is like fighting Alexandria. You just don't."

There was a sharp intake of breath over the line.

"What is she doing?"

Selvaria had stopped in the middle of the road, lance pointed before her. Something was off about that lance, a shimmering effect that—

It was spinning. That was what he was seeing, the weapon revolving in the manner of a drill. Blue flames materialized out of thin air, swirling up and down the length of the lance, the effect accelerating over time.

"She's aiming at you. It's an attack and she's aiming at you. Jaune, get in the air, now!"

The panic in her voice brooked no questions. Heeding her, Jaune shot into the sky. The lance rose to follow. The flames surrounding it soon coalesced into an inferno.

With a thrust of the lance, Selvaria launched her attack.

It sounded like thunder. That was Jaune's thought as blue flames washed over his vision. Thunder, and a lightning bolt going the wrong way. Angled up, the beam of blue fire struck the top of a building, and seared through it like nothing was there to pierce the sky, the walls and floors flattened in its wake. The structures to either side buckled from the pressure alone, the windows blown out and roofs crumbling.

The beam glanced by Jaune, never even touched him, and yet it whipped him around. Around and around until he couldn't tell up or down, rattling him within his armor to point he was ready to puke. A hard impact on his back knocked the breath from his lungs.

As his vision returned, Jaune came to half-buried in the side of a building, overlooking the street where he fought Selvaria. From Tattletale and Marina curled up on a roof to the Gallian soldiers lying prone to Escha sitting on the ground after her legs gave out, utter silence greeted the woman who stood down the road. A ring of scorchmark decorated the pavement beneath her feet.

One by one, the scared mortals peeked out from behind their hands to behold the monster among them. Their hearts were leaping from their chest, the animal part of their brains screeching for them to run. Others held their guns in shaking grips, struggling to level it at the threat that must be killed now, now, now.

And then Selvaria began charging up her lance again.

For one terror-stricken moment, Jaune searched frantically for his escape route, but he had it wrong. His heart sank like a stone as he realized where she was aiming. The center of the Gallian line.

Pandemonium reigned. The tank treads of the Edelweiss screamed as it tried to adjust course. Garrison and Militia troops dove for the nearest rubble and divots on the road in the hope that it would shield them, with too many caught out in the open. Jaune's eyes zeroed in on the little white figure among them.

Tattletale tried to say something, but he was already in the path of Selvaria's lance before she got the second word out. Jaune summoned both his shields and slammed them against the ground, digging into the road to help it hold. Escha took shelter there a moment later, with Walter, Corporal Rosie, and a mishmash of their people piling in behind Jaune, desperate for anything to stand between them and the Valkyria.

One certainty gripped him, it wouldn't be enough. That attack had blown apart a building. He would not hold for long.

A split second lasted an eternity, and a dozen different avenues of thought ran amok. All solutions were discarded, for there were none—it was a foregone thing. The best he could do was to stack the deck.

The adventurer card appeared between his fingers. He fumbled to grab it tight.

His Level according to it had skyrocketed in the weeks he spent in this world, the skill points racking up as a result. He had been saving them, waiting for an ability that wowed him. There was another aspect to those skill points. The possibility existed to increase one's attributes.

He had fantasized of nigh magical powers, to split a bullet into ten or run upon the falling leaves, but they wouldn't grant his wish. Then and now, what he wanted was only this.

His fingers smashed on the Strength and Vitality stats. The numbers began to scroll higher, faster and faster as he threw into them all he had accumulated so that he may hold back the world which desired for him and his to die. As the final skill point slammed into place, he released a shaky breath.

It had to be enough.

He looked at the spiraling beam heading for him. His eyes flicked below, to the shivering Escha burying her face into his shirt. Glanced behind, to the hands pressed on his back belonging to those he led into this battle.

It wouldn't be enough.

He curled down over Escha to better cover her, and braced.

It wouldn't be enough, but it had to be enough.

Jaune did not know the reason why, when he closed his eyes, he dreamed of Sundancer.
