Chapter 51: Valkyria, Valkyria​

It had begun as a steady rhythm. Thump. Thump. Thump.

His world fell silent but for that sound. In the space between the heartbeats, memories emerged. An autumn forest encircled him, and skyscrapers rose to the sky. The details may change, but he had stood here before.

There then came a distant roar from far away. Louder, louder it grew and that, too, he recognized. It was the world that would not wait for him to grow into a hero, to leave him with a choice to be made now. His friend, or himself.

Why did the roads he walked always seemed to lead back to the same moment? Like a story playing again and again, waiting for the ending in which he breaks.

"You saved me."

He did not want to see their story end. He never believed in destiny.

He had to be good enough. Thump. Thump. Thump.

A burst of invigoration soothed his weary limbs. Warmth pulsed in his veins. Jaune raised his head, and opened his eyes to stare into the blue flames. He was already set afire, glowing from within.

The spiraling missile struck the shields, light crashing into light, and it encountered a wall it could not pierce through. Harder it pressed, yet, as his back bent and his bones creaked, Jaune shoved against the near physical flames to keep the barriers standing and he found the world rearing back. As the balance see-sawed, the lance of light almost but never quite able to overwhelm him, he pulled on the mysterious well of energy he could sense at the edge of consciousness and his stance firmed, the roiling heat just a little more bearable, and in that place he held.

Without anywhere to go, the missile bloomed into a flower upon his shields, petals of blue fire unfolding in every direction. They seethed with a violent rage, scattering across the area to burn at whatever they could even as they dissipated with the passing moments. Screams and cries arose, but Jaune did not dare turn to look.

Then, he felt the balance tip back the other way. His shields shifted as the pressure assailing them began to dim. Singed and beaten from the abuse, they remained steadfast as he seized the momentum and rose up to slam a foot forward.

His arms strained, and with a shout Jaune batted aside the remnants of the beam. Behind her blue flame, Selvaria Bles stood with lance held aloft. Her red eyes slowly widened as she recognized his form.

Jaune had no time for her. His gaze lowered to the quaking bundle of fluff clinging onto him with all four paws, her face buried in his shirt.

"Escha! Are you okay!?" he cried.

Upon hearing him, the felyne cracked one eye open. Her head then snapped up, turning every which way before she looked at him.

"I'm… I'm alright?" she said. Then, louder. "I'm alright!"

There were voices behind him, elated and half-disbelieving shouts. His ears pricked up, attempting to pick them apart to search for the people he knew—looking meant seeing those whose voices he would no longer hear. The babble made it an impossible task. He heard his name pass from person to person, spoken in the mirror tone of a hushed stupor. It swept across the avenue.

Escha continued to stare at him, blinking. She started to reach for his face. "Jaune, Jaune, your eyes are glowing! They're so pretty!"

Glowing? His eyes?

Jaune drew a sharp breath. He knew of one thing that could mean.

A Semblance.

No sooner had he put a word to it, that the well of energy coalesced to settle at the back of his mind. A part of him that had always been there hidden by the thinnest veneer, it no longer faded away now acknowledged at last.

He did not get the chance to dwell on it. An echoing whisper carried across the length of the street.

"How?"

Selvaria looked unwell, a shiver wracking her body and her gaze jumping from place to place. Those mesmerizing eyes found him again.

"That power. That radiance. Are you truly a…? But then that would make them the same, and that's not possible!"

She sounded rather lost, with a trace of plaintiveness that she struggled to hide. The cold demeanor was nowhere to be found.

"You cannot all be Valkyria!"

Jaune and Escha looked at her, then at each other. The gears in their heads took a while to turn—they weren't the thinker in the group. Still, the two of them got there in the end. As one, they peeked over Jaune's shoulder.

The scene was a far cry from what he dreaded to find. Selvaria's attack had been weakened after smashing against him, but it had wreaked indiscriminate havoc at the end. His people, he had confidence in their odds. On the other hand, Squad 7 would have suffered the brunt of it.

And yet, the only bodies to suffer the blue flames wore the armor of the Empire, already dead from their clash with the Gallians and now burning to a crisp. Between these figures, three dozen or so garrison members and Squad 7 soldiers were staggering to their feet. They bore scorchmarks, with a fair number hugging themselves for comfort after having stared death in the face, but they were alive. Every single one.

Had he protected them, as he did Escha? No.

They carried a light about them. Many were flickering, pushed to the limit. A few burned bright. It was an unmistakable sight. In every hue, the Gallians shone with the colors of Aura.

Some, he had a hand in. Walter, Mica, and the others from Yuell who fought alongside him. Tattletale would have torn into him had she ever thought to inspect his troops in person, but it was how they could weather weeks of battle and walk off falling debris.

Those from Squad 7, however, he never awakened their souls.

Well, that wasn't quite right. He had done it for one.

The Edelweiss sat further back. It dodged the worst of the blue flames, which still resulted in the threads on one side melting into the road, turning it into a sitting duck. The lieutenant, Welkin, was kneeling above the hatch with a hand reaching down to help another figure climb out. Jaune zeroed in on that girl, Isara Gunther. The only possibility to explain what had occurred.

How in the world had she figured it out?

"No, you… you are fakes," Selvaria reassured herself, despite the uncertainty in her voice. She straightened her back and firmed her stance, finding comfort in discipline. "You are playing a trick. These are not the flames of Valkyrur!"

From Jaune's phone, a voice called out, shouting so Selvaria would catch it. "Different circumstances lead to different evolutions. Duh. Who made you the authority on what can and can't happen?"

"I am a Valkyria!"

Jaune had a choice between the simple truth, or a big, bold-faced lie.

"And so are we," he said.

A silence ensued in which he could feel the looks of all his allies within earshot on him, including the cat, asking his game. There was a goal here somewhere, but if pressed, he would admit that he was still working on it.

Selvaria shook her head in denial, opening and closing her mouth yet unable to dismiss his claim outright. It was punctuated by a little voice murmuring over the phone.

"Oho."

The ground cracked as Selvaria pushed off with one foot, clearing the space between him and her in a single bound. With a powerful cry, she swung her lance.

Escha darted away, and Jaune raised his mechashift shield.

Her blow, when it landed, was still heavy. Oh so heavy. His knees bent under the force, his arm holding the shield turning numb upon impact. This time, however, he held her there, giving not another inch. Tapping into his Semblance, a surge of strength filled his arms, amplifying the effect from his increased attributes and amplified in turn by the bone charm he attained so long ago.

He rebuffed the lance and manifested his own. Pivoting, he slammed Red Rook into Selvaria.

Earlier, the attack would have done little to nothing. Now, her heels screeched along the road, scraping lines in the ground. Selvaria stared down at her lance as if it had betrayed her.

"Oho?" he said to his phone in the aftermath. "She's flipping out. I messed up!"

"No, this is good. What you said affected her. All of you need to get back in there. Fight her!"

"Bwah?" he replied, suavely. "Pardon me, miss?"

"It's the best hope for us to not get slaughtered. We can't give her free rein to use that laser again. Stick to her like glue."

Selvaria had taken a guarded stance, her eyes locked onto him. Unlike before, she studied him with care, hesitant to open an exchange. In turn, Jaune watched her warily, resting his gunlance on a shoulder with his shield held in front of his body.

A closer look at the shield half of Crocea Mors, and Jaune swapped it with the Red Rook version, which had fared better under the heat.

"Tattletale, what are my odds here?"

"...Good."

He couldn't tell if she was speaking the truth.

Tattletale listened to his silence, and added, "That woman is all brawn and no technique with that lance. She hasn't had it long, days at most, and wields it in the style of a fencer."

"Her experience is with the saber," Jaune mused.

"Exactly. She isn't using it to its fullest potential. What you did to block her laser beam looks like how you described Semblances to me. Can you do it again?"

"I can. Easy-peasy." Now that he understood what to look for, the process became almost dead simple. He just had to really want it. From time to time, the connection to his Semblance pulled away from him, seeming to fall asleep. A mental tug, and it would soon respond.

"Then you aren't hopeless here. Go hit her for me."

Jaune took a deep breath and exhaled, mustering his nerves. Selvaria Bles was Death in high heels, and his best idea to defeat her right now revolved around hitting her harder. Tattletale seemed to have an inkling of a plan forming, though, and he could only trust that she knew what she was talking about.

Huh. All of a sudden, he was feeling a whole lot worse.

Ah well, nothing for it, then.

His rocket boots activated, and Jaune kicked forward to skim along the road. He stayed at a slow speed at first. Then, as he approached within range of Selvaria, he shot ahead.

Instantly, Selvaria struck out with a thrust to his chest. The lance hit his shield, deflecting on an angle off the Rathalos scales. Jaune spun with the motion to get even closer, planting his foot and pushing with his shoulder to slap the gunlance resting on it down on his opponent. Her shield nullified the impact.

For a brief time, their faces were inches apart.

"How did you become stronger?" she asked him.

"Didn't I just say? I'm like you," Jaune replied with a small, sly smile, barely visible through the gap in his helmet. Selvaria caught it, and he watched as she was torn between a reply and an attack.

The moment broke as Escha landed on his shoulder, and used it as a springboard to leap for Selvaria. A shield bash flipped the cat into the air, Selvaria arcing her lance upward in order to impale Escha on the tip.

The felyne howled in pain, yet no blood was drawn. A shimmer of light, more pink than white, prevented the lance from piercing through.

Selvaria gawked at the sight. It could have passed beneath notice before, but presented with the possibility that all the people facing her were Valkyria, she now had to entertain the thought that the cat was one, too.

That opening allowed Jaune to crack her on the chin with his shield. Her head snapped back, the incredulity still evident in her expression. She recovered quickly and, with a flip, cleared some space between them, while he stayed to catch Escha before she hit the ground.

"You're willing to kill a cat?" he spat at Selvaria, soothing Escha with pets.

"That cat was willing to kill me."

Jaune cocked an eyebrow, and Selvaria paused as that statement caught up to her. The barest grimace passed over her face, thereafter shoved deep below the surface.

"You are trying to disturb me," she accused as her chilly demeanor made its return.

"As if that's hard at all," Tattletale chimed in, her tone mocking. "Torturing small animals and slaughtering innocent people are the kind of things someone already utterly unhinged would consider. That prince sure did a number on you."

Crude and provocative, the harsh indictment was meant to get a rise out of Selvaria. Her best move would have been to let it pass. The little hooks Tattletale set within those words made that impossible.

"Do not speak of what you do not understand," snapped Selvaria, emotions bubbling up again. Without the culprit here to vent her ire on, she launched at Jaune to pummel him with her lance, a one-two combo to hammer on his defenses, knocking him off his balance. Blue flames began to swirl around her lance.

[Third Arm] shot for her face, blinding her and pulling him in close. Jaune's eyes shone white, and he shoulder-checked the lance to shove it off course, the unyielding strength in Selvaria's arm meeting its match.

Right on cue, Tattletale spoke. "Don't I? I bet I understand him more than you ever did."

The lance fired a beam that blasted another building to pieces. At the same time, the shadows over her eyes dispelled, letting Selvaria see Jaune rearing back. An instant later, his helmet met her forehead.

Despite the layers of protection stacking one atop another, pain bloomed to blind him—he had done it with those in mind. Jaune stumbled over the cobblestone away from Selvaria, expecting a retaliation that never came, instead hearing the sound of her high heels clicking as she staggered a couple of steps in the opposite direction. That blow had probably contained enough force to turn a Beowolf to paste on impact, and seemed to have surpassed the Valkyria's ridiculous damage tolerance.

"It's working!" Tattletale cheered.

"Yaaaay," he deadpanned, still seeing stars. "Why are you winding her up even more?"

She lowered her voice to let no one else hear.

"Selvaria is scared. Jealous. Bit of one, bit of the other. On some levels, she understands that her status as the 'true' Valkyria is important to her prince charming, and he's her whole world. You've rattled her by proving your power. I'm pushing that further."

"Okay, what does that mean?"

"I've seen that kind of girl before. They're held up by pillars. Give a knock to their worldview, and they break. Now hit her with all we got while she's distracted!"

…Were they the bad guys, here?

A sensation of deep unease made itself known, but he stamped it down. His partner had a brilliant plan, he was sure.

Heeding her, he fired a gunlance shell. Too late, Selvaria had the awareness to read the angle and dodged right as he pulled the trigger; it sailed over her to smash through a window. A blue beam sliced across her shoulder before she could recover, burning away the fabric to sear the flesh beneath. The damage looked more akin to a bad sunburn than what a laser should have done to a person, and had already begun to heal, but the hiss of pain (or was it discomfort?) was heard by everyone. She had felt it.

Gunfire erupted on her, providing Jaune the chance to close in. He whispered instructions to Tattletale, and as the bullets ceased, he bashed Selvaria's shield with his lance and fired off another shell that made a lot of noise and not much else. All the momentum seemed to blink out of existence as it encountered that metal disc. Selvaria lashed out with a kick.

"Incoming," a tinny voice informed him.

Rather than avoiding it, Jaune accepted the attack. He laughed as the high heels slammed into his hardy frame, because he felt to his bones the certainty that he could have stood his ground. It didn't hurt so bad, was his thought, except the situation called for him to roll with it, so he fell limp to let Selvaria send him rocketing back.

A good trade for the grenades bouncing past his flying figure. They detonated to saturate the Valkyria with shrapnel, interrupting her pursuit of him. Her shield could not block from every direction, forcing her to weather the damage as Jaune landed a distance away.

Her clothes, anyway. The flecks of metals bounced off her flesh, unable to mar her pristine pale skin beyond little dots of blood that healed over as they occurred. The military uniform enjoyed no such ability and developed great, rending tears.

Selvaria looked down at herself, taking in her state of …well, Jaune wouldn't say dress by this point, more the opposite… then up at him. Her eyes narrowed to slits.

Jaune gave a nervous chuckle, and braced for impact.

"Selvaria!" a voice interrupted them.

Welkin Gunther knelt on the hull of his tank. In his hand, he held a megaphone. Jaune had to wonder what was going on in his head. A tank commander of an abandoned tank should probably be booking it for safety.

"Selvaria!" Welkin repeated, his voice amplified by the device. "Must we fight?"

Jaune glanced down at his lance, and he'd bet anything Selvaria was doing the same, with both of them reaching an answer along the line of 'Uhhhh, yes'.

And on that note…

He rushed in, baiting an attack. The instant her lance moved, he dropped and launched [Third Arm] to zip across the ground, ending up behind Selvaria in a blink. Red Rook swapped for Crocea Mors, and he stabbed the sword with both hands into her back.

Her power deviated from Aura in the small details. The shrapnel from the grenades had come in contact with her flesh rather than the barrier of blue flames surrounding her form. His blade encountered the same, a body durable to an enviable degree yet still yielding in a manner that he wouldn't be with his Aura. With the right amount of force concentrated at a sharpened point, the tip of his sword pierced through.

His reward was a soft grunt, followed by the blade stopping short. Selvaria tilted her head to look over her shoulder with one eye.

"An admirable attempt," she murmured. The inch or so of his sword inside her slowly slid out, pushed by the wound knitting together.

"So unfair…" he whined.

Her shield snapped around, clocking him in the face. He grinned and bear it, not even rocking back, eyes shining within the depths of his helmet. Selvaria pursed her lips.

All the while, Welkin continued on.

"We didn't ask for this war!" he said. "We were happy to live in peace. Happy to trade and learn and live alongside the Federation and the Empire. It couldn't have brought you joy to burn our homes to the ground! I refuse to believe it!"

Selvaria glanced at the lieutenant and scoffed. She twirled, and her lance swept in an overhead arc to hammer down on Jaune.

"Does he think that I am not aware of my actions?" she asked, pulling away then dashing right back in with a stab that he diverted to impale the ground. "I have fought in the name of my prince for half a decade. A great cause demands sacrifices."

She used the stuck lance as leverage, vaulting over it to kick at him with both feet. He thwarted the blow, and Selvaria spun her body around the polearm to return to her previous place, yanking the weapon out of the ground as Jaune advanced on her. Their lances clashed together.

"And I bet the people who cut you up said that same exact line," Tattletale commented.

In Jaune's mind, the pieces clicked into place. He thought Welkin was acting oddly. The words may be Gunther's own, but behind them he sensed the hand of Tattletale. Platitudes to tease out responses for the supervillainess to work with.

"They can never hurt me again," was Selvaria's simple reply.

"That's… interesting. You're absolutely certain of it. Where is that confidence coming from?" Tattletale then answered her own question. "Your prince must have told you that."

"And he would never lie to me."

Tattletale's mocking laughter answered her.

Selvaria's lance suddenly whirled, revving up like a drill to grind against Red Rook and almost ripping the weapon from Jaune's hands. He threw the gunlance in his Pocket, trading for his sword.

Before he could act, the pommel of Selvaria's lance whipped up to clip him under the chin. Jaune saw the sky.

The rifle Ruhm filled his hands as he staggered backward. He needn't aim—Selvaria could only be in front of him. He held the trigger, blasting her at point-blank range until the gun clicked empty, swapping to the shield as he detected her perfume.

Her knee clanged against the hard Rathalos scales in the next moment. A flash of light, and all her forward motion stopped cold. The follow-up hit with her lance lacked the distance it needed, with Jaune shifting his stance to block it at her elbow. He then seized her collars with a now empty hand and swung her over his head to slam her against the road.

His foot stomped on her chest, blasting her with a gout of rocket exhaust. He pressed down as she thrashed about, trying to prolong the attack.

"Incoming," Tattletale warned. He took to the sky.

A tank shell impacted the area to consume it in an explosion, fired from an Edelweiss that turned out to not have been abandoned after all. Lasgun beams poured into the obscuring smoke, hoping to hit Selvaria while she was down.

The tank turret swung its cannon back and forth in a wave to him, a gesture Jaune returned.

The reprieve ended with Selvaria shooting out of the smoke as a blur, and Jaune paled as instead of reengaging him, she raced across the ground on a course for the Gallians supporting him. Plunging from the sky, he intercepted her, summoning his sword and whipping out in a wild swing—

It was a trap.

Tock.

She vanished from his sight. Locks of silvery hair brushed his cheek.

Tock.

Jaune spun toward the sound to find she had pivoted hard in his direction, punching at him with her shield. He received the hit in order to catch her with a stab. The blade whiffed empty air, Selvaria ducking under the blow to sweep out his legs.

Tock.

As she straightened, one of her heels bounced off the cobblestone to kick up high in a vertical split that displayed her long, long legs. It dropped with the deadliness of a guillotine, and Jaune ate dirt, Semblance activating to nullify the impact. He scrambled to get on his feet, tensing for an imminent blow.

In a strange turn, she did not press the advantage. By the time Jaune recovered, he saw why. Selvaria was rampaging among the Gallians.

A casual swipe of her lance blew three soldiers off their feet, throwing them into a wall clear on the other side of the street. A second blow slapped two more out of her way. The Edelweiss sat in her path.

Welkin jumped down to put himself between her and the tank, and the person inside, both arms spread wide and his Aura shining a deep blue. Selvaria's lance speared through the air without a hint of mercy, spinning like a drillhead. A moment before impact, the lieutenant squeezed his eyes shut.

A meowing bundle of ferocious felyne hit Selvaria in the face, pulling hair and scratching at her eyes to distract her for Jaune to move into the gap between Welkin and the lance. The weapon drove into his chest as he reached for the well of energy resting within him. It stuttered, but obeyed, and he was pushed barely a step.

Corporal Rosie slid over the hull of the tank, and shoved the barrel of her machine gun next to Jaune, his shoulder a platform to steady her aim.

"Escha, withdraw," Tattletale ordered, and Jaune had a split second to curse before the corporal fired at close range on Selvaria, each shot booming in his ear. Welkin added to it, drawing his sidearm to shoot by his other ear.

The noise level alone managed to ping his Aura. Jaune had to weather it, contributing by latching onto the lance with both arms to hold Selvaria in place, the rotations of the weapon meeting his gauntlets, metal screeching on metal. She lifted the weapon, and him along with it, whipping around to crush him into the road, her shield coming up to block the soldiers.

"Let go!" she spat.

"Does that ever work?" Jaune spat right back, trying to angle his foot to shoot fire at her. He would have said more, but Tattletale decided to cut in. Her snide tone had lessened, forgotten as she spoke in a rush.

"You don't realize what that prince is doing to you, do you, Selvaria?"

Selvaria paused. She glared at the spot of Jaune's armor behind which the phone hid, at the base of his throat.

Jaune almost felt sorry for her. Tattletale knew the buttons to press to make someone want to listen just a little bit longer. The lance pressed down harder on him.

"It's all there in how you act and talk about him. The classic brainwashed victim behavior."

"Silence!" Selvaria commanded. "You know nothing!"

Behind his helmet, Jaune rolled his eyes.

Oh, yes. That would certainly calm Tattletale down.

"Really?" Tattletale snarled (as expected). "Because I can tell a stupid little girl when I see one. Let's see if this sounds familiar. You were a child, forced to show your amazing abilities on command everyday like a dog by faceless men as they try to harness your powers. Did they want to steal it? Sell it?"

The grip Selvaria had on the handle of her weapon tightened until they creaked.

"Who did they work for? A secret cabal? The government? Some greedy criminal who dreamed of being a bigshot? You had absolute faith that the prince could protect you from them. They worked for the Empire."

Jaune's eyes narrowed in suspicion. "Selvaria… How did you meet the prince? Did he seek you out or the other way around?"

"Preeetty sure she was made on Maxie's order."

The lance rose up, and slammed back down. He hung on like a limpet. Undeterred, Selvaria did it again, and again and again to drive him deeper into the road each time. Bullets and lasers impacted her, ignored as her vision was reduced to her, Jaune, and the annoying voice on the line that just won't shut up.

"He liberated me! Of all the people in the world, it was him to save me, and I, to be saved. Do not befoul his kindness with your lies!"

"How, little girl? Did he storm the compound, sword in hand? Did he march at the head of an army?"

The silence was telling.

"Did he just walk in? What's a prince doing, gallivanting about a lab that experiments on humans? Listen, stupid. The people who know about that kind of place are usually the people involved in it!"

Wisps of blue flames alerted him to another laser beam charging up. He let go of the lance. His rockets activated, and he rammed into Selvaria, pushing them both away from the Gallians. They bounced and rolled along the road, fighting to control where the lance aimed its beam.

In the end, the blast ripped through the empty sky, and Selvaria growled in frustration. Hair disheveled, chest heaving, she laid on the ground, pinned under Jaune. For all her power, she was not so inhuman that she would not tire like the rest of them.

Or maybe it was Tattletale's unrelenting spiel all this while to blame. The safety of the phone allowed the girl free rein to speak, and with great relish did she spin a tale about a plan to deprive a young girl of any sense of happiness to the point that she was little better than an animal, all so that she would latch on to the first person that showed her regard. In her version of the story, Prince Maximilian transformed from a shining knight on a white horse to a mastermind, controlling every piece on the board to dance to his tune. It was his royal authority and coffers to establish the project, and that which cruel researchers obey. On that fateful day, an owner arrived to collect his trained pet.

"Bravo, little girl. Maxie led you by the nose. I'm almost impressed. That prince sure is a master at his game."

That last part was what Selvaria reacted to the most. Had Tattletale belittled the prince as a drooling infant, perhaps it would have been so much easier to dismiss. After all, it clashed hard with her admiration for him. In praising him, Tattletale raised the possibility that someone of his brilliant intellect could conceive of this plan.

"And now he has you killing the old and young, parents and children. Killing people just like you, the Valkyria. Slaughtering those that could have been your family."

That was his limit. Jaune snapped at his phone. "Lisa!"

"What? I'm just telling it how I see it. Because I refuse to blind myself to the truth in front of my eyes like that idiot. Don't say that you pity her, Jaune."

It was really hard not to when Tattletale was going at it with no brakes.

He lost much of that sympathy as Selvaria smacked him with her shield. Slipping out of his grasp, the woman surged past him to rush the others. He grabbed her long hair and yanked her back, an unyielding anchor that won't let her go. At this range, it was better to not hold weapons at all, and with a grip on her hair he pummeled her with a gauntleted fist while she wielded her cumbersome lance and shield.

His foot cut behind her high heel and he checked her with his shoulder, tripping her. She dragged him to the ground.

Skill went out the window, as did any sort of honor. Twice, Selvaria almost managed to stand up. Jaune kicked out her foot both times, then wound a leg around hers, bringing his Semblance to bear to lock it down. His helmet was gone, Selaria wedging her shield under his chin to rip it off. It had opened him up to a pommel strike aimed at his nose that smarted ever since, worsening as he smashed their faces together and Selvaria abandoned dignity to bite him.

Back and forth they went, bucking and throwing one another about. Neither of them could do more than disorient their opponent, hanging on in the hope that the other would run out of steam. From time to time, Escha darted into view to whack Selvaria with her felyne-sized sword, while striving her best to not accidentally do the same to Jaune.

Unerringly, Selvaria would return to a particular spot at the base of his throat, because Tattletale still refused to shut up. Anytime they thought she was done, she would have a little more to say.

"Is he watching you right now? Your big debut. He'll get a report of your pathetic performance, either way."

"He heard about a male Valkyria and immediately wanted to investigate. Maybe he thinks a man would be easier to control."

"Or maybe he just prefers men."

"You're replaceable!"

Selvaria's eyes opened wide, a mirror to his own. That last one had not come from the phone.

Along an empty stretch of the avenue, stood Tattletale. Looking like a girl from a well-to-do family, except for her voluminous militia jacket, she gave a jaunty wave with the hand holding her phone.

A growl emerged from the back of Selvaria's throat. It grew louder as the girl walked toward them, unhurried strides lending the image of a lady on a stroll.

Tattletale then screamed and dove to the side as a laser beam fired in her direction. Jaune got it to go wide, but evidently it was too close for comfort to the skittish girl.

"Jaune?" she asked through the phone, poking her head out of hiding.

"It's under control now." Barely. "No worries."

Reassured, she approached them.

Standing over the struggling pair, she studied them from head to toe. The smug grin she wore somewhat faded as time passed.

"Getting an eyeful of her, aren't cha?"

"Not"—he landed a punch, took a shield's edge to his temple—"the time, Tattletale. Should you really be here?"

She gasped theatrically. "Uh, yeah? I have to give our friend here the good news." She leaned down, hands on her hips, to look at Selvaria. "Hi there!"

Selvaria attempted to break free of his grip. He dropped an elbow on her, and she snapped out with another pommel strike to his nose. He definitely didn't tear up a little.

"Wow, you are just so… grrrr, girl!" Tattlate laughed. "I bet you never show your prince charming that face."

"Mock me now, but I will show you the errors of your ways. You have no means to defeat me that would not risk harm to this man. It is only a matter of time—"

"Until you will get the better of him? I wonder about that. Too bad we will never find out. Like I said, I brought good news." Tattletale squatted to sit on the balls of her feet. She mimed giving Selvaria taps on the nose, keeping a healthy distance to not risk getting hit. "The thing is, the battle is already over. Do you hear that?"

Jaune craned his ear. Now that they were not so concerned with beating the stuffing out of each other, he noticed the sound of a klaxon horn, unfamiliar in pitch. Interspersed within it were gunshots, but they were lacking the desperate rhythm of a two-sided firefight. He chanced a glance behind him.

Past the rubble of the fallen buildings separating them from the larger battlefield, the tip of a flag was waving back and forth. Its blue cloth billowed in the wind, a unicorn emblazoned at the center.

"It's amazing how narrow your view could get on the ground. The Batomys should have broken the city. You were supposed to defeat our Valkyria. Without either, the Imps are retreating." Tattletale grinned. "They're leaving you."

Selvaria could not see the flag, but she recognized the sound of the horn. She had a lost look on her face for a second before it smoothed out.

"As long as I am here, victory is assured." She gave a sudden thrash of her shoulder, attempting to turn the table on Jaune. He strained to hold her.

Tattletale really needed to get on with it, was his opinion.

"True, true. You're a weapon in your rights," Tattletale agreed as she slipped one hand inside her jacket to rummage around. She soon fished out a strip of metal. An innocuous thing, smooth and black, it looked harmless.

Its name sprang from the depths of his mind. He must have read the entry ten times before he took the plunge and bought one like it, way back when.


Inhibitor Collar

Universe: DC

Ancient Americans once said, "Everyone is equal."

Modern Amanda Waller says, "Challenge accepted."

Crafted with mundane yet unexplainable science, this marvel of plot device engineering cuts off access to abilities from a wide variety of sources, including metahumanism, magic, and alien biologies. Sleek, stylish, and trendy, each collar comes outfitted with an electric shock function, gratis.


All for the measly price of ten Points.

"We could just kill her," Jaune offered. Selvaria might even thank them. According to none other than Tattletale herself, the woman placed an inordinate pride on her power as a Valkyria.

Tattletale shook her head. Without another word, she approached, motioning for Jaune to hold his opponent still.

Despite not understanding what the device was, Selvaria sensed from their reaction that it was detrimental to her and she went ballistic, firing a laser then attempting to brain Tattletale with the lance. It took Jaune pulling on his Semblance to keep her from succeeding, with Escha piling on for what little good it did.

Tattletale waited on the sideline for him to reestablish a stalemate, and once she spotted an opportunity, she placed the device at the back of Selvaria's neck. The metal flowed over the pale skin to form a loop around her throat.

The blue aura, the 'flames of Valkyrur' Selvaria so treasured, winked out. Immediately, Jaune fell forward due to the abrupt shift in strength, almost squashing the woman under his frame. Selvaria's lance and shield crashed to the ground, too heavy for her to lift in her position.

She had a second to stare blankly at the sight, then it hit her.

"What have you done?" Selvaria whispered in muted horror. Then, a louder scream. "What did you do!?"

Only then did Tattletale reply to his earlier comment. "Oh, I'm sure there were kinder solutions we could have gone for. I had this whole plan to bluff her about us finding her prince and sending a hit squad to take him out to make her leave the city. But then, you decided to become Mr. Universe all of a sudden and managed to hold out against her." She shrugged. "The plan changed bit by bit after that."

She next moved towards the lance lying on the road.

"Whoof! This is heavy!" Tattletale gave up on lifting the whole thing, and just rotated it nearer to him. "Jaune, touch this for me?"

Getting the idea, he nudged it with a foot while Tattletale fiddled with the Company scroll. The girl studied the screen.

"Ooh, too bad, this is no good for you. The thing's a conduit for her Valkyria power. All the flashy stuff is locked to that."

With a tap, the lance vanished into thin air.

A choked gasp escaped from between Selvaria's lips. She stared at the spot where her weapon used to be, unable to form words.

Her will seemed to snap after the shield went the same way, and she slumped in a boneless heap.

Really, it might have been kinder to kill her.

"You can let her go, now," Tattletale suggested.

"Hah?" was his answer. Next to him, Escha frantically shook her head. Fighting Selvaria had been an experience.

"Let her go. Free her. Release your grips. Deliver her from her hunky shackles." Tattletale gestured at the catatonic woman. "She's not going anywhere in that state."

"...If she rushes for you, I expect you to put our training to use."

Tattletale scrunched her face at the thought of throwing hands. As if she was some sort of caveman.

Rising to his feet, Jaune waited for Selvaria to make a move. Escha scampered to a spot nearby, brandishing her sword.

Yet, the cool, dangerous woman wasn't there anymore. Her eyes have yet to stray from the empty patch of the road, as if willing for her weapon to come back.

"Like I told you, Jaune. I've seen her type before." Tattletale's grin sobered a touch.

"Was all that stuff you said true?" He asked. "The masterplan, beginning to end."

She tilted her head, tapping her chin with a finger. "A good half is guesswork, I suppose. Good guesswork, mind. I'm pretty certain about the prince manipulating her emotions." She sighed. "Honestly, I was hoping to drive a wedge between them that would turn her, but she was a stubborn one. That kind of indoctrination takes time to unwind. A large part of it has to come from the person themselves."

And Selvaria was just too loyal, the prince her world. Easier, to take the opportunity when she was preoccupied to end the battle.

"We could have done it," suggested Jaune. "Or you could, at least."

"You could, you could!" Escha agreed, believing wholeheartedly in the girl.

Tattletale leaned down to gush over Escha. "Aw, thanks for the vote of confidence, sweetie. Maybe you're right, and a seed is definitely planted in her head." Her gaze flicked up to him. "But I also had five artillery pieces trained on this location, and I trust that more. I had options and I just picked the best one available."

Jaune looked from her to the Selvaria that was close to tears, to her again.

She rolled her eyes, and reached up to pat him on the cheek. "She didn't factor into it. The best outcome was the one where you didn't die."

He turned his head. One hand came up to massage the smile away from his face. He shouldn't be that easy.

In the end, Selvaria Bles was an opponent without a simple answer. Had they the strength, they could have done it differently. Lacking that, they did what they could to survive. In fact…

"We have our win, don't we?" he said. "The Imps are routed, the supertank is super gone, and Selvaria is neutralized. The Gallian Army can't ignore Yuell now."

Tattletale gave a nod. "I'm getting Gunther and Landzaat to send out missives within the hour. I expect this place will be fortified to hell and back in the days ahead."

Yuell was safe.

Which meant his time here was coming to a close.

A fake cough interrupted his thoughts. Tattletale had read him like a book, and she gave him a mischievous grin.

"I doubt you're gonna be able to slink off in the night." She pointed behind him.

He faintly detected a rumble beneath his feet. Turning his head, he watched as his allies from Yuell garrison members to Squad 7 soldiers bore down on him, shouting in the triumph and joy of another day won.

A great cry passed from one person to the next, racing throughout all of Yuell. A name for him who brought them victory.

Valkyria.

#3,852
Chapter 52: A Farewell in June​


Night has fallen, but one would not think it. Lit by a thousand lamps, the university plaza resembled noontime, with the entire city of Yuell awake and present. A celebration was in full swing.

At first, the retreat of the Imperials had brought simple cheers. After scouts reported them pulling back from the region rather than just to the forest, that became a burgeoning hope. Then, when the mighty Valkyria of Yuell proclaimed that the Imperial advance had been broken, there arose what seemed like a great, deep sigh of relief to overtake the entire city. Nobody questioned him how he knew, and would never guess that all he did was take a jaunt down a certain alleyway to check for signs of reality beginning to glitch out. They accepted him at his word and called it divine revelation.

The wider war was not yet won, the losses were still to be mourned, but in that moment a crack formed in the wall around the people's hearts. Weeks of crisis had hardened them, nearly shattered them. Having made it through the other side, their emotions swelled in a tide and streamed out as a flood. Relief grew into jubilation, and resulted in a party the likes of which Yuell had never seen.

A big bonfire had been constructed on the university's front lawn as a matter of course because, apparently, it wouldn't be a festival without one around these parts. Propped on wooden posts, strings of lights crisscrossed overhead to further illuminate the grounds. A band, mixed between civilians and soldiers, had scrounged up musical instruments from the performing arts department. Parked right in front of the founder statue, they played a jaunty and upbeat tune, a 'modern' style that people could dance to. Swept up in the music, couples foxtrotted amidst the bomb craters.

Throughout the plaza, long tables were set up and they heaved under the weight of dishes stacked upon their surfaces. The food stores had been broken out with no thoughts given to tomorrow. For the simple fares, victory was a spice beyond compare. Some cried as they ate, with offerings made to those who would no longer share the table with them.

Amidst the festivities, a hooded figure skulked through the crowd. Along the way, he witnessed the smiles and the tears, passing those like little Hans and Greta sitting with their mother, the woman in good cheer but holding onto them as if fearing they would disappear. He walked behind a group of local garrison members, listening to a pessimistic Mica whining as the others ragged on him for spending his time at a party writing in a diary, with him insisting it was a manuscript. Near them, a crowd of young men clamored around a cooking station, raising a commotion about 'Alicia's homemade bread baked with love' or some such nonsense.

The hooded figure gave those men a wide berth. Same with the prostrating worshipers gathered in front of a makeshift shrine, with him flinching as one of them glanced his way. He pulled his hood low and walked faster, hoping that the great number of white-and-red themed clothing would obscure his own poncho.

His journey brought him to a table populated by Squad 7 and Yuell militia. Beer tankards littered its surface, testifying to a few rousing rounds of drinks already. Corporal Rosie and Sergeant Largo appeared to be competing on who can drink the most, with Walter the only local able to match pace. Upon spotting him, all three of them laughed at his manner of approach.

"Jaune, why do you look like a hunted man at your own party?" Walter asked. "Trouble with the missus?"

The drunken lot seemed to think that was quite a hoot, laughing harder.

"Yeah, yeah," Jaune grumbled, swiping a beer mug and sitting down. He downed a gulp before continuing, "I was hiding because it's getting too much. I couldn't go three steps without getting mobbed. People kept getting on their knees for me—"

Walter lowered the pair of shades he was wearing, cocking an eyebrow. Jaune smacked a hand to his own face.

"Not like that," he said into his palm. "It was the 'forehead to the ground, we're not worthy' sort. I think I started a religion." Judging from the looks these guys were now giving him, he most certainly did. "Everywhere I go, they're asking me for blessings and words of wisdom."

"Did you say anything?"

"Build a better wall." It had been the first thing to pop into his head. "Last I heard, they were chasing down the Militia engineers to press-gang them into helping."

"So that's where Karl disappeared to," muttered Rosie. "Poor bastard."

Jaune nodded, taking another sip of his drink. "People are being a teeny-tiny bit too zealous about this, so I figured it'd be easier on everybody if I keep a low profile." He eyed Rosie enviously as she ate from her plate. "How nice…"

The corporal hunched over the plate, covering it with a hand.

"Get your own, kid," she said through a mouthful of potatoes.

If only. With so many gathered over that way, he had to miss the food lines lest they recognize and swarm him again. His stomach growled at the sight of the others at the table relishing their meal.

Clack.

Jaune looked at the plate in front of him piled high with a little of everything, then turned his head to look up at the person who had put it there. Magari, the girl he often encountered working at the food distribution center, stood beside his chair, fidgeting from one foot to the other as she worried a finger around a lock of her dark hair.

"Is this for me?" he asked.

She nodded, her face flushing as their eyes met.

Jaune brightened. "Sweet. Thanks a lot!"

He grabbed a loaf of bread (crisp crust, almonds, baked with the patented Alicia love) and tore off a bite with his teeth, humming in happiness at the taste of warm, buttery goodness.

A little smile grew on Magari's face. Seeming emboldened, she rummaged inside a pouch she was carrying before bringing out an object that she also offered to him. It was a strip of cloth with beaded strings at either ends, and Jaune peered with interest at the distinctive pattern stitched into the fabric. The people at the table didn't bother to show any tact, crowding in for a better look.

"Reminds me of those charms the Darcsen like to wear," Walter said.

"Charm… like a good luck charm?" Jaune asked the girl, glancing at the hair ties she wore bearing the same pattern. Again, Magari nodded quickly at that.

Rosie scoffed. "It's just gonna give you bad luck—" She was interrupted by an elbow to her ribs courtesy of Largo, and turned away to drink her beer with a sour look as she noticed Jaune frowning hard at her.

If Magari took offense to the comment, the girl didn't let it show. She was more preoccupied with teaching Jaune how to tie the charm around his wrist as a bracelet.

"Really, thanks for this," Jaune said afterward.

He then looked down at his arm again, because Magari hadn't let go of his hand. There was a certain cast to her expression, terror warring with resolve. Just as he went to ask her what was wrong, she made her move. Magari swooped in, and planted a kiss on his cheek.

It lasted no more than a few seconds. Time enough to ensure the sensation of her warm, soft lips lingered in his memories. Then, she pulled away, and he had a fleeting glance of a bright red face and a beaming smile before Magari was racing off as fast as she could go. His eyes trailed after her, mouth parted in surprise, until she vanished among the crowd. In the background, Walter, Largo, plus the rest of their merry band were hooting and hollering, resembling nothing so much as a frenzied band of monkeys.

"…I still haven't gotten a single word out of her," he finally said.

"Shy types are the best," Walter said sagely as he slapped Jaune on the back. "I guess she heard about you setting out and wanted you to have something to remember her by." The man paused there, and coughed. "Which reminds me. I have a gift for you, too."

That broke Jaune out of his happy mood. "I'd rather not receive a kiss from you, thanks."

"You're dreaming if you think you're getting some of this," Walter snarked in turn. The man kicked back on his chair to reach for the next table over, swiping a bundle there and throwing it at Jaune.

He caught it and peered at the bundle with a curious eye, running a finger over the hardy fabric. Unfurling the thing revealed a Yuell militia field jacket, Gallian-blue. Less complicated than the ones worn by Squad 7, the jacket sported a unicorn's head emblem over the left breast as its sole decoration. He took it in for a moment before looking at Walter, feeling a lump rise in his throat. The man affected a nonchalant shrug, but could not quite hide the embarrassment on his face.

"Me and everybody got together and agreed that you should have one." Walter motioned to the others from the garrison. "We… Well, we know you have your colors, but you're one of us, so… yeah."

Jaune barked a laugh. He didn't correct the mistaken sentiment. Red and white were only his colors due to the people standing before him. Somewhere along the way, the Panacea poncho had become a symbol in their eyes. Who knows, he might look good in blue.

Off went the poncho, and he donned the jacket to whistles and applause. Rosie mentioned that civilians tend to find a uniform dashing, leading to many crying out in jest for Magari, wherever she was, to come back and give her opinion. That was soon forgotten as Jaune decided on the present he would give them, sweeping a hand over the table to deposit on it a cache of Spirytus and 'oolong tea', and the drinking games began to a roaring cheer. They will remember his sendoff as the party of the decade, or they won't remember it at all.

Once it got too crazy, he moved off to a nearby table to find a bit of peace. That was the plan, anyway.

Blank, gray eyes stared at him, and he stared back.

"Soooo…" He indicated with the hand holding his beer mug. "What the heck is that thing?"

That thing being the small pig that Marina Wulfstan was hugging in her arms. It wore a bell on a ribbon around its neck, meaning it was probably a pet. Fine and good, his neighbor back home had one. The part he had difficulty understanding was the pair of bird wings sprouting from its back.

"This is Hans, Private Third Class of Squad 7," Marina answered softly.

The questions just kept adding up.

"It has a rank?"

Marina nodded with a dead serious expression, leaving Jaune to rub his temples in the hope it would alleviate the budding headache. He turned to Escha, who was squatting on the table and munching on fried potatoes from a plate that Marina must have gotten for her. The felyne noticed his look, and she shrugged her little shoulders before going back to her meal. Of course the one that lived in a world with giant pickle-shape dinosaurs wouldn't see anything odd.

"Okay, cool. Cool means great. Anyway, you know what, I'm not going to even ask."

After all, he was the weird one around these parts. Ask somebody the chances of a person with nigh magical powers coming out of nowhere to take on the title of a mythical figure as he lends help to a city garrison outnumbered a hundred-to-one in beating back an invasion, and they would say it'd happen when pigs fly. A 100% certainty in Yuell, on both counts.

Marina took his response in stride. With a cute creature in her lap and another snuggling against her arm on the table, she appeared in a state of bliss. Jaune stayed to chat with her for a while, and they made a game of tossing morsels of food to Hans the winged pig—a porcavian, was the species name. It must look odd from the outside. Marina tended to reply with grunts and hums, sometimes one-word answers, so their talking was really more him yammering on and on to himself, with her chiming in on a rare occasion.

That changed as the subject pivoted to the future. Though she had known he was leaving, he hadn't realized that she would be doing the same.

"Squad 7?" he asked.

"Mm. Their commander saw me in the last battle. Wanted me to enlist."

"Your skill with a rifle is pretty impressive," said Jaune. "Still, I'm surprised you're taking him up on the request. I thought you wanted to head back to your cabin in the woods." It had been one of the things he managed to learn from their conversations (if it could be called that) during the late night hours they spent atop the belltower. He glanced down to her lap. "It's not because of their fluffy animal mascot, is it?"

"...No."

He observed her closely. There was the slightest curl to the corner of her lips. Marina had told a joke.

What a strange day.

"My team has an adorable cat," Jaune reminded her, hinting hard. Hearing him, Escha proved the point by making her eyes go wide and round, purring at Marina.

The young woman snorted. She reached out to scratch the felyne under the chin. Most people seemed to have dismissed the sight of the cat wielding weapons as a fever dream, refusing to speak of it lest those who were not at the battle think them insane. Marina was among the rare few. She simply didn't care—cute was cute.

"Where will you go?" she asked in reply, sounding a touch too disinterested for it to be genuine apathy.

"Oh, you know, here and there. My work is like that."

"Far?"

Jaune nodded. "Yes."

"Past the continent?" She judged his reaction. "Past the sea?"

"Maybe further."

"Good luck," said Marina. She frowned as she petted the winged pig. "I can't leave. My work is here until the war is over."

"I guess it is a little difficult to enjoy the quiet life with the Imps running around."

Marina shot him a soft glare. "Not really. It's just, I know I'm no good with people, but I still…" She cast a lingering look across the university grounds, then gave a huff and waved him off. "Whatever. You get what I mean."

She still wanted to be a part of it. Still cared, despite her lonely nature. In her own way, Marina loved Gallia.

With nothing left for them to say on the matter, the two of them let the conversation fade away. It would, perhaps, be the last chance for them to experience a moment like this, and so for a time, they took joy from the silence surrounding their little corner of the world. Unlike their first meeting, which began with a bullet and the cacophony of war, their parting went without a sound.

The night carried on, and Jaune traced a winding course through the revelries. He ended up in the company of Welkin Gunther and, as it tended to happen, the two men's talks turned to the subject of women. One, in particular.

Selvaria Bles, the Valkyria. A conundrum in need of a solution, she was currently held captive and under a heavy guard presence. With a medic on standby, in case of… well, just in case.

"What do you think should happen, if I may ask?" said the lieutenant.

Jaune blinked once, twice. "Wasn't the plan that she'll go in front of a tribunal? Something, something, formal recognition of the crimes the Empire committed in invading Gallia?"

Sue him, Tattletale was the main person participating in that conversation.

"Let's see…" Jaune listed out on his hand, "She invaded your kingdom. She invaded this city. She's an enemy." He looked at Welkin. "Yup, Selvaria should answer for her actions."

Welkin weakly chuckled, and rubbed the back of his head. "You heard what Faldio said about General Damon. He will be the ranking officer arriving here, which makes him the one to take custody of Selvaria. It's possible he would execute her after extracting all the information she knows."

Or pass her off to those that would experiment on her in an attempt to unlock the powers of a Valkyria. Or worse things. Faldio Landzaat had not pulled his punches when he outlined the many likely scenarios.

The lieutenant studied his cup with an uncomfortable look on his face. Despite the bar snacks on the table, the man had opted for a glass of milk instead of alcohol and Jaune joined him so as to give his liver a reprieve.

"Everything that lives wants to survive, even her," Welkin said, seeming to himself. "Deserves to? That's harder to judge, but… I think death shouldn't be such an easy thing. Penance is making up for your actions, and dying won't do that."

However, it was final. It solved the problem. Selvaria had been willing to destroy Yuell, and that power may yet remain in her grasp. All it took would be a broken choker and another set of weaponry capable of channeling her Valkyria abilities.

She was docile now, because she was weak now. Put her in a position of strength again, and watch heads roll.

Welkin smiled grimly when Jaune raised that point.

"Have you considered Faldio's proposal?" the lieutenant asked.

"What, the one with me as her jailer?"

It had been a suggestion raised in a joking tone while not at all being a joke. They had ways to defend against the requisition of the lasguns and the people with Aura should the Army demand it, rights and protections afforded to Gallian citizens, their property, and so on that even nobles had to finesse their way around. An enemy combatant was a different story, and Faldio believed that Damon could not be trusted with the power of a Valkyria. The general was apt to use it for a coup rather than for the benefit of Gallia; he had a thirst for ambition and was weak to temptation.

The solution, as Faldio suggested, was an uncomplicated one. There was a single individual in this world with the strength to keep Selvaria in line should the choker fail. This person has no intentions to cause trouble for Gallia because they already stated their intention to leave, and existed outside the chain of command in a way that put him above instead of below it.

Ruefully, Jaune shook his head. "I'm not risking her murdering my companions in their sleep. The Aura you now have"—he flicked the other man, causing him to glow a deep green—"isn't invincible. There are workarounds, and she has the motive to pursue them."

He could try throwing her into a new world the moment they returned to the apartment, but considering her unwell state of mind, all that amounted to was an execution with extra steps. The point, as Welkin mentioned, was penance for her crimes. Justice, and what she deserved.

Perhaps a life, at the end of this.

Jaune mulled on that. Something was niggling at him, related to the sentiment.

Tickticktick. A light bulb flickered on in his head.

"Hey," Jaune began, and Welkin leaned in to listen, "we've been going on and on about who has control of Selvaria, who is stronger than her, but that might have been the wrong way to look at the issue."

Welkin nodded along, unsure of where it was leading. Jaune's gaze sharpened, and he clapped the lieutenant on the shoulder.

"We should have thought about who among us held the most empathy for Selvaria. That's the kind of person that could get through to her." It clicked into place for Welkin. Too late, Jaune tightened his grip on him. "You're clearly the best man for the job."

A person who agonized over how to stop Selvaria from being used as a weapon would, in Jaune's opinion, hesitate to abuse her powers. His concern with ensuring she faced justice would, obviously, stop Welkin from ending her life outright. Finally, that he has already aided in formulating a plan to smuggle her out from under Damon's nose would, and this was important, meant he was willing to ignore the pesky legalities involved with the act.

The only thing Welkin lacked was the ability to match Selvaria in combat.

"Except, without the lance she isn't bulletproof," Welkin mused. "There are ways to bring her down in the worst case scenario."

That was easy.

"Take the night to think on it," Jaune advised. "Have a drink. Enjoy the party." His expression turned sly. "Spend time with a girl."

"What do you mean—"

"Welkin!" called out a voice just before Welkin Gunther found himself pulled to his feet.

"Alicia?" the young man stuttered.

The person in question, who Jaune supposed must be the baker extraordinaire of Squad 7, showed Gunther a bright smile.

"What are you doing, hiding over here? Come on, let's go dance!"

The lieutenant put up a protest, halfhearted at best, and allowed his fellow soldier to drag him along. He threw Jaune a salute over his shoulder, and their voices soon became lost in the general din of the festivities. Thus, Jaune was left alone to nurse his drink… while looking at the other person at the table, who had been hiding behind Welkin Gunther's frame up until now. Instead of addressing her right away, he gave it a minute to really let her stew. Then, he spoke.

"You've been rather quiet, Isara." He sipped from his glass of milk. It lacked the gravitas of a wine glass, but he made do by being twice as dramatic with his tone. "I was hoping to talk to you."

Partly raised from her seat, Isara Gunther froze in her tracks. With her attempt to escape thwarted, the panicky girl looked left and right in search of aid. Finding none, she changed tack.

"I-I don't know what you could mean…" Isara clasped her hands behind her back, the very picture of innocence.

Jaune took another sip of his drink. The thin smile on his face was threatening to break into full-on laughter, and it was an ongoing struggle to maintain the serious mood.

"Bahahahaha!"

Nevermind, he failed entirely.

As she struck upon the realization that he had been messing with her, Isara underwent a shift from scared to displeased. She crossed her arms, and pouted.

"Why do you always make fun of me?" she asked, stomping a foot.

"Because you make it too easy," he replied. Wiping a tear from the corner of his eye, he motioned for her to sit down. She was suspicious, but did as he bade. A nudge, and the bowl of shelled peanuts on the table slid over to her side. Isara took a few then passed it back. She nibbled on the snack one by one as she watched him.

"You… said you wanted to talk," she stated uncertainly. "So, um, you aren't mad at me?"

"That you awakened other people's Aura? No." His answer caused her to slump over in relief. Jaune leaned forward in his chair, gaining her attention again. "I am, however, curious to know how you did it. I don't remember ever telling you that was possible, little miss."

Here, her expression turned impish. "But you did show me."

Understanding shortly dawned for Jaune. The proof was there from the beginning. If he could do it for her, then of course she would entertain the possibility that she could for others too.

"Was that all it took?" he wondered aloud.

Isara nodded. "Mostly. After you told me that 'Aura' can block bullets, I had to try giving it to Welks. It didn't work at first." She squinted her eyes at him. "Did that poem do anything? I spent an hour thinking I had gotten the words wrong because nothing was happening."

"Uh, yeah? The chant is critical, thank you very much." His eyes darted to the side. "It has to be a problem on your end."

"I don't believe you."

He raised a finger, wagging it before her face. "I'm not lying. It is very important, depending on how you look at it."

From the look of Isara, he had confirmed something for her. The girl lost her cheeky demeanor to appear almost at peace.

"I could have recited the recipe for a stew, and it would have worked," she ventured a guess, studying him for his response.

He cracked a grin.

The words themselves may change. The sound of one's voice was a superfluous detail. The chant was intertwined with the process at a level so basic, so simple, that one could miss it entirely.

Emboldened, Isara continued. "When I succeeded, I was thinking of Welkin."

And there it was.

Words were constructs. Artificial, in a way.

Aura came from a more honest place. One had to think of the other person. To be willing to give their soul to them. The chant helped to shape these intentions, able to be mangled to hell and back so long as the feelings beneath remained true. For the sake of her brother, that was all too easy for Isara to do.

A stew recipe could function as a chant, if it was one that a person cooked for their precious family. In the same manner, to 'really really want to' was a perfectly good answer. The Nora method, Jaune liked to call it.

"You astound me, Isara Gunther," he said, and it was the truth.

A tinge of color crept up her neck. Isara held her cheeks in her hands, squirming at the praise.

"Once I figured it out, it was easy to repeat the process," she explained in a quieter tone.

"You wouldn't have had much time. We mustered for battle less than a day later. Did you rest at all?"

"A few times, when I became too tired. Giving someone Aura takes a part of yours, doesn't it? Like a sort of fuel injection to ignite the process?"

Jaune pinched his fingers together. "A little bit. It comes back."

"You must have a lot. I nearly passed out, and even during the battle I still wasn't feeling right…"

"Yeah, you went overboard. Saved a lot of lives, though. Good job on that."

The pretty blush had barely faded when it made its return. Isara laughed, and leaned closer to peer up at him from beneath her eyelashes.

"Does that mean I can keep going, then?" she asked, mischievously.

He spread his hands. "It's your soul. Do whatever you like."

"Good," she replied with a nod. "Because the rest of Squad 7 needs their Aura. I'm going to make sure every single one of us is going home after this war."

Which was why even if he could stop her, he never would. She understood Aura's purpose—a shield to protect one's companions.

He spent almost an hour there by her side. As the celebrations continued into the night, the two of them were content to hover on the periphery. They spoke of paper airplanes.

In the end, it was her who brought up the matter first.

"I heard from Welks that you aren't staying in Gallia," said Isara. "That… That's going to affect the war."

Jaune heaved a sigh. His hand came up to run through his hair, tousling it in his frustration. "I know, and it doesn't feel right to just leave things halfway. This is out of my hand, though. It's a case of having to, rather than wanting to."

"It must be hard to be a Valkyria."

Was that how she interpreted it? He supposed it was as good an explanation as any. True, in a sense.

"Can you do me a favor?" he asked.

Isara blinked her eyes, before quickly agreeing. "Anything!"

He waved a hand at their surroundings.

"When they ask, tell them that I'm out there, somewhere, fighting on for Gallia. It'd keep up morale."

The request was easy enough and she saw the point to it, assuring him it would be done. But as he rose from his seat, Isara hopped to her feet and stopped him.

"What if—!" She lowered her voice to a more controlled volume. "What if I- everybody said we wanted you to stay in Yuell?"

"Were that I could," was his answer accompanied by a shrug, and in that, the girl read no lie. Nodding her head, she made her move.

Isara swooped in close, and like a different dark-haired girl tonight, she kissed him on the cheek.

"Magari had the right idea," she said afterward. "Now there's two reasons for you to come back. On that day, I hope that together you and I can see the true blue sky."

Laughing sweetly, Isara Gunther turned away from him and skipped off into the crowd in the direction of Welkin and Alicia. Jaune watched her go, a hand on his cheek. There went another dreaming fool, and another 'could have been'.

After that, he drifted from place to place, throwing himself into the festivities to draw out every last second he had left in this world to the fullest. The music had changed to some kind of traditional folk dance and he joined that for a while, learning the movements on the fly. Then it was roasting sweet potatoes by the bonfire, and a game of football that had dozens of players on each side jumping in and out as it suited them. It was right as he took leave from the match that he found Tattletale.

The little island she had staked out amidst this sea of revelries was piled high with assorted knick-knacks of all stripes. A family of three had just finished dropping a basket of textile onto the table when he approached, cluing him in that these were gifts. Offerings, if he was being honest. He really did start a religion.

Oddly, Tattletale seemed less than happy with this bountiful harvest.

"Why so glum, Lisa?" he asked as he sat down.

Tattletale drummed her fingers on the table, glaring at the pile of gifts. "I've been waiting for something worthwhile, but it's all junk."

"I see a gold necklace over there."

"Yeah. Junk," Tattletale repeated. "What's so special about gold? The ragnite next to it would sell for better."

"Oh, relax. We made a pretty tidy sum from the Empire." Artillery pieces, tanks, the Batomys. Selvaria's used weapons sold for a surprising amount. Even with his numerous outlays, the Points balance ended up at almost quadruple what it was on their first day here.

"We earned those ourselves," Tattletale retorted. "The locals barely played a part. We spent weeks here and the best they can manage for our time is, ugh, that." She waved a dismissive hand at the small mountain on the table.

He resisted the urge to roll his eyes. They made bank and she still found a reason to complain.

"Well, if you don't want it…" He reached for the golden necklace.

Tattletale smacked his hand and snatched away the accessory. "This is mine. Get your own."

Yup, that tracked for a sticky-fingered thief. He huffed in amusement, and helped her put it on. Gaudy and pretentious, it suited her to a tee.

As he was connecting the clasp, Tattletale muttered, "We should confiscate the weapons you handed out."

He spared a moment's thought on it, though in truth his mind was set.

"Nah, they need it more than we do. The guns would sell for a fraction of their cost, so it's not worth the bother."

"Not what I meant, Jaune. Leaving that sort of tech in their possession is a bad idea. At some point, people will figure out the mechanics, and—"

"They'll arm themselves with it, yeah. You've mentioned before. But, you know…" He leaned over her shoulder to meet her eyes. "Bullets or lasers, what does it change, Lisa? A better way to wage war? They were already well on their way. It'd come out a wash in the end. Do you expect me to take back Aura, too?"

"Don't even, mister. You really made a mess of it there. Without those Grimm creatures as a counterbalance, it's a guarantee that everyone on the planet would have Aura someday."

"Then it'd take ten times the effort and ten times the cost to win a battle. Wars might end up so boring that people give up on them."

"Yeeeah, that's not how it works."

Jaune's reply was a lazy smile and a shrug of his shoulders.

In what felt like a lifetime ago, Corvo Attano had warned them against the spread of Aura. The consequences of such a power in a world that had not seen its kind would shake the foundation of kingdoms.

Yet, lives were saved by what he had done. The Yuell garrison and Squad 7 counted among the faces in this crowd that in another life would be absent, dead at the hands of Selvaria Bles. In the same vein, he liked to think that his actions would prove a boon over the course of time. Aura was not born in man for the sake of war. Way back in the depths of Remnant history, it manifested in their direst hour to protect them from harm, or so the story went.

Why else would it shine so bright? Little lights in the dark, Aura was meant to give hope.

"They'll do just fine, Lisa. If there is anything that this city has shown me, it's that we can trust people."

Could he have made a mistake? Sure.

He had been too weak, that was the long and short of it. A single person stood no chance of turning the tide. Banding together with the defenders of Yuell, he had scraped by, but it still was not enough. Defeat remained ever a step away with a siege that dragged on for days on end. To break the balance had required greater measures, and he used what came to hand, going for broke to win it back.

Perhaps a hundred years from now a war would come about, filled with lasguns and Semblances on both sides. Perhaps it would all end in tears.

But that was a worry for another time. Tonight was a victory. Tomorrow, a new day.

Yuell would live to see the morning, and that was the best someone like him could do. He's got a long way to go.

"Hey, so, I was thinking," Jaune began, changing the subject, "one of the hotels stayed intact, and the owner offered me the penthouse suite for the night. You want to see what it's all about?"

Tattletale looked like she had a lot more to say. Ultimately, she relented, taking note of his restless energy and seeming to read from it something quite flattering about herself (which was also something quite wrong). A teasing glance, and she tapped her chin as if in thought.

"Hmmm. I guess I can be convinced—wait just a darn minute!"

"What?" Jaune asked, taken aback.

"Didn't you put a bunch of your adventurer skill points into improving your Vitality attribute?"

"Yes, I did."

"As in, your endurance?"

"In basic terms, I suppose."

"Huh."

Tattletale looked down at her wine glass sitting on the table. She had hardly touched it. Lifting up the drink, she drained it to the last drop, and slammed the empty glass on the table surface.

"Alright. Cool." A familiar grin, bold and confident, appeared on her face. "That's no problem, I got this."

She did not, in fact, got this.

Universe: Valkyria Chronicles. Location: Yuell.
Event: Imperial Advance.
Loot: Ruhm (machine rifle), Gallian lance (Lancaar model), conventional ammunition, gunlance shells, ragnite crystals, ragnite fuel (1 barrel), ragnaid (4 boxes), Gallian beer, bread (1 basket, made with love), assorted valuables and goods, an Edelweiss flower.
