#4,102
Chapter 53: The World is Not Beautiful​


On a morning not long after getting back from Yuell, Jaune returned to his daily routine. Goodbyes were a constant of his life nowadays, and wallowing in memories and what-ifs would do him no good.

Someday they will meet again. He would believe in that. In the meantime, the center of the apartment had been cleared out, as it often did, for the sake of training. For the gains.

Here, however, he encountered a problem.

"Do you think you can add any more?"

"Jaune, you have half the kitchen and a couch on your back."

An exaggerated, but true enough summation for the precarious tower of knickknacks stacked atop him. His gunlance was tucked in there with the tip jabbing into his rear in a painful way, and a potted plant balanced on his head. With both hands placed on the ground, Jaune tried to do another push-up and found it all too easy—which was awful, because easy was quite the opposite of how a training session should go.

"Yes, well, I need heavier weights," he grumbled. "Hop on my back, Lisa."

"Excuse the fuck you?"

Jaune mentally played back what he said, and winced. "I meant hopping on my back along with the other objects. If we keep adding to the pile, I can maybe get something out of it."

He had not considered before today the consequence of improving himself through unnatural methods—unlike with Aura, which was totally normal, thank you Lisa. The surge of power gained from the adventurer card boosted his physical prowess beyond what months, if not years, could do for him. How it worked when his muscle mass remained the same was a mystery. His body might block a speeding car with barely a flinch in his current state, yet it lacked the hard and unyielding quality that a person capable of that feat should enjoy. Magic, he concluded in the end.

The big, glaring problem was that those stat points seemed to lay at a sort of halfway point between being a part of his body and a part of his soul. Despite experiencing no changes to his physique, he now drew out so little benefit from his usual practice regimen that it became an exercise in futility. The drills failed to develop his muscles, failed to strain and tear and build them back up into something better. The Nikos's Endless Training Hell ought to feel grueling. Instead, it was an easy walk in the park. He did not think he would ever miss the sense of sheer exhaustion that one got after hours and hours of swinging a sword at empty air, but it sure beat flailing around without results.

"Training at this level is moot," he finally admitted. Such a shame, because if he had gotten stronger naturally, then he suspected it might turn out to be a case where the boosts worked off of those parameters. "I need better equipment, the kind of stuff that Beacon would have."

Coco Adel was not born with gorilla arms, after all. The academy understood what it took to churn out stronger graduates, and breaking through one's limits in its gym just meant adding another hundred pounds to one of the reinforced barbells that qualified a legendary weapon in its own rights, forged by master smiths and whatnot.

"I'll put it on the shopping list," Tattletale idly commented, a hand on her hip.

The stuff on his back vanished for the most part, letting him get up without causing a cascading din of falling objects.

"We could buy it now, from the Marketplace," he said as he walked around, summoning the items back to their proper places.

His suggestion was met with a cute pout. "Mundane things like that can be found anywhere, so no. I'm not wasting Points on it. Wait until we pass by a modern world, and pick it up there. For now, why not dial it back?" She smiled, and it was almost kind. "Relax."

"Lisa…" His voice shook with fond emotions. And then it died. "So when are you going to start on your practice? You don't have my excuse."

Oh, she could. Her levels were low, but she had a bit of savings to spare. Except, she insisted that unlike him she would be 'efficient' and put it all in intelligence to maximize her job advantage aaand he tuned her out after that. One could only withstand a certain amount of smugness before needing a break.

It worked out better this way, anyhow. Her lacking stamina, strength, speed… everything… meant she had an easier time achieving improvements.

The smile on Lisa's face turned decidedly nervous.

"Soon." She averted her eyes, feigning interest in the blank wall.

Jaune remained adamant. "Yeah, no. Get to it. Make the Meowscular Chef proud."

In this matter he reigned supreme, and even had past-Lisa's word on putting in effort, which she was likely regretting today. The girl shuffled over to the spot next to him, grumbling all the while.

"Escha isn't doing this," she whined, making fists with her hands and putting up a guard. Jaune stepped in to fix her form, then stepped back to observe.

"She is taking care of the garden," he refuted, and sent a glance over to the small field of jars and pots set next to the window.

The felyne hadn't appreciated how long her plants and bugs went unattended, and if a cat could look reproachful at him, she did—it was adorable. The good news was that the hardy specimens lived through their extended absence, and were in recoverable states, beside. In fact, a day or two should see them harvested to be turned into tools, medicine, and the like.

Jaune continued. "In any case, Escha can already protect herself and keep pace with me if we have to escape from a threat. You can't. Come on, Lisa, who knows when we will run into a Selvaria or Accelerator?"

"There's a lesson you can learn there," Lisa replied, sounding a tad snide. "Keep out of their way and we wouldn't have that problem. Stop hanging around for the danger to find you, while you're at it."

"You're breaking form." He moved in to fix her stance, ignoring the sullen glower. As he did, he kept talking. "You say that, but sometimes there's a good reason to stay."

She scoffed, and threw an angry punch that overextended. He caught her to prevent her from stumbling.

"Don't get in that habit. You're not nearly buff enough to be the berserker type," he admonished, letting go. After observing her next few punches and finding them satisfactory, he nodded in approval, soon returning to the subject at hand. "The reason might be a small thing. 'I don't want this person to die'. 'I hate that guy'. Whatever works. You should know, you stuck with Yuell from beginning to end."

He didn't set out to become a Huntsman so he could run away from people in need. Time and again the many worlds proved to him that somebody had to stand at the center, and hold the line. A spearhead, that others may form the wings. In this manner, a siege was won.

The places he went to did not always have a person like that.

Lisa frowned. "Don't do that."

"What?" he asked.

"Expect things of me." She scrunched her nose. "You're building an entirely wrong image of how we should operate. We aren't a band of heroic capes here to save the day."

She tried to shove him for emphasis. He blocked it with a casual ease that pissed her off even more, and positioned the hand to where it was supposed to go.

"You're breaking form."

"Uuugh, you are so annoying!" Lisa complained. That said, she heeded the instruction.

"Training is important," he said with a dull inflection, the phrase borrowed from many a night of Pyrrha telling him the exact same thing.

Lisa continued speaking between punches. "Being subtle isn't a bad thing. Stand outside the limelight, and you might be able to solve a problem without anybody realizing until it's too late to stop you."

"I mean, I get that."

"Do you?" she accused. "Then why don't you follow that?"

This time was his turn to avert his gaze.

A little smirk took its place on her lips, and Lisa began to put visible effort in the practice drill. Winning always did put her in a good mood, as petty a victory as this was.

The training session continued on, with Jaune serving as the coach for Lisa on her path to becoming a champion fighter. The girl might not have realized it, but she had grown head and shoulders above the wimpy maiden she used to be and can in all likelihood beat a man twice her size into a pulp... Even if the fight Jaune envisioned would end up a lot messier due to her relatively poor techniques. Lisa just wasn't interested in the brutish, sweaty affairs of physical combat.

Probably because she had seen the monster laying in wait out there, and intended to never again stand across from one if she could help it.

And that was the rub, wasn't it? Where, oh where, were they going to set their new base to avoid those types? The Points they accumulated have at last put the next phase on the table. A part of Jaune still found it hard to believe that they managed to come this far.

"Someplace easy," was Lisa's choice.

Jaune rather disagreed on that, and said so. "Skipping that step and buying access to a higher rating world would give us better returns."

Yes, he picked up that terminology from Lisa. She enjoyed talks of revenues and profits.

"Faster, you mean," Lisa corrected. "Only thinking of what you can earn is how people lose their fortune speculating in the stock market. Repeat after me." She puffed up with a pretentious air. "Contingencies. Save. Lives." Then, she pointed at herself. "My life, to be exact. Ergo—"

"Well, well. Don't you sound all smart."

"Ergo, we are going to stick to my plan and proceed with caution. Take our time, explore our options. It doesn't matter how fast you go in a race if you can't reach the finish line."

"That… sounds good to me," Jaune admitted. The wish to hurry things along had been an idle one, borne of a small, nagging sense of worry that he was starting to forget something important. It most likely meant nothing, paranoia at its best. "Pick wisely, and I suppose the world will pay for itself in a few weeks."

Lisa gasped. "Look at you, being all reasonable! Oh, you are learning, aren't you?" She scratched him under the chin as she would a puppy, snatching the hand back as Jaune mimed biting her, sharing a laugh. "I'll grant you that a Rating 0 world won't make complete sense with how we are now. That's why I would like to get a better idea of the scope to each rating before we commit. I want a safe place, but not too safe since those never have interesting stuff we can sell lying around."

"Good fashion, though," Jaune said, thinking of Okinawa.

"Point. Hmmm, what to do?" Lisa pondered. "What to do?"

What else?

Journey on, and loot.


-o-​


The cafe rested on a road that saw very little traffic, lined by buildings on either side. The stone facades were well cared for, though worn by age; the buildings have stood here for a long time.

The owner of the store, a rotund woman of middling years, had set tables outside for customers. Few were occupied on this calm, quiet early afternoon. Just a dandy old gentleman at one, and a pair of blonds at another. The clinking of porcelain on porcelain provided the only sound for the past few minutes.

With a contented sigh, Lisa put the delicate cup of latte down. She made sure to catch his eyes, smirking at the empty spot in front of him. Jaune was still waiting for his drink to arrive.

Did it make sense that they placed the same order at the same time, and his was currently taking twice as long? No, and he was a tad miffed about it, more so when Lisa kept slurping her coffee with exaggerated relish.

That attitude did an about-face when the waiter, a teenager about their age, returned from within the cafe to place a second cup on the table.

"Here you are," said the waiter with pride.

"...Whoa."

Jaune looked at his coffee, and a small cat stared back. Made of milk foam, the figure had two little paws hooked on the rim and a smiling face drawn with drizzles of chocolate syrup, the curved handle of the cup incorporated into the art to form the tail. Sprinkles of cinnamon lent the impression that the cat had just come back from rolling around outside, happy and energetic.

The confectionery in a cup very much reminded him of Escha, and he briefly wondered whether she would be elated to see something so cute or horrified at the sight of a fluffy white cat disappearing into a person's stomach. The felyne had opted to remain in the apartment this go-round to take care of her plants and bugs, though, meaning he won't get to enjoy her reaction. (He snapped a picture of it with his scroll for that purpose.)

Lisa, now. The girl was alternating her gaze between his coffee and hers, and that expression on her face spelled nothing but jealousy.

"It looks amazing," Jaune said to the waiter. "What's the occasion? All I asked for was a latte."

The waiter laughed. "The owner likes you, she thinks you're a good boy. Your meals will be out soon."

With that, he left them to it. Jaune wasted no time, turning to Lisa and grinning.

"See? I'm a good boy."

What greeted him was a pout.

"I want that one," Tattletale demanded, pointing at his coffee.

"If you request it, I think they will make one for you." He craned his neck to peek inside the store. The duo staffing it were doing mysterious barista things, but at the sort of pace to suggest they had all day. "It's not like they're busy at the moment."

Lisa chose instead to move her drink in front of him, then hooked a finger through the handle of his cup.

"Hey," Jaune said, entirely without surprise.

"I'm taking this, and you can have mine."

He peered into the cup sitting before him. "You already finished half of it."

"Still taking this," she replied in a brash tone, watching him carefully for his reaction. That became a squawk as he reached over and ruffled her hair, to her vehement protests.

Now satisfied, he pulled his (technically her) latte closer. The wary Lisa stared at him for a little while longer, her hands covering her messy hair to protect it from further depredation. When she was sure he would not do anything, she relaxed and grabbed her new cup of coffee, turning it this way and that to admire the foam figure.

Jaune sipped his drink. Throughout the whole motion, he maintained a careful eye on their surroundings. After, he set it down with a soft clack.

"So," he said, drawing his companion's attention, "what made you want to visit this place?"

Lisa gave a shrug of her shoulders. "Morbid curiosity, I guess. How can it be a beautiful world, if that is allowed?" A rhetorical question, suitable for a most curious conundrum. "Although, it is surprisingly much more peaceful than I envision. I was hoping to put my detective cap on."

Jaune cast a gaze at the landscape. Once in a while, a car would roll past. Pedestrians greeted one another with a friendly demeanor. On the surface, it resembled an ordinary city scene.

"Don't let your guard down. You saw the scroll said."

"Phone."

"Scroll."

They went through the motions of the old, familiar joke, the words and beats to it spoken by rote. It rather proved that despite everything they said, they could find no sign of danger here.

A chuckle rang out behind Lisa, and she turned her head to look. Jaune leaned to the side for a view.

The dandy old gentleman had risen from the nearby table. His clothes featured a simple and elegant cut. Well-to-do without a fortune, Jaune would put it. Strangely rough hands held on to a cane, but he walked without its aid.

Lisa's gaze lingered on the cane.

Approaching them, the gentleman doffed his fedora. "A good afternoon to you. Would you perhaps spare a minute for a stranger?"

Neither of them objected.

"I could not help but catch your conversation, and I noted your unfamiliarity with the ways of this fair city." Keen eyes observed the pair with a glance, the gentleman nodding and humming to himself as if having confirmed something he suspected. "If I may ask, are you travelers, or do you intend to immigrate?"

"We're travelers, stopping by for a few days," Jaune answered.

"Truly?" said the gentleman, a hand smoothing his white beard in thought. "My, and here I was, so certain otherwise. You would have been a good fit."

Jaune's head tilted to the side. "What makes you say that?"

"Because you, young man, have the look of someone who would not hesitate to kill a person."

Jaune did not know how to respond to that, and so sat there with a blank stupor. Lisa, on the other hand, snapped right back at the dandy old gentleman.

"Wooow, how rude can you get? Did you miss your meds, old-timer?"

The gentleman blinked in honest befuddlement. "I did not mean to offend. It was a simple statement of fact."

For whatever reason, Jaune was reminded of the Outsider. The comparison soured him a bit on this person.

"Okay, fair enough, I have killed before," Jaune said, half-hoping it would shock the guy. He was disappointed there. "But I did it for a reason," he insisted.

Their guest held up his hands, and Jaune saw no judgment or scorn in his eyes. "Please, there is no need to explain. After all… Here, it is no crime to kill a man."

The words were spoken with an easy air, lacking the gravitas that it should possess. Nevertheless, the mood grew tense in the resulting silence. Some thoughts went beyond the pale.

As she often did, Lisa broke the moment. "Yeah, what's with that? There shouldn't even be a city left."

"Well now," the gentleman said, and smiled kindly, "what do you see around us, then?

Grudgingly, Lisa muttered, "A city."

"Quite. You are travelers, yes? Why not spend some time in town, and get a firsthand look at"—he chuckled again—"the lawless jungle that you have stepped into."

The waiter came by, setting down plates.

"After you have tried the local specialty this land is known for, of course."

Jaune and Lisa stared at the two stacks of crepes before them. Creme, pastry, and strawberries were piled up high as a mountain. These were proper Huntsman portions. Monster Hunter portions, even.

They shared a look.

""Race you.""


-o-​


They heeded the suggestion of the dandy old gentleman. The rest of the afternoon had them visiting all the highlights of the city, which was in fact considered a nation unto itself in the same style as the Great Kingdoms, albeit smaller in population and power by magnitudes.

Their first stop was the tall wall past the farmlands that encircled the whole territory. Made from white stone, it towered over the surrounding scenery. Very sensible.

Next came the main thoroughfares and shopping streets, where they mingled among the crowds. Gold was gold, and the pair restocked on some of the basic supplies that were running low. They passed by schools and museums, spending time at a park. Toward the evening, they ate at a restaurant overlooking the riverfront.

Once night arrived, they retired to a small hotel just a couple of buildings over from the cafe. Lisa made a commotion in their room to watch how people would react. She apologized when she was asked politely to stop. Then, later on, she was asked politely to stop again. This time, both Jaune and Lisa apologized for the noise.

Altogether, they found a city that was not as described, and the next morning saw three figures sitting at the open air cafe for brunch. Business for the store was bustling today.

"I think I get it," Lisa proclaimed through a mouthful of crepes. Jaune and her were sharing a plate this time, having learned from yesterday, the undertaking watched over by two foam cats sitting in latte cups.

Jaune turned to her. "You do?"

"What, you didn't notice?" she asked in response. "Are you blind?"

Mildly ticked off by the tone, he said, "No. What are you talking about?"

Lisa twirled her fork in an absentminded manner. "I guess it is common in your world." That didn't explain anything to him, and she knew it. "I still think there are glaring issues that undercuts the whole system, but until it happens, I can't tell for sure which way it shakes out." She motioned at the peaceful street. "What is in front of us shows, at least, that the city hasn't blown up yet. I can't deny that part."

On the sideline to their chit chat, the dandy old gentleman merely deepened his smile and continued to stir his tea. He perked up as the doors to the hotel that sat a couple buildings over opened, and out came a person.

"It seems our other traveler has arrived. Would you mind terribly if they join us?"

Neither of them objected, and the gentleman called out to 'Kino'. Soon, the newcomer was approaching their table.

Jaune took the time to observe Kino, having been curious about the mysterious guest who took a room on the same floor as Lisa and him but he had not seen at all. Slight of build, Kino appeared to be a boy at first glance due to the short haircut and the thick black vest, but on closer look was in fact a very cute girl. She pushed along a motorcycle laden with supplies, and Jaune wondered why that had been allowed on the hotel's shiny floor.

The girl greeted the dandy old gentleman with a bow, then threw Jaune and Lisa an assessing look as she pulled out a chair.

"Good morning, Kino, Hermes," said the gentleman."This is Jaune and Lisa. Like you, they are staying here for a few short days."

"Hello," said Kino.

"Howdy!" said the motorcycle.

Said the motorcycle. Said the motorcycle. Said—Jaune's brain rebooted.

""It can talk!"" shouted both Jaune and Lisa.

As if to prove the point, it- he spoke again in the voice of a young boy. "What else am I supposed to do, dance? Have you never met a motorrad before?"

Jaune swiftly left his seat to kneel by the vehicle, and he searched for the source of the voice. "A motorrad? Do they come with radios? Is that how you're doing this?"

"All me, baby. My type is becoming pretty rare nowadays, though, so I'm not too surprised you haven't met one like me. More and more people are building boring cars and bikes that don't talk for some reason."

"Oh gee, who wouldn't want an AI uprising?" Lisa muttered, rubbing her eyes as if hoping she was just hallucinating.

"And aye-eye?" asked the new girl, Kino.

Seizing on the topic as a lifeline, Lisa launched into a lecture on artificial intelligence and the dangers thereof, which both Kino and the dandy old gentleman were willing to humor. It allowed her to shove the topic of a talking motorcycle, or 'motorrad', to the side for Jaune to deal with.

He liked to think that his travels have inured him to some of the absurdity of the world. Indeed, the speed at which he grew used to holding conversation with Hermes once they got to talking bordered on the surreal. Beneath the steel and aluminum frame was a person even if he still couldn't find the voicebox, a chatty one as interested in his story as he was of the motorrad's.

The land of visible pain, the land of books, the land of identical faces, a kind land that never saw tomorrow. The roads that Hermes and Kino have ridden on did not always lead to happy places. This world, like many he had visited, was an imperfect thing.

That said, the 'battles' that Hermes recounted were probably exaggerations, and where Jaune drew the line. They strained credulity, replete with explosions at their backs that neither girl nor motorrad looked at while walking away.

"The three-day rule?" he later asked after Hermes revealed a bit on how he and Kino operated.

Hermes nodded… How did he know that the mottorrad nodded?

"It lets Kino see most of a country without overstaying her welcome, and time for her to visit all the countries left out there. Life doesn't last for never."

"Did you mean 'forever'?"

"That. Can you imagine being stuck in one spot for years and years? It makes me shiver imagining it."

"…Does it?"

"Of course it does. Do I look heartless to you? I have feelings, you know!" said the motorrad.

"Not quite the part I was doubting. Still, I kind of get your point, Hermes."

He might have started traveling out of necessity, but to learn of the open horizons beyond the walls, in lands where the Grimm never roamed? His heart was not made of stone. Wanderlust, too, had taken root within him. He wanted to experience so much more.

"What if you have to stay for longer?" he asked. "Like, say, there's a war going on."

Just an example, no particular incident in mind.

"That doesn't have anything to do with us?" Hermes replied, uncertain. "People fight each other all the time to the point that it's almost a sport. We'd ruin their game if we barge into the middle of it. Besides, Kino isn't in the habit of starting anything, and I'm a motorrad—no hands."

With steadfast resolve, Jaune ignored the vindicated look Lisa leveled his way from over at the table. The circumstances of their respective groups were totally different, and should not be compared. Yup, yup.

"I suppose you two do give off fairly inoffensive vibes," Jaune said.

Hermes gave a sheepish chuckle. "Well, that's not completely true… Kino, trouble's coming."

"You! I found you!" a person shouted, rushing out of a store. The young man wore a delirious grin, one that promised a great laugh for nobody but him. On his hip hung a gun, and he was resting his hand on the grip.

Lisa looked at Jaune as if to ask what he had done now. He shrugged and looked right back at her to ask the same, receiving an identical answer. They then both turned to the dandy old gentleman to get a bemused expression.

Kino was the one to stand up. The girl dressed in boyish black vest and pants took a couple of strides that put her alone on the road, with no one else in the line of fire. That once tranquil and lazy morning vanished with the simple action, sharpening into focus. People, whether shopkeepers, pedestrians, or cafe customers, read the writing on the wall and began clearing off the street. The gentleman sipped his tea, remaining where he was, as did Jaune and Lisa.

"Hello, again. What do you need?" Kino asked, her hand far away from her own revolver by her side.

"Leave all your stuff here and scram," said the young man.

"May I ask why I should?"

"Since you were too weak and frail to help carry my luggage for me on the way into town, then you must be having a hard time with the heavy supplies on that motorrad. I'll do you a favor and take it off your hand for you. Aren't I generous?"

"Very, so I cannot in good conscience ask it of you. I will keep my things."

The young man smirked. "Then I'll just kill ya. It's not a crime here. Care to change your mind?"

"You immigrated to this country, did you?"

"That's right. I'm a citizen now and I'll have a blast living here, free to kill anyone that pisses me off until the end of my days." His grin turned unfriendly. "Starting with you."

Kino hummed in thought, and said, "You don't behave like other people here."

"What are you—no, you're stalling. Last chance."

Jaune leaned forward. Go time.

Lisa bounced out of her seat to stop him, an arm across his chest. "Don't interfere." She glanced over her shoulder. "There's no need for that."

"Are you kidding right now?" he hissed.

She sighed.

A fwip, and an arrow sprouted on the young man's arm before he could finish drawing his gun. The young man screamed. Jaune spun to where the attack originated, catching sight of the doting cafe owner hefting a crossbow.

He had faced down monsters, yet he shivered at the eerie expression she sported on her face. Far too casual for what she was doing, far less kind than what she had been.

The cafe owner fired off another shot, the bolt striking the young man's foot this time. He fell, still shouting in pain and confusion.

"What are you doing!? What are you doing!?" was his cry.

The chair near Jaune slid back with a screech, and the dandy old gentleman stood up. Gripping his cane, he walked toward the young man. He was joined by a crowd of people newly returned to the street. Each person held a weapon of some kind. A teenager with a rifle, a man with a sword, an elderly couple carrying knives. The common thread connecting them was that the weapons were very well maintained.

Jaune noted the many individuals, old and young, with rough hands. Hard eyes assessed him every once in a while. He recalled the places he had visited during the sightseeing trip of the city. What had been present at every location, whether blade or firearm. It had seemed natural to him that weapons would be around, not worth acknowledging with more than a passing glance, and only now did he realize what Lisa had already figured out about the people here.

Civilians he had thought them, right up until they weren't. Regular people, but what things have they seen?

The young man failed to notice this, and remained brash and belligerent despite his injuries. He demanded help and threatened death in equal measure, the panic in his mind muddling his thoughts. No sympathy for him was found.

The gentleman stood over the young man, peering down at him. "It is no use, we did what we meant to do. We had to stop you."

"Wha… What?" gasped the young man, losing steam.

"You just tried to kill that girl, and that is not allowed in this country."

The young man did not understand. "What kind of joke is that?" he yelled. "Murder isn't prohibited!"

The gentleman nodded.

"Yes, it is not prohibited. That does not mean it is allowed." Around him, the crowd murmured their agreement.

"What does that even mean!? Help me, dammit! Or I'll kill you all!"

Jaune thought Lisa would have raised the objection. In her absence, he did it instead, calling out to the crowd.

"The guy hadn't actually killed anyone yet."

That drew everybody's attention to him.

"Oh? You would speak in his defense?" said the gentleman.

The young man's eyes sought out Jaune's, who saw in it a desperate hope.

"I didn't say that," Jaune stated, dashing that hope. "I saw what he attempted and anyway, as he keeps reminding us all, there isn't a law to protect him—"

Jaune stopped talking.

Oh. So that was it.

The dandy old gentleman noticed the pause, and gave Jaune a knowing look. He said, kindly, "He wanted to, you see. He would have, given his way. That someone stopped him is not a point in his favor. In fact…" The gentleman chuckled. "There are no points in this matter. It is a simple thing."

"Aaand this is where I go," Lisa remarked. "I don't want anything to do with this."

She sent him a significant glance, and jerked her head in the direction of the hotel, silently asking if he would leave with her. He shook his head, and as she left he turned back to the scene.

"Those who have killed others in this country were themselves killed," said the gentleman. "Those who have tried to kill others in this country were themselves killed. Those who try to kill others in this country… are themselves killed."

Here they say that murder was not prohibited. They also say it wasn't allowed. A contradiction, but so was the other way. Laws prohibited murder, and yet it would still happen.

Jaune rather thought that the people of this country must have seen every reason under the sun for it, to end up here. An understanding between neighbors who have walked the same road.

The young man finally got it through his head, the trouble he was in.

"No! No! Like he said, I didn't do it! You can't do this!"

The dandy old gentleman would not listen. "A weapon is not a toy to wave around. It is a tool for killing." With a twist, the head of his walking cane pulled out to reveal a sword. He took up a stance that belonged to a once much younger man, the blade aimed at his target's heart. "But you already know that. You are dangerous."

Jaune had not noticed Kino moving to stand by his side. She said to him in a quiet voice, "In the jungle, most things would prefer the tiger dead."

And, really, that was the long and short of it.

He glanced at the gun on the girl's hip. "Hey, Kino."

"Yes?"

"Do you see yourself using that revolver in the future?"

"I do. After all, I want to live."

"Right." Jaune sighed. "Life sure would be great if everyone could get along."

He felt something touching his shoulder. Kino was patting him in what the girl might have thought was a comforting manner.

"The world is not beautiful, therefore it is."

Lisa had left in order to avoid what came next. He stayed, and let it unfold. It bothered him that he understood.

Jaune stood there beside Kino, and watched people kill a man.

The reason did not matter, but it was important.


Universe: Kino's Journey -The Beautiful World-.
Location: The Land of Permitted Murder.
Event: A Curious Incident at the Cafe
Loot: daily supplies​


Author's Notes: Opening the new page in their lives on a light note.

Kino's Journey is an odd duck as far as light novels go. Its author enjoys playing with story structures and themes. If anything has had an effect on my writing, and stoked my desire to write and travel in the first place, it would be this series.

And on that note, I'll be traveling for a few weeks. Let's see if I can do some writing along the way. No motorrad, but a car will do.
