#4,229
Chapter 54: Boots, Jacket, Blade, Aura​


On a day like any other, the sweet and lovely voice of Lisa Wilbourn rang out across the apartment that the team had come to call home.

"My voice without da lies, this is what it sounds liiiiiike~"

It sounded better than one might think. Honest.

Fresh from a shower, she wore comfortable silk bathrobes, the hem of which swished and flicked as she pranced back and forth like she stood on a stage. The orchestration playing from a phone set on the kitchen counter lent itself to her performance. The girl sang her heart out, grinning as she delighted in the pure emotion of the music.

For Jaune who was in the midst of doing maintenance on his gunlance, the constant distraction brought nothing but bother. His annoyance grew and grew as he listened to the singing. It soon hit the last straw, and he set the lance aside to groan into his hands.

"Oh, for the love of… Lisa, quit it!"

Lisa stumbled mid-dance, giving him an interesting view. She turned around with a bewildered look. The glass of water she held in front of her face as a microphone instead of drinking from sloshed with the motion, spilling some.

"What? Why?" she asked, quite alarmed.

"Because if you don't," he said, and pointed at himself, "I'm going to start singing, too."

Lisa's expression cleared up, realization dawning as to the problem. Laughter found its way to her lips.

"It's catchy, isn't it?"

"Very."

"Haha!" She spread her hands, as if to say 'what can you do'. "I guess singing's got me a little thirsty anyway, so this is a good time for a break."

Jaune nodded his thanks, leaving it at that. Soon, he was once again immersed in the task of cleaning the gun chamber.

Out of his periphery, he saw Lisa opening the fridge door. Bottles and cans clattered as she rummaged around inside. She seemed to have found what she wanted, and the fridge door closed.

Pssst—pop!

Upon hearing the distinctive sound of a soda can tab being pulled, Jaune's palm met his face. That did it, it was over. He opened his mouth, right as a very smug Lisa also began.

""Hey, hey!... Hey, hey!"" they sang in stereo.


-o-​


Seoul was bright.

Jaune meant that in the very literal sense of it being broad daylight at this hour, sure, but also in the sense of smiles and liveliness and unfiltered energy as people went about their morning, the sort you'd get in the weeks after the Huntsmen got done taking their gunswords to the Grimm population near the town. People walked with a pep in their steps, heads held up high. Within their first few minutes here, Jaune had deemed it a good indicator that things were peaceful in this corner of the world and not at all in imminent danger like he expected, although at the same time it seemed to have somewhat unnerved Tattletale to see everyone so cheerful.

Her apprehension hadn't lasted long. The girl soon got over it and took to the city like a fish to water. With Escha in tow, she now raced through the crowd ahead of him, never a moment's rest as she set out for the next destination to catch her eyes. Already, she had purchased several new outfits and pieces of electronics.

That she could stand to let her guard down like this must be a sign she trusted him to handle whatever sudden development might arise, surely? He'd take it as such.

His own interest ran more toward the street foods sold in carts and stores along the way. Seoul food, or perhaps he should say 'Korean' food, trended toward the Mistral side of cuisine with some definite influences from Vale. Delicious, in short. Corn dogs, rice cakes, grilled squid, a sort of cross between a sushi roll and a sandwich, scallion pancakes—he tried a little of everything, having discovered an even deeper appreciation for food recently. The weeks of stale bread and boiled potatoes had thereafter turned any cheap grub he bought off the street into culinary delights.

In this manner the morning passed in relative peace, until their aimless course put them in a plaza surrounded by businesses and digital billboards. At once, Jaune noticed that something seemed to be going down. People were milling about, flyers in hand and confused looks on their faces while a bouncing beat underlaid the city noises. The sight gave Tattletale enough pause for him to catch up to her.

"Any idea what's happening?" he asked. Despite himself, his head moved to the music.

Escha took the initiative to scramble over to a flyer lying on the ground. She retrieved it, and hurried back to hand it up to Tattletale. In return, the girl dispensed many scritches under the chin to the felyne.

"Thanks, sweetie. Let's see what this is about." She blew a wayward strand of hair out of her face, before giving the piece of paper a quick skim. Her eyes then darted to the clock on one of the digital billboards. "It sounds like there's a street performance today. Here."

Right on cue, a cloud of purple smoke billowed from the other side of the plaza.

"And that should be it." Lisa motioned to him. "Come on, let's go check it out!"

They moved through the crowd, some of whom were also drifting over in that direction. Most stayed put, uncertain of what to do. What was causing that smoke? What did it mean? They had not the confidence born of Aura to head there and find out.

As he walked closer, Jaune heard a sound reminiscent of a soda can tab being pulled open. The music that had been playing in the background grew louder. Voices, all male, reverberated around the plaza.

"Hey, hey!... Hey, hey!"

A silhouette appeared within the purple smoke, tracing the shape of a tall figure. A man, at a guess. The figure suddenly sprouted a second pair of arms, followed by another, in time with the beat. Then, the smoke swept away to reveal…

A boy band.

Immediately, they broke into song, and the crowd at Jaune's back went wild. People ran forward to gather round the street performance, and he had to move with the rush lest someone got crushed against his back. It put him, Tattletale, and Escha near the front of the audience, a couple of rows away from the cleared area where the performers were dancing.

And, my, could they dance.

"What. Is. That?" Escha whispered in awe from her new perch on his back. Her fur stood on ends, and she wiggled to the music as a child would, knowing not one bit of how to imitate the performers but nevertheless giving her best try at it. Thoughts of staying hidden were forgotten. Nobody paid her attention anyway, caught up in flashy movements and sweet tones of the boy band.

"K-pop!" answered Tattletale with a happy squee. "Holy crap, it is still a thing here!"

Jaune didn't know K-pop from bebop. However, the tune was one he found his feet tapping to and was something Tattletale took to with enthusiasm, the girl grabbing him by the hand to drag him forward for a better view, shimmying her shoulders to match the beat.

He detected a vague Mistral bent to the rhythm, but the thing that stood out was the sheer energy the five men were putting in for what sounded like a simple love song, a downright silly one at that. The lyrics likened the person that the singer was addressing to a soda pop, the meaning easy to understand. Needing someone, wanting someone in their life. Loving their taste, their presence a burst of invigoration to the singer's day.

Filling the singer up? He'd admit to being rather shaky on what that part was about, beyond the obvious.

Simple it may be, the boy band threw their whole heart into the performance. Always dynamic movements, never staying still. They bounced rather than walked from place to place, each person operating in close quarters with four other people without a hitch to their steps. It told of ceaseless practice.

They were dressed quite casually. The front man had an untucked shirt over jeans. One guy wore a sweater, another an undersized shirt with its buttons carelessly undone. One went for puffy sleeves, pretensions undercut by the bashful glances as he adjusted the garment. The last member didn't even comb his hair out his eyes before getting on stage. The disparate colors and styles nevertheless formed a common theme. Little ostentation, none of the frills. This was who they were.

They looked… genuine. Just people, who you might meet on the street. (Albeit, very handsome.)

To contrast it, their every gesture was made with great exaggeration. A hand reaching out, the fingers curling one by one in a come-hither motion. Closing their hands over their hearts and sighing like a lovestruck fool. A thumb-suck to mime drinking from a soda can, at once innocent and flirtatious. Embarrassing actions that a normal person would not be caught dead doing, yet they appeared more real for it. Jaune got the impression that he was watching these men bare their souls to the world.

A tug on his arm pulled him out of the performance.

"Hey Jaune, did you see that?" asked Tattletale.

He rolled his eyes, and gave her a little smirk. "No, Lisa. The singer wasn't winking at you. It's a performer's trick."

Tattletale spluttered, "That wasn't what I'm talking about—mmph!"

She looked down at the finger pressed over her lips, then up at him.

"Come on, let's enjoy this song and not argue about who's right or wrong," he said in a kind tone, leaning close so their faces measured inches apart. "We can talk later… did those guys just shimmer in rainbow colors?"

Tattletale slapped his hand away. "Like I was trying to tell you, dummy."

Huh, now didn't he feel silly.

"They're magicians!" ""They're demons!"" cried a number of voices from beside him.

He flicked his gaze that way, registering a suspicious trio of women who stood out for their distinct unhappiness with the performance. The dissenter among them was in the middle of amending her words to match her companions' ludicrous claim that the singing troupe were demons, while the others looked ready to murder someone.

"I don't know," he chimed in, speaking quietly so he would not interrupt the show, "they could be magicians. Making pretty lights is kind of a core part to parlor tricks."

Three heads snapped toward him, mouths agape. They shared similar mannerisms and tics, their expressions a mirror to one another. It suggested a close relationship of years spent living in the same home. His sisters tended to do that, and he was guilty of it to an extent.

"He heard us!?" one of the women whispered out of the corner of her mouth, oblivious to the fact that he also heard that part. She seemed the most normal of the group, her black hair covered by a yellow hat.

"Uhhh."

That came from the tallest one. Red hair hidden under a cap pulled low, she looked shady and not because of the sunglasses.

"Y-Yeah," she continued, plastering on a smile, "those are definitely magicians. Right, Rumi?"

She nudged the hoodie-wearing woman standing next to her with an elbow. For whatever reason, this person had a cardboard box filled with juice packets in her arms. Jaune's wariness of her grew as the big, wide smile transferred from one face to another.

"Totally magicians," said Rumi, rapidly nodding her head. She then nudged the dark-haired woman, the slasher grin infecting that one, too. "Right, Zoey?"

"Uh-huh, no demons here! Right, Mira?" The now-named Zoey wiggled her elbow in the direction of the redhead, trying in vain to bridge the distance. Her friends pushed it down and told her to 'act natural'.

For a beat, silence reigned in the little bubble formed by their two groups while the performance continued to play in the background for everyone else. Then, Tattletale turned to him.

"Okay, sooo…" She vaguely gestured at the trio. "They're lying out of their butts right now, if you somehow haven't noticed."

He did not bother to question her further, because Tattletale could spot liars from a mile off. He looked at the boy band, who had moved off to the side of the area during the brief moment he took his eyes away from them and were passing out presents to kids while still singing. His mind raced ahead, making the two short leaps to the conclusion that those pretty boys were demons. Flesh-rending, soul-eating demons.

They did not seem the type. Which, he supposed, was the point.

A sword appeared in his hand. "Are we killing them, then?"

Shame. He enjoyed their music.

"Ooooh, I like how this guy thinks." The tall redhead, Mira, gave him an approving look. She motioned with her hand, and a shimmering effect traced the shape of a spear-like implement for a second before the one named Rumi slapped the thing to make it vanish into thin air.

"Mira, this is way too public!" Rumi chided.

Which wasn't a no, Jaune noted. These gals could have made great Huntresses.

Rumi grabbed Mira by the jaw, turning her toward Jaune. "Also, here's a bigger question: how did he just do that? The only people who can should be…" She pointed at each member of the trio in turn.

"What?" asked Mira, voice muffled by the fingers gripping her cheeks. "Are you saying he's one of us?"

Zoey gasped. "Like an overseas version? How come Celine never told us this?"

Off on the sideline, Lisa remarked in a quiet tone, "We've found the K-pop, the demons, and, apparently, the hunters. That was quick."

He went to reply, but before he could, the ground rumbled beneath their feet. More purple smoke blew, and the demon boy band began to rise above their surroundings, borne on a platform that seemed to have sprouted right out of the plaza bricks.

"Jaune, are you seeing a giant soda can, too?" asked Tattletale.

"Yup."

"Just checking." She held out her hand, and Jaune quietly placed a Piero's Remedy in it. She wouldn't need it yet, but they were getting there.

The performance was hitting a high point, the five men pitching their voices louder to whip the crowd in a frenzy. A shared look and, in tandem, they jumped up to then slammed their feet back on the platform. Thereafter, a change overtook the plaza.

New colors swept over the world, emanating outward as a ring from the stage. Don't ask him how, but everything touched by the effect—the road, the buildings, even the clothes people wore—bloomed into vivid shades encompassing the full palette of colors. Purple where there was once white. Gold in place of black. Beige became blue, brown became green. His jacket stayed the same, for which he was glad, possibly due to being already bright and eye-catching. The crowd surrounding him marveled at the wonderland scene, and screamed themselves hoarse for the boy band.

Esha was right alongside him in shouting out their amazement, as Tattletale ran her mouth a mile a minute with theories on the phenomenon, tinkertech special effects at the top of the list. Jaune had an easier answer for that, it was magic. Of the stage or of the ethereal, he could not guess. Some trick of the lights, perhaps, but life grew more real with its presence. Looking around, only now did he realize how subdued the city used to appear, the past a drab and mundane gray. A part of him could imagine that this colorful, shining world was the city as it should have been this whole time.

It… might be worth it to let the demons live.

He then noticed the absolutely feral expressions of the demon hunters. They were not, it seemed, inclined to agree with him.

"The show is ending, this is our chance. Get ready to nab them as they leave," ordered Rumi with none of the earlier silliness. She sounded as if she was used to command. The three women braced to charge ahead.

The performance came to a close with the front man blowing a kiss to the audience that had a fair number of people swooning at the gesture, fans for life going forward if Jaune was any judge. The man followed it up with a devastating finisher.

"Remember, Saja Boys love you!"

"This is it," said Rumi. "Go! Go!—"

With a snap of their fingers, the demon boy band vanished from place to leave only purple smoke.

"...Go?"

Mira pushed down her sunglasses. "What the hell? Where are they?"

"Gone," Tattletale supplied, and she spoke quickly as the trio of demon hunters whirled on her. "The air was displaced, it isn't some kind of illusion or camouflage. Those guys teleported off of the stage."

"They might still be nearby. We'll look for them," Rumi decided.

"Ahem." Tattletale cocked an eyebrow.

Rumi paused, then indicated Mira, Zoey, and herself in turn. "Us we, not you we. But we will need to talk to you later. What are your names?"

He and Tattletale shared a glance. A minute nod of her head, and he spoke up.

"Jaune."

"Lisa."

"Escha!"

He and Tattletale both winced as the demon hunters peered past his shoulder at the cat snapping off a salute.

Mira pointed a finger at her. "Did that cat just—"

"Cuuuuutie!" In a flash, Escha was trapped in Zoey's arms, the woman cuddling the felyne with all her might. "We're taking her home!"

"Zoey, this is not the time!" Rumi growled. "Were taking them all home. But later." She looked back at Jaune. "Meet us at Huntrix Tower. Security will show you in if you give them your names."

Tattletale squinted her eyes. "Huntrix? Where did I—wait, the idol group plastered on every billboard?"

There was no answer. In a blink, the hunters (Huntrixes?) have rushed off into the crowd. They darted past the numerous people in their way without jostling them, the ease of which told of experience that went beyond prancing on a stage. In no time flat, they were out of sight to leave him and Tattletale amidst the dispersing audience.

"What do you think?" Jaune asked, directing a last cursory scan across the plaza before giving up. Things were moving in directions he hadn't anticipated, but by this point he was used to rolling with it. The world was not kind enough that it would wait for him to finish freaking out. "Should we do as she says?"

"We have to, since that Zoey person still has Escha," Tattletale replied.

Jaune slowly blinked at that piece of news, and played recent events over in his mind. Nowhere in there did the woman put down the cat.

"Wait a minute, did we just witness a kitten-napping?" (Not to be confused with a kitten napping, which was a very common sight in their apartment.)

"It should be fine. We know how to find them, and signs point to them being the white hat faction in these parts. For now, let's get out of this crowd and figure out where that tower is." Tattletale looked around, before pointing at one of the side streets branching off of the plaza. Jaune nodded, and led the way. "I also need access to a computer to suss out the story on this demon boy band."

He turned his head as he walked, speaking over his shoulder. "Yeah, what's with that? I was expecting, you know, monsters with big horns and sharp teeth, not pretty boy looks. Is this an Earth thing?"

"Nope. Our concept of them mirrors yours, which is why I'm worried about a second threat. If all these guys do is sing, then it really doesn't justify the danger rating of this world."

Neither of them had any idea of what a 'Broken Honmoon' entailed, but the last time Jaune ventured into a place with this rating, he had a scrap with a fellow named Leviathan. By all rights, the people in their surroundings should be dead men walking. That did not match the vibe he was getting throughout today.

"Maybe we'll have some answers soon from those demon hunters—whoops, sorry!" He had rounded the corner and almost immediately ran into a person there. Stepping back, he slapped his hands together in apology. "My bad, I should have looked where I… I was…"

He fell silent, the smile he wore slipping away.

The front man of the Saja Boys took it up in his place. On his face, it looked just a little too wide. With one elbow propped on the brick wall, the handsome young man leaned forward, and though they were of a height, he seemed to loom over Jaune. At his back stood the rest of his crew.

"So," the man said casually. "Come here often?"

Jaune opened his mouth. Closed it. Opened it again.

"Why does that sound like you're hitting on me?" He could feel Tattletale taking cover behind him to study the situation, a light grip tugging on the hem of his Gallian jacket.

One of the other boy band members shoved his way forward. Back on the stage, he had acted with delicate mannerisms, his more effeminate stylings lending him a gentle air amongst the Saja Boys. Now, he harbored a manic look, staring at Jaune in rapt attention as saliva dripped down his chin.

"Because you look"—he sucked in his drool—"delicious!"

The front man chuckled, taking point again. He put one hand on the other guy's shoulder, the other hand motioning for calm. "Romance, down."

"But Jinu!"

"I told you that we will each get a piece, to make it fair," the front man—Jinu—reassured his ally. He turned to Jaune, showing a disarming grin. "Sorry about him. I'm sure you get this all the time, but you have a beautiful soul."

No. He did not, in fact, hear that often. How flattering.

"Why, thank—"

"Jaune! They literally want to eat you, and then me!" Tattletale hissed.

He slumped in disappointment. "I sort of figured that, yes."

The entire boy band group were sporting yellow eyes by now, and they jostled each other in order to inch nearer to Jaune, prevented only by their leader Jinu. Colorful lines that Jaune had spotted earlier traced up and down their skin, adding an uncanny glow to them.

Jinu leaned even closer and opened his mouth wide, showing off the sharpened canines that weren't there before. He took a deep breath in, and that was when Jaune felt a pull. Unlike the gentle pinch to his jacket by Tattletale, this one plucked at something which had neither weight nor grip. His Aura flickered as it registered damage, and Jaune shivered as he experienced the sense of himself… fading.

Nope. Nopenopenope. He did not like that feeling at all.

He whipped out his hand in the direction of Jinu, his mind running the gamut of options. Should he go for a crowbar or a hammer from the toolbox? The Ruhm rifle to make a serious threat? Red Rook, for the splatter effect?

His sword materialized, sans the malfunctioning shield half that won't retract into a scabbard anymore. The front man startled at its appearance and hurried to back up, but was stymied by his allies behind him blocking every avenue of escape. The blade sliced right across Jinu's throat. A swift, clean end.

"Ahh! AHHH!"

—Or it should have been. Jaune had to admit, he was not expecting the man to have the breath left to scream, and stood there gawking as the person he just killed stumbled around in a panic. That was, until Jinu paused in between shrieking like a little girl and checked over himself with his hands.

"Wait, I'm not dead?" said the man, half in disbelief.

"…He's not dead," Jaune muttered, a bad feeling rising.

Jinu was beaming now, a bright and happy smile with all the elation of a person escaping the noose. He pumped his fists in the air. "I'm not dead! Whoohoo!"

Then, the smile turned downright evil.

"Oh, I get it," Jinu said, resuming his advance on Jaune again. The movements were playful, a stalking gait to draw out the moment. "You can't kill me. That sword is just a hunk of steel, so it"—the hunk of steel slashed through his neck—"doesn't carry"— the blade reversed course to slice his belly—"the power"—neck again—"of the Honmoon and would you please stop that, it's very annoying!"

"Quit trying to eat my soul! That's annoying to me!" Jaune retorted right back. He kept up a steady defensive zone, weaving his sword in quick and snappy arcs that held Jinu at bay while his opponent darted from side to side in the hope of faking him out.

Demons, as it turned out, were not that much stronger than a normal civilian. No faster, either, and so in the span of seconds Jaune had managed to give Jinu a dozen additional cuts for good measure. Horrible rends formed and healed in the blink of an eye on Jinu's body, never quite harming the demon but did interrupt further attempts to nibble on his Aura.

What broke the stalemate was a small click of the tongue. Jinu abandoned his futile endeavor and leapt away from Jaune, turning his head to call out to the demons behind him.

"Guys, a little help here?"

The other four demons heeded the request with a feral eagerness. They snarled and snapped their jaws, abandoning the pretense at humanity to rush forward in anticipation of a feast.

"I'll get the girl!" the one named Romance shouted.

Jaune got to her first. His odds of victory against five indestructible, soul-sucking demons were looking pretty bad—he would go as far as to call them his natural enemy—so he quickly decided that a retreat was in order. Throwing Tattletale over a shoulder, he booked it down the street with the demon boy band hot on his heels. (And hot in general. No, he wasn't jealous.)

"Tattletale, what do I do!?" he screamed as he ran. "This sword can't cut demons!"


-o-​


Apparently, a pocha was the place to go for late night cheap eats in Seoul. So said Mira of the Huntrix, Korea's biggest idol sensation, and she had provided him directions to a good spot she knew. Jaune wasn't sure if that was the same place he currently sat in, since he got lost along the way and ended up just following the smell of cooking, but it turned out for the best, he felt. The big orange tent set on the sidewalk with plastic tables and chairs inside, and three little food carts pushed together to serve as a kitchen, was a place he could vibe with. It was the kind of establishment where a person might find overworked salarymen in one corner, college students at another, and an old granny at a third. One never knew what one might encounter or who one could meet by eating here. It was an adventure.

He needed this, a time for himself to unwind. The rest of the day since the street performance had been… hectic, was a good word.

Running away from the Saja Boys was an easy matter until they decided to teleport. They could, and did, do it consecutively, the bunch of cheaters. In the end, Tattletale came up with the solution, which was to take refuge at the Huntrix Tower before their Aura ran out. Jaune thought it was very helpful and forward-looking of the idol group to have their name emblazoned on the side of the skyscraper for people to find.

The ploy worked, and it said something of the formidability of the Huntrixes that the Saja Boys chose to break off the chase rather than risk encountering the demon hunters. The safety provided by the tower became ironclad once the three women showed up along with a thoroughly-spoiled Escha. Of course, what followed was a grilling of Jaune and Tattletale on both their confrontation with the demons and their background, the latter of which Tattletale managed to fib a story that seemed plausible but did not actually answer any of the Huntrixes' questions beyond the surface level. In turn, they received an explanation as to the circumstances of the demon hunters and the conflict they've stumbled into the middle of. (Plus a secret Tattletale discovered concerning Rumi that Jaune had no clue what to do with and that Tattletale had to be bribed to cease prying into.)

In essence, demons preyed on people and the Huntrixes squashed them flat for the audacity. It was so beautiful a story, Jaune almost shed a tear. The deep connection between them and him had been palpable for a minute there.

The next bit that they revealed sort of broke apart the Huntsman/Huntrix comparison from then on, though.

According to the demon hunters, the Honmoon laid at the center of the affair. A barrier to separate Earth and the place where the demons live, it kept them from running amok all over the planet. Powered by music, music, the ritual worked on a scale he could scarcely believe, the idol unit weaving changes into the world itself each time they put on a concert. Since its inception, humanity only ever faced a fraction of their enemy. From his perspective, the whole business went beyond magic to border on miracles and godhood, done by a couple of singers.

Well, not merely singers. Going on a hunt for demons alongside them made for quite an experience.

The least of it was a cardio workout, because they moved like Ren. A hop, a cartwheel, and suddenly they were running on the rooftops, then halfway down the block in a blink. It took him a fair amount of creativity with [Third Arm] and his boots to stick to their route.

Then, there came the actual fighting. Even if the best he could do was keep the demons in the bathhouse occupied by throwing them around until one of the women finished off the things, he got a first-hand look at the effectiveness of their armament. A shame that the weapons were tied to the Honmoon, and he wasn't a good enough soprano to tap into that for an upgrade to Crocea Mors.

He had brought up the possibility, purely theoretical, of the Honmoon breaking. They… didn't take it well. That subject died quick.

Such talks had given way to a sleepover. Putting aside the awkwardness of being the sole boy there, it felt too nostalgic. So, he left. Tattletale and Escha would be at the safest place possible in the city, meaning he didn't have to shadow them, while he got some midnight grub. With Huntrix on speed dial in case demons showed their faces, he had nothing to fear. A perfect plan.

Hence, him, here. Sitting at a pocha, a place where one could end up encountering anybody. For him, that happened to be a guy named Bobby. And Bobby? Oh, he was great.

"Here, Jaune, try this," said his dining companion, whom he met not half an hour earlier. The short and stocky man—but with hair to die for—pointed at one of the dishes he ordered. Bobby might be a little addicted to his phone, but that came about from work habits instead of introvertedness, and the man had been all too happy to introduce a tourist to the good eats of Korea after catching sight of Jaune hesitating over the menu.

That said, there was a catch.

Jaune leaned closer to the table for a better view of the food. The fried morsels looked tasty enough, albeit unidentifiable.

"What is it?" he asked, having learned his lesson.

"Chicken."

Jaune did not leave it at that. His eyes narrowed.

"Which part of a chicken?"

Bobby waggled a finger at him. "Ohhh, you are in for a treat. This is gizzard, the best accompaniment to a good cup of soju, and don't let anyone tell you different!"

On the one hand, Bobby knew his stuff. His selections thus far had been stellar, from the drinks to the food. On the other hand, gizzard sounded less like meat, and more like an organ.

He understood, in an academic way, that every edible section of a chicken, a cow, a pig or what have you had made its way into his stomach at one point or another. People ground them down and stuffed them in sausages.

But did that mean chicken feet should be grilled as-is and served on a plate? And now this?

"Can I get fried chicken wings, instead?" he asked.

Undeterred, Bobby plopped a hand on Jaune's shoulder. "Trust me."

With a rueful breath, Jaune plucked a piece of chicken innards with his chopsticks and popped it in his mouth. The tough, chewy texture threw him off for a bit, and he spent a long while just working on the gamey morsel. Finally, he swallowed it down.

Bobby, silent this whole time, leaned forward in his seat. The plastic chair creaked under his frame.

"Hmmm?" he said, leadingly.

Jaune avoided his gaze. "...It's delicious," he grumbled.

A whoop, and Bobby raised his glass of soju wine. Jaune followed suit to take his own in hand. They clinked the cups together before knocking back the alcohol.

Afterward, Bobby refilled their glasses.

"Was I right, or was I right?" said Bobby. The man cocked an ear and motioned for an answer, grinning. It turned into a guffaw as Jaune pulled the dish closer to his side of the table. In minutes, the pair had finished off the fried chicken gizzards, along with the last third of the soju bottle.

The bottles sold here came in small sizes, and bore a wide variety of flavors. Jaune was looking forward to trying a new one.

"And we have a lot more where that came from," Bobby continued, which Jaune hoped was meant in a metaphorical way and did not refer to further chicken parts on the horizon. The stocky man rubbed his hands together, peering down at the small menu sheet taped to the table. "Now, what next, what next…"

Jaune pointed to one item. "What is this… jap-chae?"

"A noodle dish, and believe me, the flavor of sweet potato noodles is out of this world, especially when you stir fry it on a fresh bed of veggies." Bobby tapped his chin in thought. "Then again, the shop tends to make it on the greasy side. A little heavy if you just want to taste different dishes, I think."

"Order the tteokbokki. They're always great."

"Oh ho, yes!" Bobby agreed, perking up. "Who doesn't love rice cakes?"

"Nobody. It used to be served in the royal palace, you know. In ancient times. Food fit for a king and his court."

Now that sounded enticing.

On another note, who was talking? Jaune turned his head.

Jinu, demon boy band front man, had taken the seat next to him. The demon poured himself a glass of soju wine, before placing his bottle at the center of the table for everyone to share. An elbow propped on the table surface, he lounged in an enviably casual fashion as if he had always been part of the group.

Recognition dawned for Bobby and he gasped. "You're Jinu! Of the Saja Boys!"

"In the flesh," answered the demon. He adopted a gentle mien, a hand over his heart. "And it is my honest joy to meet a fan."

"Oh, I'm not a fan," Bobby denied with a shake of his head. "The girls were very clear that I am not allowed to be your fan… Great debut, by the way. I watched the video, like, a bajillion times!" He pulled out a notepad, flipping quickly to an empty page. "Can I get an autograph? Right here, thank you. Use my pen."

A giddy squee escaped the thirty-something's throat as Jinu obliged the request, penning a message and signing his name with a flourish. The demon returned the notepad with both hands, an oddly respectful gesture.

"Here, for my not-fan." Jinu finished it with a playful wink.

As Bobby stowed the notepad away, Jaune and Jinu shared a look, holding a conversation with their eyes. Since they were not mind readers, it boiled down to Jaune glaring as hard as he could at the demon and Jinu showing a placid gaze in turn, hoping the intent got across.

I'm stabbing you.
Settle down, snack.

With deliberate care, Jaune changed his grip on the chopsticks, the utensils now poised to drive into Jinu's eye at the first overt sign of aggression. Seeing that, Jinu raised his hands in mock surrender.

The byplay continued on as an oblivious Bobby drew the table into a discussion on the Saja Boys' street performance that morning. He worked in the entertainment industry or something similar, and had a lot of offhand, yet incisive, advice for Seoul's newest superstar sensation. On the other side of the conversation was the fact that his responsibilities involved acting through his ever-present phone against Jinu, and he admitted that right to the guy's face. The stocky man seemed to be tapped into all the happenings on social media, and watching him play public opinion like a piano was a lesson in the liar's art to take to heart.

Delay, distract, defend. The golden trifecta of PR management for an organization under fire. Jaune didn't get much of the whys and wherefores behind this media campaign, but it was an education nevertheless.

He got the chance to put it into practice within the hour. As the tteokbokki, a dish of chewy rice cakes simmered in sauce, and a bottle of plum soju wine arrived at the table, the three men dug in. Immediately, Jinu choked on the food.

"Gack—ahuurgh!"

After a beat, Bobby shot out of his seat to take action. Jaune did not, because if a soulsucker died in purely accidental circumstances? Oops.

"Jinu! Are you okay, buddy?" Bobby called out, trying to slap the demon on the back to dislodge the morsel.

Rather than spitting out the food, Jinu waved Bobby off, miming through desperate gestures that that wasn't the problem. Tears streaming down his face, his eyes bulging, the demon chewed on the rice cake with an expression of torturous agony. Finally, he managed to swallow. His hands then shot out for the soju bottle, forgoing a cup as he gulped down the contents at prompt speed.

Slamming the bottle onto the table, Jinu wheezed for breath.

"Why—" He covered his mouth with a fist, suppressing a burp. Jaune used that moment to snap a picture with his scroll of the demon sporting a frog-eyed look, and resolved to figure out how to post that on the inter-net later, because PR mattered. "Why is it so spicy!?" Jinu cried.

"Tastes fine to me," Jaune said, picking up another piece. The hot sauce drenching the rice cakes held a certain charm he found difficult to explain. A bite of it, and he felt compelled to sip at the plum soju, the sweetness of which then encouraged him to go for more of the spicy snack. They formed a perfect combination.

"Same here," said Bobby as he retook his seat. He bit into his rice cake with relish, and leveled an amused gaze at Jinu. "Have you ever eaten tteokbokki before? Be honest, it's not at all childish if you haven't."

Jinu rubbed at his puffy eyes. "Yes, I've eaten it, and a proper tteokbokki is simmered in soy sauce, not… this! Can somebody please tell me what is the obsession with spicy food nowadays?"

The question drew an intrigued look from Bobby. "Soy sauce? My grandfather loved that version of the dish. He always complains that things went downhill for Korean cuisine after the fifties. I didn't take you for the old-fashioned type, although I can see the quirk working for you. The fans will go wild for it."

How long did demons live, Jaune wondered. Jinu had made a comment that the dish was once served within the royal palace. It now sounded like first-hand experience.

The episode soon passed from their minds, Jinu's embarrassment blunted after a couple more rounds of drinks. For the sake of the culinary-impaired demon, the subsequent plates they ordered fell on the milder side, even if it did not pair so well with soju.

As it often transpired when guys got together, and it seemed demons were no exception in this, conversation drifted toward the subject of the women in their lives. It began with Jaune recounting of Lisa's antics during their time as cohabitants, from her impaling the wall of the apartment with his sword to the disastrous incident where she, relying on her new state of fitness, attempted to practice parkour using the furniture and an instruction video on her laptop. Jinu, in a clear challenge, followed up on it with a story about a stalker almost impaling him with a sword.

Bobby mentioned a group of girls he knew that crashed the company's private airplane into a government-owned conservation area, winning the crown then and there. His prize was a bottle of peach soju, magnanimously shared among the three.

Back and forth they went, the hours passing in a boisterous mood. Once the many tales of bedlam and destruction ran dry, Jinu changed track to 'complain' about the girl who entered a private sauna when he was inside, sounding oh so smug about it. Jaune had to roll his eyes at that because he knew the true circumstances behind the tall tale, but it didn't stop him from firing back with one of his own to kick off a brief, albeit heated, exchange as he and Jinu tried to one-up each other in regard to their experiences with that sort of thing.

It was deep, deep into the night by the time they exited the pocha tent.

Jaune's palm met that of Bobby, then the back of their hands collided. A series of complicated movements later culminated in a finger snap and them shooting finger guns at one another.

"Reeeally?" Jinu asked them, judgment in his eyes. "You have a secret handshake?"

In answer, Bobby turned to him, wiggling his hand in offer. Jinu sighed and proceeded to mimic a pretty spot-on rendition of the ritual. Then, the same took place between him and Jaune.

Midway, the demon leaned in and whispered, "Thirty seconds headstart, go."

"Here's an idea: I'll just lop off your head until you go away," Jaune fired back.

"I'm stubborn."

"So am I."

"Guys?" said Bobby from the sideline, giving them an odd look.

Demon and Huntsman both put on a bright smile, and waved. "Bye, Bobby!"

And as Jaune ran into the night with a demon giving chase, he thought that if this was the life he would lead in this world, then Seoul might not be a bad place to live in.


-o-​


Seoul was a bad place to live in!

Yet again, Jaune leapt high in the air to avoid the demonic security force. At the height of the jump, he stole another few seconds of hang time by activating the rocket boots, spinning round and round as he searched for Tattletale. In his hand, the handgun-like Olfactory Sensor beeped and whined, the bars on the screen oscillating.

The entire time, the Saja Boys proceeded with their concert. The stadium at Namsan Tower was packed with tens of thousands of people, all going "Saja, Saja" in a trance, and the demon boy band was beguiling the masses with their voices to keep them pacified even as a giant, sentient bonfire grew larger and larger.

It annoyed Jaune how in this situation he was still enjoying the performance. He knew he shouldn't, since it seemed to be heralding the end times, yet the song refused to get out of his head. It held an almost hypnotic quality, and he wasn't talking about the brainwashing effect hitting everybody right now. The dance moves meshed with the scary costumes in a way that he felt was plain unfair. Seriously, these guys were evil, but they were good.

The tracker tool emitted a sharp note. He followed the direction it pointed, and zeroed in on the girl he was looking for clear on the other side of the stadium. She wore the same blank face as the people around her and stood way too close to the inferno for Jaune's comfort, the purple flames of the bonfire cast her in its eerie glow.

His boots started to sputter, heating up to an uncomfortable degree as the batteries ran into the safety limit. In the seconds before he dropped out of the sky, Jaune looked for a spot to land. The crush of bodies forced his hands, and he touched down on the long, y-shape traverse stage extending from the main platform. Here, there was no cover, no hiding. He stood facing the fiery visage of the demon king Gwi-Ma.

The flames smiled at him. It was not a nice smile.

"My, does your soul shine."

Jaune cursed, sensing what would come next. He had been largely overlooked by Gwi-Ma these past couple of weeks, at least according to what Jinu let slip. No such luck, now. Direct sight has brought his Aura into focus, meaning it might not be long before the demon king noticed the two other beacons of light hidden amidst the sea of souls populating the stadium—the trapped Tattletale, and Escha who was on the same rescue mission as him.

One thing has been made clear to him during his time in this world. Aura tempted demons like nothing else.

"I would love to taste it."

No sooner had Gwi-Ma declared so, that portals cracked open on the stage. Demons streamed out of them, racing down the walkway.

Jaune maintained a steady calm in the face of the charge. He noted his current location and Tattletale's spot, calculating the best path between them. Along the walkway, then down one of the side wings. Two flights up the staircase would put him on the correct row. It sounded like a plan.

The only hitch to it was the hundred or so demons barreling toward him. Snarling faces filled his vision.

"I keep telling her, 'Put your [Blank] on, I've been hearing voices', but does she listen? Noooo."

Complaining all the while, he drew his sword. The demons were far less afraid of it than most people would be, safe in their knowledge that a simple hunk of steel posed no threat to them. He had no song to empower it with.

Which was why he watched the approaching demons with a careful eye. As the first one came into range, he snapped his fingers and pointed at it.

"Dokkaebi," he identified.

A fistful of red beans appeared in his hand, and he tossed it at the demon. At once, the monster recoiled from the beans, shrieking as if they were spiders and not legumes. In that moment of distraction, Jaune threw a roundhouse kick to its right side.

That detail was very important. The right side.

The demon crashed to the ground in agony, incapacitated even if it could not be killed. The momentum of the creatures behind it caused them to trip over the flailing body, resulting in a pileup that stalled out the horde.

Jaune grinned.

"Beacon taught it best. You have to know your monsters."

A demon climbed over its brethren, glaring balefully down at him. Pale as a ghost, it seemed to exist in a constant state of drowning, droplets of water falling from its long and stringy hair.

"Fool! Let's see that work on me!" it hissed at him.

"It wouldn't," Jaune replied, stepping forward. "Not for a water demon. Your kind doesn't have a specific weakness."

The demon laughed a high, cruel laugh.

That stopped when a glass jar materialized in front of the demon's face, the monster blinking in confusion at the sight. A split second later, Jaune's fist punched through the glass and smashed into the demon's nose. Pale fire thereafter erupted, the demon screaming in pain.

"But, you know what? I came prepared for that!"


Holy Water
Universe: Konosuba: God's Blessing on This Wonderful World!
Blessed by Aqua, the goddess of water herself. Anathema to the unnatural, lukewarm water to everybody else.
Remember her tenets:
1. Never let demons and undead live.
2. Eris pads her chest.
Now, go forth and spread her message.


The world that the item came from had caught his eye back when he was browsing for answers to the demon question. A few tests showed it was good enough for hunting work, in that it burned demons with the efficacy one would find in a vat of acid… and he had more where that came from.

A new jar popped out of his Pocket, and Jaune inched closer to the suddenly uncertain band of demons. One of them tried to shove the demon beside it forward. That became moot as he sprinted at them, roaring his new battlecry.

"Holy water, holy water, holy water, holy water, holy water, holy water, holy water, holy water, holy water, holy hell why are there so many of yoooooou—!"

Jaune raced out of the melee with the demons on his heels, because as it turned out, he hadn't brought that much holy water.

His Aura began ticking down, the demons he couldn't kill sucking away bits of his soul in passing. As he ran, he rang up another order on the Company scroll, and swept his sword through the delivery box as it appeared, smashing apart the glass jar to coat the steel in holy water.

The blade sliced into a demon to dispatch it for good. The next one met the same fate. It worked less well on the third, requiring a new coating. Still, he had a process going to grant him passage all the way to the center of the 'Y', where he ignored the bonfire to advance down the offshoot walkway. Priorities.

He heard the telltale swooshing noise of teleporting demons. The Saja Boys have left the main platform to take up residence on the traverse stage, with the one called Baby then launching into a rap solo.

Jaune happened to pass by Jinu along his path, close enough that either could have reached out and struck the other. Their gazes met, blue to yellow.

Jinu looked away first, and Jaune moved on without a word. Because what the fuck were you supposed to do with a traitor that might have become a friend?

A question he didn't know the answer to, and didn't want to know. Jaune shoved it aside to climb the steps leading to Tattletale.

She barely acknowledged him once he got to her. A dazed flicker of the eyes before turning back to the concert, and not much else. Thinking fast, his solution was to shove a Piero's Remedy between her lips. The label touted a clear mind, after all.

It seemed to bear an effect. Tattletale stumbled, reaching out to grab onto him for balance. She turned this way and that for a brief moment, then clutched her head.

"Wha-Jaune? Who's talking—"

Oh dear. Gwi-Ma still had his hooks in there.

"Tattletale, Lisa, listen to me. Turn on [Blank] right now."

That did it. Tattletale fully returned to herself, which was to say she panicked as she remembered in dawning horror what had happened to her. For whatever reason, she looked at him, and he could have sworn he saw guilt in her eyes.

He raised her chin. "Lisa, focus. We need a plan. Put that mind of yours to work and figure out how we're going to help these people."

It had stuck with him, the thought of what next after this step. Problem was, he had run down the list of options and found no real avenue forward. What even was the threat? A fire? A god? He needed the power of the Honmoon.

And he had it.

The stage grew dark but for a single light. Gwi-Ma growled, and Jaune followed its glare to a figure standing at the stadium entrance.

Rumi had resurfaced from wherever she disappeared to, and suddenly Jaune didn't feel so hopeless about this anymore. That feeling grew as she began to sing, her words replacing the Saja Boys' crooning.

Light shone from elsewhere in the stadium, and he noticed for the first time that Mira and Zoey stood among the audience. The implications of that spelled nothing good, but he took heart as they seemed to wake up from the trance.

"Okay. Okay!" Jaune said, thinking. "The pieces are coming together. We have a shot."

Tattletale did not give a reply. Jaune turned to her, and saw her shrinking back.

"I…"

"Lisa?" Jaune leaned down, looking her in the eye. "What's wrong?"

"He took over my mind…" Tattletale sounded as if the comment had ripped away all her strength.

The mind control had hit her hard, Jaune realized. Harder than it would for him, an instinctual terror born of growing up hearing the horror stories. Her mind was her weapon, her armor, her confidence. To lose it in a blink, it was a fate comparable to death.

"It's alright," he said. His sword vanished, and he held Tattletale with both his hands. "It will be alright."

She shook her head, and in this moment, she resembled nothing so much as a scared teenager in over her head.

"Tattletale, steady. This isn't the worst you've faced. You got this."

Her lips wobbled. She shifted to hide behind his bulk from Gwi-Ma's flames. It was little more than an illusion of safety, but it allowed her to muster the nerves to actually speak.

"He's…He knows everything. Everything. He's a god. A monster. We have to escape." Her voice cracked. "Now."

"The others are here."

Rage, induced by terror, flashed by her face. "So!?"

"I can't leave them—"

Tattletale turned pale as a ghost. Her grip on his arm strengthened. "Then you're going to leave me?"

"No," he replied sharply. Hearing the sound of clashing, he glanced back over his shoulder. The three demon hunters have engaged a new wave of demons, one magnitudes bigger than the wave he battled previous.

They sang in the face of death, and it would be death. The numbers arrayed against them increased with the passing seconds.

Jaune turned back to Tattletale. "Come on, we can't run." Tattletale refused to listen, or let him go. He licked his lips, and spoke again. "Look, you don't think I'm scared?"

She shook her head a second time.

His answer to that was short and sweet. "Ha."

"But… you're you," Tattletale refuted with a lost expression.

He got her point, crude and hurtful as it sounded. He was Jaune Arc. Too dumb to understand fear. Impulsive to the point of fighting Endbringers and armies. The absolute fool.

Huntrix sang their song, and it resonated to the core of his very soul. He closed his eyes, letting the music crash over him as a tide.

"I'm a liar, I'm a coward," he echoed, a confession to the world. He opened his eyes. "I pretend, Lisa. Well enough that I could trick you, because I have to believe it myself."

After all, a hero was brave. A hero was strong.

"It's odd, though. I want to kill my fear, but I always find a new reason to be afraid." He squeezed her tighter, their foreheads touching together. "And that's why… I'm always going to charge back in there. Hang tight, Lisa."

He let her go, summoning his armaments. A scan of the battlefield for where he would do the most good, and he was on the move.

As he left, he felt a shove on his back, pushing him onward.

Elsewhere and a few minutes from then, an angry demon king pushed to the brink manifested his wrath as a gout of eldritch fire. It slammed down upon the target of his ire, and would have ended her life if not for a repentant demon getting in the way of the attack.

Rumi gazed upon Jinu, and tears filled her eyes.

"Jinu? Jinu, stay with me! You can't die!"

The demon gave a gentle chuckle. "Heh. I'll be with you. Always. You gave me back my soul, and now, I… I… Wait, how come I don't feel hot anymore?"

"You still are!"

"No, I mean hot hot. But thank you."

Jinu turned to look over his shoulder. Rumi leaned to the side for a better view.

Jaune, clad in fire-resistance armor, held his shield high to block the flames of Gwi-Ma, steady in the face of annihilation. His arm groaned and creaked, but a flash of light, and he held firm.

"Sorry to barge into your moment," he said. "Are you on our side now, Jinu? When did that happen?"

Also, if Jinu wasn't, then Jaune was totally going to let the shield drop and jump out of the way.

"H-How?" Jinu asked. "Gwi-Ma's flames—"

"It's not all that."

"They don't just burn flesh, they penetrate into your soul!" the demon snapped, incredulity written across his face. "Ripping apart your thoughts! Wiping away your mind!"

He cheated, that was how. "I, uh, I took lessons," Jaune lied. "Never you mind that, does anyone here have a plan to kill him?"

"Why do you think I was trying to hand my soul over to Rumi, fool? It might not have counted for much, but it should have increased the strength of her soul and her connection to the Honmoon to give her a better chance!"

Hold up. Pause.

"It can work like that?" He twisted his neck to an uncomfortable angle to look at Rumi."The Honmoon works like that?" The pop idol nodded. "Oh. Then, we're in business."

And he shoved his free hand in Rumi's face.

"For it is in…"

Power blazed forth from Rumi once he was done, her Aura almost clear as glass. The sword she wielded grew three sizes, and the woman spent a brief instant just marveling at the ease with which she lifted the heavy blade.

"Do you think you can do something with that?" Jaune asked.

Rumi checked over herself, performing some sparkly, swooshy things with her Aura that Jaune was pretty sure shouldn't be possible. In the end, a toothy smile full of confidence was her answer.

"Heh. Heheh. That's great, Rumi. I'm glad it worked out," said Jinu with a satisfied expression, before he slumped to the floor of the stage. Rumi dove for him, holding him in her arms as Jinu hacked and coughed.

"W-What? Jinu, what's wrong?"

"I'm sorry," said the demon, heaving for breath. "The blast—Agh!—the blast took a lot more out of me than I let on."

"Why didn't you say anything?" Rumi cried.

"Didn't… Didn't want to worry you. Needed to know you'll be okay." The demon groaned, his face twisted into a rictus of pain. "Like I said, his attack burns the soul. Looks like… this is it…"

Jaune watched over the scene with solemn dignity. Within his head was a different matter.

Had he really made that entrance just to arrive too late?

Uhhhh. Oops?

No. No, he could still fix this. Demons had souls, right? The man said it himself, he was about to pass his soul to Rumi like spare clothing. That changed things. A way forward remained open.

Jaune backhanded Jinu to interrupt the moment between the two singers. Again.

An abbreviated chant later, Jinu shone with a golden color. More importantly, he appeared fit as a fiddle compared to his previous state. Jaune patted him on the back in congratulations.

"There we go. You're welcome."

Jinu leveled a deadpan gaze at him. Indecipherable thoughts passed over his face. Then, he deliberately coughed into his hand.

"Oh… Ohhh… cough, cough," said Jinu in monotone. "I'm not going to make it…"

Rumi shoved him in a halfhearted manner.

"Quit it, you big baby. Sorry you didn't get to make your big sacrifice, but I'm happy with this."

Rumi looked up at Gwi-Ma, and her eyes gleamed with determination.

"Now, let's take Gwi-Ma down!"

-o-​

As Jaune reminisced of an epic battle, that night's dinner took shape in front of him. Noodles as a main dish, inspired by a few recipes he had the pleasure of recently tasting. Grilled cuts of meat—or rather, the parts of a chicken that was not meat—that hopefully won't poison them all. And, rice cakes simmered in a spicy sauce.

In the midst of cooking, he heard Lisa, who was on the couch playing with Escha, singing under her breath.

"But dive into the fire~" she sang.

Jaune raised his voice. "And I'll be right there by your side~"

A laugh, and Lisa leapt off the couch as Jaune spun around with a ladle held like a microphone, the song's next line on their lips.

Even if they weren't the best singers, their voices combined made for a pretty okay song.


Universe: Kpop Demon Hunters.
Location: Seoul City. Event: Broken Honmoon.
Loot: Huntrix merch, Saja Boys merch, chart-topping playlist of songs


-o-​


Within the Void, a strange and heretofore unknown phenomenon was occurring.

The lovely voice of a girl, singing. Silver hair bounced and swished in an energetic manner as she danced upon an imaginary stage.

"Gonna be, gonna be Golden~!"

If the Outsider could feel annoyed… Well, he wouldn't. What a novel sight in this dark, dark place. A lonely corner of the world, shining bright.

Golden, almost.
