#4,357
Chapter 55: Cat, Bunny, and… Wait, No, Not That One​


"What are those things?"

The words, spoken in what the speaker must have thought a low tone, carried on the wind to reach many ears. Similar questions sparked up and down the city street.

"Naked mole rats? Elephants?"

"Can't be. They're the wrong size on both counts."

"That one's a fox. She smiles like one."

"Careful there. You're profiling."

"Maybe they're pandas."

A brief lull followed the comment, as if everybody was looking at the speaker.

"Wiiith a bad trim? What? It happens. Goes to show how people should always go to their kind of barber."

"There's no way they're shaved pandas. You're an idiot."

"Have you ever seen one?"

"Well, no—"

"Aha! I rest my case. More importantly, though…"

"Are they prey?"

"Or predator?"

Such whispers surrounded Jaune as he strolled down the block. He tried to not let it get to him, striving to see things from their point of view. Confusion colored those comments, rather than outright hostility. Perhaps a touch of fear, too, but not to the level where he should be concerned. Yet.

The thought occurred to him that this might be what a faunus experienced, sometimes. How the tables have turned, with just a small change.

"I think I prefer Rapture," he said, casting another glance at the buildings and roads. The city resembled Vale, somewhat. Perfectly ordinary, in most ways.

Beside him, Tattletale walked with near silent footsteps. The girl looked at him, and scoffed. "The place was a hellhole."

"I'm talking about what it could have been," he clarified. "Ignore for a moment the psychos, the cracked and leaking glass windows that's the only thing keeping the ocean from drowning the city, the psychos in diving suits, the powers that give you cancer, the megalomaniacal psychos, the mind control experiments, and all the other stuff."

Tattletale gave him a deadpan stare. That was a lot to put aside, Jaune would admit.

"In its heyday, the city must have looked quite something," he said.

Rapture was one man's vision, and what a vision. The haunting beauty of the underwater city remained with him, even now. City lights banishing the darkness of the ocean floor. Coral reefs growing alongside highrise buildings. Schools of fish swimming past the viewing window of a lonely upscale private lounge. He could spend a lifetime just staring at it all.

Not to mention the many, many vending machines that the team broke into, as teenage delinquents were wont to do. None of them partook of the needles promising superpowers, because even teenage delinquents shouldn't do that. Selling the lot earned them a tidy sum.

Here, he beheld neither beauty nor profits—at least not outside the norm.

"I'll grant you that," Tattletale remarked. "It was sorta pretty." A pondering expression stole over her face. "And those Vita-Chambers were… interesting."

She fell quiet afterward, and they continued walking along.

A little ahead of the pair, Escha skipped her way down the street. For her, Jaune was giving this world a chance. Dressed in clothes purchased not long ago that she sometimes tug at, she blended in with the local denizens to a startling degree now that they have moved beyond the first frantic hour of finding her things to wear. A wave here, a cry of "Hello!" there, she took to the city like a native.

Nobody batted an eye at her presence, despite her being a walking and talking cat. After all, everyone around them was an animal of some kind.

Every species. Too many species. Llamas exited a department store laden with shopping bags, almost colliding with hyenas in suits rushing back to work from lunch, the commotion watched on by koala children clinging to a playground jungle gym. Cars traveled in two directions, a mammalian face behind each windshield. Horses pointed at him, discussing what manner of creature he was behind their hooves.

A hippo in a polo shirt passing by bumped into him.

"Watch it, freak," the hippo growled, lumbering off.

Surreal.

"You know, I just realized. It's possible that humans don't exist here," he said idly.

"No, duh, genius," Tattletale snapped in a waspish tone of voice. She hadn't taken to this world well. "Nothing we've seen is ideally shaped for humans. The doors, the sidewalks, the cars. They're either too big or too small."

"Right…" Jaune came to a stop, and peered up at the tall, blocky building in front of him. "Let's hope this hotel has rooms that can fit us, then."

Finding accommodation turned out to be a real ordeal this time around, because hotels here came in different sizes. Sure, they 'accepted all customers', but when the door measured half as high and wide as him, Jaune didn't feel very accepted. The building before him ran the other way, the steps leading up to the entrance twice the height as he was used to. A family of porcupines were struggling to climb them while hauling their luggage.

After putting those luggage on the top steps, Jaune moved to the entrance. He had just placed his hand on the door handle when he heard a shout.

"Help! Help! She's gone savage!"

He spun around, nerves and focus shooting up to a state of battle-ready alert. His eyes darted up and down the street. Further back the way he came, he spotted a familiar hippo huffing and puffing as he ran. Behind him, a coyote gave chase, racing on all fours with her teeth baring in an absolutely bloodthirsty expression. Despite the repeated cries for help, the people nearby either froze where they stood or cleared a wide berth in a panic.

Some of his concern bled off, and Jaune relaxed a tad.

"That hippo's got a few hundred pounds on the coyote. He could save himself by falling over…"

A white blur sped past him during his musings. Escha had made no assessment of the situation, didn't care for matchups and advantages. As the coyote leapt for the hippo's back, she found a fluffy furball smashing into her face with full felyne fury, bringing her to the ground with paw punches that had the coyote seeing stars. A boomerang, pulled out from a jacket pocket too small to have fit the weapon, followed up the combo, bonking the coyote on the head to knock her out. In mere seconds, Escha stood victorious over her opponent.

Jaune offered her a high-five (or, to him, a low-five) as he walked up to the scene.

"Nice takedown, Escha," he said.

Escha beamed, lightly slapping his hand.

A sobbing hippo barged between them, knocking Jaune over and sending him rolling along the ground. By the time Jaune raised his head, the hippo had grabbed Escha's paw in both his hands… front feet… appendages, and was shaking it up and down, lifting Escha into the air with the motion.

"Thank you, thank you, thank you! You saved my life!"

Jaune thought it rather overblown for a problem that the hippo could have solved had he not been such a scaredy-cat, but the actual cat here seemed to grow several inches taller as she basked in the gratitude, so he kept his comments out of it. Instead, he moved toward the coyote to ensure there would be no round two.

Tattletale was there, also. The girl knelt beside the unconscious body, curiosity clear on her face.

"Huh…"

"What is it?" he asked, squatting down beside her.

Tattletale shook her head. "No, I'm just surprised. This coyote is a florist. I can practically smell all the bouquets she arranged today. Her clothes suggest mild manners and conservative tastes."

"Not the first person to come to mind as a rabid killer, then?"

"Not even for a minute. I'd expect something less obvious than an attack in broad daylight from that type. Poisoner, maybe." She furrowed her brow. "There's blood on her fur."

Jaune looked where Tattletale directed him. Specks of blood, not much, dappled a spot at the back of the coyote's neck.

"Escha wasn't responsible for that," he said. "She was landing punches to the front."

Tattletale brushed the fur aside, and brought her face close to the coyote for a better view. "I see a raised dot on the skin. It matches what one would get from a needle. That bruising—high velocity impact, shot from a distance. She didn't get this from a doctor's office."

"Might be a tranquilizer dart," he suggested.

"Certainly didn't work," Tattletale muttered. "No, if we consider the timing, it would have done the opposite. Whatever drug the needle held riled her up into this state. She pulled it out in a panic, hence the blood. Then…"

"She went ballistic," Jaune finished for her.

Now, that was a bit more worrying than random street violence. Chemicals that turned regular people into killers sounded like a movie plot.

Like a conspiracy.

He pushed to his feet. "I think we've found the event."

"A part of it, at least," Tattletale agreed.

With the danger passed, bystanders began to congregate. They shifted nearer and nearer to the group, never quite willing to get close to the 'savage' coyote, but too nosy to stay away.

"Did you see that?"

"You mean the way the cat moved? It was amazing!"

"Cheetahs are faster."

"At that size? And look at how she beat down that coyote. Strength of an ox."

"Mom! Mom! She's like a superhero!"

Indeed, Escha had, once again from her seemingly bottomless pockets, produced a domino mask. Jaune always assumed she threw it out after their stint as capes in Brockton Bay, yet there the felyne stood with the mask placed over her eyes, turning this way and that to wave at the spectators.

Envy grew as Jaune realized that Escha was getting the chance to live his dream of masked vigilantism.

Sirens sounded, signaling the arrival of the police. People dove aside as squad car after squad car poured into the vicinity. Officers streamed out of the vehicles, and soon the bulky frames of tigers, bears, rhinos, and a dozen other species surrounded them.

…Why did they have their guns out?



-o-​

​

"...I must reiterate that this city is no place for crazy kooks in masks taking the law into their own hands. They present a clear and present danger to the good people of Zootopia, spreading panic that would disturb the peace.

"If you have information on the whereabouts of this 'Meowsterious Cato Cat' that may lead to their arrest, we urge you to come forward, or leave an anonymous tip by calling…"

"Well, dang," Jaune said, turning off the radio. "This was not what I expected to happen once we gave our statements to the police."

Tattletale, sitting on the parapet wall of the apartment rooftop they were currently on, let out a huff of laughter. "Oh, you sweet summer child. Why would you think that it would end any other way? That there is a person out there solving problems means that there is a problem. Remove the person, and—poof! —no problem."

That was not at all how reality worked, but he got the point Tattletale was making. Superheroes sometimes gave the police a bad look, shining spotlights on crime that the officers had failed, or were unable, to prevent. In an ideal world, the two forces would work together. In Zootopia, the law preferred to maintain the status quo.

The end of that evening's incident had devolved into a chase, with the team forced to find a different place of lodging on the outskirts of the Savanna Central District. The rundown apartment building with peeling wallpaper asked no questions beyond 'where's the money', which suited their purpose fine enough. Gold spoke softly, but carried far.

"I'm not a crazy kook," Escha grumbled. She, like Jaune, stood on the edge of the roof. Windy gusts whipped her fur into a mess, and she peered out over the city from behind her mask, striking an appropriately valiant pose (for a cat).

Jaune leaned down to pat her on the back. "No, you are not. You're a superhero now. Ready to start your training?"

The felyne perked up, grievances forgotten as she rapidly nodded her head.

"Good. Let us begin."

Jaune adopted a wise look, or near enough. Events had pushed him into the mentor role, and while he had little experience as a masked crusader, comic books and his life thus far lent a certain familiarity with what the job entailed.

"You have the heroic pose down already, so I'll skip that for the moment—we can get back to it later to account for different scenarios. What I'm going to go over with you right now is even more crucial: your landing strategy."

"Jaune?"

He waved at Tattletale, indicating that she should leave whatever she wanted for later.

"It is especially important for you. Cats always land on their feet, so cat-themed heroes have to be capable of the same. From any height."

"Jaune?"

Escha slapped her paw to her forehead in a salute. "I'm ready, ready!"

"Escha? Jaune?"

"Remember, it's not just a matter of hitting the ground and living. You have to look cool while doing it. In fact, that's the top priority. The three-point landing is classic, but there are a number of… of…"

Jaune trailed off, staring into the distance. His eyes widened as time went on and he recognized what he was looking at.

Above the city skyline, a beam of light pierced the night sky. It blared a picture, a symbol, to all corners of Zootopia. A round head with vertical-slitted eyes, and two triangular ears, to create an unmistakable outline.

Jaune peered down at the felyne, and she peered back at him. Squatting to match her level, he put his hand on her shoulder.

Two hours in, and Escha had a Cat-Signal.

"Escha, you've made it."



-o-​

​

The police station was a grand edifice of glass and stone, decorated with green spaces atop its roof. A searchlight sat in one corner, still beaming its message despite the building having gone dark for the night. Escha led the team in approaching the apparatus.

They found a small figure pacing back and forth near the light, done for so long that a shallow groove had dug into the grass. Long, pointy ears sprouted above her head, and they twitched and flopped in time with each half-hop, half-footstep the person took. She wore the same police uniform of those that tried to arrest them earlier, raising Jaune's suspicions. Yes, that was the part that he had a problem with.

"A bunny?" said Escha, focusing on a different detail.

Said person stopped in her tracks, turning to the group. Her pink nose snuffled, and on instinct, Jaune recoiled. Crocea Mors appeared and vanished in the blink of an eye.

"Who—Oh—OH!" The bunny caught sight of Escha. "Yes, that's me. I'm the one that put up the searchlight. Judy Hopps. Hi."

Judy Hopps struck a confident pose, chest puffed out. Undercutting it was the fact that she vibrated in place, full of nervous energy.

Escha replied to the gesture in kind. Paws on her hips, she grandly declared, "Lo, citizen. You stand be-fur the Meowsterious Cato Cat. State your business, so that I may enact… justice!"

A short distance behind her, Jaune nudged Tattletale with his elbow.

"I taught her that," he said under his breath.

Tattletale rolled her eyes. "Yes, I know. I was there. Why, of all the things you could have done on our way over here, did you choose to show her how to be a ham actor?"

"A hero does more than punch bad guys."

It seemed to have had an effect on the police officer, in any case. Shedding her jitteriness, Judy Hopps… hopped from one foot to the other, beside herself with glee.

"Wooow! I'm honored to meet you, ma'am—Cato Cat." She zipped forward to shake Escha's hand. Jaune took a big step back. "I've heard so much about your long and storied career." She peeked behind Escha. "And you're the shaved pandas everyone is talking about! Wooow!"

"I… my what?" said Escha, thrown off-balanced.

Jaune chimed in, "Wait, back up. What long and storied career?"

They'd get to the second part of her comment later.

Out of a tiny pocket on her uniform, Judy Hopps retrieved a tiny phone. A few taps on the button and she turned the screen so it was visible to them. Boy, girl, and cat leaned forward, squinting their eyes to read the bunny-sized display.

Tattletale soon gave a long sigh, massaging her temples.

"Of fucking course. People are idiots."

Oblivious, Judy Hopps gushed, "Ever since you stepped out of the shadows, reports about your exploits are surfacing from all over the place. I haven't even heard about half these incidents."

Try one hundred percent, judging by what Jaune was reading. Among the common populace, rumors abounded at the speed of light on Zootopia's newest—or perhaps he should say, oldest—superhero. People were swearing up and down that they had seen, been saved, or, and Jaune didn't know why anybody would tell this lie, been defeated in the middle of committing a crime by the Meowsterious Cato Cat. An entire backstory had formed surrounding Escha's past, dating to almost a century centering on either an immortal hero or a (nonexistent) cape passed down through the generations, complete with an equally 'meowsterious archnemeowsis' orchestrating events in Zootopia from the shadows. Debates raged between detractors who stressed her status as a wanted person and believers in the moral weight of her mission.

Once again, Jaune patted Escha on the shoulder.

"Escha, you've hit the big leagues."

"But I haven't done anything!" the cat whispered in his ear while glancing at Judy Hopps.

"Sure you did. You gave them hope that there's someone out there fighting the good fight. That's like Lesson Number Ten in my (made up) hero course curriculum. You're a day away from graduation."

She stopped short, blinking. "Really?"

"Yup. Nice job."

Escha squirmed with happiness from the praise. Jaune gave a chuckle, and turned his attention back to the bunny.

"I'm amazed they uncovered so much." Yes, he was absolutely running with this. "Which begs the question: how come a police officer wanted to meet a dangerous vigilante instead of arresting her?... Actually, before that, how did you make the signal so quickly in the first place?"

Judy froze. Her eyes darted to the side, sending a guilty look toward the searchlight, and the group followed suit. Laid atop the contraption were pieces of curtain cloth, cut up and sewn in the shape of the symbol they saw in the sky.

"Eheheh. Heh." The bunny scratched her cheek, displaying a shaky smile. "The chief probably won't miss those. I think. I hope."

"Someone thinks they're getting fired~" Tattletale sing-songed.

"I won't!" Judy insisted. "As long as I can solve this case, it will be okay, and with your help…" She looked to Escha. "I know we can do it."

Jaune saw the moment Escha made her decision. Her stance firmed, losing the last of its uncertainty.

"What do meow need help with?" the cat asked, trying her best for a booming voice.

The ecstatic Judy launched into her explanation.

In short? For the past month, predator species within Zootopia were reverting to a feral animal state, popularly termed 'going savage'. Fine one day, rabid the next. They attacked anyone and everyone.

"Mayor Lionheart kept the epidemic silent for weeks until we arrested him for imprisoning affected people in secret, but since then we haven't made any headway in the case. Nobody wants to investigate further! They say it's 'just a thing that happens', and pretend tension isn't rising between prey and predator species. And… and I'll admit that I was responsible for worsening it because of what I said at the interview, but I was wrong. We have to do something before it's too late!"

Above the two shorter members of the conversation, Jaune and Tattletale shared a glance.

Conspiracyyyy!

I called it, he mouthed to her.

No, I did, she mouthed back, bumping him with her hips.

Judy Hopps resumed her pacing. "I can't find a single clue that the chief considers actionable. He's afraid, but he also gave up hope of fixing things and that blinds him to the fact that there's a pattern here. And there is. Somehow. I haven't figured that part out either. Everybody thinks I'm paranoid." She whirled on them, a manic look on her face. "I'm not paranoid!"

One of her eyes was twitching.

Once it became clear that she had finished her spiel, Tattletale spoke up.

"Jaune, bring out the Olfactory Sensor." He did, and she took it from him, brandishing the object before Judy Hopps. "This, might be your answer. It is capable of following hours-old scents even through congested population centers, like Zootopia." Judy's jaw dropped. She beheld the device as if it were a holy relic, understanding its potential in police work. "We can use it to trace the path taken by one of these supposed victims that have gone savage, which could give us a clue on where and how they turned… if Cato Cat thinks it is a good idea."

Escha had been a little lost for a while now, enthusiastic but clueless on how to proceed. Upon hearing herself mentioned, she perked up. "It's purrfect! I agree with that plan. Good work, Tattlemeow!"

Tattlemeow grinned, overlooking her new title (Jaune won't). "Doing my best for the team." She refocused on Judy. "How many people have been captured? Can you gain access to them for us to take a scent sample?"

Here, the police officer deflated. "They were taken away for the sake of everyone's safety. I'm not sure where."

"Who ordered that?" Tattletale asked suspiciously.

"Uh, mayor Bellwether? The police chief, maybe?" Judy sounded unsure, one foot worrying against the ground.

"Hmmm. Investigate them, anyway," Tattletale advised. "For now, we will have to find a new savage animal to tag."

"Can you not say it like that, Tattletale?" Jaune asked, distinctly uncomfortable.

"Like what?"

"Nevermind. We can talk about faunus issues later."

Before they left the rooftop of the police station, Escha requested a piece of curtain fabric. Judy handed over the lot, eager to dispose of the evidence. With Jaune's and Tattletale's help, the felyne fashioned a cape from the cloth.

"Heeeelp!"

Right on time, because duty called. This city cried out for a hero.



-o-​



It didn't take long to find more people that have gone savage. Between a couple of muggings and a break-in, the Meowsterious Cato Cat stopped three feral attacks before the clock even struck midnight.

According to Judy Hopps, the incidents used to number once a week at most. It pointed to an escalating pattern that had the bunny fretting with dread.

The first specimen yielded nothing much of note. They found his home, his workplace. He lived in the central area of the city, near downtown. Signs indicated he spent his whole day in that vicinity. The second mirrored the story. In both cases, the areas where Tattletale suspected they became feral had long been swept spotless—Zootopia hired a pretty good street cleaning crew.

The third person, they traced to an alleyway. The brawny tiger thought to take a shortcut to his house from a late night snack run. He never made it home, or got to eat his pudding.

That alleyway held a needle syringe. The scent gained from it was still fresh, and led them…

"Are you s-sure it's here? This place is kind of d-dark," said Judy Hopps, peering into the partially—the suspicious mind might say hastily—bricked-over entrance to the abandoned subway.

"And s-scary," Escha added. She wrapped her new cape around her body for comfort.

Judt turned to her. "Hm?"

"Nothing. Ahem." Escha deepened her voice and straightened up. "It's nothing. Fear not, citizen, fur I shall head in first, and we will solve this case in two shakes of a cat's tail!"

Judy moved aside to allow Escha passage, in the process forcing the felyne to commit to her boast. As Escha inched her way deeper into the tunnel, the bunny squeed in a quiet voice, "So cooool!"

Jaune hurried forward to catch up to the trembling Escha, handing her his scroll with the flashlight on. It earned him a grateful nod, and he hung back afterward to walk beside Tattletale, letting Escha have the floor. She still didn't seem to like the tight confines of the passageway, but the bright illumination helped somewhat to steady her nerves.

The abandoned subway ran beneath the city, most of it below the new subway system itself. Once in a while, the whole tunnel would shake as a train raced overhead. Every time, it caused water to drip down on the group, the growing dampness of their clothes and fur not helped by the puddles of water, inches deep, splashing up due to their footsteps. Various bugs and creepy crawlies inhabiting the cracks in the wall added to the slog.

There were sounds in the darkness. Wails and groans to raise shivers up their spines. It was as if they had entered the underworld.

At one point, Tattletale shifted a step closer to murmur in his ear. "Jaune, your five o'clock."

He made a soft noise in his throat to acknowledge her instruction, and directed a subtle glance over his shoulder. As they reached a bend, he performed an abrupt dash back the way they came. Movements in the dark revealed his target, and he seized them by the neck.

"Got you!" he crowed. Strained grunts answered him, flailing limbs trying and failing to make him let go. Ignoring the pathetic blows, he hauled his captive into the light, revealing their face.

"...Tattletale, is this your long lost cousin?"

"Oh, shut up. I look nothing like that."

The fox in his grasp displayed a very familiar grin. Feigning nonchalance despite the hostility most of the group directed his way, he waved at them. At Judy Hopps, specifically.

"Hey, fancy meeting you here," said the fox, voice raspy due to the fingers wrapped around his throat.

"Nick?" Judy asked incredulously.

"That's me."

Judy stumbled nearer to the fox. "What are you doing here!?"

"Oh, you know. Was in the neighborhood. Thought I'd say hi."

"You… You said you didn't want anything to do with me anymore…"

Okay, there was a story between these two. That didn't sound like words a police officer said to a perp.

The fox averted his gaze, shrugging. "I wasn't lying. Saw you earlier, walking into a rough spot of town with a pair of shaved pandas. Figured I'd check it out."

Aaand now the bunny was getting teary. Judy wiped at her eyes, then rushed forward.

"Tall guy, bring me up!" Nick yelped, slapping Jaune on the arm. "Bring me up! Bring me up—Aw, too late," he whined and fell limp as Judy squeezed him in a hug.

To undermine his show of reluctance, he eventually returned the embrace.

"By the way, for the non-mushy types among us, there's something up ahead," the fox added after an uncomfortable silence.

"What?" Judy shouted, releasing him and spinning around.

From four different directions, the group hissed at her. "Shhhh!"

The bunny clamped her hands over her mouth, and said in a softer volume, "Sorry."

Heeding the new information, they crept forward. Well, most of the group crept forward. Jaune carried Nick by the neck for part of the way until the fox awkwardly coughed into a hand, which reminded him to let go. Barring that bit, they were working as a well-oiled machine.

The object that the fox pointed to turned out to be a subway train car, rusting and graffiti-ed, sitting in the middle of the tunnel. At first glance, it looked like an old piece of equipment left behind by the times. The music at the edge of their hearing that emanated from it suggested another story. Escha shined the scroll's flashlight onto a window, and complete darkness greeted them instead of the train car's interior.

"The dust is disturbed," Tattletale observed. "People have been here recently. Windows are covered with black tape. Needless to say, that's the kinda trick you do when you're up to no good." She pointed the Olfactory Sensor at the train car, and the graphical display went nuts. "Oh my! Who would have ever guessed? The serum driving people mad originates from there," she deadpanned.

Escha and Judy Hopps looked at one another. As one, they nodded.

""Chaaaarge!"" the two cried as they rushed the train car. The door crashed open, revealing a purple tint to the inside, then slammed shut as cat and bunny entered within.

After a beat, a far more subdued "Chaaarge…" followed from Nick, who jogged over to the train car. He slid the door aside, and politely closed it behind him to plunge the subway station into darkness again.

Screams, gunshots, and squeaky battlecries soon rose from the train car. The carriage shook on its rusty wheels, rocking from side to side.

"You're not going in?" Tattletale asked him.

"Nah," he said, crossing his arms and leaning back on a pillar to wait out the battle. "This is Escha's show. Let her have her moment."

Jaune Arc's (Fake) Hero Lesson #11: A hero did more than punch bad guys. Until it was time to punch bad guys.



-o-​

​

"Shame we never found the mastermind behind the drugmaker," Jaune said as he lounged on the couch of their otherworld apartment.

"Eh. We resolved the event." Lisa gave a casual shrug, fiddling with the Company scroll. She used her feet to shove his legs aside, vying for more couch space. "All's well that ends well."

"True."

With the lab pumping out the feral serum turned over as evidence and the sheep producing them behind bars, the spate of attacks were expected to subside. The portal had acted up soon after, signaling the end of the crisis.

The continuing battle for justice laid in the hands of Judy Hopps, police officer by day, Zootopia's newest caped crusader by night.

Suddenly, Lisa bolted upright.

"Holy crap!"

"What?"

"The drugmaker is a sheep. The new mayor who piggybacked on the chaos to get her position is a sheep. They were in it together!"

"Lisa, that's profiling. Speciesist, even."

She gave him a gimlet stare for a bit before deflating, sitting back on the couch.

"Aw, whatever. I'm definitely right, but who cares now? I'm not exactly keen on going back there."

"Is that a no go on living in Zootopia?" Not that he expected otherwise.

Lisa nodded. "It feels too much like an eternal furry convention for me to settle down in."

"A what?"

"Never mind that. What about you, Escha?"

Over by her garden, Escha put her watering can to the side. She mulled on the question, rubbing her chin with a paw. Then, she smiled.

"Humans are funny, so I want a world where there are some around."

Lisa laughed. "Glad we think alike. I'll keep that in mind."

The apartment settled back into lazy repose, each person doing their own thing. It didn't last long.

"Speaking of conventions," Lisa remarked, tapping on the scroll, "want to go to one?"

Jaune raised his head off the couch's armrest. "What do you mean?"

Lisa turned the scroll around, letting him see. It was opened to the Marketplace app, and in addition to the usual category tabs and item pictures, there now featured a new banner rolling along the top of the screen.

Advertisements in the app. Greeeat.

"There's one happening in a few days, sponsored by the Company," Lisa explained. "We can get a peek behind the curtains."



Universe: Zootopia.
Location: Zootopia. Event: Night Howlers Conspiracy.
Loot: The Meowsterious Cato Cat's superhero outfit.​

#4,478
Chapter 56: Jaune and Lisa Go to the Convention (Pt. 1)​


Three people stood before a blank wall. Each of them had their own tells, from hair-twirling to hands clenching, which conveyed the mix of eagerness and trepidation warring within their chests. Today was the day they attended a convention. Only a few minutes remained until their designated entry time slot.

"Valuables to trade?"

"Check."

"Investigation list?"

"Check."

"Weapons?"

"Che—" Jaune fell quiet with a guilty look. Lisa paused between her questions, and looked up at him like the cat that caught the canary. Over time, she shifted to a stance of arms crossed and her foot tapping against the floor, regarding him with a half-lidded gaze.

"Jaaaune."

He raised both his hands to ward her off. "Hey, you never know when we'll need a quick (and violent) exit."

"Don't think I didn't hear that part," Lisa growled, and Jaune glanced away. "We're going to keep a low profile while we're at the convention, right? So no fighting, right?"

"Definitely. Heard you loud and clear." A pile of weaponry appeared next to him. Notably, it was missing Crocea Mors.

Lisa gave him a pointed look, before letting it go. "The rules were clear. That Company is guaranteeing neutrality and I don't wanna find out what they do to people that break it. I'm not ending up in that damn catalog."

Right. The catalog. An entire section of the Marketplace that he dared not to touch. That was another issue he didn't know what to do with. Curiosity burned, but he had a feeling he wouldn't like the answers.

Lisa looked from Jaune to Escha, who was scratching her ear. "[Blank] check."

Both of them saluted in reply. "Done."

"Good. Keep it on."

"Lisa?" Jaune asked.

"Yeah?"

"[Blank] check."

She matched his gaze for a beat too long, then huffed. "Okay, it's done now."

"I'll trust you on that." Not like he could verify it. "Just remember Jax and all those abilities he had on the scroll. I know you said the rules of the convention basically prohibit mind-controlling others in attendance, but I wouldn't put it past people to try anyway."

He kept the Company scroll open to a nifty little power called [Mind Defense] for that very purpose. It went further than the ever-reliable [Blank] that hid him from those that might target his mind to promise outright protection against all manners of mental manipulations and related methods of emotionally enthralling a person. For good measure, Lisa suggested leaving the device with Escha, in the thinking that a bad actor was sure to target him or Lisa first, but overlook the cat. One tap of the screen would free him.

As he watched faint swirls of energy forming on the wall, Jaune considered the scenario further to weigh what he could do in a matter of seconds under someone else's order. Could he truly take that risk?

"Escha, change of plans. Can you press the purchase button?" He nodded to confirm as she peered up at him. "Let's play it safe."

That meant 2,000 Points from the joint funds, but who was counting. Money well spent for peace of mind, quite literally in this case. Even Lisa did not object, and in fact she breathed a sigh of relief, her cheapskate tendencies regarding their balance dulled by concerns of being 'Mastered'.

"Got it!" said Escha, giving him a thumbs-up. "So I just… touch it?" She slapped her paw on the holographic display.

A whole lot of nothing happened, which was to be expected for such a power. Times like this, he wished the status screen wasn't stuck on a dead man's profile and instead showed his parameters. Still, drawing on his experiences with [Blank] and the Pocket, Jaune searched the depths of his thoughts for some form of trigger or dial to the new ability.

After several futile seconds, he tilted his head. "What the hey?"

"Um. Ummm!?"

Something odd was going on with Escha. She hopped up and down with her ears turned to the ground, as if trying to dislodge an object stuck in them. When that didn't work, she wiggled in place for a while, until whatever bothered her went away.

Jaune had a bad, bad feeling.

"Oho," Lisa muttered. "I had wondered."

"What is it? What's going on?" he asked.

"It was just a minor suspicion of mine, but… Whenever I buy items from the Marketplace, they appear in front of me. Not you."

It took a bit, but understanding dawned for Jaune. The assumption was one he never thought to test, whether the Company scroll belonged to him and him alone. The inventory page suggested so. Yet, the status screen seemed adamant that the scroll was owned by a dead man. Meanwhile, Lisa shopped on the Marketplace from time to time, and the delivery boxes were always sent straight to her. The difference between commodities and powers… Were there any?

"You're telling me the one among us least in danger of getting mind-controlled is now the one with defense against it?"

"Yuuup. Good thinking, Jaune." Lisa retrieved the scroll from Escha, navigating to another page. "Thanks to your brilliant plan, a maybe 2,000-Points purchase is gonna have to be a definite 10,000. And you wonder why I say to run things through me first, silly man," she rebuked, and pressed to confirm sharing the talent between them all, at four times the cost of the original ability.

Despite hiccups, he found it hard to be too upset over the outlay for what he was getting in return.

Gone were the days where Jaune Arc could be manipulated, and that was just fine in his books.

Lisa grinned.

"Let's go to a convention."


-o-


ConCon ~ Where Dreams Come True​


"They copied that straight from Disney," Tattletale complained the moment they came through the portal and saw the banner. Decked out in her supervillain costume, stylized eye at the center of her chest, she sniffed in disdain at the unoriginality on display.

Jaune did not remark on it. Never mind that he held little notion of who this Disney was, he… he had bigger problems.

In another life, one in which Jaune failed to reach the scroll in time, perhaps Jax would have gotten his last bit of revenge as Jaune joined him in the grave. It was one of those midnight thoughts to keep him awake in his bed staring at the ceiling, remembering in vivid detail how he had come so very close to the end of his tale. An upsetting what-if, and nothing more.

Except, Jax Darkphenix was standing in front of him.

Right in front of him. Jaune would recognize those unruly yet silky locks of dark hair anywhere. Blood pounded in his ears as he stared at the monster who should be long dead.

The boy was taller than Jaune, bearing a lean frame that one might call svelte if not for the compact muscles visible beneath his tight shirt. Handsome features adorned an angular face, intelligent and kind. He stood with his back turned and his head on a swivel, emerald-green eyes taking in the massive room they were standing in, oblivious to Jaune standing behind him.

The perfect position for a stabbing.

Tattletale caught his hand as it formed an empty-handed sword grip. She hissed at him, "What are you doing?"

The interruption caused Jaune to lose his chance. Jax proceeded down the ramp of the futuristic portal serving as entrance and exit to the convention. His footsteps rang out on the cold metal as he moved in a manner Jaune remembered all too well from their Beacon days, with a swaggering gait that told of utmost confidence. He passed by another person coming up the other way.

Who was also Jax Darkphenix.

Tattletale followed his stupefied gaze to the object of his focus. She squinted her eyes, puzzled.

"Holy handsomeness, I get why you were looking—Wait, that lighting-shaped scar! Is that Harry Potter!?"

Literally who?

He pulled Tattletale to the side as the second Jax passed by them, and prepared for a fight. Yet, their eyes met for a split second, and in those pools of emerald Jaune found no recognition. The dead man walking continued on to vanish into the portal, his dark cloak trailing wisps of smoke in his wake.

He felt a tug on his pant leg.

"Who was that? Did you know him?" asked Escha.

He let out a heavy breath. "Yes. That, was Jax Darkphenix. I killed him."

"No, that's Harry Potter, and Voldemort was the one to do him in!" Tattletale retorted, with the same strange emphasis on the unfamiliar name.

Or maybe not that unfamiliar. Jaune had a vague recollection of hearing it before, somewhere.

Seeing his confusion, Tattletale added, "He's a character from a book series. Messy hair, green eyes, and a scar on the forehead? There should have been glasses, too, and I thought he was supposed to be kind of short, but in broad strokes, it's him."

Jaune furrowed his brow. "You mean, that's not Jax?"

Tattletale opened her mouth to reply, but stopped short as she scanned the crowd.

"...Ask again later," was her eventual answer. She pointed down the ramp. "I'm seeing, like, twenty of them right now."

The convention space was big. As in, 'multiple sports fields' big, with doors leading to offshoot areas. Booths were set out in long rows, back to back to minimize wasted space. At the basic level, Jaune could wrap his head around the concept they were going for.

The details were where he floundered. The 'contractors' that gave ConCon its name had taken an individual flair to their booths, with temporary walls of canvas, energy barriers, actual trees, and whatever else to tickle the stall owners' fancy springing up to partition each space into its own spacious cubicle, measuring almost the size of their apartment. Inside them, special effects abounded and it was a coin flip on whether they came from magic spells or sci-fi machines, lights and shapes crashing into those of the neighboring booths to create explosions of colors that hurt the eyes, competing for attention.

A second market of booths floated high above. It resulted in less traffic, but that seemed how the people manning them preferred it, most of their time spent spectating the rowdy hubbub below.

Within this scene strode a parade of identical faces. A cold shiver danced up and down his spine as he spotted dozens of Jaxes (or Harrys, as the case might be). They differed in manners of dress, the colors and cut and whatnot. Still, all of them carried that unmistakable presence of kindness mixed with what Jaune now recognized as arrogance. It created a rather uncanny deja vu effect, and furthermore begged the question of why somebody from Remnant would share a face with a fictional person he had never heard of in his world yet was instantly recognizable for a girl of another universe. The Marketplace offered a slew of visual enhancement options, he knew that, but the sheer coincidence of selecting one that a whole bunch of other people chose stretched the limits of credulity. Unless, it was a bestselling pick?

That said, the Jaxes represented nowhere near the biggest example of this phenomenon. A young man with blond hair and what looked like drawn whiskers on his face took that title. At least for this one, Jaune was dead certain he never met a version of them before in his life. The young man and his doppelgangers possessed tall, lean frames that one might call svelte if not for the compact muscles visible beneath their clothes.

A man with dark hair and a cool expression also shared a few brothers. As a group, they possessed tall, lean frames that one might call svelte if not for the compact muscles visible beneath their clothes. Occasionally, wisps of a blue, flame-like Aura emanated from them. They appeared very antagonistic to a different set of identical siblings, often engaging in staring contests with white-haired men whose eyes glowed with the luster of the Okinawan ocean.

And yes, the white-haired men possessed tall, lean frames that one might call svelte if not for the compact muscles visible beneath their clothes.

"There has got to be a word for that body type," he said, pointing at the nearest specimen.

"A swimmer's build," Tattletale informed him while staring hard at the young man in question. "Only… ramped up to the 0.1 percentile. Olympic athletes would sacrifice their firstborns to be that cut."

"Don't drool, now," Jaune said, and winced as he realized that had been a tad unkind. The uncanny level of beauty that these men shared had stoked a ugly feeling in him, a crawling envy that soured his thoughts. It didn't save him from the scathing glare Tattletale sent over her shoulder as she, Jaune, and Escha made their way forward.

"I could say the same to you. Try to keep your eyes above those strippers' neck level, Jaune."

That, too, was unkind. The gorgeous women that he had done his best to overlook —not well, considering he could describe their beauty—might work in any number of professions. The fact that some were wearing what amounted to strings undermined the point a little, but on the other hand, some dressed chaste as nuns.

Jaune passed by a group of women moving in the opposite direction.

—Or just straight out dressed as nuns.

Leaning over, he sniped back at Tattletale, "You talk like you aren't getting eye candy of your own."

Here, a group of men in classy butler outfits. There, nothing but speedos and bulges. The swimmer's build was in vogue, with Jaune among the rare few men in attendance missing out on the trend. Not to mention, they had faces that put regular guys to shame.

Jaune and Tattletale shrank smaller the further they walked, confidence fleeing as they examined themselves. There really was no comparison.

"You are cute, don't think otherwise," Jaune said to cheer up Tattletale.

She returned the gesture in kind. "And you aren't awful on the eye or anything, so there's that."

They both sighed.

"You two are silly," Escha opined. She moved through the crowd with calm aplomb, unaffected by the ranks upon ranks of supermodels that all belonged to the wrong species. The convention had a serious flaw, a dearth of felines. Cat ears? Oodles of them, both faunus and of the artificial headband variety, but no actual cats.

"Life sure is nice for you, Escha," Tattletale groused, before turning back to Jaune. "Whatever. Have you noticed?"

"That the ratios are skewed weird?"

Tattletale nodded.

At a glance, the convention hosted a similar number of men and women. Scale it down to the group level, and a pattern started to emerge. Many women to one man, or many men to one woman. Even behind the booth counters, this trend prevailed.

"But the outnumbered person holds the leash in these dynamics."

"Did you get that from your power?"

"No, it's just obvious."

And enviable, once again. Few alive had not imagined a retinue of beauties catering to their whim. Jaune definitely was guilty of that. Yet, the people here lived it, walking tall with their companions hanging onto their every word, their charming wit raising laughter and blushes.

Jaune shook his head to clear away the useless fantasies. An uncomfortable sensation settled in his gut. The situation was pinging his memory, the loving expressions on some of these faces reminding him of old Beacon schoolmates. But surely not? On this scale?

"Different world, different dating norms, I suppose," Jaune reassured himself. "Putting that aside… Why is there so much porn?"

So, so much porn. Now that they were wading in the thick of things, he got to have a good look at the wares on offer, and he quickly learned that it did not matter what the theme of a booth was, they had smut for sale. His third time in a minute walking through a holographic nude dancer (Actual* AI, the advertisement promised) drove home the point. Even Tattletale, who tried to steer them away from the booths that carried porn at first, soon had to revise her criteria. It was ubiquitous.

He slowed his pace at a particular booth, whose walls featured life-sized posters that bared all. The reason why he did it escaped him, until it clicked for Jaune that the women helping the stall owner sell those posters were the models.

Tattletale scoffed, reading the placard on the table. "The Norns? Credits for creativity, I suppose. Was the classic 'Aphrodite' not available?"

"Section BB, Aisle 18, Table 6," a passerby helpfully provided, drawing a strange look from Tattletale. The lizard faunus moved on, scaly tail undulating behind him.

A lot of lizard faunus around here, now that he thought about it.

Once they had made peace with the prolific amount of porn, other goods for sale began to stand out. Bottles filled with glowing substances that were surely good for you. Portraits that moved and talked to the customers. Mangy dog-things hissing and spitting acid, sharp teeth biting on their cages.

They stumbled across a bookseller, whose features should have made him plain and nondescript, and he humbly described himself as such, yet ended up with him appearing as beautiful as the people browsing his wares. The dusty covers that a busty shop assistant wouldn't let Jaune touch promised magic at his fingertips should he learn the spells contained within. The prospect of throwing around fireballs held his interest despite the bookseller spending the whole time trying to segue into stories of how he acquired the collection. That was, until he saw the price.

"Is there an extra zero by mistake?" he blurted out.

"Look, this isn't Skyrim magic. It's DnD."

"You say that like it's supposed to mean something to me."

The bookseller leapt from his seat, hands held out in a strangling motion. He stopped before making contact with Jaune, settling instead for a scowl.

"You buying or not?" spat the bookseller, eyes crackling with arcane light.

Not, as it turned out, and Jaune left the booth with hurled insults of 'philistine', 'sword polisher', and 'Miles Luna self-insert', whatever that was, at his back. He put it out of mind, a more important concern making itself known.

"Tattletale, I don't think we can afford much here."

Having picked up Escha, Tattletale hugged the felyne to her chest. "We have gold and gems…"

Jaune pointed. "There's a tree growing them at that booth, I'm pretty sure they're worthless to these guys. And not to diss that bookseller, but the spellbooks were kind of underwhelming for what they cost."

"Oh, all of it was junk," Tattletale agreed.

Escha gasped. She, too, dreamed of mastery over the elements (mostly so she could water her plants) and to hear the magic books dismissed out of hand had given her a shock.

"How he sneers at his customers is a dead giveaway," Tattletale explained. "I bet you he kept the good ones for himself and just wants to make an extra buck scamming rubes like you."

"Hey! I didn't fall for it!"

"But you almost did, until you caught the price tag. Didn't he, Escha?"

"Uh-huh, uh-huh, you were reaching into your pockets. I saw it."

Betrayed by a cat. Woe was Jaune Arc.

"Should we dip, then?" he said, scratching Escha under the chin in an effort to slowly win her over to his side again. "I can't put my finger on it, but something about this convention creeps me out."

The shop girls smiled too much.

Tattletale bit her lower lip, thinking. "Not yet," she decided. "It's still early on and if possible I want to sniff out details on the Company. Besides, if the contractors are selling stuff they don't need, then they could well settle for lower than market price. There's an opportunity for us to gain better stuff than otherwise, we just gotta be careful with our spending. Haggle with them."

The occasion arose a few stops over from the bookseller, at a booth styled in militaristic decor. Flags of unknown nations festooned the walls, and the blond man with his boots kicked up on the counter wore the clothes of a general, rows of medals pinned to his chest that clashed with his youthful countenance, and especially with the whisker markings on his face. This stall was more Jaune's speed, showcasing weaponry of all stripes. Lightsabers hung on a rack, allowing him to see the energy swords in person for the first time. A video screen set next to the rack followed the general as he battled an army of robots while dual-wielding the lightsabers, as a display of their effectiveness.

"Each one taken from a named Jedi or Sith," the general boasted.

Jaune didn't understand why that was an impressive feat, considering the rarity of a person lacking a name of some sort. He refrained from asking, so as to not reveal his ignorance further—the elbow nudge from Tattletale was quite unnecessary. In any case, Crocea Mors worked as a perfectly serviceable blade for his purposes, making the Jedi weapons a curiosity at best.

His sword cut, and what it couldn't cut, he'd bash with his gunlance. Simple.

It was what laid beyond those scenarios that he sought an answer for, and as he skimmed over the various laser guns, most of which he could find comparable performance in his Ruhm rifle, he directed a question to the general.

"Do you happen to have anything with a little more oomph?"

"Do I—Who do you think you're talking to? Of course, I got more oomph. Check this baby out!"

The general snapped his fingers, and one of the women working the booth immediately placed a cigar between his lips, lighting it up. His eyes crossed to look down at the cigar, then up at the woman in form-fitting red bodysuit.

"Asuka, go into the corner."

"What? Wait, did I get it wrong? Hang on, let me—"

The general's voice brooked no disagreement, the earlier boisterousness turning flat to become almost devoid of emotions. "Corner, now. Rei?" The general did not spare the woman in red another glance. Oblivious to the looks that Jaune, Tattletale, and Escha were giving him, he snapped his fingers again. A woman dressed in a white bodysuit took it upon herself to cross the floor, and pulled on the tarp covering a bulky figure in the back of the booth.

The cloth slid to the ground, revealing the metal form beneath. Painted in a deep blue, it bore a rugged appearance, resembling a person without a head. Angular steel shaped the arms and legs, and glass panels created a canopy where the torso would be, allowing Jaune to see the seat within.

At the sight of the mech, a name sprang to the tip of his tongue.

"It's a Pala—"

"Meet the Amplified Mobility Platform!" declared the general, growing animated once more. He tilted on the back legs of his chair to better look at the mech. "Coming at you straight from Pandora!" He coughed. "The thing's a Mitsubishi, but let's not hold that against it. I picked it up during a hot alien binge—it happens," he insisted as an aside. "Never used it myself, so it's in great condition."

Jaune noticed a problem right away.

"There's no weapons." Disappointing.

"There could be." The general pointed at the robot's hands. "See the articulated fingers? Inside the cockpit are openings for the pilot's arms, enabling precision control. It also allows a bit of tactile feedback so you can feel what the suit is holding, which is usually a huge, fuck-off autocannon that fires 5-lb rounds. The army used them to fight giant blue aliens."

Tattletale barged forward, cutting into the conversation. "What are the specs? We would like to see those before we consider making a decision. Do you have benchmarks? Service records and field test results, too."

A blank stare greeted her. The general then turned his head to look at Jaune. As the silence stretched on, Jaune was compelled to speak.

"Yeah, all of that."

The general shrugged. "Don't got them. It's a mech. You get in and pilot it. It can lift a ton, punch through brick walls, and survive in the vacuum of space."

The man could see that he was losing them. Sitting up, he changed his tone.

"It's a steal, believe it. Forty thousand Points, comes with a complement of weaponry and ammo. You won't find a better offer."

His assistant rolled a cart next to the mech. Jaune would describe the rifle resting on the cart as more of a gun emplacement or a tank cannon. It would take a team of normal people to barely lift. A bayonet was affixed to the underside of the barrel, with a combat knife scaled to the robot's size leaning against the gun, the blade measuring three feet long.

If Jaune had one of these when fighting some of the things he faced, there wouldn't have been a battle.

"The store page is listing it for twenty," Tattletale remarked, having looked up the mech on the Company scroll.

The general blinked in confusion, glancing from her to Jaune.

"Wait a sec, wasn't he the…"

Tattletale cut him off. "We'll give you seven thousand for it, since it's secondhand."

"No way," came the immediate protest. "I told you I never used it!"

"Well, somebody died inside the robot." The girl pointed to a stain on the seat.

"What, that? Don't mind it."

"Too late," said Jaune. "So, seven thousand? You said it yourself that you don't ever ride the thing. It's gathering dust."

Even he could tell that was a lowball offer. Still, it sounded palatable when compared to the eye-wateringly prohibitive price the general wanted. He looked at Tattletale, getting a nod in return. Like him, she believed the mech was a decent possibility for purchase, representing a marked increase in their firepower.

Not the best option for a lot of the situations they find themselves in, but effective for what it was made for, war.

"Twenty, market price." The general noticed Jaune's hesitation. "Still too much? Man, you must be broke."

Unable to deny it, Jaune racked his brain for a counter, and struck on an idea. He lost an inch of height, the shoes on his feet now in his hands.

"Eight thousand, and I trade you these rocket boots."

"Poor man's flight, heh?"

Despite the condescension, the general inquired into the piece of tech. Unfortunately, the details Jaune provided caused the man to laugh at him.

"Yeah, that's worthless. You got anything else?" He frowned as Jaune shook his head. "Not a single thing in your Dimensional Pocket?"

The suspicious tone set off alarm bells, and Jaune pivoted to deflect before he could even register the need. "No, I do!" he said in his best confident voice. "But not here. I left them at home to save space."

Understanding dawned. "Ohhh," went the general. "Didn't upgrade the inventory space? Tell me you don't game without telling me you don't game." He gestured at the mech. "Fifteen thousand. You can't be that poor."

He ignored the jibe, checking with Tattletale. She held up her hands, fingers spread.

"Ten," Jaune relayed the offer. The judging look on the general's face confirmed a precipitous drop in his opinion of Jaune, but hey, broke was broke. He wasn't about to pretend just to save face, because down that path laid an empty wallet. Push came to shove, he would walk away.

After much deliberation, along with muttered curses about 'an oversized paperweight', the general turned back to them.

"Twelve, and I'll throw in an Extension Charm-ed bag to carry it in."

Jaune froze, and looked up at the big, heavy mech.

The general barked a laugh. "Yeah, didn't think about that, didja?"

"Twelve thousand, guns and ammo, Extension Charm-ed bag, and you spray down the inside with industrial cleaner," Tattletale pressed. None of them knew what an Extension Charm was, but the hint was clear. The man spoke of it like it was trash. To them, it sounded like a treasure.

"Sold!" cried the general.

With a snap of his fingers, the man summoned his assistant, directing her to take care of the menial details now that the fun haggling part was over. She took to the task of wiping down the pilot seat, hips wiggling as she climbed into the cockpit, while the general motioned for Jaune to come closer.

"I remember my days starting out, so I'm gonna give you a piece of advice."

Attitude aside, Jaune had to admit that the man was in a better position than him. He leaned in to listen.

"Quit wasting time."

Jaune blinked. "Hah?"

"I mean it. You're new. Don't lie, I can smell the poverty on you. My advice is to quit wasting time and hit the big leagues as fast as you can. Did you pick RWBY as the starting world?"

What did Ruby have to do with it? Jaune gave a noncommittal grunt while filing that away. Traveling through worlds in the manner he did meant that oftentimes, the name of the universe was one of the scant few details he had to go on. He learned from experience that they held significance, and if his world was named after Ruby Rose? It bore investigating.

"Figures, with that Jaune Arc Substitute," said the general, unaware of the turmoil behind Jaune's blank smile. "The choice isn't bad, Remnant has a lot of females to collect." He chuckled. "But that's the trap. Hoarding shitty waifus is the classic noob move that contractors fall for. You need to take the long view if you want to succeed in this business. Pick the ones you want to keep and sell the rest, the more the better. Like Ciel Soleil."

Jaune had a lot of things he wanted to say, the anger surging within him backing much of it. Except, that last part drew forth one question ahead of all else.

"Who's Ciel Soleil?"

"Exactly," the general concurred. "Not like we have enough time in the day for each and every one of them. Sending the extras along lets you ramp up faster, so you can go and grab the girls that matter." The dismissive glance at Tattletale, who was checking on the mech, provided ample hint of who he considered unnecessary.

"I…" Jaune clenched his hand into a fist. He might misunderstand people sometimes, but he was hearing this loud and clear. "I'm fine as I am, thanks."

The man was taken aback by his tone. However, he soon played it off.

"Hey, I was just being friendly. You do you." The fake sense of friendliness roiled off him in waves. "Don't wanna listen to good advice? That's on your broke ass. You do you," he repeated.

A noise reminiscent of a vacuum attracted their attention. The shop assistant was in front of the mech, a cloth sack in her hand. Tattletale and Escha stood beside her, marveling as the mech proceeded to vanish into the bag, space warping to somehow enable the several tons of metal to fit into the small opening. In the span of seconds, the mech was gone. The shop assistant lightly pulled on the strings to close the sack and handed it to Tattletale, guiding her through the process of paying through the Marketplace app.

"There you go," said the general. "Have fun with it. Sell it to the next newbie that comes along. Circle of life. You buying anything else?"

Jaune shook his head.

"Then, get."

With that, the man moved off to leave Jaune standing alone. As Tattletale and Escha rejoined him, they noticed his mood.

"What's wrong?" asked Tattletale.

He put on a smile. "Nothing. Nothing at all."

There had been a moment there, where he convinced himself into thinking this place was on the up and up. It was easier that way for his peace of mind. He wouldn't be making that mistake anymore.

What else did this place have in store for him?
