#4,642
Chapter 57: Jaune and Lisa Go to the Convention (Pt. 2)​


A familiar face in the crowd at an unexpected place. The phenomenon did not happen often, but anytime it did, it tended to leave one with a sense of marvel. How small the world was. What strange serendipity guided the course of our lives. People would usually walk away with a pep in their steps, the ordinary day becoming just a little more wondrous.

Jaune panicked right the hell out, turning white as a sheet. He pushed through the crowd to get closer, and hoped he was wrong.

Around an intersection and past a group of spectators for a booth offering 'VR isekai experiences', he caught up to his target.

"Ruby? Ruby Rose?"

A girl in a red hood turned around. Jaune had a fleeting moment to confirm that it was indeed the person he suspected, before the full force of her beauty struck him like a speeding train, taking him aback. That part was new.

"Yes?" Even her voice sounded odd, the squeakiness gone. "Wait… Jaune, right?"

"Oh snap, it's a Jaune!" said another girl, long blond hair swishing as she turned her head, and Jaune now registered the familiar faces accompanying Ruby. Her whole team stood by her side. Yang Xiao-Long, bright and sunny as ever. Weiss Schnee, reminding him anew of why he had an interest in her once upon a time. Blake, cat ears standing proud above her head… with a tail behind her?

"Is he an insert, do you think?" Blake said. She tilted her head as she observed him, the tail weaving back and forth in the slow movements of a cat that had caught onto something mildly interesting. "Or a husbando?"

He tried to parse those terms. No luck. More importantly, he needed to know one thing.

"What are you doing here!?" he asked, failing to hide his dismay even as he began to note the differences from his memory. They stood several inches taller than the last time he saw them. Ruby's cloak lacked the bulky imprint of her ever-present mechashift scythe. Weiss had an actual chest, and he was not talking about the one filled with gold and gems that everyone assumed the Schnee had in her room. Also, again, cat tail on Blake.

Certain words he heard earlier, spoken by the man dressed like a general, rang in his ears.

Confused looks passed between the members of Team RWBY.

"Why wouldn't we be?" Yang said.

"No, Yang, I think he has us mixed up with his world's version," Blake chimed in.

Ah. Yep. As he thought. An old question of his finally had irrefutable confirmation. Other Remnants existed out there. It wasn't just an endless parade of Earths.

The situation, however, remained the same. Team RWBY was attending the convention, and there numbered only a few methods he knew of to allow that.

"Is someone mind-controlling you?" he blurted out. Unspoken was the the opposite circumstance, where one or more among them participated in this madness. At the corner of his vision, he glimpsed Tattletale and Escha taking position beside him, peering with curiosity at the scene.

Weiss gave a scoff, and it sounded sweet as a songbird. "As if. We're not like the unfortunate people you would find here. We love our darling master, and he loves us."

Jaune and Tattletale directed an identical deadpan gaze at her, then looked at each other. A whispered conversation flowed between them, reaching a conclusion that they were both sure of.

Weiss Schnee was totally being mind-controlled.

"Do we have a problem here?"

The sophisticated voice came from behind him, and Jaune turned right as someone passed by. He had to look up, because the newcomer used his height to loom over him. To contrast the bored drawl of a gentleman, the person's face was set in an angry scowl. He had a hand tucked in his pocket. Dressed in high class finery, a dark coat sat on his shoulder with the sleeves swinging empty, and the garment pulsated from time to time with smoke. The tap-tap of a cane accompanied the young gentleman as he moved to block Team RWBY from Jaune, and the way their eyes lit up at his presence told a story of true love.

Jaune could gag. That fairy tale was full of lies.

The gentleman in the dark coat removed his hand from his pocket to sweep back the bangs of his brown hair. "What do you think you are doing with my gals?"

A slight smirk grew on the gentleman's face as titters followed his words, the members of Team RWBY flushing red. They seemed to take their cue from his mood, and the looks sent toward Jaune thereafter conveyed a cold apathy.

"I was making conversation," Jaune said, maintaining a smiling demeanor to help defuse the sudden tension. "A bit of Remnant solidarity for people far from home."

Derision, and a roll of the eyes. "Whatever you say, American boy. You do not even look like a proper Jaune Arc."

Jaune Arc felt more insulted by that than he should.

"Oh, I doubt there's one as authentic as me," he joked.

The gentleman studied Jaune with a keen eye. "You do still give off the impression of a potato, so that is more accurate than the rest of you supposed Jaune stans could say." The gentleman turned briefly to Tattletale, then wrinkled his nose. "It would be wise to invest in a face lift, it is why we have the Catalog. Your women will thank you." Tattletale bristled, but the gentleman ignored her to look back at Jaune. "So what, did you think substituting into the Miles Luna self-insert somehow gave you, aha, 'dibs' on all the RWBY girls? News flash, he does not get with any of them for the run of the show."

"The show?" Jaune said under his breath, too quiet for anyone else. And 'substituting'? That was the second time he encountered the term.

To switch one thing with another, and if that thing was Jaune Arc…

A hand touched his back, moving soothingly as his heartbeat picked up to a frantic pace. Tattletale also tried to speak comforting words, but he couldn't hear them. The gentleman said something, too, and he definitely wasn't listening to that.

With a weak and shaky grin, because that was all he could muster, Jaune said in the friendliest of tones, "You know, I never finished watching that show. Is it any good?"

"Would have been better without your boy in it. A lot of hotties every new season, though." Quieter, the gentleman said half to himself, "Which was convenient. Hallelujah, RWBY."

He nodded along. "Right, right. I hear you… Could you, pretty please, turn off whatever mind-control bullshit"—whoops, the mask slipped—"you got going with those four?"

"Jaune, keep your cool," Tattletale advised softly, still patting his back.

"Uhhh, no?" retorted the gentleman, with a face that said 'what the hell'. "Remember your etiquettes, now. What business is it of yours?"

"I like to think that they'd make the same request if I was in their shoes."

Jaune did not know what he expected, only that mirth wasn't it. The dry chuckle invited others to join the gentleman, and in fact did draw a bit of laughter from those in the crowd forming around them who had overheard the conversation. The gentleman slightly tilted his head back to glance over his shoulders, addressing the spectators hungry for entertainment.

"Oh, look. Another one made it to ConCon. Ah hahaha!" The gentleman laughed, a gloved hand delicately held over his face in a pose fit for a movie poster.

Jaune cocked his head to the side, eyes narrowing. "And what is that supposed to mean?"

"Let me take a guess here," the gentleman answered with a drawl. "You plan to 'save' them. To 'nurse' them back to their proper selves, with no expectation of a reward. Oh, but of course they will be so very grateful for what you did."

"I—"

The laughter dropped. "You are not the first holier-than-thou prick to show up and go on and on about how 'enslaving waifus is bad', wrapped up in your delusions of a savior complex. Except, if any of you really believe that, you would not be here. All you want is to poach!"

Jaune balked. "What? No! I don't!"

His protest fell flat with the crowd. The sneers and scoffs rolled in from every direction, sounding exasperated as if they had seen it a thousand times before and have long grown tired of the farce.

Emboldened by the reception, the young gentleman spread his arms in a theatrical manner. "The thing none of you ever get is that all you do is whine. Oh please, sir, may I have a little less slavery," he mocked. "Boohoo, think of their natural dignity. No, now cry about it." He counted on his fingers. "Stamped, Shrouded, Charmed, Fairie Feasted, Hypnoed, True Routed, Collared… Good luck finding a counter to a single one of those and I bought them all! For you to steal my girlfriends from me is a pipe dream!"

Then, one would think the young gentleman had nothing to worry about. Perhaps there was truth to that, as Team RWBY revealed no discomfort upon hearing the methods by which their companion kept them under his thrall. He could never lose the people he saw as his. A man talking to his girlfriends presented no danger to him. Yet, the way the gentleman stepped to the side to shield—by total coincidence, Jaune was sure—the four women from his view suggested that the long litany of powers available at his fingertips reassured the gentleman none. That the spittle flying as he ranted and the growing mania in his eyes spoke of a person trying to convince himself.

Escha pulled on his pant leg. Jaune looked down, and she pointed to the ground in front of them. He soon noticed the reason for her worry. Shadows were moving across the floor, originating from the gentleman. They flicked and snapped in violent motions. Sensing the prelude to a fight, Jaune shifted the hand bearing the Outsider's mark behind his back, the smoky shape of [Third Arm] superimposing over it, primed for a blow.

Sucker punch. Transition to obscure vision. Plunge a sword through the darkness, then wing it. Simple enough for a plan A.

The gentleman in the dark coat squinted his eyes, and smirked. An attempt at intimidation, Jaune would assume.

Intentions of launching the shadowy fist faltered as he caught sight of Team RWBY gearing up to support their man. It struck him, looking at their weapons, that they truly weren't the people he knew from Beacon. The guns in their hands might glow with a malevolent light and hum with power, but they remained boring old assault rifles at their core, the gray metal bearing no trace of personality. Ruby Rose surprised him most of all. Even Jax hadn't managed to convince her to ditch her scythe. That said, it changed little of the fact that the odds tilted decidedly against his favor. This was Team RWBY.

"Did the rules for the convention mention how the organizers are ensuring neutrality?" Jaune whispered to Tattletale in a hurry. "Because they are looking awfully aggressive to me."

Tattletale gasped, covering her lips in feigned astonishment. "Oh my, you didn't forget what I said." Caring nothing for the tense situation, she patted him on the head and gave a "Good boy!" before sliding around his frame. "Leave it to me," she added for only him to hear.

Her eyes were trained on the floor, and a wide grin split her face as she saw something there. Jaune looked and found the moving silhouette had retracted, forming a semi-circle around the girl. She took another stride forward, and the shadows retreated further.

Tattletale turned her head so that their eyes met. "It's telling, the way everyone else took a big step back when they realized a fight was about to start. Strong people, tough people, and they ran."

Her gaze trailed over to the spectators for emphasis. As she described, the people who had up until now tried to close in to better catch every word of the exchange seemed to have made a lot of distance in a very short amount of time.

"You see, Jaune, this fine fellow talks a big game, and yeah, it has a bit of truth to it. It is futile for you to raise a stink here. But he neglected to mention one important caveat to that." Tattletale looked at the gentleman. "He. Can't. Do. A. Thing. Either," she mocked, jabbing her finger at him on each word.

The gentleman rolled his eyes. Directing his attention to the spectators, he flapped his hand in a yapping gesture.

"Tattletales, amiright?" he said, and covered a yawn. It lent the impression of nonchalance, and got him a few chuckles. "Yeah, yeah, we get it. The security system will kick in if a fight breaks out and blah, blah, blah… Only idiots like your hypocrite of a boyfriend would ever forget."

Undeterred by the attempt to take the winds out of her sail, Tattletale rolled with it and nodded along with the spiel. "All that to say, the best you can do against Jaune is play chicken. He can talk smack about you all he likes at this convention, and you'll have to take it because you're so… small." She cocked her hips and planted a fist on it, oozing smugness.

"Ha," the gentleman barked. Then, louder. "Ha! Keep dreaming. I'm playing nice because I pity him."

Yet, and this gave away the game, he did not make the one move that would flip the table around and prove them wrong, which was to attack them. Taking cue from Tattletale, Jaune stayed in place. It was a novel concept, doing nothing as a win condition.

During the resulting lull, something changed. Murmurs passed among the spectators. With the promise of drama fizzling out, they had begun to grow bored, and one by one, they slipped away to go look for other amusements.

The gentleman didn't last much longer than them, and his eventual exit featured a whole production of brushing imaginary dust off his coat while recounting the list of important matters awaiting his attention, which honestly might be true as compared to Jaune's intention of wandering the place. In the end, they saw the back of him and his retinue.

Tattletale watched the gentleman go, a victorious grin on her face.

"Heh. I'm never wrong."

Jaune failed to muster the rebuttal she was clearly inviting. To him, this had not been a win, for her explanation highlighted one crucial truth. He was as useless as everyone else here.

"What would have happened, if we fought?" he asked her. "Could I have maybe claimed self-defense?"

He would love a workable excuse to ram a sharp blade down the young gentleman's throat. After all, it was how he freed himself from the mental effects that Jax put him under.

Tattletale spun around, and spread her arms in a helpless shrug.

"The rules never exactly said, and I think that's intentional. Let's not test it out."

Jaune gazed after the departing figures. Team RWBY did not spare him a single glance. He supposed his version in their world was even less acquainted with the four women than him. Looking back, they had been strangers, almost.

He had a choice, and he made a decision. Crocea Mors appeared in his hand. He moved to follow after them.

Without a word, Tattletale seized him by the wrist and pulled with all her strength. A moment later, the gentleman in the dark coat and Team RWBY passed out of sight.


-o-​


"Are you mad at me?"

"No."

"You're mad at me."

"I'm not."

As Tattletale continued to badger him, Jaune picked up a big toadstool mushroom with two eyes, turning it this way and that. It had a springy texture that would go well in a soup. He glanced at the nearby placard. The short blurb claimed that the mushroom would make 'stuff' bigger. What, he dreaded to ask. It went back on the shelf, and he picked up the pretty crown next to it to test whether he could pop the thing into his Pocket without paying. A shame that it turned out he could not. The convention space played by different rules.

Tattletale lingered in his periphery. Despite his reassurances, she fidgeted from foot to foot. In her arms, Escha sent him a reproachful look, her fur a frizzy mess due to Tattletale ruffling and plucking at it in her worry. That grumpy cat face demanded he do something about this.

His hand ran through his hair, and Jaune exhaled a long breath.

"You might well have saved my life, Tattletale. I could never be mad at you."

The problem, as ever, lay with him. Today was another day where he had not been good enough. He entered the world of unlimited power thinking Jax the strongest of it, and found the ceiling high as the blue sky. Then, above even that, there was something at this convention that Jax's ilk feared to wake.

"I'm just going to have to get stronger, aren't I? And maybe someday, it will all work out."

Or maybe he would die in a ditch. Life was like that. Go to bed one night, wake up with a Grimm to the face. The lucky star laughed at the long view.

Their little group moved from booth to booth, but their hearts were no longer in it. Each new destination reinforced the bleak reality that they existed on the bottom rung in a society where they did not belong.

With a significant part of their Points set aside for their goal of purchasing access to a world, plus the portion allocated to emergency 'throw anything and everything at the wall' situations, what remained for them to spend freely was not a large amount. In relative terms, that was. Personally, he considered his share of the balance a fortune. Upward of 10,000 Points allowed him the ability to buy a number of nifty gadgets or minor powers. Tons of food, were he so inclined. It just didn't count for much in this place.

The paper talisman now tied to the hilt of his sword should come in handy, though. Originating from a place called the Akamatsuverse, the paper bore written characters he didn't understand, but the demon-repelling properties it conveyed meant that, in the future, he'd be the one chasing the Saja Boys and similar supernatural types. And if that didn't work, then the stack of disposable talismans he could paste right onto the blade would hopefully do the job.

See? A step at a time, and one could scale mountains. Or, again, die in a ditch.

"Dragon or bust. That's the key. Either you're a dragon, or you're food."

The lizard faunus that sold him the talisman seemed adamant that Jaune was making a bad purchase, but she extended no effort to stop him. What she did, and this was a behavior shared with a lot of the contractors Jaune encountered thus far, was to wax on at the poor, deprived unfortunate about what she called a proper build. He ignored most of it, because scary mind control. The dragon part, on the other hand…

"Any downsides I should know of?" he asked.

The woman grinned, her mouth full of sharp teeth. "None. Zip. Nada. I mean, we're supposed to get bleedthrough of a dragon's nature, arrogance and greed and whatnot, but that feature has to be bugged because it doesn't actually do anything. I've certainly never experienced it."

The hoard of gold below her throne begged to differ. Before he had a chance to mention it, the fawning men draped around the area began a chorus of praise over the many sterling qualities of the dragon faunus, which she accepted as her due. Stomach churning, Jaune departed from the booth.

A lengthy search through the scroll revealed that a good half of the components to that so-called optimal build the contractor swore by wasn't even showing up. Had she lied? Did she have access to sections of the store barred to him?

All questions that he did not know how to ask without appearing suspicious. So, he left them for another time.

Back in the aisle, he scanned the crowd for Tattletale and Escha. The three of them had agreed to stay close. Within eyesight, at the least. He spotted them four booths down at an exhibit themed around costumed superheroes, displaying shelves of comics along with artifacts, posters (porn), figurines (porn), and other memorabilia (mostly porn).

He recognized many of the faces and costumes.

"Worm…" he read aloud from the banner hanging above the booth, shaking his head. "No matter where I go, you're there."

A white-haired man lounged at the table. He wore a blindfold that covered both of his eyes, and boasted a carefree expression.

"Come in, welcome, are you her master?" the blindfold man said and gestured at Tattletale, who had the presence of mind to not deny it outright. "Good taste, getting yourself a Sarah."

A twitch developed on one of Tattletale's eyebrows.

"She prefers Lisa," Jaune corrected.

"Or just don't talk to me. I'll take that, too," Tattletale added under her breath. A quick grin passed across her face when Jaune chuckled at her joke.

It faded as she returned her attention to the object on the table. Calling it a book would be generous since it was little more than a thick sheaf of paper with holes punched in them then bound with metal rings. Jaune sidled next to her in order to read the cover, with Escha clambering onto the table for a peek.

Worm, by John C. "Wildbow" McCrae.

"The true, blue original right there," said the blindfold man. "Not a fanfic. Not even an attempt to fix the plotholes. I printed it as-is, for all of you who didn't bother to read the canon."

Jaune gave a sidelong look to Tattletale, who picked up the book to peruse within. She seemed calm at the moment, without signs of distress. By now, he knew that meant little. Tattletale had a knack for hiding her troubles from him.

While keeping an eye on her, he cautiously struck up conversation with the booth owner.

"So, you mentioned canon and… fanfic?"

"Ugh." The blindfold man performed an odd gesture, then stopped and moved the blindfold aside so they could see him roll the startlingly blue eyes he shared with his doppelgangers. "Don't get me started," he complained, resetting the blindfold. "You won't believe the number of times I talk to a fanon casual and they would tell me all about how they adore Taylor or Amy or whatever other woobified Mary Sue of a character that they hallucinated is canon. Half the fandom never read the book, and the half that did can't keep their facts straight. They're why we need to gatekeep—What are your opinions on Purity?"

Thrown by the sudden question, Jaune floundered. "I, what, is… is that a movement in the 'fandom' to keep that canon stuff pure or something?"

Judging from the shell-shocked look, Jaune had just confessed to running a car over the blindfold man's mother.

"No, Purity. Divorced from Kaiser, raising a baby, light powers E88 nazi cape Purity."

That did it. Jaune brightened up, snapping his fingers in recognition.

"The demon worshipers!"

The man slammed a fist on the table, head dropping low. "Fuck, I'm talking to a fanon casual."

What a troublesome fellow.

"Jaune?"

He felt a tap on his shoulder. Tattletale had the book open, her eyes on a page.

"Heyo."

"Do I have a vulpine grin?"

He scratched his head at the sudden question. "There is a certain foxlike cast to it, yes."

"So you would call it vulpine?" she stressed.

"I suppose. Why?"

"Oh, nothing~" A little smile, more coy than vulpine, played on her lips.

Tattletale decided to buy the book, and the blindfold man was all too happy to sell it to them, albeit while shooting Jaune a sneer (and staring at Tattletale's chest). The man made a demand that Jaune read the story, a request which he fully intended to ignore.

As they prepared to leave, a voice rang out.

"Honey~!"

Jaune cringed at the high and nasally pitch, the kind that one got when a grown woman tried to sound younger than she was, but failed. It then occurred to him that Tattletale had spun around the moment she heard the voice, and was now goggling with her mouth agape. A turn of his head resulted in him mirroring the stupefied expression.

A person that resembled Tattletale was approaching the booth. He hesitated to say she was Tattletale, since there were… differences. A thick layer of pink covered her fat lips, and her breasts and rear bounced as she flounced her way over to them. The purple-black costume she wore retained its central motif of an eye but not much else, being more skin than fabric.

"Like, I missed you soooo much," the woman whined, sliding across the table to end up in the lap of the blindfold man.

"My Tattletale," the man crooned, stroking her with affection. "Did you succeed in the task I gave you?"

The woman fished out a small disk from between her cleavage, exaggerating the motion with a wink. "Yeppers! The info worked, and you now own an invite to the Tomcat VIP Lounge, plus a couple of favors you can call on. That idiot folded like origami."

"You are worth every Point, ahahaha!"

Tattletale stared unblinking at the alternate version of herself, one who had been enhanced to suit the taste of the contractor. There was intelligence there, not an iota lost. Simply buried beneath a new purpose. The woman could not stay still for longer than a few seconds, squirming and rubbing on the blindfold man as they spoke to one another. Her ditzy choice of vocabulary, deliberately chosen, pleased him to no end.

When their eyes happened to meet, Tattletale recoiled as if her other self was a viper.

"Is that canon, then?" Jaune accused, pointing to the alternate Tattletale's bust. The size of watermelons, they were.

"Not as such, but if you read the book closely, you would see that with the presence of Bonesaw and Panacea, it was actually very possible for this to happen in chapter—"

Tattletale pulled him and Escha out the booth before they had to listen to any more of that.


-o-​


The convention hosted its food court in a separate concourse. There, the restaurants stacked three stories high, with more of them set on small islands floating in midair. The higher a person went, the more Points the dishes cost.

Jaune and company stuck to the first floor for the sake of their wallet. The ramen they got tasted phenomenal anyway, which was annoying. It made wallowing in angst harder.

Currently, he was trying to forget recent events in the best way he knew how. Alas, the PAB method of wiping memories failed to help him today, and the rice wine tasted of guilt as he watched the people on the other side of the restaurant counter run to and fro. None of them had the appearance and bearing of a person whose goal was to stand in a kitchen, though they carried on their work with big smiles. A stern woman with white hair displayed the poise of one used to command. A blonde that reminded him of Glory Girl wore a cape, a stylized 'S' on her chest—a superhero of some sort. The woman who brought the food to them, giving her name as Elizabeth, kept asking him about the places he had traveled, eyes alight with wonder and yearning. He hadn't seen the contractor who owned the store yet, but at a guess the person was a sadistic one.

On the next chair over, Tattletale picked at her food while reading her new book with pointed focus. Escha sat directly on the counter, blowing on her bowl of ramen to cool it down.

After much dithering, he asked them, "Should we go home, you two? I'm at my limit."

Escha looked up, a strand of noodle slowly pulling into her mouth.

"Please let me finish this!" she said around the mouthful of ramen. "The food has no sin!"

Tattletale closed her book and gave a sigh, adjusting her grip on her chopsticks. "Like everything else, a hunger strike won't do jack, Jaune. That said, there also isn't much good we can do by staying. Let's just eat, then we'll leave."

"And toss a bomb on our way out?" Jaune asked, setting the cup of alcohol aside to concentrate on his lunch.

"No."

Sadness.

"Besides, I already gave that a shot and it didn't work."

Tattletale? Miss Tattletale? Please repeat that.

"Heh heh."

The three of them froze upon hearing the chuckle, because they had made sure to speak at a low volume so as to avoid notice. It came from the end of the counter, several seats over. There, a drunkard sprawled on the table surface with bottles surrounding him. He raised his head, and Jaune felt a pang of jealousy at the way the man managed to make a drunken binge look sexy. Spiky blond hair and whisker markings, his face was a familiar one by now.

"Mighty odd things you've been talking about," said the drunkard.

Jaune thought fast. "We're working on a comedy routine."

"Nah, you're not. I listened the whole time." The drunkard's bleary eyes zeroed in on the bottle in front of Jaune. "Ahhh, whatever. Wouldya mind sharing that wine?"

Well, he couldn't refuse, now could he? Not after having blackmail waved in his face. Jaune pushed the bottle along the counter with his fingertips. At the limit of his reach, the drunkard performed a gesture, and the bottle slid the rest of the way on its own. Forgoing a cup, the man gulped down a mouthful.

Jaune, Tattletale, and Escha observed him, waiting for the sign that they need to drop everything and run. To the contrary, however, the drunkard simply lowered the bottle once he was done, exhaling a satisfied breath.

"God, that's good. This place has amazing booze, huh?"

After a beat, Jaune answered, "Sure does."

The drunkard nodded. "Knew it was a great idea. I said it to Kara, I said, I said 'ramen and sake, it'd be a hit' and it was!" He grew somber. "It was."

The tone suggested ill tidings. Jaune looked around the area, meeting Tattletale's gaze. She motioned for him to keep talking to the drunkard, likely not for any good-hearted reasons. With great reluctance, he shifted a couple of seats closer.

"Is that so? I bet you anything that Kara would be proud of you," he said gently.

The drunk man glared at him. "She's not dead, she's right there."

The girl in the superhero costume waved, then carried on. Jaune coughed into his hand.

"Alright, so it's a different problem you're having. You, ah, you want to talk about it?"

For a while, the drunkard said nothing. He rapped his fingers on the table, head swaying as he studied their group. Abruptly, he grasped one of the alcohol bottles yet to be emptied and took a long draught, slamming it down on the counter afterward.

"I ran into a vampire."

"Ooh, sounds rough," Tattletale opined, without much sympathy. "I hear sunlight works on them."

"Not on this one."

"Holy water," Jaune said. One must never underestimate holy water. Praise Aqua.

His spoon slipped out of his hand. Before he could catch it, it struck the corner of the ramen bowl at an angle that sent it straight to the floor.

"Oops." How unlucky.

"Don't mind it," said the drunkard. "Jaina will get you another." The man looked ready to cry when the woman with white hair did as he bade. "The old her… the real her wouldn't have," he muttered once Jaina moved further away.

Jaune arched an eyebrow. That was a take he hadn't heard around these parts.

Noticing the look, the drunkard explained by continuing his tale. "Before I escaped, the vampire got her fangs into me. Only, she sucked out more than blood. She took one of my Skills."

"Was it a good one?" Jaune asked.

"Gamer's Mind."

Jaune had no response for that off the top of his head, and stayed quiet for a touch too long.

"You don't know what that is. Interesting…" The drunkard rubbed his chin in thought, before pointing at the side of his head. "It keeps me calm and clear-headed. Emotions hit an upper limit and—poof!—it's gone."

"You put yourself under a master effect!?" Tattletale blurted out, astonished.

The drunkard nodded miserably. "And now it's gone. And now life sucks."

Empathy has to do with emotions. Hell, everything has to do with emotions. To stomp his feelings on things down for however long this man did, and then to have them come roaring back, Jaune could understand the need for a stiff drink.

Tattletale leaned in. "Can you request a replacement copy?"

Jaune gave her an odd look. This sounded like a situation they would want to encourage instead of offering solutions, given the contractor's reactions to the women working the stall.

"I tried," the drunkard answered Tattletale. "Didn't work."

"Hm, then going up the chain might be your best bet. Have you spoken to a manager?"

So, that was her game. Tattletale wanted to fish for a contact and get at the inner workings of the Company. He supposed it was a fair gamble to assume that a business would have a hierarchy of positions.

The drunkard fell quiet. It stoked within Jaune a small suspicion.

"What, is there nobody you can talk to?"

The man jolted. "Oh no, there is. Definitely is." He scratched his nose. "At least, I think. That's the problem."

"Okay? And?" Tattletale pressed, too impatient for the runaround.

"Hey now, he's getting there," Jaune soothed her. He turned to the drunkard. "She has a point, though. You may feel better by just saying outright what is wrong."

Glug glug glug glug.

That… was mildly impressive, he had to admit. Half a bottle of an amber liquid disappeared down the drunkard's throat in no time flat. The empty flask joined its brethren.

Having mustered his spirits, the drunkard spoke.

"Most communications come through the Company Device and that's how I like it. I don't have to talk to anybody. We might get summoned for a meeting once in a while, and I usually see my manager then."

"Care to give a name? Could be that we have something in common," Jaune said casually. Tattletale sent him a surreptitious thumbs-up.

"I can't pronounce it." How unhelpful. "The point is, she's usually there. Not always."

The man's hand slipped around the neck of a whisky bottle, holding there for the moment.

"I've met other contractors behind the desk," the drunkard said quickly, warming up to the idea of spilling his heart out. "I've met people who looked like desk jockeys and insisted they weren't other contractors, but I was pretty sure they were. I think I got an actual, original Naruto once that somebody plucked out of his world to read a script."

"That sounds…" Jaune searched for a good way to put it. "Rather haphazard."

"Tell me about it." The drunkard blew a puff of air to clear stray hair from his eyes. He began rapping his fingers on the table again. "I still asked all of them what I should do, because hey, what do I got to lose, right? You should have seen their faces. Should see how they start flipping the papers on the desk like it had all the answers."

Slowly, the drunkard stopped paying attention to Jaune and the others. He stared into his bottle with a faraway look.

"Then… Then I remember the times where it's just the papers on the desk in an empty room." Unable to resist, he took another swig of alcohol, and stared at his lap. "The one sitting dead center would always detail the assignment and the funny thing is, I never reject it. No matter what it asks, I take the job. It got me thinking…"

The haunted look drew them all in, with Jaune speaking for all of them.

"What's the deal with the paper?"

"It tells me what to do." The drunkard raised his head. "That's the purpose of it, right? It tells me, it tells you, it tells those people pretending to be my manager what to do!"

"Oh, whoa… Wait, is that it?" Jaune asked, causing the drunkard to blink.

"Huh?"

Jaune sat back on his seat, shaking his head. Tattletale huffed in disappointment, while Escha returned to her meal.

"It's called instructions, genius," Tattletale spat. "People write things down. What's so special about that?"

Frantic, the drunkard stood up. "No! I meant- I meant that it's more than it seems! Haven't you noticed? Our powers don't work right! I can't get drunk, except sometimes I do! Don't you see?"

None of them had the heart to inform him what it was that they saw. Jaune glanced at the people behind the counter. They were unwilling to look him in the eye, covering their faces in embarrassment.

Thus, with a rueful sigh, he stepped up to the plate.

"You may have drank a little too much—" He was cut off as the drunkard leapt forward, grabbing his shoulders. He leaned away from the warm breath that smelled of a brewery.

"If everything does what it says on the tin, why don't dragons work right? Why do our defenses and templates crap out on us at crucial moments?" the drunkard asked with desperate eyes. "Where do they go? Where do the merchandise we find and sell off go? How come nobody ever saw a Company warehouse? Gamer's Mind should be bound to me, but now it's gone, and that's not possible which gave me the clue! We've all been passing around our powers and privileges to one another, each of us thinking that we earned it from some nebulous omnipotent being that we never get to meet. It comes back to the paper, I'm sure of it. Like, what if it's the form, right? The Form. The one we all filled out. And it only has the power we give it. But we believe. We believe and that makes it real, but we couldn't imagine every detail so it glosses over them, except when we go way off-script it wouldn't have an answer and that's why nobody can help me!"

The tight grip on Jaune's shoulder released their hold, and the drunkard collapsed onto his seat. He was crying, unable to control his emotions.

"And that's why… I'll be like this forever… I'm sorry, Kara… I'm sorry, Elizabeth… I'm sorry…"

Peace and quiet returned to the ramen stall. A blanket settled over the sleeping drunkard, courtesy of Elizabeth. She patted him soothingly, lovingly, on his back before turning to Jaune and the others.

"My apologies, customers. The loss of his ability has caused him some distress."

"That's more than some," said Jaune, one hand smoothing his chest.

"It is only temporary. He will return to his old self in no time, then it'll be back to conquering worlds and defeating armies for him," the woman asserted with confidence. "As compensation for the disturbance, please enjoy your meal for free."

Beneath the generous offer was a firm tone declaring the conversation over. Elizabeth turned away from them and busied with cleaning up the empty bottles littering the area, her back a hint that they shouldn't press the issue.

Jaune looked at Tattletale. Tattletale looked at Escha. Escha was already chowing down. They took their cue from the cat.

Yet, even as they ate their food, the subject was impossible to ignore for long.

"What did you think of that, Tattletale?" Jaune finally ventured to ask. "Could he have been right?"

The girl shrugged, munching on fishcake. "It's nothing that complicated. He literally described a pyramid scheme. Muddled leadership, the use of patsies as faces, and moving defective products are classic signs of the set-up. Heck, the way the contractors aped the scheme on the convention floor by pushing stuff they don't want down to newer people like us is a key part of it, too. If you ask me, he was looking for an excuse to blame his situation on 'everyone' rather than admitting that he was a rube that fell for the scam. Either way, does it matter?"

Jaune thought on it.

"I suppose not."

"Exactly. We still have no leads on who to talk to about the whole shebang!"

"Oh, that's what you mean," he murmured.

"Hm?"

"...It's nothing. Let's eat and go home. We can try another day."

Since the drunkard would not miss it, Jaune retrieved his bottle of rice wine and poured himself a cup. As he sipped the drink, he cast his gaze over the convention.

What an ugly place.

Strong, powerful people strode these grounds. He had envied them. The floating islands above represented where he needed to be, and the floor a mire where he was forced to wallow.

Peel back the curtains, and nobody understood what was going on or had a leader to tell them the reason why. In that void, they dreamed up causes for the actions they took, breaking as they discovered the cracks to the narrative. To him, it seemed that rather than what they wanted, more power only gave these guys the fear of losing it all. They strutted and swaggered like they owned the place, but adhered to the rules with the meekness of lambs.

Everyone was some form of delusional or a wreck. Everyone lied to themselves.

He didn't think he would come back again.


-o-​


Someone built a golf course in the Void.

Scratch that, Jaune was giving it too much credit. The thin strip of land stretched impossibly long, but measured less than five strides across. A bed of artificial turf covered the dark stone which formed the island. Off in the far, far distance, a flag on a pole marked the 1st hole.

"What are you up to now?" he asked the young man with black eyes, who stood on the tee with feet apart and a golf club aimed at the little white ball.

The Outsider answered without looking at him. "Working on my swing."

A second golf bag blinked into existence next to Jaune. He alternated his gaze between it and the Outsider, then gave up on questioning the situation to begin rifling through the selection of clubs.

"Okay, I'm game. Just don't start spouting socioeconomics at me, and we're good."

"Ah, yes. 'Are you a man or a slave' was how it goes? I did appear within his dreams, near the end. I posed to him a similar question, in case he happened to have the answer."

"Really? What did you say?" With no clue of what the different ones did, he copied the Outsider and grabbed the club with the biggest head.

"'What of I?' I asked him. I am a god, but am I free?"

Done with his practice swings, the Outsider lined up for a shot. Only then did Jaune realize his disadvantage.

"Don't you control this space to an extent? I would think that makes the whole game moot."

"You are not wrong," the Outsider replied. As ever, there was no change to the expression of boredom he wore. "I can perfectly predict what each shift of my body will lead to. Before it leaves the tee, I can name the number of seconds that the ball would take to land in the hole, insofar that we perceive time here. Calculations play no part of it. I simply know."

The Outsider pulled back his arms, body rotating until the head of the golf club hit its zenith. The scene paused for a brief eternity, fit for a picture.

The resultant swing was so effortless that it appeared almost carelessly done. The club struck the golf ball with a sharp thwack to send it careening through the empty Void, a dot in the endless darkness.

Jaune followed the course of the ball, and at first, he was certain in his opinion. No way, no how would it work out. The distance was too far and the course too narrow, the very end of it seeming to compare with the width of a rope to his eyes.

Then, he revised that assumption. The ball flew nearer and nearer to the little flag on the horizon, and he soon became adamant that it would not even bounce once on the grass before reaching its target.

And, as expected, it…

It missed?

He spun toward the Outsider, incredulity written clear across his face.

"What was all that talk about being all-knowing!?" he yelled.

The Outsider showed no anger or disappointment at his failure, his deadened emotions keeping him blank. But as Jaune looked into the pitch black eyes, he could have sworn he saw a flicker of something there.

"An unexpected deviation."

"Here, in your world? Pull the other one."

"It is the truth," the Outsider stated matter-of-factly. "A guest of mine wishes to see my surprised face. It would never work, of course, but they were undeterred by the prospect and have made a game of it. Luckily for them, they retain a measure of their power. Enough to effect a small change in the probabilities."

The Outsider moved off to the side, allowing Jaune to take position at the tee.

He had never played golf. That was a city game. Thus, his stance and technique might qualify as an insult to the sport. He pressed on, nevertheless, mimicking from memory what his opponent had done.

Halfway through the swing, he faltered.

"Tell me if I'm wrong, but couldn't you have corrected the course of the ball as it flies?"

"I could, yes, but you know me. It is far more interesting to watch where it goes."

Meaning, he would likely also refrain from cheating on Jaune's turn. With greater confidence, Jaune swung the golf club.

He experienced a brief burst of elation, for the ball managed to cross a bigger distance than he expected. He wasn't half-bad at this, was his thought. That grew into confusion as the ball continued to fly farther.

Then, farther.

Then farther and farther and still farther until… it landed in the hole.

Jaune stood slack-jawed. Speechless, he forgot to even celebrate.

"A cheater to the end," the Outsider said after a short beat.

Waking from his stupor, Jaune balked. "Whuh? I don't even know how that happened!"

"I do, and no, I am yet to be surprised." The Outsider strode past him, and the golf course shrank in a blink to measure a mere few yards from them, allowing him to walk over and retrieve his golf ball. "Next hole, now."

A new course bloomed into being, a mind-bending tract of terrain that Jaune wasn't sure existed in three dimensions. The Outsider was unfazed by the accusing glare Jaune leveled at him, taking his turn on the tee. With a huff, Jaune joined him.

And as he played golf, Jaune thought and thought and thought. It really was a fascinating game.

An unexpected deviation. A small thing that could change the entire scenario.

The contractors were a blight. They were also beings capable of supreme abilities that broke the rules of reality over their knees. He had wondered how he could possibly fight the whole lot of them, dreaming of methods to shield entire worlds from intrusion by people the likes he had met at the convention. It required powers on a cosmic scale that was very easy for him to think of… only because he had not the beginning of an idea of big that was. He might as well be a kid shouting 'Ultimate Barrier'.

This grand endeavor called for a hero, in truth. But it hadn't been a hero to bring an end to Jax Darkphenix. A middling nobody of no import did that. There were a whole lot of those out there in the many universes.

Jaune killed Jax, and met no retaliation. Whatever the Company was, it did not care. So, what would happen if someone else killed the contractor of their world? What if every contractor faced the risk of dying to someone? It need not be him.

A chance. That was the best a person like him could offer.

As sure as the tide, a world coming to the attention of a Company man would fall under his thrall. And yet, the possibility would always remain that one among the populace might set it free.

Didn't that sound doable?

Of course, the notion belonged to a far-off future. He had more immediate concerns.

Because from that day onward, Tattletale stopped leaving her bed.


-o-​


The girl thought she would get her answers. She found many, too many. Terrible things, about the world and about her own person.

And yet, even here, she failed to find what she had always been searching for, the reason why.

In the end, the only thing Lisa Wilbourn truly learned was that she hated herself.


Author's Notes: Is the Company just a pyramid scheme? A memetic device?

Maybe it hides among us, like some sort of… Among Us.

Whatever the case, the mysterious Company remains an elusive thing.

#4,840
Chapter 58: Youth, Adventure, and Other Delusions​


Daylight greeted the otherworld apartment, and it ran smack dab against a wall of gloom.

What once used to be a bright and airy place seemed to have had the life sucked out of it. Absent was the merry (or more like, annoying) click-clacking of a computer keyboard often heard throughout the day, the random bouts of singing gone the way of the dodo (a turn of phrase introduced to Jaune by Lisa which he didn't quite get, since the dodo was alive and thriving so far as he knew). On the bed tucked into the corner of one side of the room, blankets formed a lump of misery with only the very top of its pretty blonde head poking out.

From the other side of the room, where it stunk of false cheer among various things, Jaune made his way over to the lump. In his hands he held the latest attempt to dispel the poor mood, a serving tray bearing a piping-hot bowl of soup.

"Lisa, time to eat. I made it extra special!" Then, quietly to himself. "Sort of, but not really. I'm no five-star chef or even a half-star cook, sooo…"

He knelt down next to Escha, who was tending to a blue mushroom set on the nightstand. She had picked the biggest, prettiest one of the lot in the thinking that seeing it would cheer Lisa up. How, he dared not ask, for the felyne mind was a mysterious thing that few men were ready to comprehend. The tray went on the edge of the bed, and he gently blew on the steam coming off the bowl so that the aroma wafted in Lisa's direction.

Clam chowder. 'New England' clam chowder. Lisa pointed the area out to him on a map once. It encompassed a section of land that included Brockton Bay, and was located clear on the other side of the massive Kingdom from where Lisa grew up.

Which, to Jaune's mind, should make it at once familiar and exotic. Something Lisa hadn't gotten much of a chance to enjoy but possibly would want to, perhaps. The 'extra special' part came from the liberties he took with the recipe, having bought clams from the Marketplace to add into the soup as the original contents of the can seemed to contain far more potatoes than the titular namesake ingredient of the dish. Not exactly a groundbreaking innovation in the culinary arts by any means, it was the extent to which he was willing to experiment given his limited skills. All he was looking for was a somewhat recognizable and—fingers crossed—nostalgic meal to draw the depressed girl out of her funk.

His heart quickened as the lump on the bed began to stir. The top of Lisa's head turned over, going from facing the wall to facing him. The blanket slipped until her eyes were visible. Dull, lethargic green peeked out from behind a curtain of blonde hair.

"Hey, good morning," he said softly with a smile. "You hungry?"

As encouragement, he scooped a spoonful of soup and held it closer to her. Lisa stared at it for a good, long while.

Then, she vanished beneath the blanket.

"...not h'ngry…" she muttered, her voice missing that lively energy he had grown so used to hearing. In the middle of tending to the decorative mushroom, Escha mewed a soft whine and patted him on the back for a good try.

He set the tray aside, and groaned, "Lisa, it's been two days. You have to eat something." The lump refused to move, and Jaune changed tack, drawing on his past experience with other Annoying Blondes in this situation. His voice grew stern. "Going hungry never helps, but I'm not going to beg you to eat. You're old enough to understand that. I'm leaving this here for you, and I'll get the bath ready for when you take a shower."

With that done, he signaled for Escha to follow him. A quick detour to the bathroom with fresh towels and hair care items, and they resettled at the dining table.

The felyne, nervous, climbed onto the table to speak into his ear.

"Is this a good idea? What if you make her feel lonely?"

"Babying her can hurt her pride more," he replied. "People know how to take care of themselves, and treating them otherwise might cause them to feel like they're useless. Lisa in particular hates that. Watch, she'll do something."

They waited.

"Any second now."

And waited.

"Aaany second now."

A minute became ten, became half an hour. As Jaune and Escha fidgeted in uncomfortable silence, they would give the lump on the bed an occasional glance. The bowl of soup had gone cold, the wisps of steam drifting above it long faded.

But then, a movement drew their eyes. A hand extended from within the blanket folds, reaching out to the clam chowder! It—It—!

It pushed the bowl of soup a couple of inches further away, and withdrew back under the sheets.

"Oh, come on," Jaune snapped, leaping to his feet and pointing a finger in accusation. "Now you're just trying to screw with me and you know it."

"...Dunno what you're mphrmrmrm…" the words trailed off, dampened under layers of blanket. Lisa did not see him stomping his feet and tearing at his hair. It was the same pattern playing on repeat ever since she finished that cursed book.

Once his latest bout of frustration subsided, Jaune said, "What could have been so bad, Lisa? What did you read to make you like this?"

Unfortunately, Lisa seemed to have turtled up again.

"You faced the whole lineup of the Brockton Bay PRT, and got through it. You met Leviathan. Bakuda, twice. What can possibly give you trouble?"

Silence.

"Is this about Skitter—"

A thick book slammed against his nose. It hadn't hurt much, but in his surprise he yelped at the blow. His reflexes were working just fine, though, grabbing the object before it hit the ground so that he now held the offending piece of literature responsible for Lisa's state in his hands, the embossed title 'Worm' mockingly sitting in front of his face. He weighed the merits of burning it.

The full force of Lisa rammed into him an instant later, which he thought was a rather drastic course of action no matter how much a person regretted giving away their stuff. The tackle brought them both to the floor. He caught a fleeting look of a mess of runny makeup and unkempt hair, and the utter panic beneath, then Lisa managed to rip the stack of papers from his hands. The girl hid it behind her as she backed off, shrinking from him as if paranoid that he would demand she pass it over. As he opened his mouth to do exactly that, she scrambled for the bed.

There was a moment where he considered outrunning her. He suspected it would do more harm than good, however, and so allowed her to dive under the covers to once again become a lump, this time with the book firmly ensconced at the center.

When it came down to it, they had gotten Lisa out of bed. All in all, Jaune would call that progress.

"Go away!"

Or not.

"Excuse me?" he asked, sitting up.

Through the layers protecting Lisa from the world outside, her muffled voice commanded, "Just go away and leave me alone!"

Jaune sighed, and let himself fall flat on the floor again.

"Yeah, that's what I thought you said…" He rubbed his eyes. "Are you asking me and Escha to sleep in the bathroom?"

"No."

He waited for more. Shortly, she obliged.

"Away, away."

"Can't do, sorry," he said. It sounded all kinds of reckless to abandon her by herself. "But…"


-o-​


How long was long enough? An hour? A day?

Jaune pondered the question as he lay back upon a grassy hill, beneath golden leaves rustling in the wind. Above him stretched the bright, blue sky. It was early autumn, at a guess.

An absentminded toss of his hand, and his scroll flew up high. The device twirled end over end, reaching a zenith then dropping back down to hit his palm with a smack. After a short lull, he did it again. The small piece of amusement helped to while away the time.

Really, what was it with Annoying Blondes that they spit on the concern of others? Always with the "I'm fine!" and barring themselves alone in their room to sulk. Eighteen years on Remnant—or not, as it were—and he still hadn't figured it out.

Ah, well. He was out of Lisa's hair, as she demanded. It solved nothing at all, but he had no other solution to offer. They did come to a compromise in that Escha would stay to watch her during his absence. Even now, the uncertainty of what was happening in the apartment scratched at the back of his mind.

"They sure are missing out," he said, gazing at the distant mountains.

Sheer cliff walls formed a broken, yet gorgeous, landscape of cascading waterfalls and river streams to lend the mountain range an ethereal air. Like spears, towering columns rose to the sky to create a forest of stone. The tallest of them pierced the clouds, adorned by groves of trees whose leaves were cast in red and gold. Sure-footed goats leapt from one precarious outcropping to the next, and eagles glided between the rocky spires.

Catching the scroll, he slid the screen open and snapped another picture of the stunning view. It went into an album with dozens of its brethren taken over the course of the afternoon. Hours he had spent here, unable to tire of the sight.

Daylight would not last forever, though. He had a decision to make.

Jaune peered down the hill. A mechanized suit of armor lay in an approximate mirror of him, the glass canopy open. The ill-advised attempt to pilot it had ended with him promptly falling flat. He'd put off the next try for later, and saw no need to mention this one to Lisa and Escha.

Beyond the AMP suit was a road. Unpaved, the simple dirt path had been worn down by decades of footprints and wheel marks. It extended across the wide plains existing at the foot of the mountains, winding through shallow hills. To the north, Jaune spied a mighty tree with, if he was not mistaken, houses built into the branches. To the south, an island floated in the air, upon its back a palace. These scenes told of civilization in full bloom unlike the dilapidated hut where the portal had placed him.

He could go home, or he could follow this road and see the places waiting at the end. The idea of coming back with a boatload of treasures to dazzle Lisa's eyes held a certain appeal.

Staying for a while longer won out. The mech returned to the Expansion-Charmed bag. As it could not enter into his Pocket for whatever reason, he looped the strings around a nice stick he found on the ground. Once done, Jaune set off with it hanging over his shoulder.

For the next hour, he followed the road at a brisk pace.

These plains seemed endless, the fantastical height of the mountains creating the illusion of an unchanging horizon. In no hurry, he took his time, detouring to enjoy interesting sights from fields of tall silvergrass to pools of water the color of jade. The picture of a small fox dipping into the water for a bath became his new wallpaper, and would be the first thing he showed his companions. The peace and serenity did him a lot of good.

At the close of the hour, Jaune spotted the first people in this world.

Immediately, rockets fired beneath his heels to throw him forward at breakneck speed as he broke into a run. Those people were being waylaid by the wildlife.

The strange creatures looked like nothing he had ever encountered. Round and gelatinous blobs of varying sizes, lacking limbs. The smallest compared to a basketball, the largest more like a couch. They bounced as a means of locomotion, and at first appeared almost cute. That was, until one decided to imitate a dragon and spat a long line of fire. Another grew a spiky layer of ice and shot at one of the humans, nearly skewering him before that boy managed to get a sword in between them.

As Jaune approached and gained a better view of the situation, some of his concern bled off. The duo contending against the blobs clearly had an idea of what they were doing.

Watching the boy fight was like looking at his past self. Clad in simple and hardy clothes, the boy charged straight ahead, the wild swings of his sword cleaving through the air. The power was there, finesse less so. It worked for his purposes even if the reckless advance earned the boy a number of blows he should have seen coming. Despite the distance, Jaune heard the boy's roars of defiance and will.

Now, the fire magic was something Jaune had no experience with, and yes, he seethed with envy as he saw the boy slam his sword into the ground to create a fiery blast that blew both him and his foe off their feet. Sword explosions? That was magic he could appreciate.

The technique required a little tweaking, though. Jaune winced as the blobs swarmed the boy while he was on the ground, pounding him into the dirt with their weight. Fire, water, and electrical zaps rained down on the boy.

His companion fared better. Jaune didn't recognize her style of combat at first, but on a closer look found that she wielded a bow. Given that, one would expect her up on a vantage point or at a remove, except she fought at near point-blank range, weaving between her opponents with grace. As one of the creatures, a red variant, breathed a gout of flames at her, the girl spun out of the way and simultaneously returned fire with an arrow of light that pierced the blob to pop it like a balloon. The arrow vanished seconds later, with two more already flying to her next targets. A bird flew around the girl, crackling with an odd purple lightning that sometimes imbued her arrows, devastating the foes it struck.

Since she had matters in hand, Jaune chose to lend aid to the boy first. Crocea Mors materialized in his free hand as he entered into range, and it swept across the air above the prone body. There was a brief resistance when the blade came into contact with one of the creatures, its skin somewhat tough and springy, but the sharp steel sliced past that and the blob at once burst open to splash water over him. Momentum carried the sword onward to cut through another blob, then the next, reducing them to wisps of air and splatters of water.

While warding off the rest with his sword, Jaune extended a hand.

"Hey, you alive?"

The boy grabbed on, letting Jaune pull him up. This close, his youth was all the more apparent. 15 or 16, maybe. Blond hair that was almost white made him seem older.

"Thanks a lot, stranger, but don't count me out yet!" said the boy. "Get ready!"

His eyes flicked past Jaune's shoulder. Without looking, Jaune stabbed his sword behind himself, spearing a blob as the other boy got a second one that was aiming for the back of his head. They separated to give each other room, then launched a united offensive on the swarming blobs. The creatures were suicidally stupid, seeming to care not one whit for their lives. The next minute became a blur of heat, cold, and wet as Jaune waged war on adorable, sentient pudding.

"Whooo! You're amazing!" the boy praised as they exploded out of the other side of the swarm.

Jaune gave the boy a once-over. "And you're… dying."

The boy's face was a mess of bruises, a shoulder singed black and blood flowing down an arm.

Yet, that boy only chuckled at his predicament. "Just a flesh wound. Eheh."

"Yeah, sure, now please drink this." Jaune tossed him a green potion from Escha's newest batch, and moved to intercept an icy blob before it could bash the boy's head in.

"My wounds, they're healed!... I'mma go handle that big slime!"

Fixing the boy up turned out to be a bad idea. A split second to marvel over his newfound health, and the boy was leaping again into the fray without a lick of concern for himself. Cursing, Jaune ran after him to help watch his back, which might have gone better if the boy would cease with his insistence on protecting Jaune from danger. They jockeyed for place at the front, each shouting reassurances to the other that they 'got this'.

Nevertheless, they emerged victorious. The blob—The slime that seemed to rule over this pack enjoyed a hardier hide than its smaller brethren, but that amounted to not much of an advantage at all given the sharpness of Crocea Mors. A good, deep stab and it exploded to drop a deluge of water onto the area. The rest of them lost any semblance of unit cohesion at that point, their predictable hops a simple matter to sidestep and return blow.

In the aftermath, he performed a flourish to shake off the slime residue along the blade of Crocea Mors, and it vanished into his Pocket.

Jaune would admit to a measure of pride as the other boy oohed and ahhed with sufficient flattery for the maneuver. Less so when the boy mimicked the move with sparkling eyes. His sword bounced off a rock laying on the ground and would have sliced across his throat if Jaune hadn't pulled him out of harm's way by the collar. A jab of a stimpak needle took care of the frankly ludicrous amount of wounds that the boy had accumulated over the past few minutes. In what to Jaune was quite a surprise, the boy possessed some sort of dimensional pocket of his own in which he stowed his weapon.

Fists raised to the sky, the boy cheered, "We did it—oh wait!" The boy whirled in the direction of the girl, whose existence he and Jaune definitely did not forget.

Their worries were for naught. Due in no small part to them distracting the bulk of the swarm, her side of the fight went at a smoother pace. It resembled a dance, almost. The girl dipped and twirled, untouchable by her foes. She even moved on tiptoes, he noticed. The slimes died in quick succession, arrows punching with accuracy through their center. Not long after Jaune's battle, hers came to an end.

Or so he thought.

Suddenly, the girl fell to her knees right before the last slime. The purple balloon thing rumbled with barely-contained electricity. Yet, as the seconds went by, Jaune realized that she wouldn't, or couldn't, kill it.

There was no time to think or second-guess himself. Rockets engaged to maximum output, he jumped to intervene. The distance between them closed in a blink.

The girl was rambling at the purple slime, overcome by terror. His heart squeezed tight at the awful scene. Never fear, for Jaune Arc was here!

He planted one foot solidly on the ground with the other swinging back for a kick. A flash of light set his eyes aglow, his Semblance pulled to the fore.

"—do not have to worry, o blessed child of Electro, for mine shall be a most benevolent rule. A feast for thine, and pamperings galore—"

With a roar, Jaune punted the slime to the far horizon.

"That's what you get!" he yelled after the glinting star in the sky.

His gaze swept across the area for signs of further hostility. Only once certain of their safety did he spin on his heels to kneel down beside the girl. She had ceased speaking, mouth hanging open in a stupor.

Gently, he said, "Are you injured? Don't worry, I have something that can help."

At that, the girl drew herself up, prompting him to stop short with his hands full of restoratives. Behind her blonde bangs, she wore an eyepatch and the one visible eye shone a lively green as it glared at him.

"T-To cruelly slaughter a fated subject of the Prinzessin der Verurteilung, are you some manner of heartless beast sent by mine enemies? I—I—"

The girl sniffled, striving to hold back tears. Jaune had never felt more like a heel.


-o-​


Three people and a bird traveled by foot on a dirt road. Besides the bird, everyone was some manner of blond, but that was just a simple coincidence. It did not mean they were related by blood in any way.

"Don't mind her, mister. Fischl isn't one to hold a grudge."

So said Bennett, the boy whom Jaune fought alongside earlier. The angry stare that Jaune could feel on the back of his neck suggested otherwise.

Also, 'mister'?

Hm. Hmhm. He truly was, wasn't he, all older and wiser and other admirable qualities? He liked it. No need for fire magic when he had respectability.

"I assure you that Mein Fräulein has a boundless heart… In other words, she will forget this matter by dinner time." Fischl's bird could talk. Jaune had seen stranger things, and so wasn't even fazed by it anymore. The fellow had a reliable air to him, although petting him was a no-no considering his nature as a raven-shaped bolt of lightning.

"No, I won't!" Fischl squawked. Then, with a jolt, she turned back to Jaune with a haughty expression. "I mean, ahem, take all that Oz proclaims in jest. It is merely that the affairs of mortals concern this one not. Forsooth, 'tis the endless cycle of our destruction that drives beast and man to seek each other's lives. The fault therefore lies not with you but with the world, so take heart that you may one day earn my forgiveness."

"She is susceptible to bribes," added the bird, Oz.

"Oz! Put it more delicately!"

Well, now. That piece of advice put Jaune on firmer footing. He was no stranger to distracting Annoying Blondes—which this child seemed to qualify—with presents.

"I'll get you something nice, I promise," he said.

With none of her bombastic air, Fischl fidgeted with her gaze turned downward. "Um, you don't have to," she mumbled shyly.

Jaune gave her a noncommittal grunt. Inwardly, he revised his image of Fischl along with his plans. A good kid deserved twice the amount of gifts.

"Still… Oz, huh?" he mused aloud. "You know, I knew a guy named Ozpin. He even talks a bit like you."

"Whaaat? Is Ozpin a bird, too?" Bennett asked in an exaggerated fashion, though Jaune learned early on that it was just his nature. The boy strode ahead of everybody, and had turned to walk backward in order to talk to them.

Jaune shook his head. "He was a human. The headmaster of the academy I attended, in fact."

"His true form, mayhap," Fischl cut in. "Yet who could say what shape he may take as his soul crosses the borders of reality. Why, Oz here is a fine example. His days in my home world of Immernachtreich were spent in equal measure as raven and dashing gentleman."

"My memories are rather hazy of those times. Apologies, Mein Fräulein."

"Oh please, dear Oz, do not apologize. I relish the chance to recount the olden tales. Few from this world know of my legend."

Home world. This world. Jaune's pace slowed as he turned the phrases over in scrutiny. With care, he observed Fischl, noting the clear disconnect between her style of dress and that of a person like Bennett. Ruffles and ribbons on a rich fabric, dyed in black and violet, in place of proper travel garb. Speech patterns that bordered on incomprehensible to those unfamiliar with her, as if deriving from an entirely separate culture.

He couldn't believe it.

Zooming in close, he dropped his hands on her shoulders, peering into her one visible eye with a serious look.

"You too?"

"Pardon?" Fischl squeaked, thrown by the sudden shift in his demeanor.

"You're from another world, like me?" he pressed.

Slowly, the startled look on Fischl's face changed, blooming into a bright grin.

"Yes! I most certainly am!" She tossed her hair, and laughed. "Verily, to imagine that our paths may have crossed with but a moment's chance. What fortune guides our fate that we meet again in strange lands!"

Quite a turnaround from earlier epithets of beast, cad, scoundrel, and the like. He was also pretty sure he never met this girl before in his life, but the time shenanigans theoretically possible with the portal made that assertion rather iffy. He might not have met this girl before yet.

"Whoooa," went Bennett in awe. "I can't believe I'm meeting a second traveler from another world! Hey, mister, is the princess's home really as amazing as she says?" he asked, almost hopping in excitement. "Is it?"

Jaune glanced at Fischl, whose face had begun to sweat profusely. She gave him a jerky nod.

"Yes?" he ventured.

"I knew it!" Bennett shouted, pumping his fists. "One day, I'm going to go there. No ifs, ands, or buts."

"Ah-Ahem." Fischl drew herself up in a regal pose. "And on that day, thou shall be welcomed with all due honors as a true companion of the Prinzessin der Verurteilung. Unfortunately, that happy occasion will be a long time yet, and so might I suggest we put our efforts toward the vital quest entrusted to our care? Royalty such as I must answer the wishes of the common masses, after all."

"Right!" agreed Bennett easily. "Oh man, I'm so stoked! The adventures are just lining up one after another for Benny's Adventure Team!"

Since he did not have his eyes on the road, Bennett failed to see the rock on the ground and he promptly tripped over it. Having been on the lookout for that exact scenario, Jaune lunged forward to seize the clumsy boy by the shirt, yanking him upright and putting him back on his feet before Bennett even realized.

The boy patted himself down, surprised at the lack of injuries. The uncertainty soon faded, replaced by the bottomless well of energy he seemed to possess.

"Thanks a lot, boss!"

Boss. Jaune liked that one, too.

"From the sound of it, you two have an idea of what's ahead on this road," he said, fishing for information.

"Yeah, Liyue Harbor should be right around the corner," Bennett explained as he pointed at the mountain crevice down the road. He then regarded Jaune oddly. "You didn't know? How come you were traveling this way?"

Jaune pushed his hands into his jacket pockets, leaning back as he walked to bask in the breeze. The sun was starting to set, and the mountains had taken on an orange glow. Beautiful, it was.

"I'm just doing what any traveler would," he said with a lazy smile.

Bennett scratched his cheek. "I don't really get it… but that's amazing! As for us, me and Fischl got a job from the Adventurers' Guild to deliver a letter. There's someone that needs to arrange funeral rites in the Liyue custom."

"Wouldn't that be a job for a mailman or a courier?" Jaune asked with a frown.

"Perish the thought," said Fischl. "Why, the uncountable dangers of this journey can only be matched by one with my forbidden powers."

Bennett chimed in. "Honestly, Katheryne was going to give it to someone else until I beg—volunteered for it. Between me and Fischl, we convinced her to let us give it a shot."

"Did she say what the problem was?"

"I wouldn't call it a problem," said Bennett. "It's just that we haven't ever left Mondstadt before."

"Katheryne does worry so," Fischl sighed. "Yet, every rose must bloom, and the time has come for I, the Prinzessin der Verurteilung, to retake my rightful position of worldwide acclaim. 'Twas the fate written in the stars, and as the proud creed of that grandest endeavor proclaims—ad astra abyssosque!"

"Ad astra abyssosque!" Bennett echoed with all his heart.

Jaune jotted down a mental note to find out what the heck that meant later.

Oz flew over to him, and whispered, "The kind receptionist was afraid they would get lost along the way. She only agreed once I assured her I had memorized the map."

He laughed under his breath at the revelation. This Katheryne sounded like quite a mother hen.

Their party arrived at the gap between the mountain, and passed under the stone arch. As they crested a slope, a city came into view. Jaune whistled at the sight.

Bustling was a good word to describe it. Set beside the sea, dozens of ships were coming and going. The docks formed a hive of activity with little figures running pell-mell. The city was built to fit the natural contours of the mountains, and further up from the docks he spied hundreds, maybe thousands, of people walking through the streets.

The buildings featured that particular style of Mistral. Sloped roofs with upturned corners. The upper floors grew smaller as they stacked higher, with outside walkways lined by intricate balconies. A lot of red and gold.

Above it all floated an island, on that a palace. It reminded him of Atlas the time his family visited, except for one thing.

Atlas had overshadowed Mantle. Cast it into an eternal gloom that seeped into the very life of the people there. He hadn't enjoyed the lower city as much as its upper half.

This island, it… illuminated. It crowned the city. Apart, yet a part.

They followed the road, and soon made it down to the grand gates of Liyue. A small setback, namely his lack of identification papers, was resolved when the two members in good standing of the Mondstadt Adventurer's Guild vouched for him, as did news of their important task.

"Wangsheng Funeral Parlor? Rex Lapis helps you poor bastards," the guard muttered as Jaune walked by him, which was not at all worrying.

Getting on the main avenue, they joined the throngs of people. The streets were packed despite the onset of evening, often forcing them to walk shoulder to shoulder. Roadside stalls hawked snacks and drinks, but also goods of all stripes. Jade figurines, gold jewelries, good luck charms, and more.

"Woooow, it's so different from Mondstadt…" Fischl gushed, twirling around and around to take in every detail. With a jerk, she composed herself. "I mean… Lo! What evanescent beauty graces mine eyes. 'Tis a fair reminder of sweet Immernachtreich which yonder lies."

Her fellow adventurer held no such reservations, and was running to and fro to look at whatever caught his fancy.

Jaune alternated his gaze between the two overexcited kids, and chuckled at the pure wonder on their faces. They were becoming distracted at record speed. That was to be expected of one's first trip far from home.

He had his own problems right now, but…

"Alright, you two, steady on." As the experienced person, it was up to him to take charge. He clapped his hands together to refocus their attention. "You have a job to do."

"They're selling books over there! Oz, let's go!"

"Swords! So many swords! So cool!"

Jaune sighed as he watched their disappearing backs. He got the sense that he was going to have a busy time wrangling these kids.


Universe: Genshin Impact.
Location: Liyue. Event: The Drowned Yaksha​
