#5,167
Chapter 65: Down Where It's Wetter (Pt. 3)​


The mud surged throughout the cavern.

Out of it arose figures to block Jaune's view of Menogias, the writhing masses warping around and around until they contoured to the appearances of people, the details sharpening into focus in a way the rest of the Domain could not imitate.

The… Dolls? Golems?… undertook activities that made little sense, from dancing to eating imaginary food to even dueling one another. Closest to him, two men dressed in antiquated clothing carried on a silent conversation over a chess board, their chests rising and falling with breath, the lips forming the shape of words, oblivious to what was happening around them.

A stutter then passed through the chess players and others nearby. Expressions shorted out, and actions ceased. A person could have heard a pin drop in the silence.

Slowly, oh so slowly, they twisted their heads to look at him.

From this angle, the wrongness stood out. The faces of the mud men were indistinct, half-finished facsimiles of life. Something like a mouth. Something like a nose. A blank expanse where eyes should be.

Jaune blanched at the uncanny sight.

When the mud men opened their not-mouths wide, no sound escaped. Yet, the roar echoed in his mind, so well did they mimic the throes of rage. Shambling steps carried them toward him, reminding him of zombies.

Dead man, so dead minions. Simple enough.

His allies fanned out behind him in a loose formation, weapons held at the ready. Bennett scanned the area with an uneasy look, with Fischl who settled a short distance behind him no less disturbed. Oz took to the air above the two adventurers, wing beats erratic from agitation. Hu Tao frowned hard as she stared in the direction of Menogias, while Zhongli behaved as serenely as ever.

"Boss, what's the call?" asked Bennett.

In answer, Jaune darted ahead to sweep his sword through the chess players, cutting them in half. The bodies collapsed into plain mud at his feet.

"What else?" he called back in a loud voice. "It's clear that he's hostile. I don't even think he's alive anymore. We're taking him down!"

With that, he charged forward. A small part of his mind couldn't help but let out a mental whoop at the prospect of this fight. A battle against a zombie god for whatever illustrious prize might await at the end, it was the stuff of movies.

The first enemy he met dressed like a soldier, and the shield to Crocea Mors popped into being to block an incoming sword strike, batting it aside for Jaune to then cut him down. He rotated his wrist as Pyrrha taught him to reverse the momentum of the swing, bringing it up to dispatch what appeared to be a teahouse waitress still holding her tray—all she needed was a bit of color and it would make her lifelike. She displayed no martial prowess, keeling over without ado.

Something about that unsettled him, but he pushed it out of mind. Pressing the offensive, he advanced with a series of slashes to fell enemies left and right.

At this stage, he was playing a simple role. The party knew very little what their opponents could do. Therefore, someone had to take on the risk of bearing the brunt of the assault.

Through the exchange, he concluded that the mud men posed minimal threat to his allies. Foes that could be struck down with effortless, and guiltless, impunity. Meaning, they could hold the line without him there. That reassurance allowed him to kick off, shooting into the air above the horde.

Up here, it hit him in full the power that Menogias wielded. The entrance he came in from counted as just one of many, with other exits leading to sections of the Domain he had not even begun to scratch. The chamber itself moved to the yaksha's will, the mud forming an ever-shifting landscape of hills, dips, cliffs, and pits; pools of water churned as the ground beneath them refused to calm. Mud figures populated the space, and barring those that have noticed the intruders, they carried on their nonsensical actions in a seeming loop, with no distinction of time and occasion. Their dense numbers combined with the obscuring darkness led to a chaotic, squirming mass that resembled some kind of orgy. In places, it was.

Between these scenes, other shapes sprang up in the dim light. Trees and animals. Walls and furniture. They framed the activities of the golems, painting a hundred little moments.

He scanned the area where he last spotted Menogias, or whatever it was that remained of Menogias after his drowning, trading shield for scroll to use the device's flashlight. A glimpse of tattered robes among the mud men, and he swapped his sword for Ruhm, swinging the long rifle around with one hand in an almost careless motion and squeezing down the trigger. His 'marksmanship' did the rest, the roaring bullets finding targets with preternatural accuracy until the barrel pointed to the yaksha, and a three-shot burst streaked across the cavern.

He tsked when a wall of mud burst upward, which the bullets splashed harmlessly against. The half-dome covered most angles, forcing him to adjust. Away went his rifle as he rocketed toward the wall. A close-range approach might see him fare better.

Halfway there, parts of the wall's surface began twisting into spirals. He had a second to wonder what the play was before the spikes catapulted at him. A roll to the side allowed him to evade the first projectile. Then, he cut out power to his boots, falling out of the air to go under the subsequent attacks.

The golem below turned its face upward right on time for him to stomp on, serving as a springboard for him to jump toward the next mud man. The second impromptu stepping stone led to a third then a fourth until he had gathered enough momentum to run on the crowd. He hit the wall in no time at all and, boosted by the rockets, scrambled up the sloping surface to swing over the edge. It put him right on top of Menogias.

Up close, the faint scent of rot lingered around him, and veins traced beneath his blue-tinted skin. His robes would have once been a thing of envy, richly-woven. Now, it hung off of his frame in pieces, with the fabric torn up to his knees and elbows, stained with muck.

A small and innocuous strip of metal appeared in his hand, easily dismissed for those unaware of its function. The Inhibitor Collar shut down powers of many different stripes, so long as he could get it around a person's neck. If it worked on the yaksha, the battle was won.

Got you, thought Jaune with mere inches to go.

The milky eyes barely registered his presence, yet Menogias snaked out his cold, lifeless hand with unerring accuracy to grab Jaune's own, squeezing down in an unrelenting grip that had him shouting in pain. Cracking noises between his fingers warned of a very fashionable choker breaking to pieces.

He discarded the plan without missing a beat, summoning a sword to his untrapped hand. Mud in the shape of a serpent coiled around that wrist, snapping his arm back with a sharp pull to suspend him in the air.

"Demons, you never learn! Bonanus will enjoy slaying you!" Menogias shouted through a mouthful of sharp teeth that contorted his human features. The yaksha's head abruptly tilted back, and he screeched at the ceiling. "Bonanus, why? Your fault! Your fault! Your faaault!"

"The time here did a number on you, huh?" Jaune said, not without sympathy. Centuries spent in the dark sounded like hell, not to mention the drowning part.

Despite that, he offered no hesitation in kicking up a foot, the rocket exhaust burning below his heel primed to sear a line along the yaksha.

Menogias sidestepped the attack with a speed and grace Jaune did not anticipate from a mad, dead body, the motion revealing the giant open palm sprouting out of the ground behind him. Jaune had only time to voice an "Ah, fu—" and then the hand rammed into him with the force of a train.

The blow shot him straight through the barrier at his back and over the length of the cavern. He tried to recover midair with the rockets, but all that did was add a stylish flip to the arc just before he splatted against the high wall, sinking deep into the muck. Everything went dark and cold, the impact rattling his brain.

Slowly, gravity took hold and he peeled off the wall to drop back toward the ground. Bennett broke his fall, not because he caught him but by acting as a cushion. A second splat resounded across the chamber, leaving the two boys collapsed in an undignified heap. A mud man whacked Jaune on the head with a chair for extra insult.

That golem burst into fire, sparing it from his vengeance. As it crumbled to pieces, a dainty pair of legs entered Jaune's field of vision.

"Aiya, he sure gave you a thrashing. Are you alive? Do you need a coffin?" Hu Tao asked, leaning down to poke his cheek with her staff.

"What, no, I held my own," he protested (lied) as he climbed to his feet, one hand reaching down to help pull Bennett upright. "It was an epic showdown, you should have been there."

A shadow fell over them, prompting all three to look up. A huge ball of hardened mud was dropping down on their heads.

"Table this for later?"

"Oh ya."

They dove aside in the nick of time, and the rock slammed into the spot where they once stood. The missile held its solid form for a second before oozing into sludge. They didn't get a moment of break, with additional projectiles already on the way courtesy of Menogias. Not wishing to stick around for that, Jaune vacated the area with the others hot on his heels, racing toward their allies.

The battlefield on this side had changed in his absence to a mess of fallen golem and strange broken pillars, the presence of which could be explained by Zhongli calling up a new one with a gesture, kicking it over to crush his opponents beneath its weight.

"Well, that's new. Are you going to tell me this is another necessary skill for a funeral consultant, too?" Jaune commented as he passed the man to decapitate a mud soldier.

Needless to say, he hadn't believed the excuse the first time when it concerned the act of redirecting lightning.

"Of course not. It is but a simple party trick," Zhongli demurred.

Hu Tao swept by. "Don't bother, Jaune. My employee enjoys his mystique." The girl hopped on a fallen pillar, and taking her cue Jaune did the same. It gave them surer footing as they fought the golems.

Ignoring his supposed boss, Zhongli inquired, "How went your encounter with Menogias?"

"He hit me with a giant hand."

"That sounds like him." Zhongli threw his spear as a javelin to skewer a charging boar. The weapon scattered into motes of light that flew back to him, reforming in his grip as he flipped to evade one of the falling boulders. "According to legends, that is," he added, almost as an afterthought.

Hu Tao squinted suspiciously at him.

"Is he lucid?" Zhongli continued.

Jaune shook his head. "He can't even tell who he is talking to from sentence to sentence." He swept the legs out of a farmer and drove a sword through the mud man's chest, then turned back to Zhongli. "If there's a mind in there, it shattered a long time ago. Still, he isn't weak, and knows how to fight."

"I wager that he is retaining vestiges of his memory in life," said Zhongli, indicating the mud figures. "That is what we are seeing now. It stands to reason that his abilities honed in a thousand battles would also remain in some capacity. Even degraded, they are certain to be prodigious. He counted among the strongest of his kind."

"Not someone to fight alone, then. Good to know."

Zhongli looked at him with keen interest. "Do you have a plan?"

He thought about it as he plunged his sword into a golem.

"Why not do the exact same thing Menogias is doing? His forces outnumber us, but if we can change it to the five of us"—he glanced at the raven overhead—"six of us against just him, we're the one with the advantage."

"A simple scheme. Honorable in that peculiar way of war. I rather think a yaksha would approve. Yet, many stand between us and him."

Jaune nodded to acknowledge the point, then raised a finger to pause the conversation. "Let me see what I can do about that."

So saying, he soared upward for a better field of view. At his direction, Hu Tao sent out a swarm of her butterflies to illuminate the cavern, allowing him to spot, and target, more of the mud men. Ruhm settled into his hands.

An indescribable cacophony followed as he performed a strafing run. The rifle bucked like a wild horse from the constant recoil, jumping haphazardly from one target to the next to smash them apart in a spray of bullets. When the ammo ran out, he summoned new clips to reload, spinning in place to blast every which way. The mud men fell in lines, in clusters, in droves. Soon, he floated over a near empty field.

He looked back at his allies hunkered in a hole, and called out, "There we go, now we can—"

The mud within the chamber swirled and bubbled. In mere moments, an army surfaced to stand in orderly formation. They wore the same uniform of an ancient design, each armed with a proper weapon, albeit made of the same material as everything else.

"Aaand I wasted my ammo for nothing." He tossed Ruhm back in his Pocket, opting instead for his gunlance and a suit of armor. Gear more suited for the upgraded mud men. The heavy weight dragged him down and he cut off power to his boots entirely rather than waste the battery, dropping from the air to hit a hill like a meteor. Mud splashed high from the impact, a crater forming beneath his feet. He stood up amidst the golems.

A swing of the gunlance shattered their front ranks to clear him space. Turning with the momentum, he brought the lance up in an overhead swing that squashed an approaching swordsman. A pull of the trigger shot a shell that tore through a column of enemies before exploding.

Big and loud, his actions screamed for Menogias to focus on him, and the yaksha obliged. The golems swarmed toward him from every direction.

They fought as a military unit, with tactics and roles, doctrine and discipline. Mud with the memory of war, they possessed a fearlessness rarely seen in the living.

That didn't help them much as Jaune waded into their ranks, laying about with his lance. Heavy steel and the hardened scales of a Rathalos won out against earthen imitations of weapons and armors, and the golems fell by the dozens without putting more than scratches on him.

Pillars of rocks preceded the arrival of his party. Fischl vaulted atop one, an arrow nocked in her bow. The shot flew high to intercept a spear cast by Menogias before it could land on Jaune. A shield blocked a blade meant for his back, Bennett then striking the ground with his sword and activating his fire magic, setting off an explosion to topple a row of soldiers on their rears. The boy ducked as Jaune's gunlance swept above his head to slap aside a volley of arrows.

"Keep one eye on the sky; combat is three dimensional," Jaune advised, and Bennett nodded in thanks.

Soldiers marched in a column up the hill to reinforce their brethren. Jaune took a step, intending to go meet them, but a rock pillar sprouted in front of him. A look at Zhongli provided him the hint, and he rammed into the pillar, breaking the base to send it rolling down the hill, flattening the lot. Zhongli pressed the opening with a kick that launched his spear end over end to destroy another couple of golems, Hu Tao following up to set a squad of soldiers on fire, rendering them brittle for Jaune to crush by simply charging through them. The instant he slowed down, Bennett was there to continue the combo, and in this vein they knocked over the golems in quick succession.

And then Menogias closed the distance.

Half a minute later, Jaune sailed across the cavern to go splat against the wall.

"Owww," he groaned, a perfect summation of the beatdown he just took.

A lot could be criticized of Menogias's martial skills. How it trended toward a savage bent due to his deteriorated mind for example. The yaksha compensated for it with a versatile flair for his chosen element, to make fighting him a horrible experience.

As he pulled himself out of the muck, a loud smack resounded and after a brief lull he ended up smushed into the wall again, his arms full of Hu Tao.

"Owww," she groaned, laying limp with her hat askew.

He spat out the mud in his mouth, and asked, "You, too?"

"Giant hands used me as a ball," she confirmed. "It wasn't as funny as when it happened to you."

Memories of being ping-ponged back and forth until he wanted to puke filled his mind, causing him to shiver.

They couldn't stay here, however. Him, especially. He was the vanguard. The one to hold the line.

The line, waaay over there.

Pushing off the wall, a glider appeared on his back, the wings unfurling. The magic in it failed to do more than slow his fall due to Hu Tao's weight, but activating the rocket boots allowed him to descend at an angle, putting them closer to the fighting. He let Hu Tao off there, and plunged right back into the fray.

He fired a shot of his rifle as an opener. A mud soldier suicided rather than let it hit Menogias.

The yaksha, meanwhile, cracked Bennett across the chin with his fist to drop the adventurer. His head jerked out of the way of Fischl's arrow, and a gesture sent a squad of golems chasing after her. He then turned back to deal with Bennett, who was getting up. His foot rose and fell, stomping the boy into the mud.

A flash of gold streaked toward the yaksha and his blade, a slender straight sword of quality forge quite unlike the replicas he armed his soldiers with, batted aside Zhongli's thrown spear. It was a mere prelude, for a ring of rock pillars manifested, each shooting on an angle from a different direction at Menogias.

By some strange twist of fate, their weight proved too much for the unstable ground, and the bases of the pillars sank down. Only inches, yet it caused all of them to veer just a little off course to miss the yaksha. Zhongli's eyes widened at the sight, looking more panicked than most of them had ever seen him. It allowed Menogias the opportunity to stab down at Bennett without hesitation.

A shadowy arm yanked the boy away before the sword could land, leaving Menogias to strike the empty ground. The yaksha stared at his dirtied sword for a brief moment, then slowly straightened to his full height and turned to look at the culprit, Jaune, head twitching to the side in an unconscious motion.

Jaune returned the unblinking stare while dragging his ally upright. "You did well, Bennett. I'll tag in here, so keep the minions off my back."

"G-Got it." The woozy Bennett threw a sloppy salute and picked his sword off the ground, stumbling off to leave Jaune facing down Menogias.

"You took it!" Menogias said with a smile that curled into a snarl. "You took it, so why won't you wear it!?"

Jaune lifted his lance and shield, setting into a stance. "He's not a coat, what are you even on about?"

With a scream, Menogias bounded forward, slashing his sword. The blade crashed down on Jaune's shield with an unnatural strength that caused him to sink a few inches into the ground. It left Menogias wide open, and so Jaune swapped from the long lance to the shorter sword and stabbed the man in the gut, piercing the swirling mud that had sprung up to protect the yaksha and striking flesh.

A small burst of fire lit up the wound, the paper seal pasted on the blade crumbling as thick, black ichor seeped out. Yet, no pain showed on the yaksha's face, not even a flinch. A swift kick knocked Jaune back, a muddy tendril with a sharpened needle point chasing after him.

Jaune ducked under the tentacle and cut it in half. His sword traded place with his gunlance, and he hid behind its bulk as mud in the shape of an ocean wave smashed into him. He braced his shoulder against the weapon to hold his position, then kicked the head of the lance so that it swung up to smack the approaching Menogias on the chin, cracking a few of his fangs. Pivoting, he slammed the lance into a giant hand to demolish it before it could fling him away, following through on the motion to break apart a protective barrier that had manifested and whack Menogias directly on the side. The blow sent the yaksha skidding over a fair distance but failed to topple him, blocked upon bare arms that bled from the harsh impact.

Menogias laughed, oblivious to his wounds. He pointed at Jaune. "Look, I made this for you. It fits well, I do believe." To Jaune's consternation, he felt the mud below him crawl up along his body. He glanced at the wider battlefield, noticing the same occurring to the others. "You will wear it, will you not, Bonanus? The next one will be for our brother Bosacius. Like me, he has been so forgetful these days. Then perhaps a robe for Alatus. I know he would consider it too bothersome, but…" His eyes softened. "It would keep you all safe."

The creeping sensation of being buried alive did not make Jaune feel safe. If anything, it reminded him of memories best left behind.

"Get off of me!" he shouted, and with a surge of strength he broke free, the mud encasing him falling to pieces.

The yaksha stopped laughing. "Ungrateful cur," he hissed.

A rumble passed beneath their feet, and giant hands appeared all over the chamber.

Jaune turned pale. "Wait, hang on—"

Slap, slap.

Slap, slap, slap.

Slap.

Jaune hit the far wall.

Soon, Bennett, Fischl, and Hu Tao followed his example, plastering the mud around him in various poses. Gradually, they all peeled off to fall down to the ground in a groaning, crumpled heap.

He was the first to get up. A field of hands greeted him, taking the place of the fallen soldiers. He made a rude gesture at them, and they mimicked it right back.

"Boss," Bennett said weakly from where he laid, eyes still spinning. "I don't think the plan is working."

Ooh, Jaune heard a bit of bite in that. Like a puppy's yip, but it was there. So proud.

Fischl sat up, and spat a lock of hair out of her mouth. "We had a plan?"

"Of course we do," Jaune reassured her. "It's a very sophisticated one that I put together with a lot of thought. With multiple phases and everything."

"Which phase are we at now?" Hu Tao asked, propping up her shaky legs with her staff.

Jaune turned to face the chamber, and inhaled a deep breath.

"Retreat! Retreeeat!"

Ten minutes later, peace had returned to the cavern. Menogias, the drowned yaksha, wandered his realm with an aimless and vacant demeanor, the intruders an old, lost memory. Out of sight, out of mind.

Deep inside a tunnel branching off of the chamber, four clumps of mud, a bird, and Zhongli huddled in a circle. From time to time, the consultant received an envious glare from his companions for his immaculate state. Aside from the man who knelt on the balls of his feet, the rest of them sat on the floor, at this stage no longer bothered by the sloshy surface.

"We might be in over our heads," Hu Tao summed up the situation. It opened the floodgates for discussion among the group.

"What is even the point of hitting mud over and over!"

"The sea of stars would fade from the ephemeral sky before our efforts bear fruit, is what Mein Fräulein meant to say."

"Can you kill mud? I feel like it's really unsporting that Meno-guy gets to have a never-ending supply of soldiers."

"Not soldiers anymore. He has a never-ending supply of hands."

A shudder passed through the four muddy clumps.

"Look, hear me out," Jaune said, and they all leaned in to listen. "What if we funnel the mud out into the sea somehow? That would leave him with nothing to control."

"Ah, yes," Hu Tao replied, nodding eagerly, "let's drill a hole into the bottom of the undersea cave… and then watch as water fills all the way to the tippity top." She nudged him with her elbow. "We can die together, hee-hee."

Jaune squinted at her. "Don't you 'hee-hee' me."

She showed an unrepentant smile. The unserious attitude got a laugh out of Bennett and Fischl, the two adventurers relaxing minutely.

Bennett sat back. "What about that loud crossbow you keep pulling out?" he asked Jaune. "Looks like a Fatui weapon. It was pretty effective."

"A gun." Jaune waved the idea away. "I can arm all of you with them, but the problem there is the supply of ammo. It isn't endless like your arrows. Besides, with you new to using them, you'll be more of a danger to each other than to Menogias."

"I don't like them, anyway," Hu Tao said. "They hurt my ears and don't even give off big fireworks for it."

"An explosion…"

"No, don't go there, Fischl," said Bennett. "With my and Jaune's luck, I get the feeling it'd bring the cave down on our heads."

For a while, ideas of that nature continued to bounce back and forth. A lot of them went nowhere. A few warranted further thought, with Jaune inevitably putting a pin on each of them due to glaring faults. As it dragged on, he passed around refreshments.

After a pitch by Hu Tao on the merits of smoking Menogias out of his chamber by setting fires at all the exits except one (Advantage #1: they would have all the time in the world, while he didn't), the heretofore silent Zhongli cleared his throat, the gesture quieting the group.

With the air of one talking of the weather, he said, "You neglect an obvious solution, and one I advise. At a time like this, why not simply withdraw? After all, this trip has yielded profits for us already."

The suggestion hung between the group after Zhongli finished speaking. It seemed to take many of them by surprise, judging by Bennett's and Fischl's reaction. Quite likely his own too, had he a mirror.

They could just… stop.

Before that idea took further root, Jaune quickly moved up to a knee, putting out both his hands.

"Whoa, hey now. That's a little premature." He cracked a winning smile, throwing finger guns as Zhongli looked his way. "This is about us planning things out, not us giving up. The situation back there is just a challenge. A hiccup. I've faced worse predicaments."

Zhongli cocked his head, studying Jaune as if he was a strange object. "You are here for treasure, correct? Riches? We have found much. More than enough to call this venture a success. I am sorry to say, but the bedraggled state of Menogias does not inspire the prospect of wealth. Why go to the trouble, if it isn't necessary?"

"Well, yeah, but…" said Jaune, smile fading as he scratched his cheek. He glanced down the passage in the direction of the cavern.

"Boooo, stop being a killjoy, Zhongli!" Hu Tao pouted.

"Nevertheless, my employer, I should remind him that we neither hold the same goal as him, nor are we beholden to his whims. And…" Zhongli drummed his fingers on a knee, betraying a jitteriness to his calm facade. His expression tightened in the slightest of frowns. "Certain signs not readily visible to you have led me to believe it is unwise to proceed. Putting you aside, Hu Tao, our young adventurers have experienced more than their fair share of danger."

"Wait, no!" Bennett protested, waving his arms in denial. "We're okay, we want to be here. Right, Fischl?"

Fischl nodded rapidly once the attention turned to her. "Just so! Let it never be said that the Prinzessin der Verurteilung quails in the face of mortality. One as long-lived as I walks with death as a dear companion."

"She is not scared, milady insists," Oz added.

"See?" said Bennett. "It's alright with us. If Jaune wants to keep at it, we'll follow him."

It flattered Jaune that they thought highly of him. Yet, Zhongli undercut that declaration with a casual hum.

"That you can, does not equate that you should. What is your reason, Mister Bennett, that makes this endeavor so pressing? You too, Miss Fischl."

The man waited for a response, and the pair did their best to meet that challenge. For adventure. For treasure. For loyalty, because they had to repay Jaune for him helping them.

Their words rang hollow, with innocence and youth and heart in place of any true desire to be here, in this place. Once Bennett and Fischl ran out of things to say, Zhongli turned to Jaune with a knowing look.

By now, Jaune had come to understand what the consultant was getting at. If he sought an easy payday, Menogias was the further thing from it, to say nothing of those cryptic words Zhongli spoke. Better to direct his attention elsewhere, rather than grow tunnel-visioned on one obstacle just because he sank time and effort into it already. At no point did he have to do anything. It was his life.

"..."

The man gave him some time to think about it, but as the silence stretched on, the atmosphere among the others grew antsy. Like Zhongli, they were also waiting for him. In their case, to hear what wisdom he could convey to justify continuing on this course, perhaps a grand ambition which drove him that they would be playing a part in. Patience soon started to wane.

In the end, Zhongli made the deciding move.

"Be satisfied with what you have, for greed has turned many an adventure into a cautionary tale." He straightened to his full height and turned his back to begin to walk away, voicing over his shoulder, "Let me leave you with this. The yakshas knew it would end in this fate. It is the karma they have earned, as ordained by the heavens." He sighed softly. "Let them be."

The departure pierced through the sea of half-thoughts, doubts, and unfinished explanations swimming around in Jaune's head. Hurriedly, he blurted out what came to mind.

"It's your fault."

That brought Zhongli to a halt. He looked back, cocking an eyebrow.

"Pardon?" the man asked.

Jaune shrugged. On his face, he once again wore an easy-going smile. It might not have been the best opener, but it rang with the truth and that was enough for him.

He pointed at the side of his head, and said, "I blame you for this, you know. You filled my head with stories. A band of heroes protecting the world, slaying monsters that threatened the innocent… I grew up on stuff like that. I wished I could do something like that. Saving the day, meeting the girl, finding my ever after."

At his side, Hu Tao snickered.

"Oh?" she said in a teasing tone. "I didn't take you for the romantic type. Just so you know, there's only ever one ending."

He snorted upon getting her insinuation. Of course a funeral director would believe that.

Their exchange passed beneath Zhongli's notice. The man had fully turned around. Hands clasped behind his back, he tilted his chin to gaze at the ceiling in thought.

"Aspirations, then." The corner of Zhongli's lips curled upward. "You dream of a fairy tale. Of making a legend for the ages, so that we should remember your name."

A desire born of ego, went the unspoken criticism. Which sounded fair enough, though not quite right.

"It's nothing that ambitious," Jaune admitted. "This is, probably, just my own silliness." That drew curious looks from the others, to which he shook his head. He ran a hand through his hair, chuckling under his breath at the memories that had resurfaced, and explained, "I once met someone, and what I remember most about him was something he told me. That no matter how bleak the world may become, the sun still shines; every morning, it rises… A small and ordinary everyday thing, and it would always get him back up after he went down, because to him seeing that sun was worth all the pain and misery. He was… silly, in thoughts and actions. And I admired him for it."

He jerked a thumb over his shoulder in the vague direction of the cavern.

"In there, is a hero."

Whatever he was now, a monster, a beast, a vengeful spirit… Menogias lived as a hero. Done his duty, and brought peace back to the land.

Jaune looked at Hu Tao, who taught a side of ghosts and spirits new to him.

"Maybe Menogias earned his fate, and this is what he deserved. But I don't like that," he told her. "I feel like he has been waiting a long time to get his rest. And that's something I want, too, I think. For him to rest. It could be a reason for me to try."

Hu Tao pondered on it, pursing her lips. Then, she showed a little smile. "I'll agree with that part, at least. In death, one dies. It's past his time to go."

"Perhaps," allowed Zhongli, his gaze never leaving Jaune's face. "It behooves me to warn you again that there may be consequences, of which all of you could well find that you cannot escape."

"I'll live with that." He looked down for a moment, barely a flicker. "I've tried taking the other option recently. All the excuses that sounded reasonable beforehand didn't really make me feel any better in the aftermath."

"It is not wrong to realize some situations are beyond you."

"Heh. That was one of them." Hearing it decided his course for certain. "I'm going to head back in there."

"I suppose I shall as well. The last chapter simply must finish on a happy note," Fischl declared in a grand manner. Jaune nodded to her in support of the sentiment. She enjoyed reading stories, and so might understand him on this more than most. "Of all the worlds I have visited, that one truth has ever been the natural order. Is that not so, my loyal attendant?"

Bennett sheepishly rubbed the back of his neck. "C'mon, you know I don't get that complicated stuff, Fischl… but I do feel bad for the guy, yeah."

Jaune broke out in laughter, reaching over to clap Bennett on the shoulder. "You're pretty much on the same page with me, then." He glanced up at Zhongli. "I'll admit it, all of this is really just for myself."

Money, treasure, artifacts. Any of it could sway him. They brought him here. But they were means. Things to use up and toss away in the pursuit of a goal.

Above them all, what he wanted was to see a different ending to a miserable tale.

Rising to his feet, he performed a stretch to limber up. Once done, his sword appeared to hand and he swung it to point down the tunnel.

A calm certainty he had never known settled in his heart, steady as a rock.

"Selfishly, I'm not letting his story end any other way."
