Something clinked among the various items within the poncho's many pockets.
The owner of the garment would not find it until later.
At the moment, he only caught a glimpse of color at the corner of his eyes.
A blazing gold.


-o-​


Jaune weaved his glider among the huge crisscrossing serpents formed of mud. Spotting a gap, he fired up his rockets and burst out into freedom. It put him high in the air over the cavern, near the ceiling. He whipped out his rifle, firing off a couple of rounds at Menogias as a diversion, then folded the wings and shot downward at the yaksha. At the last second, his body flipped to lead with his legs.

His boots slammed down on arms caked in mud, the material hardened to the likeness of steel. If that hurt Menogias any, he showed not a sign. Blue eyes glared into milky-white.

The sound of a splash alerted him, and he ducked his head just as a tendril shot past. A backfist smashed apart the limb before it could reconstitute into a new attack. His frame then suddenly lurched as Menogias swung his arm to toss him aside, Jaune's weight proving no obstacle to the yaksha.

Jaune landed in a squat, and immediately charged forward again.

Far behind Menogias, Bennett brought down one of the mud hands. The action went unnoticed by the yaksha, whose eyes only saw Jaune.

Summoning his sword, he slashed at Menogias, the blade meeting another blade—or rather, an odd barrier encasing Menogias's blade. The two vied for an advantage, pressing with their full strength. Jaune counted the beats. One, two, three—

He stepped aside, allowing the spearman golem to stab through the space he vacated, right at Menogias. A dead man followed habits more than thoughts, a flaw that the living could exploit if they grasped the pattern, and Jaune had ample chances to do so. (It was either learn or get wrecked, giving him great motivation to improve quickly.)

The spearman lost its form before it touched Menogias, and the yaksha walked into and out of the mud without harm. By that time, Crocea Mors had swapped for Red Rook, the gunlance screaming through the air. The huge lump of metal and scales caught Menogias across the torso, whipping him into the ground to bury him.

Not even a second later, Menogias burst out of the mud, sword aimed at Jaune's throat in the moment that the follow-through of the gunlance pulled at his balance. The blade did not find its target, clanging against a shield that 'coincidentally' blocked the yaksha's view of Fischl as she dispatched another giant hand.

It was impossible to tell what the yaksha could or could not see, or how his mind interpreted things. Jaune chose to play it safe, holding the shield for longer than he needed to despite it resulting in a powerful punch to his gut that sent him skidding back.

A quick glance over his shoulder confirmed that Fischl had moved on, disappearing behind a hill. Hu Tao was visible, however, so he bashed his sword against his shield, creating a racket that ensured Menogias continued paying attention to him. It turned out to be an unnecessary move, for Menogias had entered another one of his manic bouts.

"Where is it? I can't find it!" the yaksha cried, dropping to hands and knees to search the muck at his feet.

Wasting no time, Jaune aimed his gunlance and fired off a shot.

Irritatingly, for someone not all there, Menogias was too aware. A creature of instinct posed a serious threat when that instinct had been honed through years-long war. A mud wall snapped into place to divert the gunlance shell, with Menogias waking from his episode. The yaksha blinked once, and then rushed at him.

"Bonanus, where are you? Why won't you wear it, why won't you wear it, why won't you wear it, why won't you wear it, why won't you wear it, why won't you wear it, why won't you wear it, why won't you wear it—"

Jaune backpedaled under the onslaught of sword strikes. The speed of the attacks grew and grew as Menogias's words blurred together in a continuous scream, slicing into Jaune's legs and arms whenever he was too slow to shield in time.

Thinking fast, he freed a hand to grasp inside his Pocket for a paint bomb, an item of Escha's devise, and lobbed it at the yaksha, whose blade near instantly sliced it in half. A cloud of pink paint exploded to obscure Menogias. The loss of sensory inputs shorted out his assault, with the yaksha slowing his steps.

The insane ravings ceased, and a far gentler voice murmured, "What if I can no longer remember you? I feel like I am going mad…"

The soft words slipped past Jaune's defenses, and he lowered his lance which had been poised to retaliate.

"I'm sorry, but Bonanus is gone," he said sincerely.

Menogias heard it. Registered it. His face slackened in horror, and around him, the mud churned, giving rise to wild, chaotic shapes that changed from one thing to the next in the blink of an eye, a glimpse into his distorted mind.

Within it, Jaune spotted the form of a woman, hair floating and body sinking as if she was falling into the depths of the sea, her face a blank expanse without features. A different segment depicted Menogias swimming after her, his expression clear of their madness, yet wracked by desperate terror.

The woman vanished, but still the man swam down, seeking a sign. Until the air ran out, and he grasped his throat.

It culminated with the yaksha's favorite move, the imprint of a giant hand pushing out of the ground, leading Jaune to regret ever opening his mouth.

"Liar!" Menogias shouted as the hand rammed into Jaune to fling him away, gunlance and shield and all.

He stowed his weapons with a thought. Glider and rockets put him back in control, allowing him to transition into graceful flight. Jaune banked left to swing around, on course to return to the fight. Arrows the size of spears launched in his direction, prompting him to take evasive measures.

At this height, he had a view of everyone else. Bennett and Fischl on one side of the cavern, Hu Tao and Zhongli on the other.

Catching sight of the consultant, the words that the other man had said on the way back to the cavern echoed in Jaune's mind.

"I am not where I am meant to be, nor are the others. His fate lies with you."

Cryptic, as far as it went. Par for the course, concerning a lot of things Zhongli had told him. Nevertheless, he had rolled with it while forming his strategy, putting them to different tasks.

The mud moved to the will of Menogias when he paid attention. With his deteriorated mind, there wasn't much of that attention to go around, and outside his purview the golems default to a more basic and far less coordinated nature. Jaune's objective for the past while, therefore, involved distracting the yaksha to let the others set the stage.

The Mondstadt adventurers, he assigned to thinning the enemy ranks. The pair stayed mobile, close enough that one could respond should the other need help but otherwise focused on knocking down the golems beneath the notice of Menogias.

Hu Tao and Zhongli took the slow approach, with the latter raising pillars for the former to stand on. More than that, it served to dry out the cave. Under Zhongli's power, earth became rock, casting out the moisture that created the element of mud. Separated, they returned to the rule of Geo and Hydro, distinct from the domain of which Menogias reigned as king. The inferno that Hu Tao brought to bear accelerated the process, cooking the water out.

He just had to hold on a while longer, and the ideal battlefield would manifest.

Heading for the yaksha, he angled the glider for a steep dive, vanishing it as he approached his target. With a gesture from Menogias, mud spiraled into the shape of a lance to await his arrival, to which [Third Arm] pulled him slightly off course, enough to pass it by. His foot had only touched down for a split second before it kicked up at Menogias in a blow aimed at the temple. A barrier sprang up, the mud shield bleeding off the momentum of the attack. Hastily, Jaune yanked back his leg.

The slender straight sword snapped out, a brutal attempt to take his eyes. The helmet to the Rathalos suit popped into being, protecting him then vanishing so as not to block his field of vision. Rockets activated to launch him up, his knee crashing into Menogias's face and breaking a swirling protective layer of mud to throw the yaksha backward. Without touching the ground, he raced in pursuit. Even then, Crocea Mors only managed to swipe a shallow line on the yaksha's flesh before a deer burst from below to gore him on its antlers. He fell to the ground tangled with the false animal, the mud shifting to try and suffocate him.

As Jaune struggled to keep the muck from entering his nose and mouth, Menogias shambled over with the tip of his blade dragging on the ground. The yaksha snickered, a harsh and reedy sound due to the inches-long teeth.

"Even the animals of the forest cannot abide a demon."

Freed at last, Jaune rolled to his feet and brandished his sword. Menogias beamed a terrible smile at the sight, and brought his blade up in a similar stance.

"A practice bout, Alatus? Please go easy on me today," he said, unable to connect the person before him with the 'demon' of just seconds earlier.

Jaune didn't have the heart to correct him. He stepped forward, giving a quick slash that the yaksha parried, the retaliatory blow a casual overhead swing that crashed down with many times the force it should bear, caught on Jaune's blade on an angle that caused it to slide until it struck the crossguard. Jaune shoved it aside, and with a twirl of the sword stabbed at the exposed torso.

He detected the feint too late. The slender blade sliced right across his throat, a mere flicker to Jaune's eyes for how fast it was. His throat constricted at the phantom sensation of a slit neck, giving Menogias the opportunity to stab him in the belly, folding him in half then launching him end over end along the ground. Groaning, he pushed upward to eat a shoe to the face, his head snapping back to contort his body into a painful shape.

A hand with nails long like claws seized the front of his shirt. Menogias pulled him up, their faces inches apart. Jaune caught a whiff of the dead man's breath, and recoiled.

"Taking the form of my sworn brother?" Menogias hissed, his overgrown teeth clacking together. "Demon, you court death."

"I didn't!" Jaune protested, for the good it did. Judging by the snarling visage, he had made Menogias even madder for revealing himself as a 'liar'. Up became down as the yaksha swung him above his head, and delivered a kick that carried the weight of a mountain, the impact echoing in his mind to rattle his thoughts.

Jaune's back hit the far wall an instant later. Something behind him cracked as he slipped off the wall. He fell into a shallow pool of water.

Disoriented, he flailed around for the first few moments without any sense of coordination. An unwise gasp for breath filled his lungs with filthy water that he hacked and coughed back out. Clarity returned as one hand found purchase on the bottom of the pool, and pushed his head above the surface.

A lurch in his chest caused him to spit out the last of the water he inhaled. He looked back and forth to get his bearings, most of his vision obscured due to the divot he had fallen in. The situation seemed to have taken a turn with his absence, because suddenly he was hearing the distinctive slapping sound of hands.

"And it had been going so well," he said with a heavy sigh.

A trickle of water hit him on the top of his head. Tilting his chin up, he noticed cracks here and there in the wall, through which cleaner—yet saltier—water was pouring into the cavern. As a result, the surface of the pool had begun rising.

The shoddy construction of the Domain, built upon a drowning man's magic an age ago, bore defects that had now surfaced after a hard impact. The wall held, thankfully, but he gave poor odds of that continuing to be the case if they carried on in this manner.

"Note to self, buy breathing masks. Drowning is a bad way to go." Depending on how things went, that note might find use sooner rather than later.

[Third Arm] latched onto the opposite side of the water pool, but the soft mud crumbled in its grip rather than pull him across. He waded through the muck instead.

As he approached the edge of land, something washed up on it first. The new influx of water had disturbed the mud at the bottom, settled for who knew how long. Coming closer, he grabbed the object.

The first thing to register for him was the softness, the ephemeral fabric so fine that it seemed almost formless. Like he grasped pure color and nothing else between his fingers.

Still more of the object remained beneath the surface, and a tug removed the rest of it from the muck. The mud slipped off with ease to show pristine cloth, which floated in the air before slowly falling down, as if it weighed barely more than nothing.

Neckline, sleeves, bodice, he held a dress, its hue a light blue that reminded him of river streams and cloudless mornings, the layers fading to pure white as it moved inward. The broad sleeves fell almost to the hemline, and strips of cloth reminiscent of the long, gauzy fins of a tropical fish draped past the floor to create a flowing silhouette. Lily flowers sewn into the dress bloomed despite the centuries.

He had seen garments like it in Liyue Harbor, in the way that a man lying in the gutters had seen the city lights. The dress made the wealthiest ladies of the capital appear as paupers.

Jackpot—wait, no, why would a dress be here?

Menogias enjoyed making clothes, the stories had said. Jaune cast his mind back to the murals that recounted the last days of Menogias and Bonanus. The squiggles at the top could have been anything from an artist's signature to a bundle of snakes. Or, a flowing ribboned dress.

Shadows loomed over him. Jaune looked up, and found the many giant hands waiting for him at the top of the pit.

"Ah, right… I forgot about you guys," he said, and gulped nervously. That turned into bafflement as the hands continued to stand there without attacking. Wary of a trick, he began climbing out of the pool with great care.

Yet, even as he stood among them, the mud figures remained docile. Or at least, confused. They reached for him from time to time, only to jerk back. Working off of a suspicion, he held out the dress.

The hands in front of him backed off, while the one behind tried to grab him. He ducked under it, and skipped out of the encirclement. They turned to face him, but stayed still.

For whom was the dress made?

"Bonanus, where are you?" the yaksha had said, over and over.

Except, Menogias couldn't even remember her face. And that gave Jaune an idea.

First of all, he needed a better view. The rocket boots sputtered, water-logged, but soon engaged and threw him high. He scanned the cavern with a quick eye. The enemies had replenished a large number again without him to distract Menogias, putting back their progress to pretty much the starting line.

Which was fine. It had been a stupid plan, anyway. Seriously, who came up with it? (He did.)

He found his allies amidst the sea of dull brown by their colors, along with Menogias whose rage had redirected to Zhongli. The closest to him, Fischl, was fighting in close range, her bow firing without rest at giant hands and mud soldiers, while Oz supported her by casting lightning down on the golems from above. Together, they held their own, albeit always a hair's breadth from danger with the situation growing worse as time went on.

It reached a critical juncture, where enemies surrounded them on all sides.

"Oz, lightning!"

"A-Apologies, Mein Fräulein," Oz gasped, his wings flapping weakly. "Just a moment!"

Fischl almost screamed when something fell on her. The fresh spring scent stayed her hand from firing an arrow, and the surge of foes away from her definitely called up questions. She fumbled with the bundle of soft—heavenly so—fabric in order to make heads and tails of it, discovering that it was a dress.

A sword impaled a mud soldier through the head, with Jaune landing on its shoulder to cushion his descent. He rolled off it to land in front of her.

"Yo!"

Fischl perked up. "Jaune! You're alright!"

"I am, but hey, I need your help. Follow me." He punctuated the statement with a wild swing of his sword that did not so much cut as smash one of the giant hands in half, and turned his head. "Hu Tao! HU TAO!" His shout reverberated around the chamber, amplified by the space to a deafening volume.

A hat decorate with a branch of plum flowers peeked above the mud figures in the distance, with the rest of Hu Tao soon rising on a stone pillar, Zhongli on another one.

"We're going about this the wrong way. Time for a new plan!" he called to them, and pointed to the dress. "We'll give him what he wants. Then, let's hold a funeral!"

On some level, Menogias's minions recognized the dress. Which meant he recognized the dress. Lingering spirits could pass on with the help of the living, and they now had an in with the yaksha.

Could it work?

Jaune got his answer as Hu Tao's face lit up with a beaming smile. Drawn by her sudden good mood, a laugh escaped him.

"Everybody, gather up!" he yelled.

While Fischl ran off to find a semi-private spot to get changed, he zoomed across the cavern to regroup with his allies. They didn't have long, as Menogias was in hot pursuit, but a wall created from Zhongli's pillars gave them a momentary reprieve, enough for Jaune to fire off orders.

"Hu Tao!"

"Me!"

"Prepare the grave."

A shovel replaced her staff, held aloft with both hands. "On it~"

He blinked. "Wait, where did— And I didn't mean a literal grave— Oh, what the hell." Bennett scrambled into the huddle, and Jaune summoned his gunlance to fire a shot at the mud figures chasing him, blowing a hole through their ranks. He then promptly shoved the boy out of the huddle. "Bennett, keep the enemies off Hu Tao's back. As for Zhongli—"

"I shall officiate the ceremony," the consultant said. "There are more steps to it than a hole in the ground."

"Right, you do that." He spied Fischl moving toward him while fixing up the dress she had hastily donned, doing her best not to trip over the long garment. "Perfect, it's all coming together."

"And what of you?"

As the barrier keeping back Menogias shook and crumpled, Jaune answered, "It's pretty obvious."

Through hand gestures, he directed Oz to Hu Tao's side of things, then motioned to Fischl. The girl nodded, and followed him without slowing down.

"Chaaaarge!"

Jaune heard Zhongli sigh, and the man's complaints floated after them. "The funeral of an adeptus is one of particular ceremony. Of timing. Tradition. Peace and harmony."

He called back over his shoulder, "Sorry, but I don't understand anything about that, so I'll leave it up to you to figure out. I know you'll pull through!"

Somebody had to keep the yaksha busy. His job was to stand in the gap, and trust in his team.

The pillars gave up the ghost, collapsing. Menogias burst through with a wild roar, the mud rampaging around him in the form of dragons. His encounter with Zhongli had produced within him an all-consuming rage, for reasons Jaune could not begin to fathom.

All quieted, as the yaksha caught sight of Fischl and the dress she wore. The mouth full of ugly fangs fell open, slack-jawed.

Jaune nudged her, and said under his breath. "Show time, Fischl, let's hope this works… The dress looks good on you, by the way."

Fischl hid her face behind one of the gauzy shawls. "Thanks," she said in a small voice. "What should I do?"

Jaune didn't answer her, because he was kind of working on that part himself. Neither of them had a clue of how to imitate the mannerisms of Bonanus.

The point became moot with Menogias scrambling forward. In a blink, he stood before them, and he couldn't look away from the dress. The dress, not Fischl. To Jaune's shock, tears pooled at the corner of the man's eyes. Even the dead could cry.

"Now, I'll know…" the yaksha said—sobbed. "Now, I can be sure… that I will never hurt you…"

The gently spiraling mud behind Menogias told a story, and Jaune watched it play out.

Come the end, the yaksha had known of the fate awaiting him. Having forgotten his companions' faces, he devised a scheme: he would make clothes for them. His best works, that he may never mistake for another craftsman's. A dress for his sister in all but blood was to be the first of his gifts.

"Who are you that stands beside her?"

The hateful hiss crawled up Jaune's spine, and he tore his gaze from the shifting imagery to find the yaksha glaring at him.

"Huh?" Jaune said, eloquently.

A fist smashed into his face, dropping him on his rear. Jaune blinked stars out of his eyes.

"What are your intentions?" demanded Menogias, as he stared down at Jaune.

Oh greeeat, the yaksha had been set off by a different thing now. Save him from overprotective brothers.

"Nothing!" Jaune answered with full honesty. "Bennett is the one you're looking for!"

"What?" Fischl squeaked.

Jaune's protests fell on deaf ears, however. Menogias leapt for him, one hand brandishing his sword. It clanged against Jaune's own. A harsh kick sent him rolling back, which he used to regain his footing, summoning shield to hand as the next blow arrived.

A deflection, and Jaune countered with a swipe at the yaksha's chest, the attack meeting the roiling mud that settled into the shape of a breastplate. Kicking the ground, he created distance from Menogias, a space that the yaksha promptly closed. Their swords met again in a clash, this time forgoing a contest of strength in lieu of rapid strikes that sought the gaps in each other's defenses.

Before it could escalate too far, an arrow shot for the back of the yaksha's head courtesy of Fischl. A part of Jaune hoped for it to land, though he also winced. An assassination was several steps in a different direction from what he had been aiming for with his funeral ploy.

A mud soldier jumped into the arrow's path to put that worry to rest. Menogias sent more of them after Jaune, then whirled around to face the new threat. His eyes widened in disbelief.

"Bonanus?" Menogias said with a quaver in his voice.

"Um…" Fischl, frozen solid with nerves, glanced at Jaune for help. He swiftly dispatched the golems surrounding him and mimed getting rid of his weapon, a suggestion she heeded, hiding her bow behind her back. "It wasn't me."

Menogias broke out in a smile, relieved beyond measure. "No, never. I know you would not."

With the yaksha occupied for the moment (and Fischl feeling very guilty), Jaune checked on the other members of the team. As he had come to expect of them, he saw fire.

Hu Tao ran with her staff twirling in her hand, the tip aflame. Around her, Bennett and Oz scrambled to remove enemies from her path, wheezing for breath as the girl refused to stay still. The fire she cast, as ever, couldn't last long on the mud. The soot remained, however, and taking flight allowed Jaune to survey the design left in Hu Tao's wake—a curving strip full of angular lines that brought to mind a drawn maze, interspersed by scrawling stanzas and paper seals.

With a flourish, the end connected with the beginning, a wide circle now sketched out on the ground.

Hu Tao planted her staff, and slapped her hands together to bow.

"The Homa flames mark the boundary of life and death," she intoned, a soft smile on her lips. "Here stands an altar, a gate for the passing of a soul."

With a rumble, four of Zhongli's stone pillars rose out of the mud. They measured at equal distance, framing the circle Hu Tao made. Jaune let out a gasp as a golden, glowing energy swept along the markings, creating a wall that rose to the ceiling. Paper seals floated in midair, and the design on the ground extended upward to fill the barrier, the scripts flowing in shifting patterns along the surface. Mud golems that attempted to cross from one side to the other smushed against the partition without passing through.

Zhongli landed atop a pillar, and rose to stand upright, his hands clasped behind his back. He turned to look at Jaune.

"It will not hold for long. From this point on, do not let the spirit exit the line."

Jaune nodded. "Got it."

His attention focused once more on Menogias. The yaksha prowled around Fischl, who stood stock still, sweat pouring down her face as she waited for the other shoe to drop.

"Be careful, Bonanus," Menogias said. "A filthy demon ambushed me with an arrow. It lurks nearby, I can sense it."

"H-How terrible." Fischl flinched as spikes of mud stabbed upward right in front of her face.

"I will find them, so do not worry. They will pay."

The culprit to the crime sweated harder. Meanwhile, milky-white eyes rolled in their sockets, until they locked onto the figure floating above.

Cutting off power to the rockets, Jaune dropped out of the air, landing with a thud. He opted for a sword, leaving a hand free—restraining the yaksha mattered more at this stage, and this gave him options.

Menogias shrieked a shrill cry, and bounded forward. Jaune had to race to meet him, so as to keep the yaksha close to the center of the space. Mud rose in the shape of an ocean wave that he flipped over with a rocket-step, coming down with a knee that encountered a thin sheet of mud with the hardness of steel.

The yaksha's hand crashed through the barrier, the mud returning to a fluid form to cover it as a glove, seizing Jaune by the leg. Jaune's face smashed into the ground a second later.

"Wait, Menogias, don't hurt him!" Jaune heard Fischl say. Turning his head to spit out a glob of mud, he saw her grabbing onto the yaksha by the elbow. That didn't seem to be setting him off like the arrow had, thankfully.

The yaksha did actually take a pause at that request, compassion and understanding in his eyes. "Ahahaha, do you wish for a turn at killing the demon, Bonanus?"

"No!" Fischl retorted at once.

"More for me, then." With a spin, the yaksha flung Jaune into the air, shaping twin serpents that chased after him.

A blast of rocket fire moved Jaune aside before a snapping jaw could bite down on him, and he rolled along the serpent's body as its brethren reared back.

"Fischl, distract him!" Jaune instructed.

The second snake launched forward, missing him by a hair and biting the first snake instead. In a flash, the two serpents coiled around one another in a vicious confrontation, their animalistic instincts coming to the fore absent of the yaksha's influence—Fischl had her hands over the yaksha's eyes, covering them.

She removed her hands as Jaune came down, and the first things Menogias saw were the bottom of a pair of boots stomping his face to drive him into the mud. Jaune followed that with a stab of his sword. The tip of the blade pierced through a piece of earthen armor that wasn't there a second ago, sinking into the yaksha's chest to draw out a spurt of black ichor.

Laughing, Menogias grabbed the sword without regard for the sharp blade, and pulled it out. The yaksha then drove a palm against Jaune's solar plexus, and Jaune almost puked at the roiling sensation that arose as he flew back to hit the glowing gold barrier.

"Whoof!" groaned Jaune as he landed on his rear. Then, the realization of where he was hit him, and panic welled up. With Menogias charging at him, he had maybe two seconds before the wall at his back got put to the test.

Surging to his feet, he ran forward with not even a plan, and rammed into Menogias in a painful collision that put them both on the ground. A slender sword attempted to slit his throat again, with Jaune wheezing as his windpipe clenched, cutting off his breath. A fist smashed down on his chest, expelling the air in his lung. Claws clamped around his throat that he slapped aside, a fist driving up at the yaksha's chin to snap his head back. Fischl's presence, the girl sliding to a stop beside them, caused Menogias to hesitate long enough for Jaune to brace his foot against the yaksha and shove him off. He rocketed to the center of the space, and flung [Third Arm] behind him to grab Menogias, the shadowy limb stretching taut like a bungee cord before it pulled the yaksha after him, putting the both of them away from the edges.

The golden wall flared, and inside the barrier, the remaining golems collapsed into simple mud. On the pillar, Zhongli spoke.

"From this point on, do not disturb the energy of the altar."

Jaune said quickly, "Explain that to me."

"Refrain from using that arm again. No flying, either."

His jaw dropped. "Are you kidding me? I really thought this was going to be easier than killing him. What ever happened to flowers and wine?" he whined.

Outside the circle, Hu Tao poked her head out of a hole she was digging.

"We'll get to that!" she called out brightly, to Jaune's unhappy groan.

The circle pulsed again. Zhongli, still in the same even tone, said, "From this point on, do not mar the body."

"What do you mean don't mar the body aaaaAAHHH—!" yelled Jaune.

Despite all his rage, Jaune listened to the request anyway, banishing his sword to go with bare hands as Menogias lunged for him. Well, bare hands and a Fischl. He ducked under the yaksha's swiping claws, and darted toward the girl, dragging her in front of him to forestall an incoming strike from Menogias. The sword stopped an inch from her skin.

Fischl made a high-pitched sound at the back of her throat, eyes crossed looking at the tip of the sword.

"Words cannot describe my regrets in agreeing to this plan," she muttered. Jaune laughed.

"Not much longer, Fischl. You're doing great!"

It bothered him how just that bit of praise got her to flip her attitude. With a small, happy grin now on her lips, Fischl allowed him to hide behind her short frame.

Something that Menogias took issue with.

"Coward!" he screamed, but the Fischl barrier was absolute, stymieing his attempts at getting past. Jaune rather thought it was a good look on him, far better than the other sort of madness that had overtaken the yaksha. He could almost imagine it a game, possibility of death aside, as he and the yaksha circled around and around with the dizzy Fischl in the middle trying to keep track of them. The adamant refusal to hurt the person he believed to be his sister, to the point that he released his sword to let it fall in the mud, spoke well of whatever part of the man that was still left in there.

The yaksha's complete willingness to hurt everyone except her, on the other hand, Jaune would prefer he worked on. A careless slip on the mud slowed Jaune down for a split second, and it was all Menogias needed. The yaksha snaked a hand past Fischl's shoulder to seize him by the shirt, sliding around her to stand between 'Bonanus' and the 'demon'. Or maybe suitor, or even replacement sibling, depending on the avenues and side alleys his madness had taken him.

A sharp crack rang out, the yaksha's fist driven into Jaune's face. Warning of not harming Menogias in mind, Jaune grabbed the arm to try and hold it back. Menogias simply clutched that arm for leverage and clocked him on the chin with his other hand.

Zhongli's voice drifted over. "Be careful. His knuckles are breaking on your face."

Jaune sniffed, saddened by the callousness of the comment.

But I guess that's okay. A smile grew, even as a fist struck him. It hurts, but it won't kill me.

The fist landed again and again, and he held on. Do not let the spirit exit the circle. Do not disturb the energy within. Do not mar the body. Jaune was right where he needed to be to do all three.

Fischl had an arrow nocked and ready to fire, uncaring that it might ruin everything if she could get him free. He shook his head and mouthed a simple 'no'. Through the flashes of pain, he listened for the instructions. A shout from Hu Tao, and the violetgrass that resembled the bluebell flowers of his home spilled out around him and the yaksha. Food and wine followed, which Fischl caught before they hit the ground.

Flowers for the dead. Offerings to ease their journey.

The altar circle emitted a hum, and the color of gold brightened to a crescendo. A mantra, a poem, echoed around the chamber, chanted in a lively and singsong cadence.

Even then, Menogias did not relent in his madness. A fist loomed before Jaune's eyes.

But that was okay. It would hurt, but it wouldn't kill him.

Something heard the thought inside his head, and responded. A barrier, a shield, his soul. It expanded outward beyond his body, and for a flicker of a second held back the yaksha's might.

As the shield cracked, the cavern became awash in color at the completion of the ceremony. The air took on the sweet scent of violetgrass, and for a moment, they stood in a field of flowers, the moon softly shining down from above.

Reality reasserted, and once more they were inside the undersea cavern.

The churning, shifting mud had calmed, flowing as river streams and absent the aroma of rot. Coldness did not soak into the bones as before, the oppressive atmosphere gone. The altar circle pulsed with a gentle rhythm. Hu Tao, Zhongli, and Bennet stood outside the barrier, each with their hands placed together as they bowed their heads.

The hand seizing him relaxed its hold, and Jaune looked into clear eyes of golden brown. The ugly fangs had vanished to leave a kind and dignified face. Menogias inhaled a breath as if it was the first he had ever taken, reveling in the sensation.

The swish of fabric drew their gazes, and Menogias gasped as he saw the dress he sewed, drinking in the sight of it. Then, his eyes drifted up to the face of the person wearing the dress, and amazement faded to understanding.

"Ah. You are not her."

Spoken softly, his voice carried no trace of madness, only a thousand years of longing.

Fischl shook her head, and blinked back tears. "I'm sorry, I-I'll take this off right away. I didn't mean to offend."

The yaksha raised a hand.

"No, I…" He looked around the cavern, as if to hope against hope, then back to her. "I am glad to see it worn at last. Thank you. It suits you."

Behind Menogias, the river streams of mud coalesced into images.

The yaksha presented to his sister the dress. In the throes of inspiration, he had committed an old mistake and the dress turned out too big and fluttery on her slight frame. For Bonanus, wracked by her own burgeoning insanity, what would have once resulted in a small amount of annoyance grew to an incandescent rage. And for Menogias, when she rejected the garment, he could not muster a smile to the stranger whose face he did not recognize. A battle broke out, of which neither escaped alive.

Menogias closed his eyes, and the imagery transformed one last time.

To a scene of five figures on a mountain peak, a great tree casting its shade over them as they spent an afternoon together. A memory of days when they were still a family, and happy. The yaksha's fondest wish.

"Where has the time gone?" he asked, opening his eyes to fix Jaune with a calm gaze. He did not need to voice the request.

Jaune looked to Hu Tao.

"Finally, a fire. A cleansing fire to burn away our regrets," was her instruction.

The gunlance settled in his hands. Jaune braced it under an arm, and hooked a finger around a small lever at the top of the handle.

Inside, there came the sound of fluids rushing from one chamber to another. At the tip, a small spark ignited to set fire to the fuel, and the metal barrel of the gunlance heated up to a cherry red glow to match the weapon's scaly hide.

He never thought his first use of wyvernfire would be for something so gentle.

A jet of white-hot flames shot out of the gunlance to engulf Menogias, who displayed neither pain nor intention to dodge. Rather, he nodded to Jaune, and thanked him.

In the end, the drowned yaksha faded to ashes with a sad smile on his face, accepting this fate.



Beneath the sunshine, Jaune walked alone along a dirt road. Fields of tall silvergrass lined the path, and they rustled in the breeze.

Ahead of him sat his destination, a dilapidated hut set among the hills, but his attention lay elsewhere. A bemused air hung around him as he held a hand in front of his face, studying the object dangling from it on a string.

The subsequent search of the drowned yaksha's cavern had yielded more artifacts and treasures under the mud, which had meant that he got to keep the spear and pocket watch he found, along with this. It only made sense, the others had said, since it went as a set with the watch.

The little bell on the mask jangled a melodious note, and something about the sound just put him in a good mood. Cast in the shape of a fox's face, complete with two pointy ears, the Summer Night's Mask resembled what one would find at a festival, made of paper and cloth that nevertheless refused to tear. Colored in red and gold, it had a ribbon and a bell adorning one side that could be taken off to be worn as a hair ornament. Hu Tao assured him that it did not look silly when he put it on.

He'd keep it, even without the magical power it imparted. He liked the sound of the bell, among other things.

Coming up to the dilapidated hut, he stowed away the mask and entered the small room within. Ruined furniture greeted him. A ratty mat, and a broken chair. A squat earthen stove, crumpled on one side. The ashes in the stove had long stained the ground beneath. It was a place that nobody would think to linger in.

The portal flickered to life as it detected his presence, unfolding into a tear within the fabric of reality. His way home.

Jaune stood before it, and breathed deeply.

He was… He was ready. After his time away, with days to center himself, he could face Lisa with patience and grace.

He had had his own experiences, an adventure that she was not a part of. He'd tell her most of it, of course. Most, but not all. Bouts of stupidity. Reckless actions. Events that would diminish him in her eyes, and that he would rather she not hear about.

And… some things were his, and his alone. His heart. His story. Moments to hold, and never reveal to another soul.

He didn't owe it to her to tell her everything. Everybody told lies, sometimes.

What Lisa chose to say to him about her life, he would accept. Nothing beyond that.

The portal snapped into place, and through it a hazy image formed of a studio apartment, one with four gray walls and a white ceiling. The time seemed to not align perfectly, as it was dark and he saw no movements. The others must be asleep.

Nevertheless, warmth spread throughout his heart. It was good to be—

"Boo!"

Jaune nearly jumped out of his skin, his inventory cycling through his hands until he was left holding Red Rook and a screwdriver for defense. He spun around, and Hu Tao ducked her head so fast to dodge the screwdriver that she left her hat wobbling in the air. Jaune caught it.

"Hee-hee. Did I scare you?" Hu Tao said with a laugh while squatting on the ground. "Oh, and, can I get my hat back?"

He responded by silently raising the hat high out of Hu Tao's reach, forcing the girl to hop up and down with her arms outstretched in futility.

Past the indignant Hu Tao, two blonds poked their heads into the building.

"Ahaha… hi, boss," Bennett said, one hand rubbing the back of his head. He perked up at the sight of the portal. "Whoa, hang on, what is that?"

Fischl slipped inside the room, moving to stand beside Jaune in a flash and jittering with excitement. "That is obvious. It can be none other than a route to the Immernachtreich!"

"Let us not get ahead of ourselves, Mein Fräulein," admonished Oz. The raven glided around the room, before settling down on the broken chair.

Bennett strode over to them, asking, "What if it goes somewhere else? Are there enemies on the other side? Do you need help, boss?"

Fischl whirled on him, stomping her foot.

"No! It must lead to the Immernachtreich, and they are certain to greet us with open arms."

The two fell into argument, with Jaune's head ping-ponging back and forth as he followed the conversation. Meanwhile, Hu Tao complained in his ear about proper hat care, and demanded he treat her hat with a gentler hand.

"What are you all doing here?"

His question cut through the din.

They had already said their farewells.

First at Liyue Harbor's finest restaurant, where they enjoyed a celebration of their success, and in memory of a yaksha. A feast afforded with the filthy lucre—literally so—from their recent adventure.

Then, at the city gates that morning.

"Zhongli sent us," Hu Tao explained, as Jaune placed her hat back on her head. "He had a gift for you."

With that, she darted over to Bennett and rummaged in the bag he carried. The search returned with a letter and an elegant silk pouch, both of which she handed to Jaune.

He unfolded the letter first.


Payment enclosed. For the consequences.​


Huh. Nice of the guy. He had been glad to put Menogias to rest and already got his loot from the endeavor, but more was always welcome.

He moved on to the pouch, untying the strings and turning it upside down. Two objects slipped out onto his open palm.

"And where was he hiding this?" Jaune mused. In his hand rested two items of a design not unfamiliar to him, their little bells chiming.

Hu Tao gave a carefree shrug. "He collects all sorts of old stuff. Always has a long-winded story about their history, too."

"Ugh, I would have listened! He should have passed this over yesterday!" Jaune complained, lamenting a lost opportunity. Shaking his head, he deposited the dart and water balloon in his Pocket. How those counted as artifacts made even less sense to him than the broken clock.

Fischl and Bennett, who had been waiting in barely-restrained anticipation, saw their chance and they clamored for him to listen to them.

"Jaune, boss, can we go to the other side of that gate?" Bennett begged. "Just for a little bit?"

"Please, can we?" Fischl pleaded.

The mirth slipped from his face. Jaune shuffled awkwardly.

"I'm sorry, but that isn't possible."

"But—"

He held up a hand to forestall the protest. "The problem is the coordinates. I don't have it so once the portal closes, there's every chance it never opens here again."

The look on their faces affirmed why he hadn't wanted to say anything about this before. Better for them to think they would catch him out there, somewhere. That it wouldn't be goodbye.

"Hey, boss?" Bennett asked in a subdued voice. "You said that you would 'see us around'. Were you…"

Lying, the word went unspoken. Jaune brought one hand up, and rubbed his neck. He found it hard to meet their eyes.

"I don't know. Maybe. "

A somber hush overtook the room, the mood having plummeted until it struck bedrock. The sight of Fischl hunching her shoulders, shrinking herself small, stabbed him right in his guilty conscience. Bennett was even worse, looking about to cry.

But then, Hu Tao clapped her hands together to shatter the silence.

"Well, who can say how life goes before the end," she said. "I'll choose to stay optimistic."

Jaune wiped at his eyes for no particular reason, and raised his head. "Yeah, I guess I will, too. Thanks, Hu Tao."

"Because—"

Oh, she wasn't done. Jaune coughed into his hand, and acted like he hadn't said anything.

Hu Tao ran outside the hut, and returned lugging a large and bulky object. The lacquered wood spoke of fine craftsmanship, the scent of pine very calming. The box seemed the right size to fit a person inside.

Placing it down, she pointed at him. "You represent my first point of contact in another world! So here, a fully complimentary coffin for you where I would have merely offered you half off five minutes ago. Just be sure to tell your friends and neighbors all about it, okay? I need their patronage to earn back the cost on this."

Hu Tao shoved the coffin into his arms, giving him no chance of refusal. She then spun to face away, her hands clasped behind her back.

"No matter which path each of us travel on, I know that we will end up in the same place again," she said with complete, honest belief.

Voice thick with emotion and arms full of coffin, Jaune murmured, "Hu Tao… do you have to be so morbid?"

The girl laughed a lively, singsong laugh. And with a hop and a skip, that was the last he ever saw of Hu Tao, the 77th Director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

The others, however, did not share in her outlook. To them, a parting was a sad thing, and to Jaune's consternation, both Fischl and Bennett had tears in their eyes as they tried to smile.

He lingered there for who knew how long, talking with them. A short few days had been enough to make wonderful memories, and they wanted to recount it from beginning to end, so that at the finish, they could say a proper farewell.

They had gotten to their second day in Liyue harbor when they began to hear the sound of rain.

"Do you remember the meat buns—" A flash of lightning interrupted him, so Jaune started over. "Do you remember the meat buns we had before we set out? Know what I think would go well with it? A bit of plum wine."

Bennett gagged, causing Jaune to defend his words.

"Hey now, I'll admit Spirytus was a bad choice for your first time, but not all alcohol is like that." Lightning flashed again. "There are mellower options that I think you'll enjoy."

"I dunno, boss…"

Before Bennett could say more on the matter, a funeral director dashed inside the hut, and Jaune facepalmed.

"Oh come on, Hu Tao. Didn't we just have a really sweet parting five minutes ago? Did you have to ruin it?"

And with a hop and a skip, that was the last he ever saw…

She made a liar out of him.

Undeterred, Hu Tao beelined toward him. "Nevermind that," she said in a hurry, bouncing on her heels. "Jaune, buddy, pal. I'm just wondering, how big is your place?"

He cocked an eyebrow at the insistent expression she was giving him.

"A bit small. Why?"

A closer look at her caused him to frown. Was it his imagination, or did Hu Tao seem a little… singed? And the dark red glow of her Aura was flickering around her body, like it would give out at any moment.

"Oh, it's nothing important. I really want to stay at your house, that's all." Lightning boomed, and she squeaked in fright. Afterward, she tried to play it off with a smile, sweating profusely. "You would not believe the killer weather out there." She glanced over her shoulder, then looked back at him.

Jaune walked past her to the exit, to the sound of thunder, and peeked outside. He thought it had gotten darker. The day had turned to a full-blown storm, clear skies now rumbling, gray clouds engulfing the sun.

As if taking offense to him showing his face, lightning bolts struck in quick succession all over the area. Jaune pulled his head inside, and wished he had a door to close.

Whatever problem with him the sky had, the five zaps since last night hadn't settled the matter. Rather, it was now spreading that ire outward.

Uncertain eyes greeted his return.

"It could be bad luck," he said.

Hu Tao shook her head, and held up two fingers. The number of times she got struck, he supposed.

"Maybe it's just you," he tried.

Hu Tao looked at Bennett and Fischl, and flourished her hands toward the exit. "Want to test it out?"

Both youths shook their heads robotically in a mirror of Hu Tao earlier. Jaune heaved a heavy breath.

"There's time. We'll figure it out, and come up with something better than you being stuck in another world."

"Uhhh, Jaune?" Fischl raised her hand. "I don't want to die by lightning," she said.

"Noted. Avoiding that goes right to the top of the list of our priorities, trust me."

"And…" She fidgeted. "If we have to, your portal isn't a bad option."

Next to her, Bennett chimed in. "Yeah, I wouldn't mind an adventure."

"That's because you two aren't quite getting it," Jaune replied. "Even if I find a way to locate this place again, it might be years in the future that you come back. If ever. You're going to be separated from everyone you've ever known. Friends. Family. Archnemesis."

Hu Tao tapped him on the shoulder, and once she had his attention, she daintily pointed a finger out the door. "The storm outside doesn't bode well for our time with loved ones in this world, either. Hee-hee."

Bennett nodded. "Uh huh, that was pretty much my thought, too. I'd rather my dads maybe see me years from now than definitely never again."

"Ah. So you did consider that," Jaune said to himself.

"You're the only one who didn't, boss."

"Did you just sass me?" So proud.

Hu Tao interrupted, "Look, I know a guy who might be the guy." That got an intrigued look from Jaune. "I'm sure we can take a small, temporary vacation while he…maybe… hopefully… negotiate on our behalf with other powers that be."

"Are you talking about Zhongli?" he asked.

She made finger guns at him, a gesture he taught her. "Exactly. I've always got a feeling he was more than he seems. I'm sure now that he risks never enjoying my excellent company again, he'd have no choice but to get off his butt and do something."

Jaune harbored many doubts on that. Still, if it meant they had a way back…

Then, he supposed today was not a day to say goodbye.


-o-​


It was the dead of night in the apartment, when Lisa Wilbourn heard what sounded like a stampede. Some might panic, but living with Jaune Arc had taught her to take such things in stride. Usually, it could be chalked down to him as the culprit.

Which meant, that he was back. Ugh. What a bother. Lisa poked her head out of her blanket.

"Are you back already? What, can't handle it… without… me?"

She saw Jaune Arc. She also saw a whole bunch of strangers that he definitely did not depart with back when he went on his trip.

Jaune spotted her, recognized the look on her face, and gave a nervous wave.

"Eh heh. S-Surprise!"

To that, Lisa… smiled.

For most, it would seem a good sign.

Jaune gulped, and pulled at his shirt collar.
