#7,443

Chapter 80: Just Another Night City Cyberpunk
​


"You're gonna get a stomachache, just say~ing."

Tattletale had to somewhat shout to be heard over a festival in full swing. What seemed like the entire city had shown up to partake in the revelries, and the combined din shook the ground below their feet. Anywhere Jaune looked, he saw people laughing and hollering with all their might. Japantown had never been so alive.

"I vetted the shop," Kiwi assured them as she handed Jaune the pair of dango skewers. He thanked her and tried to pass one to Tattletale, who pushed it right back towards him. "The food is of decent quality. Very little bot reviews."

"That's a good enough endorsement for me. Thanks, Kiwi!" said Jaune as he dug into the fake sweet with gusto. He had downed an antidote before instead of after this time, so hopefully that would have an effect on staving off any issues. Tattletale shook her head as she watched him, grumbling about how Kiwi didn't even eat this stuff and wouldn't know good food if it hit her in the face. He was going to have to talk with her about that, as it fell under the 'don't talk smack and alienate your allies' rule they had been working on (the darn thing could never move out of the early test phase for some reason).

They relocated to a free spot at the nearby balcony to get some privacy. Tattletale and Kiwi rested their arms on the railings whereas he leaned on it with his back. He had once again worn a cap pulled low for anonymity. His poncho could have presented a problem if Night City hadn't been so on the ball, and the high number of people donning bootleg facsimiles of its red-and-while ambulance design ensured that nobody gave him a second glance. Tattletale enjoyed an even easier time of it, as not a single person recognized her in the first place.

(Enjoy was, admittedly, the wrong word to use. She raged for near a minute over her lack of notoriety.)

From this vantage point, he observed the festival as he snacked on the dangos.

Lanterns crisscrossed above them, the lights inside flickering to mimic candles and casting the scene below in a red glow. The event grounds spanned a wide main road, but as the map they so meticulously studied had shown, the cliffsides formed by far too many buildings smushed together stretched upward to the point that it made the street seem cramped. Scattered across this urban ravine were assorted plazas built to varying standards of safety codes, each a party of its own competing to be the star of the show. Utter bedlam dominated as a result, with his level hosting an impromptu rave in the far corner. The DJ was at the center of a crowd, holding a data tablet high, spamming music at top volume as around her dancers bounced up and down. Head on up the set of steps to his right, and one would eventually encounter her supposed eternal rival doing the exact same thing.

Meanwhile, giant screens strapped to the side of buildings advertised a host of special performances and events happening at this floor or that floor, some of them hacked into the itinerary by those with netrunning skills, contributing to a never-ending flow of pedestrian traffic. The higher a person went, the pricier and more exclusive it got. Gambling ran rampant.

Overlaying it all was a folksy, techno beat that reverberated for the length of the street, fading in and out depending on where a person was. He couldn't help but bop his head to the catchy tune.

And okay, yes, some of that stuff didn't sound so great. Also, the trash was piling up like nobody's business, the prices were downright criminal, and two fires already had to be put out. But on the whole, people were coming together for the celebration, losing themselves in this sense of camaraderie that had been missing for much of Jaune's time in this world. It felt amazing to be part of the crowd again.

"All teams are in position. Ready for your go," Kiwi reported, her eyes flashing intermittently as she fielded calls. Apparently, the edgerunners lending their aid today had a chatroom situation going on in addition to the individual conversations, and it was just as wild in there as the party out here. The mood of the festival had swept them up, bolstered by the discretionary funds—Tattletale's turn of phrase for what he simply called pocket money—that he handed out to the various crews for the sake of morale.

"Same with our people," Tattletale informed him. "Look, they're waving at us."

He followed her finger pointing down and across the street, and soon spotted Fischl and Hu Tao. Dressed in casual kitsch fashion, they both struck silly poses as he held up his scroll to take a picture of them. A few floors away on this side, Bennett peered over the edge of his building, balanced in so precarious a manner that Jaune feared he would tumble at any moment. Elsewhere, Escha slunk low atop the awnings of a plaza, completely unseen by the festival-goers.

They dithered here for a while, chitchatting, but soon Kiwi pushed off of the railings. Jaune straightened up.

"You're going now?" he said. "I still want you to know that I think it's a risky move."

"I can't let them suspect that I've gone off-script," Kiwi said, brushing off the concern. "Anyway, being near Faraday will let me head off problems before they become an issue. Maybe I'll see how he plans on luring you out."

Past Kiwi, Jaune saw Tattletale very slightly nodding her head. The girl heard neither lie nor betrayal in those words. Jaune hadn't needed that, or at least would not admit as such, but it was reassuring to know.

"Good luck, then," he said, and signaled across the street. The hidden felyne began scampering toward a bridge. "Don't hesitate to call out to Escha at the first sign of trouble. That cat will be on you in seconds."

Kiwi hmmed as she began to walk away. "Will do. But I doubt it's necessary."

With a small wave over her shoulder, Kiwi faded into the crowd to leave Jaune and Tattletale by themselves. In her own way, the netrunner would be standing at the eye of a storm, spying on Arasaka's movements and passing that information along to Tattletale who held overall command. It had taken some work to connect Tattletale's phone to everyone else's holocall function, plus to the headphones Jaune passed out to his teammates (no, there was no agenda), but the resulting web of communication channels should see them coordinating in a speedy fashion.

Everyone was in place. And as the music took a turn, they all welcomed the parade.

It began with the sound of drums, carrying far and loud over the night air. A rousing rhythm that thumped in a person's chest to awaken the senses, and stir the spirits. In time with the beat, lights dimmed one by one to a uniform shade that tinted the world in blue.

With the stage set, strange shapes bloomed in the distant mist. Jaune peered into the gloom, searching for a recognizable form amid the undulating movements just out of sight. His eyes grew wide as they came into focus.

Any prior conception of what made a parade rewrote itself in his mind as he beheld a school of fish, big as buses and painted in all the colors of the rainbow, swimming in between the buildings with the road as their river. The half-transparent forms of the holograms were welcomed with shrieks of joy as they crashed into the crowds, weaving into and through the walls, then out again. He could hear the chatter of his friends from the phone in Tattletale's hand, the marvel in Bennett's tone and Fischl's shouts. Hu Tao overtook them all in voicing her approval when the lanterns relit, like ten thousand fireflies, to herald the first of the parade floats.

The 'float' measured wide as a house, a wooden boat riding a current only it could see. How it stayed airborne was a mystery of engineering beyond his understanding, as so many things were. On its back sat the tall statue of a fox, the head turning from one side of the street to the other. Its eyes happened to meet his gaze, and ignited in a fire-red glow that he had to admit caused his heart to stop for a moment.

The drums swelled in volume, and the next float rolled in. And the next, and the next, each bearing a new motif. A warrior's head. A snake. A tree in bloom. On and on. They held meanings that escaped him.

Except for one.

"Target spotted on the seventh float. It's David Martinez," said an unknown voice from Tattletale's phone, a lookout posted near the front where the Arasaka presence was thickest. "Goddamn, what did they do to him?" The comment got them a few prying looks from people in their surroundings, but it mattered little at this point.

What the lookout referred to soon grew clear. On a float decorated with shrine gates, those red curving arches sitting between poles that he sometimes saw here and there, knelt a young man chained to the floor, out in the open. He wore no shirt, and in front of him there was a low table on which rested a sword. A susurration swept through the crowd as more people caught sight of the figure.

"Torii gates," Tattletale murmured, holding her chin. "Hmmm. In Japanese traditions, they mark the boundary between this world and the spiritual realm. It looks like they've put him in the pose of a person committing ritual suicide." She tched. "Arasaka is trying to be cute. They're saying that he's not leaving here alive."

"I'm not so sure they're wrong," Jaune commented, leaning over the railings for a better look across the distance.

The only reason he could recognize Martinez was because they left the boy his face. Starting from behind the ears and traveling downward, metal had replaced any semblance of flesh. Sleeker than the clunky cyberware he previously used that had bulked him up to surreal proportions, this new form slimmed Martinez down some yet cast him in the dark gray of a cold machine.

"Wasn't too much cyberware supposed to be bad?" he wondered. "Something about mental overload, I remember. Well, I don't know where the line is, but I think he's gone past it by a few miles."

Martinez's face seemed oddly blank. He twitched from time to time, although the distance made it hard to tell whether that was a trick of the light or not.

Tattletale groaned. "What really concerns me is the sword. It's a katana. The blade is too long for this sick show they're putting on, which suggests they intended it for another use…"

The big TV screen opposite them flickered to interrupt Tattletale. Up and down the street, others of its kind followed suit, the ads swapping out for a man sitting behind a desk with a grainy video playing in one corner. He shuffled the papers on the desk and leaned forward.

[A car chase on the highway occurred late last night caused quite a stir—]

The recording switched to a woman in a crisp suit. The video playing next to her showed a shootout.

[The local gang Maelstrom was ambushed by an unnamed mercenary moving at sonic speed—]

Barely five seconds in, that changed an amateur video clip of two people landing on an AV. Then, to figures balanced on top of a moving train. On and on, it went.

The stories rang with a familiar note, even the ones he had no part in. Each featured either him or Martinez. Bullets flew and explosions rang, it looked like a montage of action films… until things took a turn, beginning with a burning building.

Crying children. People mowed down. The destitute living in squalor. An altogether different flavor of images flashed across the screen at a rapid pace.

Tattletale remarked, "Uh-oh, I know what they're doing."

Jaune found that he did not need her to explain, for Arasaka was not at all being subtle. That first part had hyped him and Martinez up, playing into the violence that so entertained the people here. It got everybody excited. It promised a show.

The slander and lies were there to turn the audience against them. It made the people want to see them bleed.

This premonition playing at the back of his mind became a certainty as the screen shifted one more time, ending on something right out of a video game. A jagged line cut the panel in two diagonal halves. David Martinez appeared first, name emblazoned below his figure, his image taken recently as it featured his new look. He roared across the screen, an arm stretched out as if to grab at someone. A big "VS" slapped down onto the center of the box, followed by Jaune shooting into the frame on his rocket boots, glider wings unfurling to bring him to a halt. He remembered that moment from the incident with the AV he sold off just before it collided with the highway. The name beneath him simply said "Johnny."

Now, while he did not need Tattletale to explain, it would be completely unnecessary, please just stop, she did it anyway. "Man, they ran a whole character arc for you two, except you're both the heels in this match."

"Yeah, I got that part."

"Sure you did, sure," she placated him with a knowing look in her eyes. Shaking her head, she returned her gaze to the screen. "Every story needs a hero though, and if I have to guess, Arasaka is setting themselves up for the role. That way, the optics will let them dispose of you however they like. Try not to let them capture you, because I don't think anybody in this hellhole of a city would go out of their way to take your side."

"Are you, of all people, advocating for death before surrender?" he joked. "Tattletale, I don't know what to say. Am I having an influence on you?"

A scoff was her answer. "You're too stubborn to die. Kinda like a cockroach."

The confidence with which she declared that made him smile. (The mean-spirited part, he'd consider it her attempt to save face.)

"That said," she continued, more uncertainly. "This rescue thing did just become a teensy bit more complicated. Now, I'm not saying we should ditch, but I have a feeling that asking him nicely to follow you wouldn't cut it."

He acknowledged that stellar and not at all obvious assessment on Martinez's psyche with a nod, but made no move to leave. "Give it a little time, Tattletale. We're not out of options yet," he said casually. "Why don't you get Lucy on the line, and help her think of how to deal with this."

Tattletale narrowed her eyes, peering at him with suspicion. "And care to share what you are doing in the meantime?"

"Well, they're blatantly goading me. I think we can all agree on that. I'll have to be stupid to go down there now."

The ones behind this ploy knew him only as an edgerunner, and they designed the message to hit him where they expected it to hurt—his reputation. After muddying his name, they then pushed forward the challenge. The threat of being seen as a coward would surely pressure him to show his face, putting him where they wanted, when they wanted.

A light hop placed him atop the balcony, where he bent his knees low, coiled like a spring. His hands each filled with a canister, thumbs on the activation switch.

"But hey, I did come ready for a fight. Send out the signal, Tattletale. We're going for it."

He lobbed the canisters into the air, and a pale white smoke bloomed to engulf the area. On its heels, rockets borne on jets of flames launched from every corner of the festival grounds, ignited by a dozen different teams of mercs. They reached the apex of their ascent to explode in a firework show that drowned out the drums and turned night to day.

With a laugh, Jaune leapt right over the edge.

"Hello, Night City!"



-o-
​


It hurt. His whole world hurt.

It never stopped hurting, not since that day.

But if he just endured, like his mom said, if he could just hold on…

One day the pain would end, and he'd have what he always wanted.

Right?



-o-
​


The thing that knelt there was not quite a man. He muttered and hissed at the noises around him, seeing ghosts and shadows every which way. The shape of him had become a little too angular, corners where there should be rounded muscles, chipped in to the max by a cruel entity that cared not if it went past his limit. That may, in fact, have been why they did it. To find how hard they could push his limits. Altogether, he looked like his depiction on the TV screens. A dangerous, dangerous machine.

His glassy eyes snapped up, for as the light show died down, a lone burst of fire remained in the night. A figure walked across the air to the sound of tinkling bells, and lightly touched down on the parade float. Red and white on a pair of blue jeans, his was an eclectic mix of colors that followed no rhyme. A water balloon dangled off his belt, dancing merrily with his movements. One of his hands checked a broken clock before stowing it away, while the other tucked an ornate feathered dart into a front pocket to serve as a boutonniere. On his face, he wore a smile. A smile, and a mask reminiscent of a fox, two pointy ears standing above eyes narrowly shaped in mirth.

Torii gates lined the parade float, the tiles on the floor mimicking an old shrine path where the weeds grew between the cracks. Neon lights reflected off the smoke surrounding his form as he strode forward, and in this moment he resembled nothing so much as a figure from the old folk tales of a different era, where spirits visit in the dead of night to torment the unsuspecting.

His words, however, were a little more mundane than that.

"Heeeey, you okay? You still in there, Martinez?" Jaune asked, holding his hands before him in a calming gesture. Beneath his feet, he felt the parade float slow to a halt.

The answer, if he got one, passed unnoticed due to a new development. With confirmation of his appearance, a concerning amount of laser dots crisscrossed the floor of the float to zero in on him. They originated from windows and ledges where snipers had laid in wait, and taken together it sent a message: don't even think of moving. On the heels of these forces, massive drones the size of tanks were descending from the sky with their heavy, heavy guns aimed his way. What really drew his eyes were the bundles of netting installed below those drones, something about how they crackled with small sparks. It would suck to get caught in that.

The veneer of entertaining the masses peeled back, and what lurked behind it was aaall business.

His mask obscured his expression as he watched them, leaving only downturned lips. He spoke into the phone hanging off his neck.

"...Tattletale?"

"Yeah, yeah, we're on it. Let me show you a magic trick."

He heard a theatrical finger-snap over the line. A good half of the laser dots vanished.

"Better?"

"Better," he said, as the world around him erupted into chaos.

The cohesion between the remaining laser dots broke apart. Some stayed on him, while others swung away in panicked jerks, the snipers behind those sights suddenly finding themselves beset by hostiles. Jaune saw one fumbling around on a balcony, his vision robbed by a netrunner. On the level above that, another sniper was tackled clear off his feet by an unassuming merc with a cybernetic arm. Similar scenes played out on both sides of the road, while confusion swept over festival-goers uncertain on whether this was part of the show.

In the air, the drones fared no better. The netrunners working with him were having fun with this one. He hadn't known about the projectors installed in them, but over time each drone began to display an icon in front of their bulky frame, from smiley faces to graffiti to cartoon samurai. A few immediately put on a race, whereas others spun in place due to Arasaka's own netrunners vying to regain control.

All in all…

"That should give us a moment to talk, don't you think?" he asked the other person occupying this place, unperturbed by the guns still trained on him. That they had yet to fire revealed their purpose as a show of force, a threat. Arasaka didn't want to hurt him too badly before they had their chance to cut him open.

Another finger-snap over the phone, and those guys soon had bigger problems on their hands.

"You're dead, Johnny. You're dead," muttered David Martinez, his eyes unfocused. "Gonna kill you. Then Faraday. Then Arasaka. Then you. Then Faraday. Then…"

The boy chanted on in a broken loop, and listening from the sideline, Jaune had to wince in sympathy.

Cyberpsychosis, he believed it was called. A phenomenon with ties to cyberware, in which a person went completely off the rails. Once he started paying attention, he tended to hear about it from the news reporting on a murderous rampage. The city was supposed to have a response team for this, but as Jaune cast his gaze over the surroundings, he suspected he would not be seeing much of that.

A beeping sound emitted from the thick shackles keeping Martinez in place. A click and they popped open, hitting the tiles with a heavy clang. Martinez startled at his newfound freedom, rubbing his wrists in astonishment.

Jaune quietly spoke into the phone, "Tattletale, were any of our people responsible for that?"

"Nope. Not at all."

"I figured," he said. He kept a close eye on the other boy, waiting for the inevitable moment when that fractured mind again registered his presence. "Okay, looks like he's here to wear me down for Arasaka to go in for the capture. Are you in contact with Lucy, yet? What's her take on this?"

"I am. We need you to stall for time. His cyberware has defense programs attached to them that resists outside hacks, but Lucy thinks she can work around them. Keep him busy—"

"But don't hurt him!" Lucy cut in, sounding well on her way to frazzled.

David Martinez jerked his head up. His entire focus was now on Jaune, and in a split second, those empty eyes filled with rage.

"Don't what? You're going to have to give me something better than that!" Jaune yelled at the phone, summoning his sword and shield as Martinez dove for the katana on the table in front of him. It was almost an old routine by this point, how they immediately charged toward one another.

Edgerunners adhered to a strange idea of fair play. In 2076, any and every cyberware was always allowed in a fight. That was a lesson Jaune learned the hard way, and one he put into practice now that he knew the signs. The tensing of the shoulders, the flash of light in the eyes that signaled the flipping of a switch. Martinez was playing his old favorite.

The Sandevistan was a force of nature that laughed in the face of skill. To truly counter it, a person had to be… built different, or something. That, or lucky beyond belief.

What Jaune could hope for was to anticipate the lightning bolt. Gold swirled around him, enclosing him in a protective sphere.

Martinez slammed into it a moment later, the ground behind him seemingly cracking apart by itself. He had the edge of his sword pressed against the glowing Geo energy, and was blinking in confusion at the barrier that had cracked but not shattered.

Behind the shield, Jaune regarded his foe with mild interest.

"They upgraded your game, didn't they? Usually it takes you a bit of a run-up to achieve that." He tapped a finger to his mask, that mystical artifact which worked on the rules of another world. "But sorry, I'm cheating too!" He snapped out a kick on that last word, one which would have broken a normal man's shin. In this case, the steel toes of the boots passed through the Geo shield to strike metal, screeching off sparks on the angled plating. Other than that, Martinez barely registered the blow.

"What did you do to Lucy?" Martinez screamed. "I swear, if you hurt her I will flatline you!"

Jaune, who was about to follow up the kick with a stab of his sword, paused.

"She's safe," he said, soothingly. "We're all on the same side now to get you out of here."

For a second there, he expected that to work. Even more so when Lucy pleaded with Martinez from the other side of the phone to stop, to answer her holocall, to come back to her.

Martinez's face morphed into a snarl.

"You think I'm an idiot, gonk? You took her!" Martinez swung his katana back, holding it all wrong like a baseball bat.

His form blurred, moving a few inches to the left. By that point, the shield surrounding Jaune had shattered to send him cartwheeling end over end. A phantom pain seared across his chest, but he had experienced far worse than that for it to incapacitate him. Three quick bursts of his rockets flipped him upright, and he dove toward Martinez as the other boy panted from the blowback of activating his Sandevistan.

Except, in a heartbeat, Martinez activated his Sandevistan again.

Or so Jaune assumed as he launched like a bullet from the parade float. Really, he was getting way too used to this.

He rode the momentum instead of fighting it, pulling out his glider as the wall of a building loomed in front of him. With fire jetting below his heels, he banked hard to hit the wall with his boots, running on its surface for a few steps before jumping off and taking flight again.

It was nice having all this room to work with. The Jaune Arcs of the world belonged under the open sky.

A sniper in an open window took aim at him as he flew close. Jaune then witnessed that soldier's head turning into a red paste as Rebecca unloaded a pair of SMGs on the poor fellow from mere feet away. The last he saw as he passed the window, Rebecca had proceeded to wreak havoc inside the room, firing with guns akimbo. Near there, Tiny Mike and his crew were trying to breach one of the places marked by Kiwi as an Arasaka command center.

He searched for Tattletale, but couldn't find her. Same, in the case of Bennett who she co-opted as a protection detail. Fischl and Hu Tao, however, were hard at work alongside teams of mercs to herd civilians into the cover of the buildings. The citizens of Night City did not make it easy, for they did so love a show. A fair number even decided to join in on taking potshots at Arasaka forces, pulling out an unholy number of guns from who knew where. Jaune was rather leery at that, having not accounted for these wannabe edgerunners with dubious survival prospects, but it was too late to stop them now. In any event, they helped to keep the snipers off his back and for that he was grateful.

After a quick survey to grasp the current state of things, he returned his attention to the parade float, and the conundrum awaiting him there. Whatever cyberware Arasaka had shoved inside David Martinez, it seemed to have fixed the downsides to the Sandevistan… or, considering what he had heard of the corporation's approach to science, it took a shortcut and just disconnected him from his senses to leave him unable to feel the strain. In which case, he would say there was a significant difference between solving a problem and pretending it didn't exist until it blows up.

Hopefully, not in a literal sense.

As Jaune closed in on the parade float, Martinez zipped atop one of the torii gates. The boy could have jumped onto there without issue from what Jaune could tell, instead of overclocking. Another mark against killing one's sense of pain. Pain was good, it told a person they were dying.

Martinez tensed up, and all over his body, panels popped open. Two on the shoulders, two on the chest, another set on the biceps. Inside each rested what Tattletale referred to as a Projectile Launch System. With a resounding boom that sent him falling back, the edgerunner blasted a half dozen mini-rockets into the air.

Jaune's first instinct was to dodge. He needn't look behind him to know that too many people were still out in the open, and anyway those missiles looked to be tracking him judging by how they curved their flight path. That plan killed, he went for the second option and increased his speed to meet the attack head on.

An instant before impact, he stowed away his wings to suit up in armor, and cocooned behind his two shields, pulling on the power of Geo to further insulate him from the coming blow. He careened into the rockets with the force of a cannonball.

Surprisingly, it almost didn't hurt. His Geo shield took the brunt of the initial force, while the layers of armor in between him and the blooming explosions blunted much of the rest. What made it through smacked him silly, yes, but more as a full body ache that faded once Aura went to work. He tumbled past the flames and smoke, and hit the ground running. Martinez was there, ready to meet him. Jaune braced for a—

"Support incoming," Tattletale relayed to him, right as Martinez engaged his Sandevistan.

The boy's lower body seized up against his will, forcing him out of his enhanced state of speed. A strange shift passed over the edgerunner's face, like he thought he should be feeling immense agony yet did not. Without missing a beat, Jaune used the opening to swap his sword for Ruhm, releasing two rounds at a range where stray shots wouldn't end up in the crowds of civilians.

Bang. Bang. The bullets cracked against Martinez's stomach, gouging into the metal plating. Jaune jumped high to avoid a punch, kicking off Martinez's shoulder to vault over him and land with his back to the edgerunner. He braced his legs, and his entire form pulsed with light. In the next moment, a harsh impact struck the back of his head and stopped cold, the blow he had been waiting for meeting an immovable object. With a grin, Jaune whipped around, rifle changing to sword to let him ram the blade straight through Martinez's leg.

"You were harder to fight when you were thinking!"

And when Jaune didn't have netrunners on his side. A body made of chrome was vulnerable in a way meat was not.

In other words, unlike David Martinez, nobody could seize Jaune by the balls from half a mile away.

Martinez ignored the damage to the leg and pulled it back, trying to take Crocea Mors with him. The blade vanished then appeared again in Jaune's grip as he moved after his foe.

"Don't kill him!" pleaded Lucy.

"See, now we're getting somewhat more reasonable," Jaune said to the empty air. He swung his sword, with Martinez dropping low to let it whiff above his head. "But I'm still going to need more than that. He's gone cyberpsycho. How do we reverse it?"

"I'm working on it! Kiwi, get the hell out of my man!"

"There isn't a cure for cyberpsychosis," Tattletale helpfully informed him.

Wonderful.

All aggression, the other boy no longer knew how to disengage. He closed in, throwing a slash that failed to make it past Jaune's guard, transitioning to a rising knee that Jaune diverted with his shield.

The eyes gave Martinez away, and Jaune swung his shield arm to the side, trusting in whoever had hacked into the edgerunner to come clutch once more. Martinez tripped back to normal speed and right into the edge of the shield. His nose broke under the impact, but with a roar, he pushed past it to shoulder-check Jaune, knocking him down. Jaune quickly rolled upright and ate a boot to the face for the trouble. His back hit the ground as Martinez dove for him, poised for a stab.

The Geo sphere manifested, throwing Martinez up and over, giving Jaune the time to rise and chase after the edgerunner. In midair, Martinez wasted a use of his Sandevistan flailing without leverage, landing with a heavy thump. He blurred, ending on his feet with his katana cutting across Jaune's throat, fast as a whip. Jaune choked on the imagined death. A kick to his chest forced him back.

Martinez had hit his groove, chopping in wild slashes that followed no rhythm. In the face of that, Jaune retreated into a guard, tight and controlled to wait for his moment. The hits to his Aura began to pile up as the unrelenting assault rolled past ten seconds, then twenty, then thirty.

But even madness could not last forever. The instant the katana slowed, Jaune cleaved the blade in half with his sword, following up with [Third Arm] to obscure Martinez's vision.

The opportunity was too good to pass up. Crocea Mors darted out, biting deep.

Lucy screamed over the line as her lover's arm separated from his body at the elbow. Jaune pretended he couldn't hear the heartwrenching cry. Martinez had to backpedal or lose the other arm. [Third Arm] yanked him right back at Jaune.

"Freeze him!" he barked the order.

Once again, Martinez's cyberware failed him, his form growing hazy before snapping back into focus. A blade slammed into his gut, with Jaune using that as leverage to flip the boy over his shoulder, following through to end up above Martinez as he lay on his back, the remains of the katana skittering off across the floor tiles.

Light pulsed around his form, letting Jaune withstand a punch to his chin without flinching.

His phone was blowing up with Lucy's voice, the young woman cursing him up a storm. He somewhat understood the sheer need to lash out at a time like this, he did have multiple occasions where he almost killed her man. As he withdrew his sword and stabbed it down to pin Martinez's remaining arm to the floor, he spoke to the netrunner.

"Look, it was all part of the plan," he assured her.

"Screw you!"

"I'm serious," he lied, hooking an arm under one of Martinez's kicking legs to stop his struggling. His arm groaned as the mechanical limb resisted with superhuman strength. "Since he wouldn't snap out of it, I thought I'll just, well, cut him down a bit and make it easier to drag him along with us."

"That—!" There was a pause. "Wait, that's brilliant."

Now was Jaune's turn to hesitate. "It is?"

"It won't solve everything, but hacking into his chrome just isn't fast enough. Arasaka installed a special self-ICE program in him that I'm still working to understand. As a stopgap, we can reduce the load by having you physically disable his cyberware and that may return him to his senses," Lucy blurted out at a rapid-fire pace. "Johnny, you need to cut him up more!"

Jaune mulled on that as he landed a punch on Martinez's face. "...I know I was the one to start this, but don't you think that's a little drastic? Whatever happened to 'don't hurt him'?"

"It's okay. I'll fix him."

It was at this moment that Jaune decided he was glad to never have fallen in love with a girl like Lucy, a beauty with a side of crazy. He regarded the opponent below him, the boy who had lost none of his rage.

"You know, I don't like you much, but even I'm not that gung-ho about this."

"Kill you kill you kill you!" howled Martinez. "Fucking corpo! If I had your chrome, I'd win. I could have gone to the top like you too! If I just kill yoooou!"

A sigh, and Crocea Mors popped back into his grasp. Immediately, Martinez threw a fist at him with the newly freed arm. Jaune batted it aside, then pulled a handgun and unloaded a clip into the joint of the arm to leave it sparking and spasming. This time, as he regarded the edgerunner, his gaze turned a little colder.

"Your teammates keep on about saving David, saving David, but looking at you now… do you even want to be saved?"

Martinez didn't seem like he understood a word of it, snarling and spitting at Jaune in the unsettling manner of a mad, cornered lion. Had reason returned to him, how would he look at this sorry state of himself? Would he have seen a beast that needed to die, as Jaune did?

Pity turned to anger, and Jaune grabbed him by the hair, dragging him close to scream in his face. "Forget about me and victory and above all else the damn chrome! What is it that you want?"

"Get off of him, this isn't the time! We had a deal!"

"...Lucy…"

Jaune blinked at the softly spoken tone. He almost dismissed it as his imagination, but the moment stuck with him as Martinez resumed his struggle to get free, and he wondered if it had been a bout of clarity or had the boy simply struck upon the name in his mad rambling. He supposed it did not matter.

"Yeah, I thought so."

It was an answer enough for him.

"Where am I cutting?" he said, sword rising.

Lucy hiccuped. Had she been crying? "G-Give me a sec." The laser dot of a sniper rifle appeared, roaming over Martinez to settle on a spot. "Here, three inches below the lowest ribs. I haven't been able to crack the adrenal booster."

The tip of Crocea Mors descended, smoothly sliding between two panels of armor to sink below. Martinez jerked at the intrusion, and something beneath his skin crackled. The boy suddenly relaxed as if all the energy had left him.

"Good. Excess hormones are falling fast. Now, move an inch to the left to hit the second stomach graft."

"Wait, what? Why was that even in there?"

Did Arasaka just put every spare part they had lying around the lab into him?

Then again, they did take the time to strap on a cyberdick, so that wasn't outside the realm of possibilities.

Jaune shook his head, not wishing to think further on that subject. He stabbed where Lucy directed him. Martinez may appear mostly metal, yet blood seemed out of him to inform Jaune that there was still a fleshy body in there. Evidently, Lucy worried about the same.

"Let's leave the pain editor, but the biomonitor can go. It's under the ribcage, be very careful not to hit the heart. I can't fix that."

The backalley surgery continued in defiance of all that was good and decent. Jaune cut and carved and tore pieces from David Martinez, while around him the fighting heated up in earnest. The upper-level plazas had drained of spectators to allow the edgerunners of the Afterlife free rein in engaging Arasaka forces there. Taking control of the elevators should have stemmed the flow of enemy reinforcement. Judging from the increasing amount of bullets flying back and forth, that hadn't worked out as well as he hoped. The bridges were theirs after the initial blitz, though, providing bottlenecks to isolate Arasaka forces from one another for the most part. It kept the two sides even. Bloody, but staving off the instant rout it should have been.

He needed to be there. At the front, to break the tide. People who trusted in him were waiting.

Which was quite unfortunate for David Martinez.

"Fuuuuuuck that hurts!"

"I told you to leave the pain editor alone, you idiot! David! David!"

"Do you see a license on that wall?" Jaune shouted back at Lucy.

"What wall?" David screamed.

"Exactly!"

He did his best, okay? His hand slipped, okay?

Martinez looked down. "What the fuck did you do to me!?"

"I cured you," Jaune insisted. "You have your legs, you have an arm. That's more than some could ask for. Congratulations."

Was he happy about this outcome? Sure, in the way that any man could be proud of his craft. Martinez was alive, free, and somewhat in a lucid state of mind—somewhat, because there was an odd twitch to him and his glassy eyes kept drifting off to a spot over Jaune's shoulder. He had completed, like, 99% of the job they enlisted him for. The extraction would be even easier with Martinez still capable of movements.

Didn't mean he had to like him.

"Tattletale," he spoke into the phone, ignoring the whining of his patient. "Where do they need me?"

His partner answered, "Forget that. Kiwi sent a message, and she's ordering a retreat."

He balked at that news. "What, no, that's not her call. Half our people are stuck here. Did she give a reason?"

"She said, 'Run. Run, run, run, it's Adam Smasher.'"



-o-
​


There were many reasons for why Jaune refused to heed the warning, but what decided it was a simple observation.

If he ran from a threat that by all rights he should not know about, then it meant without a doubt there had to be an information leak. Kiwi's cover would be blown.

So, he waited, and watched as an aircraft descended from the night sky. Emblazoned with the crest of Arasaka, it carried within an enemy… and an ally. The aircraft drew gunfire from multiple directions, but no attack managed to pierce the hull. Its pilot ignored all else to zero in on the parade float that Jaune stood on.

A door on its side opened while it was still in the air, revealing a darkened interior. The first thing Jaune saw were soldiers in black body armor, kneeling with long rifles in their grips. Behind them, a number of figures sat back in the gloom, revealing only glimpses of themselves. A crisp suit, and a finger tapping on a knee in impatience. A feminine silhouette in red, one leg crossed over the other to affect a nonchalant manner.

And in the center, where the shadows were deepest, there glowed two crimson lights.

A massive hand reached out to grab the edge of the door, the steel crunching beneath the fingers as the figure pulled itself forward. The shadows swirled and shifted, coalescing in the hulking metal frame of a robot. It resembled a bigger version of Arasaka's work on David Martinez's slimmed-down robotic body, just several steps further along the uncanny valley. Its one nod to humanity was in the face, where it mockingly mimicked the features of a person. A skull-shaped head with a wide nose, and red pupils set within deep eye sockets. Anything below that gave up the pretension, metal through and through. In places of skin and muscles, thick armor plates were strapped to bundles of cables shaped as limbs.

Jaune suppressed a shudder at the sight. There was an almost Grimmesque aesthetic to it all, this dark form in a bone-pale mask, nature twisted into the monstrous.

"Martinez, is that your big brother or something?" Jaune asked, standing with his sword resting on a shoulder.

"Whuh? I don't look like that," Martinez protested. "I'm still handsome… right?"

Jaune refused to comment, but Lucy was happy to pick up the slack in between her shouting for Martinez to bail. Something, something little pogchamp. The meaning escaped him.

With a push that rocked the AV, the robot leapt out. He cleared an impressive distance, fearing nothing of the long, long drop in between the aircraft and the parade float. His landing crushed the ground beneath his feet, and shook the torii gates. Broken tiles flew every which way.

The whole world seemed to fall to a hush as the robot rose to his full height. He turned his head to look at one side of the festival grounds, then the other. Edgerunners whimpered as his attention fell on them. Even his own fellow Arasaka soldiers faltered.

The robot turned back to Jaune.

"You—"

That was the furthest the robot got before Jaune blasted a gunlance shell at him, risking it with the relatively short distance between them.

The robot's arm, quick as a whip, smacked the shell aside to let it explode at the base of a torii gate. The wooden construct went down in a burning wreck.

"Nice try, meat."

The robot said the word with the connotations of an insult, the sneer coming through on a face that never changed its expression. His voice held a scratchy, artificial reverb that grated on the ear.

"Adam Smasher, I presume?" Jaune said politely, and it surprised him how well he maintained a steady voice.

Perhaps it was due to that same image stuck in his mind which had so thoroughly unnerved him ever since he laid eyes on the robot, the thought of those creatures of darkness lurking beyond the walls. Don't fear the Grimm and don't hate the Grimm, for that was how they get you. The adage was a comforting white lie, but it seemed that sometimes they do work.

"You have heard of me, and yet you stand here. You must have a death wish."

Jaune waggled his hand from side to side, making a face. "Ehhh. I've met scarier things."

Smasher grunted, unimpressed. "Make your excuses, deadmeat. It matters not. You and the junkheap there are the property of Arasaka Corporation. Kneel… or don't, and make my day."

A new voice spoke from his phone, murmuring, "I told you to run."

Tattletale took over, speaking quickly.

"Kiwi just sent over what she managed to glean out of Adam Smasher. He's what they call a Full Body Conversion, a cyborg with almost nothing left beyond the brain. The thing on his shoulder is a rocket launcher. His arms can shift to a cannon. The gun he's carrying is a Militech model heavy machine gun intended for mounting on vehicles. Reinforced legs for distance jumping. Top grade Self-ICE, that's the antihacking software—"

"You missed the cyberaudio enhanced hearing."

Tattletale fell quiet, and Jaune's heart went cold.

Smasher turned his head a fraction, glancing back at the AV. He chuckled darkly, before looking back at Jaune.

"I knew that fine cut of meat was being shifty. It takes a special kind of nitwit to cross me. I'll get to her soon enough."

Jaune's eyes narrowed.

"Yeah, well, I have an objection to that."

The robot boomed in laughter, yet its body did not go through the accompanying motions. "Fine by me. That fuck Faraday thought he could order me around, whining about bringing you in alive." He gave a loud growl of displeasure. "Like I give a damn. The only good Johnny, is a dead Johnny."

Wham!

Adam Smasher had not even twitched before seemingly teleporting across the distance between them. The only thing that managed to register for Jaune were those red eyes, and then he was airborne with the wind rushing around him. Pain bloomed on his chest like an entire truck had just ran into him, his body rotating with an unnatural force radiating from the point where Smasher's fist struck. He crashed through the torii gates behind him, across empty space, and into the upper level of the shrine sitting on the next float over. Wood gave way against his momentum, burying him halfway into a wall before he came to a stop.

"Owwww," he groaned, feeling like he had gone a second round with Accelerator.

Well, maybe not to that extent.

Multiple voices were shouting to him through the phone, but he was a little too woozy to parse it. Carefully, he raised his head out of the wreckage.

Way, way back there, Adam Smasher silently regarded him, his head cocked to the side. That had been a lethal blow for anybody else in this world. Jaune staying alive after that must be such a surprise.

Just not enough of a surprise that he would stop. Smasher lifted his huge machine gun with a single arm. Martinez dove aside, but the robot paid that no mind, aiming the barrel in Jaune's direction to spit out a stream of bullets.

They tore the wooden shrine apart, bringing down the pillars and beams. Splinters whipped up in a storm that bombarded Jaune as he dove for the stairs. He crashed to the bottom of the steps on a shoulder, rolling to squat low against the wall. The ceiling above him creaked, nearly buckling under the collapsing building.

"Tattletale, make a note," Jaune said weakly. "He also has a Sandevistan, and is insane."

"What's the plan, Jaune? Can you still fight?"

"Yeah. Yeah, I can. What's happening to Kiwi?"

Instead of Tattletale, Kiwi answered, "I'm still on the AV. Smasher hasn't outed me yet, or Faraday would have made a move. Don't know why. Maybe he wants to…" Her voice grew smaller. "Deal with me himself."

That sobered Jaune right up. He rose to peek out a new hole in the wall, thinking hard.

"You'll be okay, Kiwi. The boat is rocking but we haven't tipped over yet." He craned his ear. "Tattletale, tell me something. Is that sound what I think it is?"

A hundred motorcycle engines roared to answer him.

The road beneath the floats had always presented the biggest challenge to him. There, the spectators gathered thickest. He hadn't a hope of a prayer to clear them out while juggling a dozen other plans in motion with the finite number of edgerunners he hired. It was a problem that hung over him, any careless move he made up top risking big and immediate consequences.

"Wakako kept her words," Jaune said as he peered below, unable to hide a smile.

Japantown belonged to the Tyger Claws. They loved saying that. So, he had put forth to the fixer, what was a Japantown festival without the gang in attendance?

They rode down the street, a neon-lit parade on wheels. Hooting at the top of their lungs, the gangsters decked out in eye-searing kitsch weaved around the police cordon, taunting the officers who took one look at the numbers involved and noped out of there. Their reputation preceded them, parting the crowd. More Tyger Claws poured in on foot, herding the civilians back further. In the span of moments, they had taken over half the road. The motorcyclists zipped around and around and around, reveling in the space to show off their moves.

His gaze panned upward along the buildings, tracking the plazas that stood empty but for Arasaka soldiers fighting against edgerunners. Of the civilians, there were no signs. The human wall that Arasaka hid behind had come tumbling down.

"How goes it, Tattletale?" he asked. The girl understood his meaning.

"The battle is seesawing. Our side is faring well, all things considered, but they could use you."

"I'll do my best."

"Also, I'm… keeping the others out of the worst of it."

Though she would not see it, he nodded along to the decision. He held the phone up to his lips. A request to Tattletale ensured his message funnel through their ad hoc communication network.

"Be advised, all restrictions on arms are now lifted. Bring out your toys, everybody."

He dropped the phone to let it dangle from the strap. The device only connected to Tattletale and a couple of nosy hackers, so he didn't catch a response from it. No, the edgerunners made their voices heard with the deafening staccato of their guns, the tide turning hard against Arasaka as suddenly their opponents brought heavy weaponry to bear.

Jaune performed a quick mental check of his Pocket. He had to reorganize a fair bit before the festival, but retained an impressive array of equipment. One never knew for sure what the situation might call for, after all.

He then kicked through the wall of the shrine, and stepped out to the other side with both arms held out before him. Two clunky chunks of metal dropped into his grip.

"Uh," said Kiwi. She likely had a good view of him from the AV. "Where were you keeping those grenade launchers?"

"Oh, you know. Around. Tell Martinez that he should probably move."

And he pulled the triggers.

One after another, grenades arced across the distance. Jaune's arms kept the barrels steady, while his 'marksmanship' ensured their aim. They bloomed like flowers all over the area around Adam Smasher, petals of lightning searing the air in crackling blue. The robot braced his arms in front of his face as his surroundings became engulfed in a field of static.

Had he scrounged up those EMP grenades over the past week in case he ever ran into David Martinez again, and arrived at the festival with them in his Pocket for use if Martinez turned violent? No, clearly not. Perish the thought.

Just like how it was a complete coincidence—

The grenade launchers vanished, and he shifted his arms to accommodate the two metal tubes that replaced them. The back halves came to rest atop his shoulders.

—that he brought along a couple of rocket launchers.

Adam Smasher had guns.

Jaune had all the guns.

Two thermobaric warheads, whatever those were, shot out of the metal tubes. The combined backblast rocked his body, with Jaune pulling on his Semblance once more to stand firm so as to observe the result. Still, he didn't get to see much of what happened after the rockets exploded due to the entire surface of the parade float going up in flames.

The battlefield quieted for a second time in the wake of that. Every pair of eyes stared into the inferno.

The muzzle of a gun pressed to the back of Jaune's head.

"Better, but still not good enough."

A dozen plans of how to proceed from here flashed through his mind, but not one began without pain as he already heard the soft click of the trigger. His world blurred out of focus to the roaring boom of gunfire.

He regained his sight, screeching to a halt on the opposite end of the parade float from the cyborg. A curious turn of event, as he hadn't done anything insofar as he recalled. His head appeared quite unsmashed by Adam Smasher.

"You good, corpo?"

Jaune gazed up at his truly unexpected rescuer. "Oh hey, you're alive."

David Martinez looked like he wanted to slap somebody. Not Jaune, surely.

"No thanks to you!" the other boy cried. His one remaining arm was in poor shape, moving in jerky motions. The less said about his torso after his impromptu surgery, the better. Will and spite seemed to be what kept him running. "A rocket launcher? A rocket launcher!?"

That same weapon popped into existence.

"...You want one?"

"Ooh! Gimme!"

Jaune's vision experienced another dizzying swirl of colors that ended with him lying on the floor close to puking, Martinez's teeth clamped on his poncho and the rocket launcher held in the edgerunner's one working hand. Their previous location was a smoking hole. Martinez aimed the metal tube and fired at Smasher, who vanished a split second from impact. The broken shrine behind the cyborg exploded instead, peppering them with flaming splinters.

"Maybe a smaller gun will do," Martinez admitted.

"Done."

Jaune twirled a handcannon that was suddenly there around his finger, the same firearm he once stole from the other boy, before offering it by the handle to Martinez.

Words were unnecessary. Protecting him twice in one day? That counted for a lot in his books. Whatever their history, in this moment they were on a side to stand against something with big ears and big eyes and big teeth.

It didn't make them friends, though.

They broke into a run as Smasher returned to view, the cyborg slamming a new clip into his machine gun. Scorchmarks left by fire and electricity had darkened his armor, but hampered him none. He took aim.

Jaune slammed a shield into place to block the stream of bullets, sheltering Martinez behind him. As the attack broke off, his body jerked to the side through no volition of his own, narrowly evading the robotic fist that whiffed the air where his head used to be.

Jaune did not question the how or why. He knew the answer to that already. Instinct guided his action, the sword he now held swiftly hunting for its target.

Nothing was there for it to cut.

Smasher reappeared to his left alongside Martinez, who had diverted the arm cannon away from Jaune. They blinked away as the screeching of metal on metal resounded in the opposite direction. By the time he snapped his eyes toward that side, they were now behind his back.

Jaune whirled around to find Martinez rocketing past him. He stretched out [Third Arm] to try and grab the other boy, but missed. Yet, there was no time to dwell on it, for just then a bullet slammed into his forehead to throw him back, directly into a second round that caught him on the shoulder and turned him aside. Another shot got him from the front to continue the revolution. His leg stumbled from a fourth blow.

In every direction, they came. Picked him off his feet and threw him in dizzying circles. An unending cacophony that deafened him, the impacts stringing together in a deluge that never ends yet lasted barely longer than two blinks of the eye. Phantom wounds and phantom pains to leave him teetering, senses thrown out of sync.

Gold spun around Jaune to break the pattern, shaking and crumbling almost as fast as it had arrived. It did what he needed it to, granting him a reprieve long enough. The battle slowed down to a pace where the speed of human thought had a chance to keep up.

Within this time, he considered his opponent's next move, calling on what meager knowledge he had gleaned of Smasher.

The cyborg liked to take things close. He went out of his way to execute his prey. Jaune knew the type.

He had to be here somewhere, pressing the killing blow.

Jaune's eyes rolled a full circle, barely registering what they saw. They recognized a smudge of color, a little spot of white at the corner of his vision that could have been anything.

Light pulsed, and it almost seemed to fill him with energy. The remaining bullets struck but he barely felt it. His heel whipped around in a spinning kick that crashed against Smasher's cheek, cracking his head to the side.

The blow outright lifted Adam Smasher. His heavy frame shook the parade float as he dropped, and broke the floor. Half his face dented inward, chips of metal crumbling off the mask.

For one moment, the speed of human thought had pierced into that realm of the extraordinary. He had been good enough.

The battle wasn't over just with that. In a flash, the cyborg was back on his feet, shrieking a string of mechanical noises as his hand closed in around Jaune's throat.

"David!" Jaune barked out, hoping against hope.

The fingers squeezed tight, and he wasn't there. The other boy had understood.

As movements ceased, David turned to Jaune. "Did you just…"

"It was faster, Martinez," he said with a scoff. "Fewer syllables."

Martinez sneered. "Yeah? Whatever. I didn't care anyway."

"You slippery eels are getting on my nerves," Smasher growled.

In unison, both boys pointed a gun at him and pulled the trigger.

The bullets plinked off the armor without doing much, but the message carried across fine—they were going to keep poking at his nerves, thank you very much. In retaliation, Smasher activated his shoulder-mounted rocket launcher, releasing the entire loaded salvo.

Martinez shot half of them out of the sky right off the bat, while the rest detonated on the rock formed of Jaune's combined defenses. The area between the two sides tore apart.

As the smoke cleared, the parade float gave a lurch.

Jaune looked down at the ground beneath his shoes. "That wasn't my imagination, right?"

To provide an answer better than the other people here ever could, the float began to list to one side. Scraps and debris from the shrine tumbled off the edge, falling the long distance to the street below. All the weight shifting to one side destabilized the float even more.

"Tattletale, please tell me we evacuated the people down there!" Jaune cried as Smasher bounded away to safety.

Tattletale's affirmation was drowned out by Martinez yelling in his ear. "Worry about ourselves first, ya gonk." The boy scrabbled for purchase on the wooden floor. "I can't jump high enough, so you gotta fly me out of here."

Not likely. Martinez was one heavy guy after Arasaka finished with him.

Thinking fast, Jaune summoned his gunlance and said, "I got you. Jump!"

Martinez jumped, putting his trust in Jaune. Meanwhile, the gunlance swung in a wide circle. Timed just right, it allowed Martinez to land on the other end of the weapon with a gentle step, as Jaune pulled on his Semblance to bring a monstrous amount of strength to bear. The edgerunner realized Jaune's plan at the last second, and screamed an invective as Jaune whipped the lance around to catapult him into the sky.

His good deed done, Jaune stowed away the lance and threw out a shadowy hand. It latched onto the top edge of the tilting float, and acted as a slingshot to propel him in the same direction as the other boy. His rocket boots increased his speed to let him catch up.

"You're welcome," he said as he drew level with Martinez.

The edgerunner ceased shouting long enough to flip him the bird.

They landed on a float depicting a cherry blossom tree in bloom, and a second later, Smasher crashed onto the scene. He fired on them, then zipped into the cover of the tree trunk and unleashed another burst as Jaune bunkered down behind a shield.

"Goddamn," Martinez said, hidden at Jaune's back. "The guy's a monster. I can't keep up with my Sandy much longer."

Jaune glanced at the blood pouring down the boy's front from his broken nose, and had to agree. He himself felt fine. Better than fine, even, if taking into account the hits he had taken. But he didn't get here alone.

"Really looks like we can't beat him with just the two of us."

"Then we're dead!"

"Not what I meant. Swap with me."

He sidled to the rear, switching places with Martinez to have him brace against the shield. A big shotgun as long as his leg appeared, and he flicked it up for Martinez to take. For himself, he went with Ruhm.

Sitting with legs outstretched, he took his time scouting the battlefield, making sure to do it right. Beyond his immediate conflict, which on a personal level seemed so very important, there were another dozen-odd firefights taking place. With the chance to breathe, he was going to interfere in every single one that he could see.

Ruhm rose, and men fell. All over the festival grounds, bullets found their way into Arasaka forces from a distance that snipers would envy. The ones with their backs to Jaune found themselves beset from two sides, cut down like a wheat harvest. Those climbing over barricades to overwhelm the edgerunners were beaten back, giving the mercenaries their opening to turn the tables against the soldiers missed by Jaune's shots.

The rifle clicked empty to a battlefield that had decidedly swung in his favor. He sent a message to Tattletale, and turned back to his own fight.

He pushed. He pushed Martinez, and he pushed himself. The other boy coughed blood as he yanked Jaune out of danger in the nick of time, only for Jaune to go charging right back at Adam Smasher, chasing the world that exists at faster than thought. The Sandevistan became a method to close the distance rather than an escape.

Smasher threw a punch, and Jaune's blade slipped into the joint as the fist blew past at the speed of sound. A handgun was already in his other grip, firing up at the cyborg's chin. Bang. Bang. Bang. They lodged in the metal.

"Useless!" Smasher mocked in his booming voice that had grown almost… happy. "Writhe. Struggle. Make me hurt for it! But know that you will die like all the others!" His knee struck Jaune below the sternum, knocking out his breath, and he tore the shotgun from Martinez's one-armed grip with his teeth. Half a ton of metal then moved with a whisper to vanish from sight. A shadow loomed above Jaune, growing larger.

Jaune fell to a knee, gun changing to a shield raised over his head, while Martinez dropped flat. The impact of Smasher slamming down with both feet buried Jaune in the floor up to his waist, but the parade float, and Jaune, held.

Smasher flashed away, his arm shifting to its cannon form. A grip on his poncho, and Martinez ripped Jaune free as the blast vaporized the spot they just vacated. As the blurry surroundings returned to focus, Jaune swung the sword that had replaced the shield in a wild, blind arc, assuming rightly that the edgerunner had put him where he needed to be, when he needed to be, to bite at their enemy. The heavy machine gun that Smasher wielded fell to the ground in two pieces, abandoned by its owner who chose to save his hand. A hand that was changing form.

Mid-shift, an arrow made of lightning stabbed the arm cannon, discharging in a sphere of crackling electricity. It induced a mere twitch for a fraction of a second, not enough to prevent the muzzle from emerging and blasting Jaune in the chest. He flipped end over end with the sensation of a wildfire on his skin, a scream torn from his throat. His sword slipped from his grasp and was picked up by Martinez before it hit the floor. Martinez and Smasher blurred, returning to sight with Smasher's arm cannon exploding while Martinez panted for breath with a chunk of his side missing.

Smasher reached toward Martinez but gunfire erupted from multiple directions, preventing him from tearing off the boy's head. The cyborg backed off, shielding his face with his arm as he assessed the situation.

Mercs of the Afterlife were making their way toward the battle, anyone they could spare from the ongoing conflicts with Arasaka. They scaled the buildings or leapt from the upper balconies, Rebecca first among them, forgoing stairs and elevators to take the most expedient paths forward. Some had seized the rifles of Arasaka snipers, turning the weapons now onto Adam Smasher to provide covering fire for Jaune and Martinez to regroup.

A curious number of butterflies converged on the float, seemingly born of flames. Smasher batted one away, and earned a faceful of soot for the trouble as he discovered that, oh, they exploded on contact. One butterfly brushed past the sculpture of the cherry blossom tree, setting it alight.

Which… wasn't that great, as Jaune was also on this thing.

Tattletale's voice spoke up from Jaune's phone. "Hu Tao wanted to let you know that that was a complete accident."

"Really? I guess that makes it totally okay, then!" Jaune said with a false cheer that got a laugh from her, as he scrambled once more toward Adam Smasher. The unseen hand of Tattletale brought the gunfire to simultaneous stop as he dashed into melee range. A kick from Smasher launched at blistering speed only to be blocked by Martinez, pinning the pair in place for Jaune to score a deep line that severed half the cables in a leg. Inky fluids pour out of the wound, and wires discharged sparks in the air.

The cyborg screamed, appearing as if he felt that. He darted back, stumbling to a halt a distance away and coming under heavy crossfire almost immediately.

Jaune barked a laugh, hauling Martinez forward. "Now that's more like it! When it comes to a big old Grimm, we just gotta bring the whole team!"

The extra guns made the battle more even. But the netrunners, ohhh, the netrunners made the difference.

It began with small things. A twitch or a tremble that barely distracted the killer cyborg. That carried on, growing in strength as dozens of netrunners charged at Smasher's cybersecurity software on a plane that no one else here could perceive.

Smasher treated them with contemptuous disregard, almost casual in how he brushed their attempts aside to focus on Jaune. He paid for it when his shoulder-mounted rocket launcher unleashed their payload and a good half of the missiles flipped around to fly right back at him. A game of tag played out with him evading the blasts, mirrored by Martinez doing the same while dragging Jaune along.

That was the point in which Martinez tapped out, and as he went down, puking up blood after overtaxing his Sandevistan system, it was the netrunners who kept Jaune in the fight.

When Smasher launched a punch, rotating his arm beyond what a normal limb could achieve in that same strange, inhuman technique that had earlier blown Jaune away, a netrunner got into the wrist joint. The limb locked at the last instant to reduce its power, pushing Jaune back a step instead of the next parade float over. He punished that opening by spearing Smasher through the gut, causing something within to give up the ghost with a loud pop. Leaving the blade there, he drove a fist into Smasher's face, cracking the mask further before yanking out his sword.

The netrunner that gave him the chance fell down, bleeding from their ears and eyes. For every blow Jaune landed on Smasher, others joined that person on the floor. The battle waged inside the Net was the furthest thing from a bloodless conflict.

But they did it. One among them shone above the rest, breaching a path for the rest to pour in.

Jaune saw her, Lucy, standing on a ledge overlooking the parade float they were on with a triumphant, bloodthirsty smile. Eyes screwed shut in concentration, she moved her hands. Below, Smasher copied the motion to a tee. The twin arm cannons that had been pointed at Jaune swung to either side of the cyborg, shooting harmlessly into thin air.

It signaled the beginning of the end. What Jaune then fought was a stuttering wreck. Smasher's armor heated up to a red glow as the netrunners overclocked absolutely everything that they could get their digital hands on while denying those cyberware a release, no time for subtlety. More and more, his movements became accompanied by hisses and pops of breaking microparts. He charged at Jaune with the speed of a normal man.

With his sword, Jaune directed aside a fist and took a step backward in an obvious bait. His foe seized it without hesitation. Another weak parry, another step. Smasher had to know what was coming, yet he wasn't about to stop.

"You're nothing, Johnny. Nothing! Another story that ends in Night City, a part of my legend!"

Jaune felt his heel swaying over empty air, his foot inches from slipping off the parade float.

This was the moment.

He looked into the cyborg's eyes, inscrutable those cold things were, and imagined that the man behind the machine sensed it, too. Calmly, smoothly, he stepped aside.

Crocea Mors gleamed in the moonlight, and severed the head of Adam Smasher.

His body actually managed to stay upright. A robotic frame was sturdier than flesh and needed not a mind to direct it, Jaune supposed. It lurched forward a step, then a second one to move right up to the edge. There, it teetered as if in indecision, while above it the blank white mask set in a metal skull spun around and around.

The body tipped as the head fell, and Adam Smasher went over the edge.

Jaune had an inkling of what that meant. Jaune had not the beginning of a clue of what that meant. This world was not his, to be fully understood at a glance.

So, he promptly turned on his heels, and that was that as far as he was concerned. After all, the job wasn't done.

"Now, what to do about this," he muttered, looking up at the flight of AV transports descending in formation.

The doors on them slid open while they were still in the air, and the occupants leveled their combined arms in his direction. It seemed that someone, somewhere was insisting on pressing the point. Could be the man there, standing at the open doors of an AV with his suit jacket whipping in the wind.

The man, Faraday, didn't look to be in the best state of mind. Sweat drenched his suit, and the row of multiple cybernetic eyes on one side of his face kept twitching. He was shouting something.

Jaune put a hand to his ear. "What!?"

His true attention lay past the man's shoulder, where an Arasaka soldier had his arm hooked around Kiwi's throat, a gun pressed to her head. Had Smasher spilled the truth as a last bit of revenge? His mind raced for a solution to the predicament, only to find Kiwi returning his glances with a dispassionate gaze.

Her hand by her hip was counting down.

Faraday shouted louder. "Do you have any idea what you have cost me?"

Jaune thought about it. It… didn't take long, honestly. Math was not his forte. He answered Faraday with a helpless shrug.

Faraday almost popped a blood vessel.

The fixer then popped more than a blood vessel as Kiwi overloaded his cybernetic eyes, dropping him to his knees with smoke spewing from his head. From shadows, a cat leapt onto the Arasaka soldier holding Kiwi in place, biting the hand holding the gun hard enough to crack bones.

As a struggle broke out behind her, Kiwi gave Jaune a small wave. His phone pinged.

"Hi."

Jaune grinned back at her, and with a jump he shot into the neon-lit sky with sword in hand.

Heading off one more time to fight the corporation.



-o-

David woke up, and the world felt like a new day.

He looked around at everything happening with clear eyes. He found her amidst the chaos waiting for him.

David picked up his gun, and got to his feet.

Now, it was a festival.
