#8,309

Chapter 84: The Man Closest to the Throne
​

It was said, the world that had once stopped in its tracks began to move with his appearance.

Coming out of nowhere, taking the Lands Between by storm, he accomplished things nobody else would dream of. Demigods that had laid countless challengers low, fell at his feet. Those who met him all agreed, his thinking belonged to another realm. Aseo, that man…

"That's Radahn? Wow, he's scary. Can we, I don't know, shoot him with one of the ballistas from here?" said Aseo, up-and-coming legendary warrior, shading his eyes with a hand as his head poked over the castle battlements. He was shaking like a leaf, having watched the hulking, mindless figure in the distance beat a long-dead corpse to paste with his swords.

Jaune, standing next to him, threw his arms in the air. "That's what I was telling them!"

In a castle obsessed with honorable combat, two like-minded souls bumped their fists together. With that exchange, the ice broke between them.

"Aseo," the warrior offered his name.

"I've heard. The Naked Parry King, right?"

"...Yeah, I guess so." Strangely, Aseo did not appear very enthused about his title, mumbling at a quieter volume about a 'Melina' and 'getting that witch back for this'. What an odd guy.

"Well, good to meetcha! I'm Jaune."

"Jaune, huh? Of?"

Now was Jaune's turn to wilt. "I don't have a title yet."

The Huntsman? The Valkyria? In bygone days (last week), he would have so proudly worn those coats, but after listening to Blaidd list out the epithets that people here threw around, they no longer measured to the same level of grandeur in his mind. His eyes had been opened, now wide and clear. The part of him that wanted to be a hero, hear people cheer his name, maybe with a movie deal or two, yearned for something with flair, something flowery and poetic.

Lisa interrupted his thoughts, lightly pushing the back of his head to snap him out of it. "Ugh, I knew nothing good would come of you mixing with this lot. Don't turn native on me after less than a day." She shook her head and turned to their new acquaintance. "Aseo, was it? This silly man is with me. Lisa's the name."

Aseo cocked his head. "Lisa the…?"

"The Girl in the Know," she answered without missing a beat.

Jaune leaned down next to her ear, speaking behind his hand. "And how long did you spend workshopping that?"

"Shoosh, you."

Despite playing it cool, Lisa could not quite hide the slight red flush creeping across her face which revealed the truth. Deep down at her core, she really was no better than him.

"Anyway," she gamely continued, glancing over to Aseo who during the lull had struck up conversation with Blaidd. "What's the deal with him? I still can't pick up anything special. Everybody got in a tizzy once he showed his face, but he's literally just another idiot." Said person was showing off little chips of colored glass to the wolfman, looking very proud of them, until a strong gust of wind swept half his baubles out of his hands and over the wall. He almost leapt after them, but Blaidd managed to stop him in the nick of time. "No, wait, he's even worse."

"Be nice," he chided, nudging her with his elbow. Yes, it was ever a vain hope that she would listen to that particular request, but he figured he should keep trying anyhow.

Still, she had a point, even if she could have put it in a nicer way. The newest champion to arrive at Redmane lacked the standout impression Jaune expected from the supposed top dog of the bunch, a young man with messy black hair and a face that Jaune might pass by on the street without a second glance. The champion also dressed in chainmail armor and tunic rather than run around naked, which made Jaune wonder what the nickname was even about. Was it a metaphor?

Then again, it could just be Aseo's peers that stood out too much. From Great Horned Tragoth with a huge stone hammer bigger than himself balanced on a shoulder to the walking, talking clay jar that Jaune mistook earlier for a communal cooking pot, this section of the castle wall was at the moment playing host to quite an impactful ensemble.

Why nobody batted an eye at Alexander (the jar), Jaune struggled to understand. He considered Blaidd a Faunus as a matter of course now that the man proved he wasn't a werewolf, but a piece of sentient pottery had to stretch the limits of credulity, he felt. If Alexander was alive, then why do people treat tables and chairs as inanimate objects? Yet, even Lisa had to declare him a thinking individual after exchanging a few words. The mystery deepened the more one looked, confounding Jaune to no ends.

Yes, he took a picture of the guy. A video, too.

The people back home would never believe him, otherwise.

"The challenge at hand is how do we approach our opponent," said Tragoth amid conversation with the other champions, his voice echoing due to the helm which covered his face. "A meteor? I trust in my hammer, in my armor. Alas, they also weigh me down fiercely. Blaidd, you seem a spry fellow. Have you an idea?"

Aseo muttered, "Follow Blaidd's lead, and we'll probably get lost on the way to the fight. Something on him is cursed with a teleport trap, it's the only explanation."

"What was that?" asked Blaidd, with Aseo doing an immediate about-face.

"Nothing!"

"I could have sworn you spoke… Ah, no matter. You ask how am I to take on Radahn? It is risky, but I believe a frontal charge would be the most honorable thing."

"Is that our biggest concern?" Aseo asked weakly, slumping his shoulders. "Really?"

As the other champions threw their own suggestions into the ring, Jaune spoke in Lisa's ear. "I guess even a guy like Blaidd has a few quirks. Who would have guessed?"

She peered up at him. "Did you somehow miss the fact that he has a wolf's head?"

"I've mentioned to you before about the Faunus of my world, haven't I? Yeah, he's a bit different from that but let me tell you, Faunus traits can be anything. Anything. Like, there was this one White Fang Faunus during the battle back at Beacon that just… she was shooting these white, sticky ropes of spiderweb out of her hands that went everywhere. Rope after rope, all over the people around her. Blaidd's case isn't so strange in comparison."

The look of utter disgust on Lisa's face said enough.

Their little aside ended there, and Jaune turned his attention back to the discussion where a debate had broken out over Aseo's idea of using sleds tied to horses to close the distance. General consensus was of the mind that it would simply result in a lot of dead horses, and Aseo was a terrible person for suggesting that in the first place. They were now calling for volunteers among them to pull the sleds, instead. A much more humane plan.

As in, a lot of humans would die rather than horses. With great reluctance, they scrapped the idea after that was pointed out.

The frontal charge was, of course, not in question.

"No, don't skirt over that. Why isn't it?" Lisa asked, instantly drawing incredulous gazes from all around. "Pincer attacks are a thing. Blaidd, you yourself told us that was how you and Alexander"—she jerked a thumb at the big clay jar standing with its arms crossed (which still sounded crazy no matter how many times Jaune thought about it)—"took down one of those dino-dogs outside the castle."

"That is that, and this is this," Blaidd said while nodding sagely. "General Radahn deserves better than for his final end to be an ambush from behind."

That got a rousing cry not just from the assembled warriors, but also from the castle soldiers within earshot. Jaune cheered along with them until a glare from Lisa put an end to that. Likewise, his subsequent protests to her that Blaidd made a great point received a withering look from the girl.

"You can't eat honor," Lisa declared, undaunted in the face of all the people arrayed against her. For they were wrong, and that could not stand.

Click.

One little sound cut through the hubbub. Okina of the Land of Reeds, heretofore content to remain silent, had raised his katana an inch out of its scabbard. The notched blade drenched in red carried an ominous glow.

Jaune very carefully shaped his hand to hold a sword, ready to summon it to hand at the slightest overt sign of an attack.

"Without honor, we are nothing more than lowly beasts, and for a meeting of champions, there are far too many cowards among us," said Okina. "My blade thirsts for the blood of worthy opponents. Yet, I find that craven hearts fill it all the same."

The samurai directed his gaze toward Aseo, who had begun sweating bullets. It moved the other way to look at Lisa, with Jaune getting there first to step in front of her. Okina cocked his head, observing him head to toe. A derisive snort told Jaune what the man thought of him, throwing more fuel to the fire.

"I see no champions," Okina said.

Right away, Aseo's hand snapped into the air. "I completely agree, so if you need me, I'll be sitting in the stands—erk!" The man's words cut off, his head now squeezed in an arm lock by Blaidd before he could make his exit.

"None here are craven!" Blaidd cried. His booming voice carried over the castle, and the wolfman seemed oblivious to Aseo's attempts of wriggling free. "Aseo has fought alongside me, and valorous was his heart that day ("Were we looking at the same thing?"). Jaune, I know but scant hours ago, and he was the first to challenge Radahn. Ignoble and pathetic though his defeat may be ("Hey!") to everyone here, courage is not something he lacks."

Okina was unmoved. "Absent of skills, he is then merely a fool with not even a 'the' or 'of' to his name."

Was everybody in this place going to give him grief over that?

The wolfman narrowed his eyes and bared his fangs, matching Okina's oppressive aura with one of his own. "They are skilled, and they will prove it to us on the training grounds."

Lightning almost seemed to crackle between wolf and samurai, such was the intensity of their bearing. Trapped in the middle, the Naked Parry King hung limply, resigned to whatever came next.

"Is anyone going to ask our opinions before deciding that?" he said. "No? Wonderful."

Jaune nodded in sympathy. This kind of pushiness was cuter when coming from Lisa or Hu Tao, and not a bunch of old guys.

As the champions bickered on, he leaned against the parapet with his head tilted back to peer over the wall. Poor Radahn awaited down on the beach there, completely forgotten by his challengers as they went off to do their own thing.

…Was this festival going to be okay?


-o-
​

The training grounds encompassed a ring set off to the side of the main courtyard. It saw use as a place where people settled their grievances or displayed their martial might. Violence came part and parcel with a war festival, and life in general in the tumultuous Lands Between.

Into that ring Jaune strode, sword on his hip and decked in armor. The scales of a fiery wyvern rippled under the faded daylight of a Caelid sun.

Lisa had been the one to suggest he went in full regalia—it sent a message while hiding their hand. Aura was a potent card should someone here decide he needed to die. She tended to needlessly worry like that. It would all come out soon, anyway, once they launched their assault on Radahn.

He took his position and brandished his sword. The blade remained in its scabbard, which made it a little awkward of a shape for a true duel of swords, but he compensated for it easily enough at his level of strength. In any case, a practice bout called for some restraint, blunted edges and things like that. His other hand held onto the shield of Red Rook.

Across from him, was Aseo. His sword belonged to the two-handed variety, tall and heavy. He braced it on a shoulder, and wore a look of absolute focus.

"What a shite stance."

"Which one?"

"Both. They bring shame upon themselves, conducting in such a manner."

"Tsk, tsk. I want to meet the masters who taught them."

A vein popped on his head, and in unison with Aseo, he scowled at the spectators encircling them who were still going off about every little nitpicky detail. The champions did this while lounging on chairs and tables, with snacks to go around, casual as could be. The pair then shared a tepid look.

"Why are we even facing off?" Aseo asked. "They're the ones with the problem. After all that, it would have made a lot more sense for us to fight them."

"Right?" said Jaune. "I wouldn't mind the chance to whack Okina's stupid mask off his face."

"Me first."

As conversation between them fell off, his gaze drifted over to Lisa, the reason he was in this mess to begin with. She sat atop a barrel, chin in hands. Having donned one of her spare outfits stowed in his Pocket, the girl fitted in with the world around her a lot better than he did.

Noticing him, she cutely smiled before sticking out her tongue. You're on your own, she conveyed with a wink.

Aseo gave a sigh, scuffing the ground with his boot. "This is such a hassle." His voice lowered in volume. "Psst, hey. Why don't we save our energy and just fake it? I'm a pretty good actor."

For a few seconds, Jaune did not answer. He adjusted his grip on his sword, glancing around. Then…

Clang!

Sword clashed on sword, with Jaune smiling at Aseo from up close. Crocea Mors, still in its scabbard, ground down on the claymore that Aseo was holding sideways over his head.

"Hold up! I thought you didn't want to do this, either!" Aseo squeaked out.

"Ohh… I wouldn't say that," Jaune replied. "To tell the truth, I've been looking for someone to trade pointers with. After all, there's always more to learn~"

He slipped his shield arm between their bodies, and gave Aseo a big shove back to start the bout in earnest.

A punch might have done more damage there, but a spar meant he had to dial it down. In the same vein, he pursued his opponent at a slower pace to allow him the time to plan his moves.

Not too slow, though.

"Come on, let's see what you got!" he said as his sword flashed through the air. At the last second, Aseo diverted it with his claymore.

Not letting up, Jaune twisted the blade, transforming it into a stab at the chest that sent Aseo scrambling to dodge. Seizing that momentum was a no-brainer, and he advanced with a low sweep of his leg that threw his opponent further off balance.

Aseo stayed on his feet, if barely. The reach and weight of his bulky claymore suited a wider distance. Fighting inside that range was a little cheap of Jaune, but the world could forgive him for that, surely. Since he tended to encounter guns more than blades, the chance to show off his swordplay didn't come around too often.

The spar quickly shifted from the center of the ring to its edge, Aseo on the backfoot all the while. Each blow from Crocea Mors, heavier than at first glance, rattled the claymore and shook Aseo's stance. It gave Jaune confirmation that his strength had grown to a point where the simple longsword bore the same sort of formidability as a greatsword, lacking only in range.

Was there a way to take further advantage of that? Get in even closer, so he was in a scrap that wholesale eliminated his foes' weapons from the equation… No, at that point he might as well become a brawler, or a knifefighter, and he didn't really have the fundamentals for that.

Haaah. It was hard to know how to improve, with him as his own teacher.

Well, he could trust in his sword, at the very least. Place it just right, behind the foot, and a shield bash would knock whoever he fought down to the ground.

"Ow!" Aseo cried as he landed on his rear. The claymore slipped from his grasp, hitting the rough castle stone with a loud clank.

Jaune held back for a bit to see whether the other man would concede the spar. Aseo chose instead to dive after his weapon, and in answer, Jaune brought his sword up to slam it down in an overhead chop. A blow that would finish any fight.

At the last moment, Aseo's gaze that had been trained on his claymore flicked to the side to meet Jaune's eyes, and Jaune realized too late that the other man had planned for this.

Aseo's figure blurred. The tip of Crocea Mors struck the ground, screeching off the stone as Aseo rolled to his feet with his weapon once more in his grip. The claymore then whipped around at blistering speed, aimed at Jaune's throat to force him to duck.

A leap backward gained him distance outside of melee range, as his mind raced to analyze what had occurred. His finishing blow had Aseo dead to rights. There should never have been a chance for a turnaround, until his opponent moved like a phantom through harm's way.

The answer came from an unlikely source.

"He may be worthy of his name, after all," Okina begrudgingly said from his spot on the sidelines, arms crossed. "And that speed, it puts him on par with any of my disciples."

Beside him, Blaidd nodded. "If it's Aseo, it has to be this. What a splendid return to form."

Jaune blinked, taking in the scene, trying to see what they saw. No matter how hard he looked, the picture refused to straighten out into something comprehensible.

"Phew!" Weapon propped like a walking stick, Aseo wiped his brow. "Thank goodness I got my armor off in time."

The pervert said that while dressed in a piece of loincloth, and nothing else. Practically an admission of premeditation for his act of public indecency, with not even alcohol as an excuse. Shocked gasps rang out all throughout the courtyard at his brazen display.

Among the champions, however, a different reaction took root.

"I see," said Great Horned Tragoth. "Removing his armor unencumbers him of excess weight, thereby increasing his swiftness manifolds."

Okina grunted, and said, "The drastic difference between the two states then creates the illusion that he vanished through thin air, and renders him nearly untouchable. That one moment should count as a special move in itself."

Murmurs continued to grow within the crowd of champions, each finding something to be impressed about. Only, none of them were addressing the real problem.

"That's not how any of it works. The difference isn't 'drastic', it should be tiny. This doesn't make any sense," Jaune cried. Stripping naked was not a winning move in a fight. Pyrrha would have told him something that important!

He heard a familiar laugh, bitter and mocking.

"That's rich coming from you, mister!" Lisa called out, hands cupped like a megaphone.

Not this again. "Everything I do is normal," he insisted, and rightly so.

"Tell that to Isaac Newton!"

"Once again, I have to ask. Who even is that!?"

A cough, and Aseo cut in. "Sorry to interrupt you two lovebirds, but uh..." The sly man had used the brief distraction between Jaune and Lisa to settle again into a fighting stance. "Doesn't me doing it means that it is possible?"

"Guh!" Jaune winced, unable to argue the self-evident truth of that statement. The proof was before his eyes, and in brave new worlds, who was he to deem it one thing or another?

He looked Aseo up and down. (More up than down.)

Nope, never mind. He still couldn't accept this. Stripping might be many things, but a superpower was not one.

His opponent refused to give him any more time to think on it, though. Aseo closed the distance in the blink of an eye, searing into Jaune's memory the image of a man's pale and sweaty body. And swinging the claymore at his arm, too, but that caused less damage to him since he caught it on his shield.

"He could have parried," someone said, he didn't know who.

"No, Jaune meant to do that," Blaidd said. "He stopped entirely the momentum of the blade. Against a greatsword, that is crucial."

The peanut gallery was getting into the swing of it now, providing a slew of commentary to follow up on Blaidd. Some were wrong, fewer than one might expect. Many of them got things right. It attested to their skills in the art of combat, and emboldened Jaune's hope that he would pick up something good by sticking around.

The spryer version of Aseo posed a much more formidable foe. He darted in and out of Jaune's range, lugging the claymore along as if it weighed nothing. The sheer speed of his movements added to the momentum of the blade, strengthening its attack. The synergy between sword and 'sword' crafted a style which shone beyond its individual components, and anyone's expectations.

Oh sure, the thought definitely passed his mind that he could slap on his rocket boots and then overpower his opponent with brute force, but that went against the spirit of what he was trying to accomplish here. Namely, learning.

Although, he wished he could be learning a different lesson from this.

Aseo stepped in for another exchange, and Jaune now had a choice to make. Dignity, or power.

In the space between one moment and the next, the suit of armor encasing him popped out of existence. His shirt went with them. He rushed forward with a burst of speed, free and unencumbered, sword lunging to meet the incoming Aseo.

A soft noise slipped from Aseo's lips. "Heh."

Clang!

Jaune's eyes flew open wide, his whole body tilted from the blow that had batted his sword off its course. His hand trembled with the effort of holding onto his weapon. Looming above him, Aseo mirrored an earlier move of his, winding back for an overhead chop.

"You are an impressive stripper, but you lack commitment," Aseo admonished. "Those pants will be the death of you in real combat."

Jaune hissed through his teeth. "Naked Parry King—!" The sword descended.

A sharp streak to separate the air, raising barely a whisper in its wake. It was beautifully done.

But…

Wham! The Red Rook shield smashed into the sword, tossing it aside with ease. Jaune spun with the motion, Crocea Mors sweeping in a crescent arc.

"I learned to parry ages ago!" he shouted.

May Solaire witness him now.

"Tch. Fine, I'll show my true skill," Aseo shouted back. His knee pulled up to his chest, the foot launching out before Jaune could land his riposte. "Kick!"

Jaune jumped to the side, abandoning his attack. "Wait, what? That's what you call a skill? If you can do it, I can do it, too. Kick!"

His foot crashed against a naked chest, and sent his opponent flying. The spectators erupted in cries of awe.

"He stole that skill after seeing it once?" Blaidd blurted out, completely floored.

"A hidden master. How could I have missed it? Argh! My blade is singing out to taste his life!" bemoaned Okina, clutching tight onto his katana that had leapt free of its scabbard. "Don't stop me!"

The champions around Okina immediately piled on him to hold him back. Others were observing the spar with new interest, no doubt itching for their turn to show off their abilities.

One stood out from the rest, and stood over the rest. The big clay jar they called Iron Fist Alexander rubbed his… chin?... and spoke.

(How? Jaune didn't know. It wasn't like the jar had a face, let alone a mouth.)

"Acceptable, as kicks go. And yet, I cannot praise them," he said, prompting Jaune to pause and listen in. "Their overhead slashes leave much to be desired, carelessly done at the slightest opportunity." The jar firmed his posture, and brought his hands together to lift them up high. "A proper Overhead Stance bracing one's whole body for the blow would see its speed and might become nigh unconquerable."

The two fighters in the ring slowly turned their heads to stare at the living jar, then back to one another. While a smile stretched wide to split Jaune's face, the Aseo that was sprawled out on the ground grew pale and threw a hand up.

"Can we talk about this?" he spluttered.

"It's for practice. I'm not going to hurt you or anything… much," Jaune said. He slipped his hand from the strap of his shield, letting it fall as he seized his sword with both hands. The blade crisply snapped to position above his head, a mimicry of the stance that Alexander was demonstrating outside the ring. He maintained that posture, muscles coiled and ready to spring ahead rather than just swing. "Now, try and escape, and I'll see if I can catch you like this."

"No, look, I've always seen myself as more of a pacifist, so—" Aseo shot forward across the ground. "Hahaha, I tricked y-blegh!"

The champion had been fast. Crocea Mors had been faster. With some mind paid to proper footwork, Jaune managed to whip the blunted blade down so cleanly that after it smashed Aseo into the ground, the sword bounced back up to give him a chance to do it again. A chance he took, striking a second time to leave Aseo lying flat on his front, twitching.

The spectators roared their approval in the wake of the exchange.

"Better!" Alexander bellowed. "You are now at least at the level of an apprentice jar." A chuckle left his lips(?). "Worthy enough, for me to teach you the spinning arts of the warrior jars and become legendary!"

Fighters of renown, that one sentence served as their call. Jaune learned that day the secret of champions. They all wanted to be remembered, in their own way.

In other words, they each thought their technique was superior and damn what anyone else says.

Great Horned Tragoth plodded in front of Alexander, bumping the jar aside. "Nay! Your stripping prowess is the perfect setup for my elegant Ground Slam." He slapped a hand on the thick armor plate of his chest. "Imagine your foe as a chair. While they are on the ground, clad yourself in the heaviest of armor and leap up high. Gravity will do the rest."

Aseo eeped, and scrambled upright while shouting about it being his turn to try out skills on Jaune. Which was fair, except Jaune didn't enjoy the idea of being someone else's chair.

Still, the choice of what to learn was many, and growing with the passing seconds. He had his picks.

"We need to consider the weapons at hand. An Impaling Thrust is a suitable skill for a claymore-wielder."

"Why not a Lion's Claw—"

"Quiet, my fellows. Peace. I believe that a skill of my own special make, the Wolf's Assault, is the best and most efficient option possible."

"Blow it out your ears, mutt. I'll show them a Quickstep. Like a normal person."

"Stab yourself in the stomach to drench it with your life's blood, which will empower your attacks!"

That last one brought everyone up short, with all eyes turning toward the speaker.

"What?" Said Okina of the Land of Reeds.

In the end, their activities on the training grounds escalated a tad out of hand. Not all warriors were calm and collected masters meditating under waterfalls. Once one among them decided a hands-on demonstration of their abilities was called for, the rest followed suit. Thus far, two people were out of the festival for missing limbs until they could find a cleric to slap it back on with a priestly spell.

On Jaune's part, it was a feast.

Many of the skills brought forward involved esoteric magic that was beyond him. No matter how many times Blaidd showed his ultimate Wolf's Assault technique, Jaune was never going to get it. Not in a hundred years, not in a thousand. How did one 'will frost into being as a blade'? He certainly tried. And failed.

On the other hand, he picked up a few quite nice tips to improve his performance out of that mess. Flight had added a whole new dimension to combat for him, but also led him to neglect the fundamentals of footwork for the sake of a shortcut. Blend the two together instead, and he might approximate some of local techniques like the Quickstep and Impaling Thrust. It was, at the core, an extension of what he was already doing, with tighter movements that were closer to actual Huntsman acrobatics. Pyrrha probably would have gotten him started on those lessons around this time, in better circumstances.

Now, Ground Slam. That one had seemed a joke at first. Then, epiphany hit to give new life to an old idea. A bigger Pocket could fit a bigger boulder, and a bigger boulder along with gravity added up to a bad time for anything he would like to see dead.

Of course, that meant a trip outside the castle. Into the Caelid Wilds, where the rotten flowers bloomed.

#8,515

Chapter 85: The Rocks that Fall
​

A rolling stone gathered no moss. But…

Crash. Bang. Oh, how hard it sang. A rock ballad for the ages.

"Out of the way, here it goes again!"

"Left! Roll left! Look at those monsters run! Hahaha!"

"Back in formation, you lot. The rest of them are coming back around. Only our guests get to pass the bridge. Burn the rot!"

"""Burn the rot!"""

The shouts were taken up by soldiers across the barren fields, as the hounds of Caelid once more charged up the hill. The men braced behind the barricades with their swords and spears and torches, awaiting the moment their neverending battle began in earnest again.

They fought against the land, against mutated life grown to monstrous sizes, against bodies of the fallen from a war long ago that yet walked. Above all, they fought against the flowers. The one flower to still sprout in this wasteland, spreading far and wide until they were met with a cleansing fire. Ash and smoke filled these soldiers' world, breathed in with each new day.

For this section of the defenses, front and center of the slope leading up to the bridge, it was the dogs that they faced. Slobbering beasts driven mad by endless hunger, those things had no concept of friend and foe beyond their pack. Their position at the front of the horde was won by dint of eating everything in their way. Several tons of boulder rolling down the hill had thinned their numbers, but there remained a fair few yet to regroup and continue the assault.

The first to hit the barricades drove itself straight onto the wooden spikes projecting outward. Even then, it kept shoving forward, a deadly jaw gnashing left and right in order to get one more bite of that most scrumptious human flesh. In the place of an eye, a crimson flower bloomed in full season.

To that, there was only one thing a person could say.

"Dibs!" Jaune called out, not that the people around him would understand the term.

Still, he proved the fastest anyhow, lunging upward to ram his blade under the monster's chin and through its head. A cheer went up among the soldiers as the dog jerked to a sudden halt. Jaune was already stepping over the barricades by then, a swing of his sword shearing off the next monster's snout with a kick following up to send it crashing against its brethren and causing a pile-up. Fire bloomed beneath him, launching him above the pack of dogs. They nipped at his heels, attention stolen, easy pickings for the soldiers of Redmane Castle to end their blighted existence.

The soldiers had no problem with him bringing out his guns for these foes. There might be envy in their eyes, but they knew better than to question a good thing, egging him on as he performed a strafing run down the hill. Their hearts must be made of rather stern stuff after their time in Caelid, because they even cheered as the fresh blood among the dogs soon turned the monsters against each other in a feeding frenzy from hell.

Jaune had seen some things in his life, but he still gagged at the sight of the dino-dogs tearing themselves limb from limb. Sheesh, talk about eating their own tail. Days like these, he almost missed fighting Grimm. At least with them, he understood what to expect.

Also, you know, the Grimm didn't spread diseases around. The guys here in Caelid had to deal with apocalyptic monsters and a plague. Lucky them.

The short burst of flight landed him next to his boulder, one much like the others dotting the area. This wasteland was lousy with them and it had taken him, oh, five minutes or so to find a nicely rounded rock with a good weight. The remainder of the last hour, he spent with the Redmane soldiers partaking in the hot new pastime of this decade, involving the boulder, a hill, and a bunch of ravening monsters. The thing now bore blood splatters all over it, looking quite ominous.

He gave the rock a hard shove to get it moving. That turned it into an object rather than a feature of the landscape. A second, lighter touch popped it into his dimensional space, to the continued amazement of the soldiers up and down the slope. It wasn't everyday a guy shoved a stone bigger than himself somewhere the sun wouldn't shine.

His Pocket. He was talking about his Pocket. Because there was no sunshine there and—

Why was he justifying this to himself? He knew what he meant.

Without the boulder to provide him cover, more dogs began to take notice of his presence, the closest leaping on its powerful legs to catch the surprise, yet welcome, snack. A gunlance shoved into its maw stopped the monster in its tracks, the ensuing blast tearing through the head and leaving the remains a fiery pyre.

Jaune shook the lance to rid it of the… giblets. As he did so, he happened to look past the burning smoke and spotted a mishmash squad of warriors carving a path through the melee. Others like them were cresting the hill in the distance. Champions bound for the festival of war, trickling in at a steady pace.

Right then, a ringtone blared from his phone. There might not be a signal tower in all of existence right now, but the tech packed into this device meant it served its purpose anyhow, at least for one other person in the world. He picked up the call, needlessly checking the ID on the screen out of ingrained habit.

"Oh, Jaune?" Lisa sang.

Instantly, he was on alert. "Yeees?"

"I'm looking at the Company phone right now, and…. what is this 'Cursed Boulder' in your inventory? It says here you sacrificed a sack of puppies to it, and that somebody called Mohg would be really impressed."

Jaune scratched his cheek, grimacing. "I, uh, I wouldn't worry about it."

"Uh-uh, none of that. How about you explain a little more?" she asked, sounding so innocent and sweet, surely not at all freaking out over this on the inside.

"You know, I'd love to but I think the signal is breaking up," he said, and made 'kshhh-kshhh' noises to sell the lie. "I'll be back soon, see you in a bit."

"I can tell you're faking it, you jack—" Click.

Ahhh, peace and quiet.

"Raaagh!"

Besides the raging dino-dogs, of course. Jaune stowed away the phone and shot back up to the top of the slope. The guys there were rummaging in their supplies for stuff to pay him with. He already earned this sick stabby sword from one of them that was supposed to sometimes put enemies it cut in a magic sleep, which should earn him a few Points when sold. And there was no telling what other goodies they might be willing to part with for an impressive showing.

The body of the dog he killed had started to bud flowers. He plucked the first to bloom, holding it up with a gloved hand by the delicate stem to take in the noxiously sweet scent. The delicate petals soft as silk, red like blood, carried with them a disease of rot and ruin.

Lisa could probably spare him ten more minutes.

Burn the rot.


-o-
​

As it turned out, Lisa could. But, there was a price.

"...should've seen those suckers trying to cheat me like I'm a rube. Hilarious! Anyway, I won everything including the clothes off their backs, so we're eating good tonight. And by that, I mean we're buying stuff from the Company Marketplace. Don't touch the food here unless you want to die. I saw one of the things they called an octopus, and it was disgusting. Like, you don't even know. They're all wriggly and…"

Connected by their phones, it was almost as if she was right next to him, yammering on and on and on until the end of time. Good grief, shoot him now.

…To tell the truth, he didn't mind her incessant chatter all that much, and Lisa already knew it. He was happy to keep up the pretense with her, though, since that girl might otherwise grow bored of a lack of reactions and decide she needed to raise her game to really annoy him. It would be so very like her.

"Hey, I made it back," he said once he was in the main courtyard of Redmane Castle. "Where are you at?"

A brief lull followed, which told him that Lisa was up to something.

"Ohhh, I'm around." Her mirth came through the line clear as a bell, spelling trouble. "Let's see how well you know me—kshhh, kshhh, uh-oh, it looks like we're breaking up. Good luck finding me!"

He could practically picture her vulpine grin, as she insisted he call it. Turnabout was fair play, it seemed.

Ugh, and she just had to phrase it that way, too. To this day he remained unsure on where they stood, and she of course saw no qualms in adding a little more to that mess, compounding the stress to leave an ill feeling in his chest. Blegh.

Jaune put away the phone in the same pocket he stored his scroll, and set out to look for his wayward partner-in-crime. During his absence, the festival had really gotten into the swing of things, with a number of new faces amid the revelries. The champions' ranks now swelled to a respectable army, the clanking of their armor contributing a noticeable part to the din. The practice ring saw a marked increase in participants due to that, with a few spars taking place at the moment.

He scanned over the audience but couldn't find Lisa among them. No surprise there. Without him, it wasn't her scene.

"That's kind of flattering now that I think about it," he said to nobody in particular, rubbing his chin.

Now, where could the wonderful(heh!) Lisa be?

Knowing her… His gaze slid past the practice ring to the other side of the courtyard. That part of the festival drew its own crowd, lively rows of market stalls conducting trades with stalwart knights and wizened mages keen to stock up before the big battle. With deals to be had and curios galore, it seemed more up Lisa's alley. A good place to start looking for her. He had been meaning to stop by for a visit, in any event.

He headed that way, plodding past the long tables that served as the eating area. The place was a party, with more alcohol than water in the cups. He had some earlier, and the drinks tasted halfway decent if a bit too warm going down. As for the food sold here, even without Lisa's warning he would have given it a pass. Stews and hard bread didn't impress him much in terms of festival fares.

At the edge of the eating area, a slim figure dressed in austere robes bowed to him as he walked by, a gesture he returned before moving on. Therolina the Fingermaiden was a polite soul, standing out among the champions for her quiet nature. Kind of an odd person, too. He couldn't recall ever seeing the woman move from that spot, or even eat anything, since Blaidd pointed her out to him. The level of self-discipline that must have required blew him away.

He entered the marketplace proper, and joined the throngs of people haggling for goods. The two rows of stalls somewhat cordoned off the area into its own little bubble, giving him a taste of the daily life in this world where things looked normal enough until an errant spark of light or a strange set of plate armor went clanging by. Where the man selling potatoes sat next to the woman touting magic staves. It was like every fantasy movie he had ever watched, minus the pointy elf ears. And with such lovely filth on people's faces.

Thoughts of Lisa moved to the back of his mind as the wares on display drew him in. These days it might be all mechashift, mechashift, mechashift, but medieval make held a certain charm for the guy who owned Crocea Mors. Simple was best, unless one could strap a cannon on it.

He paused for a moment at one booth, kneeling down next to the sheet of cloth on which a selection of weapons lay. The majority appeared mundane at a glance, with the rare striking piece among them. Call him shallow, a sword crafted from a blue rock had to be special in some way.

With the trader's permission, he picked up the two-handed sword, grunting at the surprising heft that did not fit the size of the weapon. That was saying something, considering it was already pretty big. A shame that he didn't have the space for a practice swing, he could tell the sword had great balance. Also, it glowed, so of course he wanted it.

"How much for this?" he asked the peddler as he fished a pair of gold coins from his pants pocket, lowballing the initial offer as per Lisa's advice. Who knows, maybe the peddler would be blinded by the shiny and accept the deal as-is.

The last thing he expected was a scoff.

"Gold will do you no good here," the peddler spat. "Runes are the currency of the Lands Between."

…He felt like he had heard this line before somewhere.

A glance at his surroundings confirmed that he had a problem. The flecks of shiny stuff trading between hands turned out to not be the gold he assumed they were, too bright by half. It didn't look right, either. Partly there, partly not.

That had better not be a person's soul, was all he was saying.

A man without means, Jaune floundered for a solution and drew out from his Pocket the sword he just got. "How do you feel about a trade? This can—"

"Yes, yes, a sword of Saint Trina that inflicts a poison of slumber," said the peddler with less awe than Jaune hoped for. "I am trying to move my goods, not add to them. You can find me some runes or you can go elsewhere."

Such was the common refrain he heard as he wandered from one stall to the next, for supply and demand held a strange relationship. The merchants had gathered arms from all over in order to offload them here. Low on funds and stocked up to the gills, trading in kind—even with a magical weapon—offered them nothing of value. They were in it for the money.

"Psst. Hey."

And yet, just as he was about to give up, someone took notice of his plight. Jaune turned toward the voice.

"Yeah, you. The word going around is that you are looking for deals," said the figure squatting on his haunches between two market stalls. Sunlight from a break in the clouds streamed down on him like a sign from above.

It reflected off the person's bald scalp and straight into Jaune's eyeballs, forcing him to blink rapidly to clear away tears.

"I… Yes, kind of. Are you a merchant?" Jaune shaded his eyes with a hand, and looked the figure over. The slim man dressed in the clothes of an adventurer, armored in key places and worn down from the road. It spoke of hard days risking one's life out in the muck, a life Jaune understood all too well. Despite that, a constant smile rested upon the stranger's lips.

All in all, he had a good feeling about this fella.

"Patches, is the name," the man said, not whispering anymore, his natural voice reedy. "Patches the Untethered, procurer of treasures most genuine in the Lands Between. So, what do I call you, chum?"

Even a simple shopkeep had a title. Siiigh.

Jaune showed nothing of his vexation, offering his hand. "Jaune Arc, nice to meet you."

Rather than a handshake, Patches reached up to grab him by the forearm and shook him that way, instead. Jaune hastily copied the gesture, but by the time he did, the merchant had already let go. The man glanced to both sides, then moved deeper into the shadow of the castle.

"Come," he said, beckoning with a finger. "Come into my parlor, and I will show you the finest wares you ever did see."

Jaune leaned to the side to look past his shoulder. "Isn't that just a corner?"

"Good real estate is hard to find nowadays," Patches smoothly said with a shrug. "Eh. Welcome, to Patches' Emporium!"

Jaune gave him a polite round of applause. The man's shop, if it could be called such, was little more than a tarp thrown on the ground with knickknacks piled on top. A number of weapons and armors leaned on the wall, the details murky in the gloom. Bits of colored stones emitted soft light in red, blue, green, and all the shades of the rainbow to provide illumination for the place.

"You know, I kind of dig this ambience. It grows on you," he said, moving closer to the objects on display.

Patches placed his hands over his heart. "Thank you, I put a lot of care into it to get things just right."

The slapdash feel was deliberate, then. The spread included more than arms, ranging into tools, baubles, and books, but Patches hadn't paid much of a mind to organization. That left the odds and ends to pile up in a haphazard way, and Jaune had to really squint to make out what he was looking at. In a way, it stoked one's sense of imagination that treasures might lay forgotten within this hastily put together shop.

Patches returned to squatting on his haunches, letting Jaune browse while providing explanations for the objects that caught his fancy. From old keys for unknown doors, none fitting the wooden chest they sat beside, to clay jars filled with valuable concoctions that somehow had the smell of cooking oil about them, the man spoke with an easy familiarity for everything he sold.

As Jaune rummaged through a stack of books and scrolls, plucking out one at random, the peddler perked up with a wide grin. One that Jaune would swear looked familiar.

"What you have there is a manual on the holy incantations, donated by a good friend of mine from the Golden Order." Patches ran a hand over his bald head, and licked his lips. "Very rare, very dear to me. I can bear to part with it, though. For the right customer who comes along."

"The Golden Order is…" Jaune put the clues together. "A religion. Yeah, of course everybody knows that." Man, he was smooth. He then waved off Patches with a small laugh. "I'll have to pass on this, since I have my own 'incantations' that I'm already trying to learn. But hey, is that friend of yours around? I would love a talk with them."

Patches looked at Jaune oddly. He said, dragging out his words, "Thinking of taking up the cloth, are we? It warms my heart to witness such piousness."

"It's nothing like that. I just want to heal injuries and throw lightning around. They're useful spells for a bad day, that's all."

"Now, now. Don't put yourself down," Patches insisted. "You have the look of a monk about you. And is that a sword of Saint Trina I spy upon your hip? How positively clerical. Heh heh heh."

Despite himself, Jaune had to admit flattery was always effective on him. That was a compliment, right? He hesitated for a beat, not quite convinced but still granting the scroll a second glance over.

Patches continued. "Why the lack of enthusiasm? If incantations don't do it for you, how about this shield? Note the painted horse crest, perfect for a young stallion out to challenge a demigod." The peddler wiped his eyes. "My other good friend left it to me after he passed. I keep telling him, don't visit those woods no matter how much treasure there is at the center, but the poor fellow couldn't contain his greed and got eaten by a giant bear. The last thing he said to me was that he wanted this shield to go to someone deserving."

Well, that took a dark turn. Jaune's eyes swam as he searched for a topic to distract the sorrowful man from the heavy mood.

"What about that one there?" he said, pointing to a shield shaped like a teardrop. Blue stones embedded in the metal glinted in the dark. "I like the design. How does it hold up in battle? It's not actually made of silver, is it?"

The peddler had pulled out a handkerchief, and said distractedly, "That's finely-crafted metal from the stars, that is. Useful for when those blasted academy stoneheads get too loose with their sorceries. Poofs the magic away. Mostly." His tone changed, growing morose once more. "It belonged to another good friend of mine who had a tragic accident over the cliffs of Liurnia. He held onto it to the end, before giving it up to me. I'm sure he would smile at us from the roots of the Erdtree if you were to wield it in his place."

"…Do you have anything without a backstory, by chance?"

"Afraid not, sirrah."

While maintaining eye contact with Patches, Jaune leaned over and with great care placed his hand on a massive sword propped against the castle wall.

"Ahhh. That one."

Jaune braced for more bad news concerning Patches's good friends. What could have happened to this one, sacrificed to a demon? The amount of misfortune to plague this man called for several rounds of drinks that he didn't have at the moment.

"What discerning taste," Patches praised. "That's a hot item you don't see often. Fell off the back of a carriage on the road to this castle. Stroke of luck, nobody could say different."

Hey now, that didn't involve anybody dying!

Relief turned to curiosity, and Jaune studied the object further. Long as he was tall, the weapon was more of a chunk of iron beaten into the approximate shape of a sword. The blade tapered slightly along the edge, but on the whole stayed as a blocky, crude tool absent an iota of elegance.

As Jaune grasped the handle to test the weight of the sword, Patches piped up.

"Careful, a scratch on that will ruin the value. As charming as our acquaintanceship, I would have to insist that you pay for any, uh… any damages…"

The peddler fell quiet then, his eyes bulging out as he watched Jaune lift the sword in one hand. Given its length, Jaune didn't have the space to maneuver it much, limited to a slow, deliberate overhead swing that brought the tip within an inch of the ground before rising up high to the sky.

"It weighs less than my lance," he observed, trying out a stab. "The handling should be similar given the shape, I reckon."

By this point, Patches found his voice again. "My word, you are a beefy one, aren't you? Eaten a horse while growing up, then?"

"Nothing like that," Jaune said, turning the sword this way and that. Good make, without an obvious defect in the forging. The edge forwent sharpness for the simplicity that remained from one principle, the heaviness that crushes all. Sheer mass would cleave through a man just fine. Through armor and horse, if need be.

A fine weapon, all told. That said…

"Forget it."

"Huh?" Jaune stiffened as a weight settled on his back. A pair of hands lightly gripped his shoulders, and the scent of a familiar perfume wafted over his senses. "Lisa!"

The girl poked her head around his arm. "Oh, I guess you do remember me. I couldn't tell since you left me waiting like that," she pouted.

He grimaced, suddenly recalling his task. "I was getting there. Honest." He twisted his head around to better talk to her, thus running smack into a strange sight. "Wait a minute, what's that you're wearing?"

That earned him a bright laugh from Lisa. She turned her body to better present the garment hanging off her shoulders, a cloak made of animal pelt stretching all the way to the floor. A big sack sat on the ground next to her, too.

"Like it?" she asked. "I won it off a card game. A good scrubbing, and it'll shine good as new."

"It looks a lot like the cloak Blaidd had on."

"It was."

Poor guy. Lisa must have fleeced that wolf blind.

"Anyway." Lisa fiddled with something behind him. He heard taps on a hardlight screen. "That sword in your hand doesn't have much going for it. No innate magic or special history. You can use it as a big stick, that's about it."

"Sometimes, that's all you need," he spoke softly, nevertheless setting the sword back in its place—the problem Lisa pointed out was the same conclusion he arrived at on his own. With actual need in mind, he indicated the shield offered to him earlier. "Let's buy that one, though."

Lisa followed his gaze, her eyes lighting up as she beheld the glittering stones embedded along the shield. "Ooh, pretty~ What's so special about this thing?"

"Besides Bennett needing one… Radahn uses magic, right? Well, this shield defends against that, as Patches here tells me."

The immediate skepticism on her face pained him. "I dunno, that meteor looked pretty damn physical to me. To you, rather."

"Point," he allowed, memories of his desperate escape from the attack playing back in stark detail. "It isn't the be all, end all solution, that's true. I mean, I'd rather not be in a position to get hit in the first place. But you know me, I get in trouble sometimes, so this is the backup for when it isn't possible to avoid getting hurt." He lowered his voice while picking up the shield. "If it works as advertised. Check the entry for me, that should help us decide one way or another."

Heeding the request, Lisa dove back into the Company scroll where the shield should have already registered as his possession by that inviolable law of finders keepers. While Jaune distracted Patches with small talk, she studied the item description, and soon came back with a different attitude.

"Everything sounds about right. The Carian Shield, it belonged to a magic knight—"

"There are magic knights!?"

"Quiet, you. Let me finish talking." Lisa poked him on the shoulder. "Anyway, yes, there is. Was. The knights of Caria wielded magic, and with these shields in hand they feared naught of magic," she recited from the screen. "Too bad this one couldn't defend against terminal velocity. There's a lesson for you there."

Jaune scoffed. "Please. I'm built different."

Every Huntsman worth their salt had a landing strategy, thank you. And these days, he had four. Glider, shadowy arm, rocket boots, and his face. That made him four times the Huntsman others were. Simple math, that.

"If you go out of your way to be dumb, I'm not saving you," Lisa warned.

He deflated. "Yeah, I know. I just wanted to try saying it."

Their conversation didn't get to hit its groove. Patches, seizing his chance to interrupt, cleared his throat to bring their attention back to him. Their interest in the shield must be pretty obvious, because the peddler was rubbing his hands together, looking from one face to the other in glee.

"Do mine treasures suit your taste, friend? It could be yours, for a pittance. For a trifle. I shan't ask for much, in these circumstances. After all, everyone wants the old dog to die, the old dog included." His mien took on an aggrieved cast. "It'd hurt my heart to relinquish something so beloved, but I'll do my part on this day."

The peddler let out a quiet, solemn breath.

"Fifty thousand runes."

"Fifty—!" Jaune clutched his heart, nearly having a stroke. Fifty thousand anything sounded scary.

Maybe it was like Japanese and Korean currency? He remembered paying wildly different amounts for a meal on Earth because of a weird practice that Lisa called 'exchange rates'. That could be the case here.

"H-How much does a bowl of stew cost around these parts?" he asked in a hurry.

"With or without prawns?"

"...Without?"

"Ten runes."

Nope, this was like back home. He could buy a rocket locker for the price Patches was asking for the shield.

"And the cost if we wanted the stew with prawns?" Lisa piped up, unable to resist the question.

"Thirty."

What was up with the prawns, he wanted to know. Were they made of gold?

"This is daylight robbery," Jaune argued.

"No, really," Patches insisted, his eyes growing watery. "You're getting the price I charge my friends, honest. But a man has to eat, wouldn't you agree? I'm cutting me own throat, giving you this deal."

"But—"

"Ten thousand," Lisa cut in.

A gasp. Patches stared agog at her. "Who's robbing who?"

From within her snazzy new cloak, Lisa withdrew a pouch spun of rough cloth and gave it a shake. The pouch jangled with the ever familiar clink-clink melody of money. She didn't have that an hour earlier, Jaune was pretty sure. It went to show that gambling sometimes does pay off.

"You're selling to a champion," Lisa pressed. "Look, you have an impressive spread here. Not many other merchants can provide the same breadth of goods. That's what we like about you. You go above."

Patches did not reply, but the little twitch at the corner of his lips suggested that he wouldn't be averse to more compliments. Which was why, Jaune had every bit of confidence that Lisa would disappoint him. It was a very Lisa thing to do.

"Still, you have to admit," she continued, "that it's all a little used. Hardly appropriate to dress our champions in before they go to war."

"Whoa, whoa, whoa there," Patches said, shifting from his squat to jab a finger in Lisa's direction. "That is just the nature of the business, see. These knights and clerics are always chasing a better set of undergarments or what have you—"

"Didn't you say that these were 'beloved' items?" Lisa asked sweetly.

Patches coughed into his hand, looking to the side. The small smile on his face had grown, the man paying a lot more attention to Lisa now. "Could be one and the other, I never said different. My friends were the giving sort, after all. Heh heh heh."

"Give and give, until your friends have nothing left," Lisa simpered. "You must have it hard, always needing to pick up the pieces. My condolences."

Jaune almost facepalmed at her rudeness. Yet, strangely, the person to whom that was directed barely took offense.

"Oho?" said Patches. "You seem to know a thing or two."

Lisa answered with that look of hers, the narrowed eyes and a smirk that bragged she was privy to a secret. Jaune tried to signal to her that he would like to be clued in, but she ignored him. That… wasn't a surprise.

Patches let out a smooth laugh. "You have the wrong idea. I love my job and the friends I meet. They're the highlights of my life!" He swept his hand over his wares. "Sure, it may be sad come the end, but better to see these treasures in someone's hands than to rot in a grave, people are always telling me," he said. "Like Aseo. Did I mention him? The Naked Parry King calls me his brother, that's how much I've done for him."

Lisa nodded. "I wonder when we'll start seeing his stuff among your collection."

"'Selection', you mean," Jaune corrected. "Since he's selling them."

"Hm. No." Lisa reached up to pat him on the cheek. "Cute try, but we agreed that I'll be the one doing the talking in negotiations, remember? Then again, I guess you're a little impatient for the battle ahead." She turned back to Patches. "Twenty thousand? I expect you're gonna swim in a surplus soon, no matter how it shakes out. You could spare a few choice bits for a repeat customer."

"Is he?"

"He will be, won't he?"

Patches considered that, rubbing his chin. It was an odd mirror to the gesture Lisa was performing, and the more Jaune looked, the more similarities he saw between them. The smiles stretched wide in faint hostility. The paradoxically casual postures. They could be siblings.

"Are you… Are you two hiding something?" he ventured at last. He needed just one more clue, two at most, and he felt like he could figure out the reason behind their grins.

The pair stared at him, then at each other.

"Where did you find him?" Patches said.

Lisa gave Jaune another pat on the cheek. "He's so cute, right?"

The bald man looked him over, and laughed.


-o-
​

The drumbeats rolled like thunder across the castle, a pounding rhythm to herald the fateful hour. The sun was setting upon the world, and upon Radahn.

The champions stood together as a united army, dozens among their ranks. From far and wide they had come, here for war. In this moment they were of one mind, of one purpose and soul.

On a platform above them, the castellan of Redmane castle, Jerren, regarded the assembled crowd with something akin to pride. In great ceremony, the blade of his sword rose high in the air, hanging for a moment before slamming into the floor. Once, twice, thrice, the crisp sound of steel on stone echoed to the corners of the courtyard, and the thousand pairs of eyes of champions, soldiers, and civilians snapped toward the old warrior.

He, in turn, scanned them from left to right, right to left. That wizened gaze paused briefly on certain faces. Aseo. Blaidd. Okina. Tragoth. Therolina. Alexander.

Jaune.

"Before we begin." The castellan's voice was a gentle whisper on the wind. "Allow me to paint you the full picture…"

A no doubt riveting tale ensued. Which was a shame because most of Jaune's view had been blocked by Lisa.

His partner, wonderful she was, thought nothing of the occasion, more preoccupied with plucking at his clothes and hair in the way many an Annoying Blonde had done throughout his life. Like them, she wasn't letting up until she had straightened out his appearance to her satisfaction.

"You didn't eat any of the food in this place, right?" Lisa demanded. Her voice drowned out that of Jerren, much to Jaune's chagrin. "Right? Because you'll catch something. They haven't learned the advanced hygienic technique called washing hands, yet."

"No, I didn't eat," he answered, a touch exasperated. This would mark the third time she asked that question.

"Eaten from the inside… wits are long gone…"

Lisa nodded, seeming pleased that he heeded her advice. That was, until she glanced down at his arm.

"Your shield strap is loose. Honestly!"

Without a care, she stepped closer, taking hold of his arm and maneuvering it as she pleased. She untied the knot that secured the strap in place, then began cinching the buckle tight, talking to him throughout.

"You have your gear? Nothing missing?"

Eyes squeezing shut, Jaune whispered, "Lisa. Lisa, please. Stop fussing over it."

The champions in his immediate vicinity were barely holding back laughter, nudging each other and pointing without a single ounce of a warrior's stoic dignity to be found. Lisa might not be paying them any mind, but Jaune sure couldn't ignore the frankly punchable look on Aseo's face, or the absolutely vulgar gesture that Alexander was making with his hands—how did a clay jar know what that meant, anyway? Even the bloodthirsty Okina let slip a snicker from behind the mask concealing his face.

These were the champions? Really?

"...Like a dog. Howling at the sky…"

"We're supposed to be listening," he said to Lisa. "Jerren's doing a whole speech up there right now."

The unrepentant Lisa rolled her eyes. "Honor, rah rah. Glory, rah rah. I got the gist of it, and I have bigger concerns than an old man yelling at clouds." A final tug secured the strap of the shield, and she took a step back to admire her work. "There, now even if you swap it out, you'll know that you can have it back on your arm nice and tight in a pinch."

That chirpy grin of hers got to him, as always. And, just as always, he plopped a hand on her head to roughly muss her hair. Gratitude and teasing went well together, for it lessened the embarrassment involved with an act of thanks.

"Stahp, stahp, stahp!" Lisa squeaked, trying to shake him off to no avail. Once he relented, she covered her head and glared daggers at him.

"Thanks a lot, Lisa," he said, the smile breaking out on its own.

That honest appreciation earned him the middle finger. An affectionate one, insofar as the gesture could be called that, coupled with a playful bump of Lisa's hip against him.

They parted ways here, as the speech wound down and those participating in the battle began filtering toward the elevator at the rear of the castle. It couldn't take everyone down at once, of course, and so Jaune joined the queue waiting for a turn.

That was a harder task than it looked, since more than a few clerics spent the time glaring at him for his blasphemous ways. Who could ever guess that bringing up miracles from a different religion would face pushback from the devout? Not him, certainly. It came as a relief to step onto the platform alongside familiar, friendly faces.

"At last, we shall cross blades with Radahn," his erstwhile guide, the wolfman Blaidd, said with good cheer. "Let's give the world a fight to remember, eh?"

His doggy tail wagged.

"And wow, does it feel good to wear proper clothes again."

The wolfman ran his hands over his armor and pelt cloak, returned earlier after Jaune had gotten Lisa to give it up. The last thing he needed was his fellow participants charging into battle naked but for loincloths and without any gear, and he'd gladly pass on the chance to make a little bit of local money for that. What were they going to do to Radahn otherwise, bite his legs off?

The person on his other side was naked but for a loincloth, but he did it by choice so Jaune wasn't about to help him out there. He didn't have the license and college degree to deal with that mess.

"Aseo." He need not say more. The man dropped his face into his hands.

"Meli-Meli said she'd knock off part of my debt to her if I enter the fight while 'on-brand.'"

Jaune side-eyed him. "How do you people even know that word?"

The gloomy Aseo seemed unwilling to elaborate further on his woes, however, and Jaune soon tuned in on the other conversations taking place atop the rickety platform slowly descending from the castle wall. The general air of excitement swept him along in its mood.

People wanted to fight. They talked about this battle as some sort of once in a lifetime chance to meet a celebrity, lacking serious bloodthirst and rancor for one of the parties that, as Jaune heard it, was supposedly responsible for how Caelid turned out. Well, except for Okina of the Land of Reeds, but he was like that with everybody.

Blaidd summed the matter up once Jaune asked about it. "After all these years, Radahn will finally have his rest. About time, I say. The best of us deserved greater than this."

"You admire him, huh? You told me the festival has happened in the past, though," Jaune noted. "There's no guarantee that this time will end in a different way."

Great Horned Tragoth pushed past the people behind Jaune to join the discussion, the immense weight of his armor causing the elevator to creak and groan in a deeply worrying fashion. "Ah, but never have the stars aligned thus. There was always another crisis, another dead thing rising that must be sealed away or another bloody dispute amongst us who sat at the Roundtable." The champion swept his hand over the crowd already assembled below. "Today, we have the numbers and that is a rare thing, indeed."

"Grander champions than us have faced Radahn, I'll admit it," Blaidd said. "Skill does matter. Yet, were that alone enough, he would have fallen long ago. He came from another age, one we can only scratch at. No less than an army would do. Radahn lived in war. Is it any surprise that he must die in war?"

Jaune gave a noncommittal hmm, the subject not one a visitor like him could comment on. His part in this began and ended with a rousing fight, plus the prizes to be won.

That said, his interests aligned with theirs, so he opened his mouth again. "If you want to be extra sure of that, the offer is still on the table."

"Your magical shield?" Blaidd clapped him on the shoulder. "Hah! Your master was right to stop you."

Tragoth shook his head, sighing. "Weakening yourself for our sake, you are a rare one. Nay, we will make do."

"Besides," Blaidd added. "Where is the honor in turtling up, hey?"

Aura was inherent to a person, nothing dishonorable about that. If he had more time to explain properly, he could have gotten them to come around. Curse his lack of foresight, and damn their stubborn pride.

On another note…

"Lisa isn't my master," Jaune said. "Wait, was that how all of you saw us this whole time?"

Nobody would look him in the eye, which said enough.

The elevator at last touched the ground, depositing their group on the thin stretch of land at the foot of the castle before going back up for the next lot. That left them to the task of crossing the inlet separating this side from the shore that was Radahn's territory. Wooden logs lashed together allowed passage, with the occasional careless misstep sending a champion into the drink, where they then had to flounder their way across and stand in soaked, briny armor.

Jaune had an easier time of it than the others, kicking over to the opposite side with a quick rocket blast, not a single toe wet. Back on solid footing, he donned his Rathalos armor and various artifacts, helmet left off so that the fox mask could sit askew on his head; an unobstructed vision benefited him more than protection for the moment, plus empowering the Geo shield might help him avoid a blow altogether.

The lumbering form of Radahn could be spotted in the distance even now, his colossal stature swaying from side to side as it traveled across the sandy dunes. No reason nor rhyme existed there, the demigod simply drifting as more beast than man.

Despite the years, his armor shone golden to catch the light. His hair spilled out of his helm like a lion's mane, red as a sunrise.

Jaune could, in glimpses, see in that broad back the hero whom Radahn once was.

The last group of champions finally joined the rest of them, and for a long minute everyone stayed quiet gazing out over the red sands, the field of broken spears and faded banners. Making plans, and preparing their hearts. They weren't used to working together at this scale, given the way they jostled for place.

Great Horned Tragoth was the first to step past the unmarked line in the sand. The knight of assistance, whose stories always began and ended with him wielding his hammer in aid of others, did so now again.

"To his rest," he said.

To his rest, to his rest. The others took up the call. It grew to a bellow that resounded across the shore, until Radahn himself heard the cry. The snarling beast knew not its meaning, recognizing in it only the call to war.

The great General reared back, and howled as the warriors charged forward.

And the meteors fell from the sky upon their heads, wiping out the army before they ever made it within reach.

Champions all, of great renown. Their deeds amounted to nothing, in the end.

A god of war commanded the field.


Universe: Elden Ring. Location: Redmane Castle of the Lands Between.
Event: The Festival of Radahn
Loot: Sword of St. Trina, Carian Knight's Shield…
​

Wait, no.

"Peh! Peh!" Jaune woke up to a mouthful of sand.
