Chapter 91: Embarking Upon a Quest
​

Crown prince Noctis and his retinue, given little recourse, wandered after Jaune to his next destination. What would they find, these brave men knew not. Yet, they sallied forth nevertheless, crossing westward from Cindy's garage over the burning pavements of the parking lot, past the mini-mart with its beguiling and resplendent treasures sold at affordable prices for people not stranded in the desert, to…

A diner.

Takka's Pit Stop, the sign emblazoned above the building proclaimed. In Jaune's opinion, the best place to eat at the Hammerhead service station, and that would remain true even if it weren't the only place to eat at the Hammerhead service station. Was he being a little biased there? Maybe so. Food that he had a hand in making tasted just too good.

He hadn't been touching the cookingware, no. Although, his job did involve a little knifework.

"There's my star part-timer!" a voice called out at the moment he strode inside. "Where's your little brother at? And your kitty cat? I have a bottle of milk for her shipped in express that is just… muah!"

Jaune raised a hand in greeting to the man behind the counter. "Takka, hey. Bennett and Escha will be back with the Mesmenir meat soon, but I got those Dualhorns you wanted."

Unicorns and rhinos, by another name. Places where he would be able to enjoy meals of that caliber could be counted on one hand with fingers to spare, and the feeling of getting to eat something he hunted by his own efforts was positively divine. Little wonder, that he had been coming back here for breakfast, lunch, and dinner since yesterday.

Well, that was a part of it. Beyond the food, something about the diner hit just right. The selfsame namesake of the restaurant was one, the wiry man in a cooking apron sporting a ready smile for any person that walked through those doors. It also had to do with all the chrome, and the red and white color scheme. With the booths by the windows and the arcade machines by the back wall. With the long, curved counter set center stage that left plenty of floor space both for the cook to work with and for the customers to move about.

A jukebox had to be in the picture. Spare a glance to a nook by the entrance and lo, there it sat. Even without inserting a coin, he could already hear in his head a classic, nostalgic tune that this world had never known.

Ignis Scientia poked his head out from behind him, dispelling the wonderful reverie with a reminder that he was far from home.

"Part-timer?" the man said, and adjusted his glasses.

Welp, the jig was up. He had a good run, all five minutes of it.

"Takka and I have something of an arrangement," he said, keeping it vague. Some—and by some, he pretty much just meant Lisa—call it the key to deception. "I've mentioned when I met you that I was on a hunt, didn't I? This man here has a shopping list a mile long."

He left it at that, on the possibility of work which would surely help these four men dig themselves out of the hole they had fallen into. And Ignis took that bait in a heartbeat, rushing to the counter along with his prince and colleagues where they struck up conversation with the cook. Thus, Jaune was left free to take a step back and to the side, out of view, sidling inch by inch across the floor to a door at the back of the diner, next to the arcade machines.

That door opened to a sizable cold room where Takka kept his supplies, among them the animal carcasses that Jaune brought back on previous hunts. They had been rendered into slabs of meat now hanging on hooks, with a bison creature in the middle of being butchered laying on a metal table.

An off-putting sight, that. Yet, Jaune barely blinked. He stepped inside without hesitation and looked around, eventually settling his gaze on an empty stretch of floor.

"Here is fine, right?" he said to himself.

A wave of his hand, and suddenly the room did not seem so big anymore. Two massive beasts flopped to the ground in a heap, hitting the hard concrete with a thump that rattled the shelves and made the hooked slabs of meat swing back and forth. The first specimen had died in a rather messy manner with one of its twin horns cleaved off and the skull bashed in, but the other bore a clean stab at the base of the throat. That second move had risked him a painful trampling, paying off with a simple method to fell the rhino that bypassed its thick skullbone while preserving the state of the body. And now, Takka the cook had enough rhino to feed a village.

Jaune spent some time looking over the carcasses, which was just good practice before handing something off. He had learned that the hard way on his first job for Takka, with one of the game birds he brought back turning out to be sick. So, impatient nature or not, only once he confirmed one final time that there were no issues with the rhinos did he retreat from the cold room.

He emerged to the scene of a massacre.

…The mood of one, anyway. Four young men were in various states of despair, slumped on the counter, the tables, and in Prompto's case laid out flat on the floor.

"It's over," said the skinny blond. "Wrap it up, dudes. Cold harsh world - one, mighty Crownsguard - zero. Somebody call the city to rescue us. Oh, wait, better idea. We torch the car and make a smoke signal."

"That car belonged to the king, so no," said Ignis by the counter. The man was massaging his temples, his demeanor gray. "But you do present a valid option standing before us. What say you, Noct? Care to call it a day?"

Noctis, draped over a booth's table, raised his head. "We'll be laughingstocks, so no," he said, mimicking the same dry tone used by Ignis.

The joke was not quite a joke when spoken by a prince, it seemed. Jaune had the curious experience of watching three different men, without a prior signal and not even looking at one another, smoothly rose from where they were to gather round the diner booth occupied by their fourth member. It was almost eerie, how they moved in sync. And from the bits he caught before their conversation faded out of hearing, they were, despite their despondent air, discussing with all due seriousness the alternate ways to fund their trip as if it were the only course they could take.

For an answer to what had gone down in his absence, Jaune turned to the only other person in the room.

"You had no jobs for them?" he asked Takka, who was busy at the cooking stoves. "Not even one?"

The cook looked away from his task. "I reckon I might not have any for you, either. You're catching them quicker than I can keep up, kid." Burger patties flipped in the air, entirely for performative reasons so far as Jaune could tell. "It's a good problem to have. But inspiration comes on its own time, know what I mean? I'm still experimenting with the sauce that'd go on the cactuar."

"That's… the bird?" he asked, brows furrowed. The names of the species here could be so unintuitive.

"Nah. The cactus."

He snapped his fingers, sounding a crisp click. "The cactus. Right, I remember now."

That had been a surreal experience, chasing a living cactus across the desert. Little bastards were fast. Escha was still picking needles out of her fur hours later.

In the middle of reminiscing, he idly noted Takka stepping back from the stove and pulling a sanitary glove off his hand in order to reach into a pocket. From it, the man withdrew a sheaf of printed paper bills, which he brought over to slap on the counter. Gils, they called it here. The filthy lucre for which the likes of Jaune traipsed around this dusty bowl.

"Before it slips my mind, here's your payment," said Takka. "Four thousand Gils. I added a little extra since it's gonna be the last request from me for a while. Don't spend it all at once, you hear?"

Fat chance of that. More weapons! ...Plus maybe some souvenirs for everyone.

That said, Jaune had to point out the obvious.

"Hang on a minute, the others aren't back yet. We're only half done with the job!"

Takka waved him off.

"I know you're good for it," was his easy reply as he returned to cooking. On a tray, the meal began to take shape with the thick burger patties landing on sesame-seeded buns, followed by a thin—very, very thin—layer of lettuce and tomato because the tender, sizzling Garula bison meat was supposed to be the star of the show. To finish it off, a basket of golden fries provided accompaniment to the dish. "Now, while you're here, you mind carrying this over to those boys?"

Touched as he was by the trust his man showed him after a single day, Jaune raised a hand to stop Takka in his tracks. "I might have worked for you but I'm not your waiter, you know."

"Please?"

"I mean, since you said the magic word…"

"Knew there was a reason I like you."

Takka hurried over to a big pot sitting on the stove, lifting the lid to reveal the bubbling surface of a chili con carne. With a ladle, the cook scooped out five big bowls of the spicy stew chock-full of peppers, beans, and what Jaune believed to be ground Anak meat—giraffes, were the closest analogue he had for the creatures. Four of the bowls went on the same tray as the burgers, with the fifth placed on the counter.

"For my star part-timer," said Takka, making finger guns. "You've been a sunny breeze in these parts, Jaune. Like we had another Cindy around. I'll put a few sandwiches out for you in a bit."

Honest work and free food. He was going to miss this place.

Jaune lifted the laden tray on one hand, balancing the thing like how he remembered waiters always did it. He somewhat lacked the elegance to really make it look good, but the light weight of the tray worked in his favor so that he at least seemed like he knew what he was doing. Crossing the diner floor, he approached the group by the window, all of whom lifted their heads as their meal hit the table with a clatter of plates.

Three of the four stared in listless silence at the food, but Ignis took charge. After sparing a moment to fix his suit jacket, he quickly set to divvying up their lunch. A burger and a bowl of chili found their way in front of each member.

"Well, gentlemen," said Ignis once done. "Our last meal. Make it count, everyone."

Just how broke were they, Jaune wondered. A glum chorus of yays answered the man, following which the group began to pick at the food. Never had the diner met such a sad and sorry bunch.

He was not heartless, and so Jaune leaned against the booth and nudged Ignis on the shoulder. Once the man turned his way, Jaune gave him an encouraging smile.

"Hey now, there's no point in getting so down," he chided. One of his arms swept out in a grand gesture. "When has it ever helped? Sure, some things in life might not be going your way. It might seem pretty bad, or- or make you mad. But you know what always cheers me up? To look on the bright side of life, that it will all turn out for the best—"

"My sincere apologies, but could you take that feel-good pep talk to the next booth over? We would like to brood in a proper mood."

And they said they weren't a boy band, the divas.

Dramatics aside, the piping hot bowls of chili soon warmed the young men to the cockles of their frosty hearts. Except for prince Noctis, whose aversion to beans as foodstuff became quite apparent in the following few minutes. On the other hand, the juicy burgers more than suited the prince's tastes, delectably spiced with fresh herbs and wild onions. The way the group praised the meal to high heaven lent the impression that they never ate anything so good.

Not an untrue sentiment, as it turned out. Living in proximity to the royal family meant that they had the chance to enjoy all sorts of fancy delicacies, but as far as mundane dishes go, Ignis—the cook among them—ascribed the excellent taste of the diner's food to the wider availability of ingredients beyond the city wall. That didn't mean much to Jaune, lacking context of this world, but as he scooped up spoonfuls of chili and chatted with the group, he learned a bit more about the situation through his guise as a traveler from a faraway land. His dining companions offered a unique insight into the subject given their status, and they never suspected a thing about all his questions.

"A 'faraway land'?" asked Gladiolus.

"Uh-huh."

"Uh-huh," the bodyguard echoed.

As they then tell it, the Kingdom of Lucis once spanned the continent, sea to shining sea. The war with the Nilfheim Empire—a war that lasted for a length of time Jaune could scarcely believe, centuries now—had seen the territories slipping away one by one. A particularly harsh series of battles from thirty years ago reduced them to a single megacity dug in behind an impenetrable wall, isolated from the outside world. Within, life went on, sometimes almost normal before a reminder of what they had given up rear its head in the mild tastes of a dish or the music of an artist long lost to the conflict. The towns and settlements that were left out in the cold survived by staying quiet, offending neither empire nor kingdom, and for them any given decade was a coin flip between war and peace.

The empire suing for a treaty-signing that would end it all had opened the dam to a new era of hope. This trip taken by the crown prince Noctis was, in a way, a part of that. A chance to see the world, and how it had changed. What it could be again.

That the four men busted up their car had kind of put a damper on those lofty goals, though. The silly goofs.

"Is that why Cindy is charging you so much?" Jaune asked at the end of the tale, to crestfallen nods. "Because she hates you?"

The nodding stopped, and Noctis balked. "What? No! How is that what you got out of this? The repairs cost a lot because the parts aren't common outside of the city."

"Isolation has worked against us here," Ignis agreed. "Goods rarely flow across the borders. Whatever does will carry a premium. It has little to do with personal feelings."

"Cindy's cool with us, right?" Prompto urgently asked. "Right?"

The matter of Cindy's affection or lack thereof must, regrettably, remain a mystery as not one person present in the diner could answer it in a definitive way. Contrary to her bright disposition, that young woman kept many things close to her chest, chief of which was her heart. Cars were perhaps the one method by which a person could enter her good graces.

Jaune wouldn't know. His best trick with a vehicle was to crash it in an aesthetically satisfying yet survivable fashion. And going by his previous experience with a cute blonde-haired, green-eyed girl, his best advice on how to get her pants off, speaking entirely as a hypothetical, involved dozing in a body of water with his own pants off.

That bit got him a lot of weird looks from the others.

"It just works," he insisted, to the belief of no one there.

The fruitless discussion went back and forth for a while. In the end, it was tabled for later as the assembled men found new figures appearing at the diner's entrance. Brave knights, here to bolster their ranks.

"That's the biggest cat I've ever seen!" Prompto practically squealed. Camera in hand, he tried to out-muscle Gladiolus in order to get out of the booth, a losing proposition from the start. The bigger man shoved him back in his seat without looking, distracted by the scene at the door.

Opposite them, Ignis took off his glasses to wipe at the lens with a handkerchief before putting them on again. "Is it… Is it dragging back its kill?" he asked.

The incredulous tone might have to do with the sight of Escha on all fours, wiggling her way backward into the diner with her mouth clamped around the long, spindly leg of a horse-like creature. The thing measured many times her size, the impossibility of her moving it for any distance alleviated but far from eliminated, at least to the unwitting gaze, by a cart cobbled together from branches and car wheels set beneath her slain prey.

Halfway in, the long horn atop the horse halted Escha's progress as it caught on the door frame. The shape was reminiscent of a curved sword, and the length of one. Far too unwieldy when transported in such a haphazard manner. She tugged and she tugged, and it just wouldn't give.

"Mrow!" she groaned in dismay around her clenching teeth, and the weakest of hearts among them stood no chance, with Takka the cook falling on his knees with a hand clutching his chest and Prompto squeeee-ing like a little kid.

Aid arrived for Escha in the form of Bennett, who from outside the restaurant adjusted the bladed horn of the unicorn to fit through the entranceway, letting Escha resume dragging the carcass inside. The boy followed after his senior hunter with a unicorn of his own partly slung over a shoulder, the hind legs scraping the floor. Both his and Escha's expressions lit up as they spotted Jaune already there in the diner.

"And that's a wrap for the hunt. Good job, you two," Jaune said, applauding as he walked over to them. Escha let go of her quarry to bounce into his arms, where she nuzzled against his cheek. "Any trouble out there?"

Escha went to answer, but held back as she recalled that there were other people in the room. Bennett replied in her stead.

"None, boss. Escha herded these two away from the rest of them and right at me. It was smooth sailing after that."

"They ran over him," Escha said in a low whisper so only he could hear. "And then they turned around and did it again."

That would explain the rough and tumble state Bennett was in, and all the hoof marks. His body itself seemed fine, however, with Bennett standing tall, back straight. Proud to have hunted without Jaune's help. Praise me, praise me, his demeanor all but shouted. Rather than picking apart the details right then, Jaune decided that a thump on the boy's back would cover most everything that needed to be said. Bennett's beaming smile told him it was the right answer.

Carrying Escha in one arm, he yanked Bennett along with the other hand. A signal to Takka got him cooking up more food, and in the meantime his sandwiches ended up in front of Bennett while he scooped up some chili from his bowl to share with the cat.

To the curious onlookers, he explained. "These two are traveling with me. Escha is the cat, and this here is Bennett." He then introduced the crown prince and his retinue to his companions as a quick aside. "Make friends, alright? I'll go put away the dead horses."

He accounted for a bit of awkwardness in his absence. He came back to find that Bennett had ended up squeezed into the dining booth with Prompto's arm thrown around his shoulder and Noctis passing him a potato fry like they were best friends.

Why is he more popular with them than me!?

With no space at the table, he returned to standing while leaning on the booth. Escha hopped up next to him, reporting in his ear of their hunt in between stealing bites of his chili. Listening to her, the lessons he taught Bennett seemed to have been applied well with the occasional mishap more due to clumsiness than a bad decision. A good result, all around.

More food arrived for Escha and Bennett, the latter all too happy to share them with the other people at the table as he recounted his experience facing down a charging unicorn. His storytelling could use work, too honest and missing the embellishments that'd make him look good. N-Not that Jaune was in the habit of doing that.

As the story got to the point where a unicorn hooked its horn behind Bennett's collar and threw him in the air for the third time, Jaune noticed that Ignis was trying to meet his gaze. Once their eyes locked, the other man slightly jerked his head to indicate a spot away from the table. A request to speak, Jaune understood it as.

He peeled off from the group, careful to not disturb the ongoing conversation. Ignis soon joined him, his exit just as smooth. A brief lull ensued as the suited man collected his thoughts, where they both continued to listen to Bennett's retelling.

After about a minute, Ignis spoke.

"You seem like a man well put together." The sky did not fall, the world continued to turn, and the vehement denial of Lisa Wilbourn failed to pierce the veil of space and time. "We have imposed on you more than I'd like, but circumstances being what they are… Might you have a suggestion for how we can solve our predicament? Chocobos won't get us to our destination, no matter what Prompto says."

So, Chocobos could move. The mystery deepened even as it grew clearer.

Jaune held his chin, thinking on what he should do. Lisa would be giving him an earful right now about letting people take advantage of him, but they weren't, not really. He could always say no to them.

Which meant he never would.

"It's not like I don't have any ideas…" His gaze trailed down to the knives strapped under Ignis's suit jacket, almost invisible. "But before we go on, I have to ask. How are you guys when it comes to combat? I know you're armed, but what does that translate to?"

Ignis placed a hand over his chest, slightly bowing. "We have trained for years to protect Noct, and he the kingdom. You need not fear for our safety, we are prepared for any ordeal on the road."

"Except for a dead car engine."

"Obviously."

Joking aside, that made the solution an easy one.

"When you can't hunt something small, go bigger," Jaune said. "Come on, then. Let's go talk to the others."


-o-
​

Jaune sat at the head of the table, fingers folded to make a bridge in front of his face.

"Tell me," he asked the assembled men and feline. "Have you felt the recent rumblings beneath the land?"

He looked around.

"No? There was one just last night." That he slept through, and Escha told him about in the morning. "That cranky old man in the car shop has a rather wild story to explain it."

"I take it that this is not a natural phenomenon?" Ignis said.

Jaune glanced in his direction. "That all depends. How fantastical do you see a big turtle that causes earthquakes? It sure doesn't seem natural to me, but Cid tells me I'm wrong."

Prompto interrupted. "Excuse me, but… A turtle?"

"An Adamantoise, to be specific," said Jaune. "It's a big turtle, big as a house at the very least. Cid said that he could never reach its chin. It has some sort of magical power over the earth to cause seismic events, because the last time the Leide desert saw earthquakes it was that turtle that done it if you believe an old man's tale. Now, you may say that's crazy—"

"It isn't," Ignis said. He jerked a thumb at Noctis. "His father, the king, fought the Adamantoise in his youth during his own road trip across the continent, or so the story goes. It supposedly took place thirty years ago, in this very region."

Not only Jaune, Noctis and Prompto were staring agog at that bit of news.

"Seriously?" Noctis asked.

"Dead serious, Noct. Your father waged war on a turtle."

"That's… That's so lame!"

"On the contrary, he always seems quite proud of it. I've heard it is one of his regrets that he could not land a finishing blow on the creature."

"He lost? But—"

Jaune cut in, waving them down. "This is fascinating, but let's get back on track." He resumed his pose. "Someone else other than Cid had seen the turtle. Great."

Downright wonderful, in fact. He had asked around about the Adamantoise with not many people able to answer his questions. That period in time was one lost to the flames of war, and no account he had listened to could agree on much of what happened in those months. There had been evacuations and earthquakes, but there had also been aerial bombardments from Empire airships and magic that brought the same airships low. The landscape hadn't survived, changing from afternoon to afternoon.

"Did your king mention what he used to fight it?" he pressed Ignis for details. "Swords? Guns? Laser cannons? Cid claimed to have been there, but he didn't reveal much beyond the shell being harder than anything he had ever seen."

Ignis scratched his head, pondering the question. In the end, he spread his hands in helplessness. The king must have been as scarce on the particulars as the Hammerhead's owner. Still, a confirmation that the Adamantoise was more than a tall tale from a dusty old coot was welcome.

"Would I be wrong to call that turtle a legend?" he asked, leaning forward to look from face to face. "One that a king failed to slay, even. They told me that a single person could never take it on, but with…" He counted the heads. "...seven people, I'm confident we can give it a go."

That confused some among them, which worried him. People joked about meatheads, but if they couldn't even count to seven correctly then that was a recipe for disaster.

No, he'd just have to trust them. Maybe spar for a few rounds to get their measure. As for now, recruitment took priority.

He held up a hand in warning. "Don't expect easy money going in. I would have left it well alone until you came along, There is no reward here but glory and a share of the loot. It's turtle meat all the way down."

Around the table, expressions grew more eager as understanding began to dawn on each man. The economics of hunting monsters was simple. The small, annoying ones were paid for by a bounty, a big and mean fella paid for itself. Fame and fortune went hand in hand with legendary feats.

"Material from a creature like that..." Gladiolus mused, leaning back in his seat. "It does sound valuable. If the shell could be processed, it'll be something the Crownsguard might have an interest in."

He was just going to sell half the meat to Takka and keep half for himself, but hey, that sounded like a much better plan.

"Are we agreed, then?" Jaune said. "I'll open the floor for questions, not that there should be any—"

"Where's the turtle?" Noctis asked. He looked rather taken with the idea now, once the prospect of following in his father's footsteps came into play.

"I don't know. West."

The old car mechanic had apparently been bleeding out at the time, so who knew whether the information was accurate. During the intervening thirty years, that could expand to any point on the compass. They would have to bank on the rumbles of the earth, going where it was strongest.

Bennett went next, bouncing up and down in his seat. "Boss, how dangerous is this turtle?"

"Let me take it on the chin, and I'll get back to you."

As for the turtle's shell that might be harder than a dragon's hide, a good Huntsman wouldn't be aiming for the toughest part, would he? Eyes, mouths, throat, kidney. Some weaknesses were shared across many species.

"This feels very ill-thought-out."

Jaune pointed at the speaker, Ignis. "But?"

"...But we are desperate."

"I rest my case."

"You said west," Bennett again raised his voice. "How do we get to 'west'? It's a big desert."

Jaune turned to the others, and his assured smile dropped. "Welp, I'm stumped. Sorry, guys. Guess you're going broke."

"Ooh! Ooh!" Prompto jumped up, so that he stood on the booth's seat cushion. "I have an idea!"

Perfect. The plan was back on once more. "Let's hear it."

"Come on, follow me outside!"

The next minute saw a flurry of activity, with both Jaune's and Noctis's party paying their respective lunch bills and racing across the parking lot. Jaune didn't get why. There was not a means of transport in sight. They ended up surrounding a rather unimpressive parking meter that he hadn't paid attention to the whole time in this world, because in his mind it was just a part of the landscape. Prompto flourished his hands at the parking meter like it held all their answers.

"I need coins," the skinny blonde urged. "Turn out your pockets, dudes."

Gladiolus bent down to peer at the rusty meter. "Is this thing even in service?"

"Only one way to find out," Prompto said brightly.

Between the four men from Lucis, they coughed up three coins. All of the same amount, funnily enough, adding up to 15 Gils. Prompto read the faded sign on the meter.

"That puts us at… a third of one Chocobo. We need to rent six."

Jaune cocked an eyebrow. Was he about to learn what Chocobos were? They moved and they could be rented, and there was a parking meter in the picture.

He was going to guess motorbikes.

The rest of the funds, unsurprisingly, came from him. He was not quite so gung-ho about the sudden expenditure, but relented as people were always telling him he had to spend money to make money. Anyway, the prince promised to pay him back and if you couldn't trust a prince at his word, who could you trust in the world?

The coins entered the meter one by one, culminating with a twist of a dial. Crackling static noises then emitted from the meter, with none of them able to agree if that meant it worked or it had malfunctioned. Jaune tried giving the meter the go-to tech solution of a swift kick, just in case.

If anybody asked, the meter had always tilted on an angle.

After running for a while, the static sounds faded out. Then, it came back. Faded out again. Came back again.

"Should be any minute now," Prompto assured them.

Time rolled by, as did the tumbleweeds. Three cars sped past them, beating the hourly average. That was quite exciting—not. Beyond that, nothing else happened.

Sweat began to bead on everyone's brows, the heat here no joke. With each passing moment spent looking up and down the dusty desert road in awkward silence, more and more people began to turn toward Prompto, who shrank under their gazes.

"Aaany minute now."

"Two minutes," said Ignis, shading his eyes as he peered toward the horizon.

Everyone, Jaune included, immediately followed suit to try and spot what he was referring to. There seemed to be nothing there, an unending landscape of dry, cracked ground with the occasional shrubbery (and not very good ones, either).

The cloud of dust was the first sign. It began as a little pocket barely distinguishable from the surroundings, then ballooned up in size, marking the trail made by… something.

Jaune squinted, striving to make out the details through the haze of heat that seemed ever-present around these parts. He spied a figure, several figures, running in their direction. Their indistinct shapes soon coalesced into something recognizable, and Escha was suddenly at attention, grabbing fistfuls of Jaune's hair for balance as she stood up for a better view.

"Jaune, Jaune," she whispered, as he loudly coughed to drown out her words from the others. "I see dinner!"

"Are those… a bunch of giant chickens?" Bennett asked, very unsure.

"Chocobos incoming!" Prompto shouted with glee.

His words were a starting signal for his friends. Shedding all semblance of dignity, the four young men broke out into a sprint.

"Dibs on the blue one," Noctis called out, to immediate protests. "Royal privileges!"

"We do not recognize that at this time," Ignis answered, committing treason in one breath.

Jaune, left behind, was still all kinds of confused. They had been waiting for birds?

Birds with saddles. Bearing long necks and powerful legs, their appearances matched with the pictures he had seen of the ostrich hordes of Vacuo. One of them had a rider, who peeled off with a wave of their hand toward the group as the Chocobos drew nearer.

No, hang on, he was focusing on the wrong thing.

"Bennett."

"Yeah."

The four Lucians ran with all their might, trying to outdo each other. Jaune caught up, then overtook them in the span of seconds with Bennett matching pace, arms and legs pumping as they put their enhanced bodies to work in winning this race. Because all men were boys, and pride was on the line.

Bennett managed to grab the blue one coveted by everybody, while Jaune settled for one of the yellow birds, swinging up onto the saddle. The bird helped him along, making up for his amateurish movements by dipping its body to catch him. They were big, bigger than ostriches, and with plumage softer than pillows that his hands sank into.

A sudden hop by his mount caused him to wrap his arms around the bird's neck to catch his balance, putting him next to the most expressive eyes he had ever seen on an animal. The Chocobo trilled in his ear.

"Kweh!"

"Well, hello to you too."

Escha jumped off of his shoulders, landing on the Chocobo's head with an absolutely feral expression on her kitty face. She held back from attacking the bird, though, glancing around at the way everyone was climbing on a mount. A tentative sniff at the Chocobo, and she eventually chose to spare it for the time being. One did not kill one's own horse.

In no time, each person there had a Chocobo to call his own. The birds never broke stride, banking to one side as a pack until their riders faced the direction of the blazing afternoon sun.

"West!" Noctis cried, pulling on the reins, his Chocobo rearing up high. "We journey to the west!"

With whoops and shouts, the prince and all his men together went racing across the land, on a quest for the elusive turtle in its shell.
