#9,084

Chapter 92: Seeking the Beast in Its Lair
​

Chocobos made for powerful runners. Nothing on a motorcycle, of course, especially one driven by the speed demon Kiwi, but the off-road experience on the back of a big yellow bird was like nothing else. They glided over the rough terrain of the Leide desert region as if it was a straight runaway, smooth of gait. The rhythmic thump, thump of the Chocobo's feet grew on Jaune until it felt as natural as the wind in his hair and the sun on his skin. In no time at all, the party left the Hammerhead service station far, far behind, diving into the endless expanse before their eyes without looking back.

The act of riding itself took little training. The ostrich-birds did the bulk of the heavy lifting. They were more intelligent than their dopey faces suggest, paying special care to the comfort of their riders. As a result, Jaune became an experienced hand at it by the tenth minute. Go, slow, left, right, jump, and 'Kweh!'—he learned how to tug on the reins to enact all the essential commands for his mount, enough to put up a good showing in a friendly race against the others.

He might have won, too, but…

No kicking people off their Chocobo! No throwing items at the riders! No laying down food to bait the other birds to stop!

One unfair rule after the next constrained him, until the contest was lost. Oh, woe was Jaune Arc.

It couldn't be all fun and games, though. Their whole group refocused on the task at hand once they experienced the first earthquake of the day, a soft rumble that swept across the land from the south to startle the Chocobos and sent Escha curling into a ball on Jaune's lap. It served as a cold reminder that half of them were in dire straits and the other half had a hankering for turtle soup. The mission reaffirmed, they adjusted their course southward and rolled into a place called the Longwythe Rest Area not long after to seek information.

The outpost sat at a spot where two long desert roads intersect, and saw a marginal increase in traffic as a result. With an old motel on one side for the travelers ready to call it a day, and a gas station and a diner on the other for the ones still on the move, it provided enough of a draw to even be considered bustling. All the busier, with the commotion raised by a pack of squawking Chocobos as they made a beeline toward a water trough resting in the motel's parking lot.

'Only 4 Birbs', the sign above the trough proclaimed. For the life of him, Jaune could not tell whether this was a numbers limit or a warning to stop some thirsty soul deciding they would stick their mouth in the drink without boiling it, animal diseases be damned. The first possibility seemed too arbitrary, while common sense would have surely forestalled the second possibility from occurring.

Anyway, the exhausted Chocobos couldn't read, but they understood the setup well. They dove their beaks into the trough to greedily gulp down the content as their riders hopped out of the saddles. Some among the birds were already tapping on the feed dispenser sitting nearby that required money to operate, and Jaune had the sneaking suspicion that this was how the business really made its money.

"Hey, there's a Crow's Nest!" exclaimed Prompto, pointing to the diner on the other side of the road.

"We just ate," Ignis reminded him.

"I know, but Noct is gonna want a picture with the mascot." Prompto nudged the person next to him. "Right, buddy?"

The young man in question crossed his arms, looking away. "I mean, if we have time. Not that it matters."

Nobody was fooled by the cool act.

"Business first, pleasure second," Ignis said, a sentiment that earned a firm nod from Gladiolus and, after a beat, a far more reluctant one from the prince. Their last member thus fell in line.

At a small remove from the quartet, Jaune, Escha, and Bennett climbed off their Chocobos. Well, he and Escha climbed while Bennett fell, rolled to recover, tripped, fell and had to roll again, then finally stuck a 10-point perfect landing that would have made gymnastics judges weep. As his feet hit the ground, Jaune laced his fingers together and stretched his hands to the sky.

"Maaan, that was great. It's nice to hang out with just the guys, sometimes."

"But I'm a girl!" Escha protested at once.

"You're a cat."

"Cats can be boys or girls. Hmph!"

He had no good response to that, and so resorted to ear scritches to distract the felyne. "They sure can, Escha. They sure can," he said while casting his gaze around the rest area.

The first thing to draw his eyes were some of the tables and plastic chairs laid out on the motel veranda. They had fallen on their sides, not yet picked up like the ones in use by guests. Calling out to the prince and his retinue, he directed their attention to the sight.

"This place definitely felt the earlier quake," he said, before looking toward Ignis. "You have a map, right? Mark down the spot where we got hit, then we'll ask around for the direction that people here think it came from. We might be able to work out its location if we have more, what's the word…"

"Reference points?"

"Exactly. We'll triangle that turtle."

"Triangulate."

"Good man. We'll do that, too." He looked over the group. "Let's split up to cover more ground—"

""""Dibs on diner!""" shouted most of the people there, the more responsible Ignis and Gladiolus included. Which left Jaune wondering.

"...But why? You don't even have money." He shook his head. "Oh, whatever. You guys can take the diner if you also check in at the gas station. My side will look into the motel."

The deal was struck without protest. As the four young men sprinted toward the mascot statue of a crow in front of the diner, camera in Prompto's hand, Jaune's group peeled off toward the building that hosted the Chocobos' water trough. Old and faded, it must have been here for a long time, with signs of many repairs. As far as people to interview went, it provided slim pickings with only two guests hanging out on the long veranda in front of the rooms. Of the two, he settled on the one not obviously drunk off their gourds, and perhaps might even have been present the first time the turtle reared its head.

"Hello there, ma'am!" he said brightly, walking over to a hunched figure in a dress sitting at a table set against the wall, their back to him.

The person gave no response, seeming to not have heard his greeting.

"Ma'am?" Jaune asked, a little more uncertain. "Old woman in the plastic chair? Hi. Can you spare some time?"

"Jaune, could she have been hurt by the earthquake? She might need help!" Bennett said urgently.

Before they could check, the person stirred. They cocked their head as if finally realizing that Jaune was talking to them, and shifted in their seat in order to turn around.

"Oh yes," they said. "That's going to make me want to talk to you, calling me old and a woman."

Jaune's smile slipped. "Ah, that was a coat, not a dress. You're… a man. Sorry. From this angle, I couldn't tell."

Below, Escha covered her face and muttered something about him now mixing up the humans, too. He ignored her for the moment, because in this world only crazy people acknowledged a talking cat.

"Are you implying something about my figure?" the stranger replied, then rubbed a hand over his stubbled jaw. "And do I really look that old? I understand that my complexion is far from its best, but I like to think that I give off a spry image for my age."

"You look fabulous," Jaune hastily assured the old— the young— the man, and spared a quick glance over the thick layers of the man's ensemble that spelled a death sentence in this heat. "Nice coat. Great hat. It's very 'in' this season." As if he would know. "Can I ask you a question?"

"Was that not one just now?"

Jaune recoiled, suddenly recognizing the man for what he was. One of those individuals that insisted upon the minor grammar rules, because they took joy in inconveniencing a conversation with the casual speakers. Language teachers, some called them.

He resisted the urge to roll his eyes, the natural response when encountering this species, and instead dragged Bennett in front of him. "Then, can he ask you a question?"

Bennett waved hello, showing an earnest face that only a monster would take offense with.

"...Well played," the man praised, the twisted desire to dot every t's and cross every i's or however it went now satisfied. Jaune carefully hid his bucketful of smug behind a polite demeanor. "Why not? I have all the time in the world. Ask away, young man."

Put on the spot, Bennett hesitated. His gaze darted to Jaune, who showed a thumbs-up in encouragement, then back to the stranger.

"Um, did you happen to feel an earthquake about an hour ago?" he asked.

"I did. Oh, it was awful." The man wrapped his arms around himself. "Had me shaking in my boots, it did." His tone suggested otherwise, sounding eager to spread gossip more than anything else. "I think someone next to me died during the confusion. Vanished into thin air!"

Jaune very much doubted that, but let it go. He leaned down to whisper in Bennett's ear, the other boy relaying his words.

"Can you remember which direction it started from?"

"Seemed like everywhere… But if I have to say it, it'll be… north." The man held his chin, putting on a curious air. "Are you hoping to do something about it?"

"With luck, yes," Jaune said, nodding.

Next to him, Bennett copied his words and gestures.

"You don't have to do that anymore," Jaune said to him. "I think we've moved past it by this point."

"You don't have to do that anymore—"

Jaune poked Bennett in the side, causing the ticklish boy to burst out in an instinctive laugh. He turned back to the stranger. "We have reason to believe that it isn't a natural event. Speaking of, were you in the area a few decades ago?"

The man blankly stared up at Jaune. "...Who wants to know?"

Well, that was not at all suspicious.

"Me? I want to know? I'm searching for something called an adamantoise. Have you heard of it?"

Are you a turtle worshiper? Are you!? That was pretty much his thinking with how off the man acted. It wouldn't be the first time he stumbled across somebody who believed in a lizard as a god with the intention of feeding him to it.

His suspicions appeared misplaced, as the man regained his cheery demeanor. "That old story is still around?" the man asked. "How delightful! I remember people used to tell their children of the great and terrible adamantoise. That it would obliterate the city if the child did not eat their vegetables."

"That… That sounds a little harsh, don't you think?"

"It builds good character."

If skittish and paranoid could be considered good character, sure. He moved on from the tangent, continuing to ask a couple more follow-up questions. Still, it grew clearer to him the further it went on that this man knew little of the turtle beyond hearsay. In the end, he brought the conversation to a close without learning much else, bidding farewell.

The stranger cheerfully waved after him as he departed. "Do come back soon. And bring that broody fellow with you next time!"

Huh. It turned out that the man was an avid royalist. Noctis would be so embarrassed to find out he had more fans, thereby guaranteeing that it was one of the first things Jaune brought up once everybody eventually reconvened by the diner.

"I'm supposed to be incognito," the prince complained as he and the rest of the party stood around a map spread on an outdoor table. "Humble and, and, one of the people!"

He supposed it fit with how the prince had not simply ordered a random bystander to fork over money for the royal coffers. In addition, that would explain the disguise.

"I'm afraid to ask, but what disguise?" said Noctis after hearing Jaune mention it aloud.

"You know, that boy band concept you have going. It really is brilliant. You're a natural at it. I bet most people would never take you for a prince!"

On the other side of the table, Prompto grimaced. "Friggin' oof, dude. Gladi-man, does that count as an attack on the royal personage? Because our Noct looks very attacked right now."

"We've told you, we are not a boy band," Gladiolus growled at Jaune… while leaning back on a barrel in a way that highlighted the curves of his muscles and the sweat beading on his arms, looking like an album cover. Jaune thus placed no weight on his words, giving the bodyguard his best 'I am not convinced' look. He had eyes, thank you.

Off to the side of the convo, Ignis pored over the map. His marker darted back and forth, drawing lines and angles and muttering about margin of error, whatever sciency concept that was, as Bennett watched on in rapt attention. The man seemed to appreciate a listening audience, explaining his thought process step by step.

"Many of the people we spoke to were too disoriented by the earthquake to determine its direction, but general consensus among those that kept a cool head points to it beginning in the north." He tapped the points on the map for Bennett's benefit. "Over here is Hammerhead station. There, our position earlier today. And here is this rest stop. The first told us that it came from the west, we felt it was more south, and now we have learned that it is north. They are inexact approximates, but…"

"We can still narrow the search area down because of it?" Bennett guessed, earning an approving nod from the older man.

"Precisely. Testimonies suggest that this area experienced stronger and more frequent shocks than our other data points, so we can assume that the epicenter of these incidents lies closer to here than elsewhere." The marker traced a circle. "Thus, a picture takes shape."

The rest of them put their bickering on hold to huddle in, looking at the spot that Ignis marked.

"The quarry we seek is hiding in the vicinity of Longwythe Peak," Ignis concluded.

Prompto was over the moon. "Oh sweet, we can get a picture of the mountain while we're there!"


-o-
​

"This is taking foreveeeer," Prompto whined.

The skinny blond drudged to the edge of the shallow pool of water, flopping down at its edge. His hands dipped into the lukewarm pond, splashing it onto his face to wash away the dirt and grime accumulated over the past hour. Beside him, Jaune was doing the same. The awful heat of the desert sun all but cooked them alive. Not far from them, Chocobos frolicked and played without a care.

Sitting on a boulder, Gladiolus sipped at a water bottle. "Are you certain that we are in the right area?"

Rather than Ignis, it was Jaune that answered him. "Oh yeah, it's around here, alright." He raised his head, blond hair in need of a cut plastering to his face due to the water, to scan their surroundings. "I've been getting a bad feeling for a while now."

Like blaring alarms popping off in his thoughts, like a twisted knot in his guts. The throbbing behind the temples everybody felt at some point in their life that drew on senses beyond the conventional to insist they watch their back. It had grown loud and unceasing ever since they started searching around Longwythe Peak, a rocky mountain not far from the rest stop that jutted out over the landscape at an angle making it look like it was tipping to one side. The barren and gray locale held little of interest beyond the wildlife and this small watering hole where the creatures went to quench their thirst. Of the adamantoise, there had been no signs, not even a set of footprints for the party to follow. The only constant thing that could be called a clue was his every instinct lighting up in warning.

As if on cue, the ground rumbled. Jaune's legs almost gave out as he felt the ground shake, felt it quake. The rest of the group fared no better, the force of these tremors surpassing the last occurrence by manifolds. Around them, birds that had gathered at the oasis all took flight, while the land-based species ran for their lives. The earth split open in deep gashes identical to ones that the party had discovered all over the land during their search of the area, and which had wreaked destruction on animal habitats and roads alike.

Something was so very wrong here. Where could that turtle be hiding?

The answer struck him like a bolt from the blue. His hand rose on its own, index finger pointing ahead.

"There," he said. "There."

Bennett, Escha, the prince and his men, everyone whirled toward the place he indicated with their weapons in their grasp. Confusion overtook them, and their stances faltered as they saw nothing out of the ordinary. How sly, their prey. Hiding in plain sight.

Jaune peeled back the curtains for their sake. "Turtles live near water. That rock by the pond, doesn't it seem a little suspicious? Like something under it could poke its head out when nobody is looking to drink and feed?"

He was referring to a big, flat slab of stone not far from them that sat right next to the water's edge. Its surface curved in a gentle slope, forming a natural platform where animals at the oasis could lie down for a rest.

Or perhaps, one could say it resembled a turtle's shell.

As he came to the end of his conjectures, all the people there scrambled into a formation. It looked rough as Jaune's side and the prince's had no experience working together, but they made it work by being of one mind on taking his words seriously and giving their target no chances to play tricks. Honor and glory (and a big payday) was on the line.

"What's our plan, Jaune?" Bennett asked, standing firmly at the front of the group alongside Jaune and Gladiolus, their shields forming a bulwark.

"Well—"

"The shell is almost indestructible, it's said," Ignis cautioned from behind them. "We would be fools to think we can end it in one blow. I suggest instead that we raise it from its position, thereby revealing the softer parts beneath."

"I'm open to ideas on how," Jaune said. His sword swapped for a baton-like stick colored in red, the impossible sleight of hand drawing exclamations from those around him. "Got dynamite if we need them."

"Was that magic? How did you—No, we can get to that later," Ignis decided. "You have given me an idea. Noct, your magic flask is filled. Dualcast Fire, I believe?"

"Yeah, got it right here," Noctis replied, hurrying to take out an object stowed in his pockets. Head turning, Jaune zeroed in on the glass sphere, paying close attention to the swirling concoction within. More air than fluid, it glowed with an intense light.

His hand twitched. It looked shiny, which meant it might fetch a pretty sum on a certain otherworldly marketplace.

"Perfect," Ignis said, oblivious to Jaune's fierce mental calculations (big lootz = big money, bigger lootz = bigger money). "Its potency should outmatch conventional explosives. Let us see how well that shell disperses heat." He thumped the prince on the back. "Seeing as your father was the one to fight it last, I can think of none better to ring in the second round. Fire in the hole!"

Noctis wound back his arm, and let fly the glass sphere. It arced through the air with a gentle grace, at its zenith catching the light of the sun to blaze in a multitude of colors shimmering with a mysterious beauty. This sight lasted no longer than three heartbeats, and the inevitable shattering as it struck hard stone raised an ugly sensation in Jaune's chest akin to watching a work of art set aflame. At the same time, a thrumming beat grew within him in anticipation of what was to come.

From a small glass orb, a conflagration engulfed the entire rock, springing up far higher and wider than seemed possible for something that size. Even at a remove, heat licked at Jaune's skin, the shield in his hand growing warm. As Escha hid behind his leg to stave off the high temperature, he watched with a careful eye for a response from their target. Thus far, it was content to sit in place.

"We're going to look so silly if that turns out to be a normal rock," Prompto pointed out what most of them had been thinking.

"Patience, now," Jaune advised. "Give the fire time to do its work. My gut says we're on the right track."

It actually said that he was on track to die, screaming to him of danger and death. The bad feeling that stayed with him all this while had never let up, growing past the level where he could call it natural.

He had definitely felt this sensation before, but where…

Another earthquake broke the moment. Jaune and the others braced themselves, waiting for it to subside.

Yet, it never did.

"It's here!" Ignis called out. "You were right!"

"Get ready, men!" Gladiolus shouted from beside Jaune. The man wore a delighted expression on his face, all grinning teeth. One that likely mirrored Jaune's and everyone else here, eager for a rousing fight and their names written in the annals of history, for full bellies and fuller wallets. Their time was now, and let none say different.

The hard-packed desert ground cracked in spiderweb patterns, the lines spreading further with the passing seconds. The members of the party adjusted their positions to accommodate this new terrain, light on their feet ready to spring forward in action.

The flat slab of stone had begun to shift from side to side, giving up the pretense of an inanimate nature. The motion was somewhat reminiscent of a dog trying to shake off water. With a sharp crack, the rock separated from the earth.

It was here, it was here, the adamantoise of myth and legend, and as the flames began to die down, it rose.

And… And it rose.

And it rose.

And it rose.

And it rose.

And it rose. And it rose. And it rose. And it rose. AND IT—

Jaune gulped.

"Dear sweet mother," Gladiolus breathed out. Ignis grabbed the man by the shoulder for balance, leaning forward with his glasses slipping down his nose.

"That… was not the shell."

It was a horn. A horn that went on a nose. A nose on a head that still had not completely surfaced yet. These details registered to Jaune's mind in pieces that he could digest, but every time he tried to connect them the image fizzled out to leave him heaving for breath. Some things simply defied belief, even as it stood before his very eyes. Just the turtle's head was bigger than the Grimm dragon attacking Beacon.

Then, what about the body?

He wished that thought hadn't occurred to him.

Part of the turtle's neck had emerged aboveground, dirt pouring aside to reveal bony ridges. Jaune traced those ridges, turning his body to keep following the long neck. Then, his gaze moved up, up, up… to Longwythe Peak.

The mountain moved.

The turtle moved.

"This is ridiculous!" said Prompto, nearly squeaking.

Absentmindedly, Jaune said, "So the mountain was the shell. How about that. Oh look, I can see the flippers now. It's a sea turtle."

"Y-You're not letting this faze you, huh, boss?" Bennett stammered.

"Eh, I've seen bigger."

No. No, he hadn't. This nonsense was the shock doing the talking. He still could not accept the adamantoise as a whole, his eyes able to only concentrate on one spot at a time. Any more and the form of the turtle would start to blur, registering as 'landscape' or 'geographic feature' to him. Its head, as it moved, cleared the height of a five-story building in one swoop.

"What do we do?"

Jaune could not tell who said it. It could have been all of them. What he did know was that everybody looked at him afterward for an answer, counting on him to be their guide in this unfamiliar place.

That brought the world back into focus. Under their gazes, he lifted up his hand, vanishing the stick of dynamite to leave it empty. His palm then impacted his cheek.

Tap. Tap. His vision cleared.

"Okay," he said. "O-kay. Let's break it down. We're here to hunt the source of the earthquakes. It's right in front of us. And as we all know, turtles are cool and calm. If attacked, they might just sit there and take it."

With a gesture, the handle of a sword fell into his grip. He fought back the sense of dread and alarm that refused to stay quiet, forcing it into a little mental box so he could think. In its absence, the answer that arrived to him was one simple course of action.

"I say we go for it. Charge!"

His command seized the hearts of his companions, and they brandished their weapons.

""Chaaarge!"" shouted every throat and voice as these brave men (and a cat) raced toward the undefended underside of the turtle's neck. Jaune's sword was the first to bite into flesh, followed by many more.

Snick.

Snick. Snick. Snick. Snick. Snick. Snick. Snick. Snick.

"I don't think this is working. It's like we're poking it with toothpicks."

"Did it even notice that we're here?"

As if to respond, the turtle raised an immense flipper up high.

"It noticed! It noticed! That is not cool and calm!"

The flipper moved in a casual and deceptively slow fashion, an untold number of tons of force behind the motion. The shadow it cast turned day into night, covering the span of a city block and engulfing the entirety of Jaune's vision.

Beside him, Bennett lifted his shield.

"Yeah, no," said Jaune, grabbing the boy by the back of his shirt collar and yanking him away. "So, for something like this that can swallow you whole, blocking usually isn't the way to go."

"But all I've done this week was learn to block!"

"That's the way it works. You think you're making progress, then life throws a wrench your way. Now, beat feet and fucking ruuuun!"

Jaune led the party in running for their lives as the wind picked up around them, air pressure formed from the adamantoise pressing down with its flipper. He leapt astride his Chocobo, and the creature needed no prompting to break into a sprint. Around him, the other birds joined the escape with their riders clinging to their backs.

Sunlight returned as they raced past the shadow's edge in the nick of time, right at the moment the flipper obliterated the area behind them with an almighty crash that shook the landscape and sent every Chocobo stumbling. A wave of dust and dirt slammed into the party from behind, carrying them off their feet to throw men, birds, and cat across the desert ground. The Chocobos barely landed on their feet, screaming their panicked kweh's in Jaune's ears.

"Keep running!" Jaune ordered his Chocobo, before turning his head to address Noctis. "Seriously, did your dad have a laser cannon? How did he fight this thing!?"

"He had magic!"

"You have magic!"

"Not his magic!"

"What's your magic!?"

"Incomiiing!" Ignis warned.

The adamantoise pushed forward with its flippers, a mountain moving across the land. Its long neck stretched out, thickly armored chin aiming for the gnats that had disturbed its day. Screaming bloody murder, the insects peeled off to either side as the turtle's head met the earth in a calamitous quake.

"We're all gonna die!" Prompto cried.

"Not if I have anything to say about it," Jaune called back. "Watch my ultimate move! Escha, take the reins!"

"Mrow?"

Jaune kicked off the Chocobo, and as it cleared the space below him, he engaged his rocket boots while summoning his wind glider. The wings unfurled, and the colors of an early morning sky greeted the world, gracefully cutting through the air. In scant seconds, he had shot above the turtle's head.

His empty hand formed the shape of a finger gun. In a blink, a boulder stained red appeared at the very tip. The big rock immediately fell in a straight line down, and though this might be his imagination, it seemed to move just a touch faster than it should. Like it was eager to mete out death.

The rock struck the turtle right atop its head.

Plink!

His ultimate move had been about as effective as a pebble. Wonderful.

For an brief moment, his eyes met one of the turtle's own positioned on the side of its head. The warning blares dwelling inside him swelled to a crescendo. There was something behind that gaze… behind that gaze?…staring back. The turtle opened its mouth, and let out a long cry that sounded almost mournful.

And then it swung its head at him. Jaune blinked, shaking off the stupor. A blast of rocketfire launched him out of the turtle's way, dipping below to retrieve his falling boulder.

After that, he reversed course, catching up to the others to land back on his Chocobo. He looked directly ahead, refusing to meet the flat stares coming at him from every direction, even from the people ahead who had to turn to look at him.

"Some 'ultimate move'. What the hell was with that rock? Are you a cultist or something!?" Noctis called over from off to his left.

"Less talky, more fighty," Jaune shot back.

Taking it as a challenge, Noctis whipped his hand behind himself and with it another glass sphere crackling with power flew toward the turtle. "Dualcast Fire!" shouted the prince.

Before the magical device could even do anything, the adamantoise spat out a glob of saliva big enough to fill a swimming pool, dousing the flames to leave Noctis wearing a stiff expression with his arm still outstretched.

"Turtle - one, prince - zero."

"I don't need this right now, Prompto. Delete that picture."

Prompto hid his camera, pretending to misheard the command. The scene would have been heartwarming, resembling a normal everyday conversation if not for the gargantuan moving mountain that was seconds away from flattening them at any given moment. Their speed was not the problem. Each lunge by the turtle ate up all the distance made by the madly running Chocobos, such was its size. A mere shuffle of its body matched their best efforts.

It was quickly becoming apparent that they could never run forever. Escaping just was not in the cards. What was left?

Cunning, for one.

"Everyone, bank right," Ignis ordered. "Make for that hill."

None of them questioned it, trusting in the shrewd man to have a plan. He explained it to them along the way.

"A turtle is at its most helpless when flipped on its back. We must unbalance the creature with every means at our disposal. The first step is to lure it onto a slope."

The Chocobos hit the barren hill, and scrambled up it. They were good jumpers in addition to running, clearing the obstacle in a blink to fall down the other side. On the back of his bird, Jaune twisted around to watch what the adamantoise would do.

Met with the hill, the turtle blasted right on through, stomping it beneath its bulk to turn the hill into a valley.

In the ensuing silence between the party, Ignis coughed into his hand. "Right, yes. I should note that a moving mountain likely could only be flipped by a bigger mountain."

"Is there one?" Jaune asked without much hope.

"In the next continent over, perhaps. It will take a two weeks of running."

A logically sound idea. In practical terms, not so great. "Put a pin on it. I've got a better plan."

"Do we die? Is this the part where we die?" Prompto asked, voice cracking.

"No," said Jaune. "It's the part where we make like rabbits and go for the kill!"

"Hah?"

Undeterred, Jaune continued. "We go high. We hit it where it hurts, and I've never seen anybody take it in the eye and not cry like a baby! Besides me, obviously." This aside was followed by similar proclamations from each man present. "If one blow won't take it down, then we'll give it a hundred little bites to tear it to pieces! Come on!"

This time when he jumped off the Chocobo, he took Escha with him. The felyne slapped the bird on the rump to make it keep running, ensuring its life and cutting off their own retreat in one fell stroke. Together, they took to the air in front of the turtle.

Seeking to draw the creature's attention, Jaune summoned a stubby machinegun painted in garish Night City gang colors. Among the lighter firearms in his possession, the effect of its weight on his glider was minimal. He carelessly aimed it in the turtle's direction with the confidence that he could not possibly miss a target that large, and squeezed the trigger to pepper the creature with bullets.

It felt it, he was sure. In the way a person would feel a mosquito's bite. The turtle jerked its head back and forth in an effort to dispel the source of the irritation, unaware that it was Jaune. At least, at first. It slowed down its course, the long trail of destruction behind it coming to a brief halt.

Then, it caught sight of him, and ooh did it get mad. The turtle released another cry, and this time it was all anger. Jaune used the opportunity to close the distance.

"Ready, Escha?"

Escha saluted him. "Aye, aye!"

Climbing onto his back, the felyne curled into a little ball, awaiting his signal. The instant they were above the turtle, Jaune gave it. The glider vanished from his back, and the pair dropped out of the sky, shouting their thrill as the wind rushed through their hair.

3, 2, 1. Jaune kicked out his rocket boots to slow their descent, landing them on the very top of the turtle's head. Neither wasted a moment, and bullets shot out at an immense eyeball while a cat broke out a pair of hammer and chisel—a Palico's bread and butter when it came to snapping off a monster's outer scales. She soon found a chip in the turtle's skin, and got to work.

The bullets tore into the eye, sinking into softened flesh that was yet tougher than a human's bones. It had a real effect, however, sending the turtle into a roaring rage. Jaune and Escha clung on as the creature thrashed its head about, finding safety in the gap between the rocky ridges.

"I feel like I'm going to be sick," he groaned as they whipped from one side to the other.

"Not on me, not on me!"

In the throes of nausea, Jaune caught a glimpse of figures dressed in black, alongside another in red, making the climb up one of the turtle's flippers. Realizing that the Lucians were following his lead, a smile broke out on his face.

These maniacs. They were his people, Huntsmen through and through.

As the turtle's struggles subsided, he left Escha to her task and sprang forward, stomping over the uneven terrain that was the adamantoise's face on a course for the injured eye.

Halfway there, a dark figure materialized right in front of him. Teleporting in. As naturally as breathing, Jaune summoned and swept his sword in a wide arc.

Clang! His blade met another, a strange sword whose crossguard clicked and whirled with the moving parts of a machine mechanism, purring like an engine. It ticked off every criteria for something Jaune wanted to grab, except for the pale face of Noctis staring back at him with wide eyes.

"What was that for?" the prince yelped, grunting with the effort of holding back the attack.

Jaune withdrew his sword. "Oops. You never told me you were one of them."

"One of who?"

"Them." The footing beneath them shifted, serving as a warning. "Whoa, hold that thought and hang on tight."

Jaune and the prince clung to the turtle as it went into another of its thrashing frenzy. This latest one saw shapes falling off the mountain on its back, wildlife that had made their lairs upon the shell believing it mere immobile stone. Some fell near where the rest of the group had hunkered down, necessitating a frantic fight in close quarters. He got a good look at the species once one landed on the turtle's neck, it looking like a leopard with unbelievably long whiskers.

It spotted them at the same time they spotted it. Then it died as Noctis, flinging his sword, zipped behind it to drive the sword that he just caught again right to the back of its neck.

Jaune whistled, giving the prince a thumbs-up as he looked back this way. Noctis nodded with a smile, and in a blink stood next to him again.

Teleporters were rather dependable when on his side.

As Noctis went to provide support for the rest of their group below, Jaune advanced on the eye. The turtle saw him coming, knew what he intended, but for all its efforts could not dislodge him. A gargantuan size carried its own weakness, and that eye was a direct route to the weakest point of a living creature. The brain.

He reached the eye at the same time that Noctis returned. The prince held something beside his sword in his hand, which Jaune recognized as Prompto's camera.

"Smile," said the prince, turning the camera to catch both him, Jaune, and the turtle's eye in view. By reflex, Jaune put up a V sign and grinned.

Click!

The turtle winced, head jerking to the side and nearly throwing them both off.

"Sorry. Prompto insisted." The prince hung the camera strap around his neck, and retrieved his sword. Watching the blade pop out of nowhere into his hand was quite a disorienting experience, since Jaune was used to that being his trick.

Still, he recovered quickly. There were more important things at stake. His scroll snapped to his hand, and he flicked the screen open.

"Smile," he said, before taking a selfie of the scene from the opposite angle. "Good pose. You're a natural," he complimented the prince.

Lisa was going to flip once she saw this.

Then, with a twirl of Crocea Mors, he jammed the blade deep into the turtle's eye. As it roared, he popped the scroll into his Pocket, using the free hand to grip onto the ridge that encircled the giant eye. Thus kept in place, he pulled back his sword to stab again.

"This is so disgusting," said Noctis as he followed suit, needing to shout over the turtle and even then sounding tiny. "If that eye pops, I'm gonna hurl."

More of the leopards had landed on the long turtle neck. Maybe they sensed that Jaune and Noctis were doing something that could get them all killed, because they raced toward the pair. Escha threw a boomerang to forestall the first, buying time for Noctis to join the fray.

Jaune, meanwhile, continued his bloody work, elbow-deep in the sickening gel of the eye. He doubted the turtle could still see him by this point, but it knew he was there by the pain inflicted upon it.

It roared, it thrashed. He hung on like a gnat. In the process, he noticed an incongruity.

The turtle sometimes flinched even when his sword did not touch the eye. It screeched to an agony he had no hand in. And this phantom pain led it to struggle all the harder.

But he could not let up to investigate.

"Almost there, almost there," he chanted to himself as a mantra. The disgusting mess he left in his endeavor to drive the sword into the turtle's brain would be an experience that stuck to him forever, he was certain. "Almost there, almost the—"

The world tilted.

He moved so fast that his stomach could not take it, emptying out in hacking coughs. Once he recovered enough to see past the tears, he found a wholly different view from previous, the turtle having contorted its neck in a near U-shape. Perched on various places atop this neck, the rest of his party flattened themselves to the hard scales as they tried to figure out what the creature was doing. The animals they had been fighting did not fare as well, falling off during the commotion.

And then, with a sound akin to a whip magnified by a thousand times, the only thing left in Jaune's vision was the bright blue sky. He heard screams around him, over the wind. The yowling of a cat, and his own shouts.

He seemed to hang weightless in the sky without support of any kind, his grip on the turtle now grasping the empty air. His mind was still catching up, putting these clues together.

His body gently turned. He found the mountain, the turtle with ease. It laid far, far below.

Which necessitated that he was high, high above. The turtle had succeeded in throwing them all off of itself, way up there in the sky.

A sword flashed by, with Noctis appearing out of thin air to grab it a split second later. The prince shoved a passenger, Escha, into his arms then reached out to clutch at his jacket.

"F-Fly!"

"Say that again?" Jaune found his voice, and it sounded almost casual with none of the prince's tension. His fingers ran through Escha's fur in soothing strokes. After all, he…

"You can fly, right? Help me get the others to safety!"

Yep, that. And a rescue would be the next step, since not everyone enjoyed the benefit of surviving from this height. His eyes rolled in their sockets, quickly pinpointing where each person was.

He stretched out a hand, grabbing onto Noctis in turn to pull him close. "I can slow their falls, nothing else. Your teleportation will have to cover the final stretch." With a nod from Noctis, he continued. "Get to Bennett, he has a glider like mine on him."

In the space of a blink, the prince vanished to carry on the message while Jaune got to work.

He picked out the person closest to hitting the ground, Ignis, then chose the next person in line, Gladiolus. Sure enough, as he put on his glider and dove for his target, Noctis teleported next to Ignis. The pair then disappeared together. That was one person accounted for.

Jaune formed his body in a ramrod straight line, and engaged the rockets in his boots to shoot down at an eye-watering speed. A light twist spun him out of the way as Bennett glided past, and the two boys gestured at each other in acknowledgment before continuing on to their respective targets. Escha waved after the other boy, her panic having faded to nothing now that she knew she would be okay.

Timing it, he drew level with Gladiolus. The man was not screaming, which Jaune considered mildly impressive given his imminent demise.

"'Sup?" the man said, as if they had run into one another on the city street.

With good humor, Jaune matched him in tone. "Yo. Jaune's Rescue Service, here to un-doom your butt."

"Thanks, but you just keep those hands above the waist."

Jaune rolled his eyes, and seized the man by his forearms. His glider had no hope of carrying this amount of weight, so he worked on gradually flattening out, catching as much wind as the wings could get to hold them aloft for a second longer. They had lost a lot of height by now, with him able to spot Ignis way down there safe and sound, then the forms of Noctis and Prompto as they joined him. The prince released his charge, who flopped on the ground, and whirled around to frantically search the sky. He found Jaune's group not long after, and with a series of sword-flinging motions climbed the air toward them.

The haggard look told of a cost to these repeated teleports, but the prince did not let up. After Jaune passed Gladiolus over, Noctis went right back to tracing a zigzagging path to the ground, bleeding off the momentum of his friend to ensure a survivable impact. Jaune followed them down, circling around them on alert for a slip.

A needless worry, as they were soon landing to the whoops and cries of those already rescued, with Noctis slumping against Prompto, huffing and puffing to catch his breath. With Bennett joining them, that was seven for seven alive with all limbs intact. A bystander would mistake them for having won a mountain of treasures.

It, honestly, had started to become fun. An exhilarating experience they could find nowhere else.

Still, how the hell were they going to bring this turtle down?

After the wave of celebration, Jaune and the others stood in a line, staring up at the turtle and looking rather lost. Because oh my word, was it big and impossible and intimidating in a way that defied thought. Unstoppable, was the term that came to mind along with a small, niggling worry. What had they unleashed?

"Ah, well. Back to work, boys," Jaune said, stepping forward.

Someone had to kill that thing. The others understood that, too. Groaning and sighing, they drudged after him. A good enough crew, in his books. Between a few warriors, a teleporter, and a cat, what more did he need?

Besides a bigger gun, of course. With a gesture, he swapped out his sword for the gunlance.

Somehow, that sparked another commotion.

"Okay, so my eyes aren't playing tricks on me," said Gladiolus. "Are you and Noct… related? Why are you using Lucis royal magic?"

Ignis elbowed him, speaking quietly in a hurry. "Shush. Do you have a death wish? You know the family tree. If you say they're related, what are you implying about our king?"

Noctis, having caught all of that, grew pale as a sheet. Jerkily, he turned his head toward Jaune, pleading with his gaze.

"It's a coincidence," Jaune said. "Don't look at me like that."

Prompto leaned over, whispering in his ear. "Bro, that sounds suspicious as hell. Can you come up with a better answer? Our Noct's gonna cry."

"I won't cry, you prick."

"Guys," Bennett cut in. "Can we, I don't know, figure out what we're going to do about the turtle first? It keeps staring at us and that's starting to scare me."

Jaune furrowed his brow at that, and observed the adamantoise with careful scrutiny. "Why is it staring at us? From there to here is, what, two lunges for it? It should be stomping us flat by now."

"I kinda like not being pancaked, so can you maybe not jinx us?" Prompto said nervously.

"No, he has a point," Ignis chimed in, one hand outstretched to bring the group to a halt. "Hold, everyone. Hold. Something is amiss. I… I believe it is done."

"What!?"

Jaune was just one among many who spun on Ignis, disbelief emanating from him in waves. Spluttering, he gestured from the turtle to Ignis then back to the turtle, trying to put into words the ridiculousness of that bold claim.

Ignis fixed the position of his glasses, confidence never wavering. His one answer to them was to point ahead at the adamantoise. Look, the gesture said. Look.

The turtle did not move.

Its head sagged to one side. The open mouth hissed, and it took Jaune a long time to realize that it was trying to breathe, every exhale coming out weaker than the one before. It looked weak. It looked done.

Lower, lower, the head slipped, until it gently touched against the ground. That simple act still raised an earth-shattering quake, but there was no aggression in it.

"We won," said Noctis in a stupor. "We won? We won. We…"

A loud whoop broke the moment. Prompto pumped a fist in the air, shouting out in relief. He seized Bennett, swinging the other boy around in glee, causing Bennett to laugh. The simple mirth was infectious, jumping from person to person as smiles began to break out on their faces.

No. No, that wasn't right.

Jaune brought a hand up to massage his temples. He should be celebrating, but he could not. The bad feeling hadn't gone away, still there in the little mental box he put it in. If anything, it was growing louder now.

"This was too easy," he said, the first conclusion he could definitely make.

"Haha! Maybe the heat got to it," Prompto replied. "I know I'm about to have a stroke!"

Jaune only shook his head, deep in thought. Countless possible explanations fired off in his mind that was working harder than at any other moment in his life. They began to filter out, one by one. What remained were the certainties, calling for proof.

Shakily, he held out his hand. Rather than a weapon as he often summoned, a card popped into existence. His Adventurer Card. Jaune scanned the words written on it, zeroing in on one line.

EXP. Whenever he would kill something, the value changes.

Today, it stayed the same with a mountain-shaped hole in the numbers. He had not slain the turtle.

So, who did?

"It moved!"

Escha's words doused them all in an ice-cold sensation. Nobody questioned how a cat had talked, attention gripped in place by a greater priority. Jaune's head whipped up from the Adventurer Card, wild eyes roaming over the features of the adamantoise.

"Uh-oh."

"Uh-oh?" Noctis asked him. "This isn't the time for 'uh-oh'. Guys, get ready!"

Once again, Ignis was the voice of reason. "I don't think that's the turtle, Noct." The man squinted. "More like, there is something inside its mouth."

Indeed, the turtle remained immobile but for one place. Its lips shifted minutely, a mere twitch that could be dismissed as a trick of the light or a death sigh. It seemed harmless.

With a slight movement, the gargantuan mouth parted. It revealed two rows of un-turtlelike teeth, each tooth at least the size of a man.

Between this gap, a small object rolled out to hit the ground. A small, white, fluffy object.

Jaune now understood what that alarm ringing in his head was. An ability he had all but forgotten, yet was the most crucial power he possessed.

"Awww, it's a cute little bunny rabbit," said Prompto.


Author's Notes: Ring in the third round.
