#9,180

Chapter 93: They Found a Rabbit Waiting There
​

The true calamity had emerged.

"Don't. Move. The bunny is not what it seems."

Jaune stated this with utmost seriousness, graver than he had ever been. Sweat beaded on his brow, and not just from the desert heat. His gaze darted left and right, too aware of the vulnerable members of their party who needed to have their Aura unlocked now, now, now. Behind that gaze, a mind firing on all cylinders calculated the next few seconds to line up his necessary moves. (It went something like this: Run? Run.)

Alas, those like him too often found their wisdom ignored.

"Oh! Oh!" cried Bennett, the first to break. "Look at it thumping its little bunny foot, it's sooo cute!"

Near him, Prompto scrambled for his camera. "I've gotta take a picture with it!"

It grated, always being ignored or thought of as crazy for trying to warn the world. Still, Jaune understood this kind of naivety all too well, having stood in their place in a time not so long ago. Any number of stories about foul-tempered rodents was wholly insufficient. The human mind quite simply could not fathom the wickedness which lurked beneath the adorable facade. Exactly as planned by the wily rabbits, Jaune was sure. The species evolved to engineer this very scenario so that they may forever hunt their favorite prey.

Probably. It wasn't like his biology degree ever came in the mail (or that he applied for one in the first place). He just knew that the damn rabbit was evil. Evul, even.

…Mad, was he? Then why, even in a world without Grimm, do people go missing in the woods?

Anyway, it was up to him as a survivor to act. Thus, despite the risk of drawing the bunny's murderous attention, Jaune bravely moved forward to protect the others.

"Jaune, why are you standing behind me?"

"Shhh." Jaune covered Bennett's mouth with a hand, eyes rooted to the rabbit.

It had not attacked, but he had seen the slight twitch it made at the moment he shifted his position. The bunny's head was now turned minutely in their direction, one red eye glancing at them, at him, with a focus that the unaware would dismiss as a coincidence. It knew they were there, the cunning hare.

"Don't let it fool you," he continued. "Open your eyes. Look at the turtle."

Support came from an unexpected place to lend his words credence.

"Listen to him," said Gladiolus, glaring about. The authoritative tone got his people to simmer down, even arresting the crown prince in his tracks while Jaune retained a hold on Bennett. Jaune nodded to the man in thanks, and Gladiolus returned the gesture in kind before addressing his companions again. "Rabbits are easy to startle and this one just escaped from being eaten by the adamantoise. It's gonna be scared. We have to be gentle in our approach, got it?"

Hold up.

Jaune quickly interjected, "I meant that that thing is trouble."

"Right, it's in trouble," Ignis agreed while adjusting his glasses. "Getting eaten could have caused untold harm to its frail body. We must render aid at once. Noblesse oblige applies to more than just humans."

"Again, not quite what I said." Even if, objectively speaking, their words sounded so much more reasonable than what he was thinking.

He looked around for somebody on his side. Out of everyone, Escha was the single person to greet his repeated warnings with the appropriate response—she had seen the rabbit in action once before. All her fur stood on ends as she squatted at his feet, and the cat hissed with her lips peeled back at the vile abomination acting cute. Perhaps an innate feline sensitivity to danger was telling her that something was wrong with it, detecting the raging torrents of bloodthirst directed against them hidden behind that blank animal stare.

The rest, however, let their guards down and walked toward the rabbit without a care, chatting with levity. The suspicious manner of the adamantoise's death mattered less than the fact that it was dead, and with the newfound joy of surviving a disaster came carelessness. The prince and his men were ready to call this day a win. The absolute fools.

Gritting his teeth, Jaune darted in front of them, stopping the group with his arms spread out.

"Stay where you are," he barked, before checking over his shoulder. He breathed out a relieved sigh as he spotted the rabbit in the same place. They were still outside the range at which it would shed its guise to launch an attack. "You don't know how close you are to death, my friends. That rabbit…" He turned, pointing. "Is a killer."

"Uhhh, okay?' said Prompto. "If we're playing make-believe, then I guess I'll be the long lost heir of the Empire."

The problem with a group of friends with the same sense of humor was that when one started laughing, the rest would promptly follow suit. Jaune could not tell to whom the first snrk belonged to, and it did not matter. The quartet cracked up, all guffaws and slapping knees.

Amid the rousing humor, Jaune leveled a tepid look at the skinny blond. "Prompto, I don't need your sass right now," he deadpanned.

The unserious Prompto laughed again, and clapped him on the shoulder. "Come on, Jaune-Jaune." Jaune froze. "Thanks for worrying about us, but seriously, you're getting paranoid. It's almost like you're actually afraid of it or something."

"Scared of a rabbit? Eh, I guess everybody's got their reasons," said Gladiolus. He moved up, knocking a fist against Jaune's arm. "We'll be fine, kid. Just watch."

Of course, they could not believe him. He was The Boy Who Cried Rabbit, jumping at shadows. As they moved past him once more, Jaune let out a heavy breath.

No choice, now. He would have to risk the very lives he wished to save.

His gaze hardened, and Jaune whipped his arm around. As it aimed toward the rabbit, the rifle Ruhm snapped to his hand with his finger on the trigger. A half-formed curse slipped out of Prompto's mouth, and Gladiolus lunged for the gun, but neither could stop him in time. The moment the barrel lined up with the bunny, Jaune fired a shot.

The loud bang echoed across the desert plain, heralding death. Yet, before his ears stopped ringing, he had already realized his mistake and traded the rifle for a shield. To a stationary target, his marksmanship should have ended the problem then and there, but only a clod of dirt kicked up into the air after the bullet struck the ground. Of the bunny, its small form stood an inch apart from where he thought it was, watching him with its little red eyes.

"You absolute monster," one of his companions said.

"It is," Jaune agreed, digging in his heels as he braced for an imminent mauling. The mystery of how it made him miss his shot was a problem for later.

"We mean you! Are you crazy?" Noctis cried, as hands grabbed onto Jaune from every side to hold him back. The prince stomped in front of him, slamming an arm against his chest. "What did that bunny ever do to you?"

"Too many things," Jaune said with a thousand-yard stare.

Ignis pointed at the rabbit, on his face a fury such as Jaune had never seen. "I don't understand you. Why are you armed? Look at it, that rabbit is frozen in fear. Terrified out of its wits."

The plaintive tone stopped the retort on the tip of Jaune's tongue and he looked, really looked, at the people around him. At the confusion and betrayal etched upon their faces. They thought he was better than this.

Despite everything, his resolve began to waver, and it was with new clarity that his gaze returned to the rabbit. The docile, peaceful rabbit that had not made a single aggressive move this whole time. He strove to see what they saw.

"Does it, in any way, scream danger to you?" Ignis pleaded.

"No."

"There, see—"

"It murmurs 'I'll eat your little toesies off. For a start.' Mark my word, that rabbit is stone cold."

Four young men groaned in exasperation.

"Forget it," said Noctis. "Prompto, go grab the rabbit and let's get outta here. The heat is doing bad things to this guy's head."

Prompto performed a sloppy salute. "Aye-aye, Your Majesty."

The skinny blond split off from the group. Jaune tried to go after him, but Prompto's companions got in his way trying to talk him down. There was nothing to worry about, they told him. It was all in his head. Tempers flared hot as Bennett joined in on his side, and Jaune and him applied their greater strength to shove the others away.

For one little moment, his attention left the rabbit.

"Aaaaagh!"

A high-pitched scream rang out, carrying within it a primal, bone-deep fear that drew a shiver from every man there. Whirling toward the noise, they found Prompto on his rear clutching a bleeding hand.

"Prompto?" Ignis said uncertainly.

The skinny blond stammered a reply, but in his terror-stricken panic it came out as muddled nonsense. He kicked his legs to push himself back, away from the small figure nearby.

The rabbit had its back to them, and its body twitched and shook as if it was chewing on something.

"W-What is it eating?" Noctis asked, horror dawning. "Prompto, what is it eating?"

Before Prompto could speak, the bunny's head snapped around. The prince screamed as he beheld a face covered in red blood.

"Squeak!" the rabbit chittered, and launched itself at Prompto once more.

In an instant, Jaune was there. With one foot pulled back, he snarled a savage curse and punted the rabbit as hard as he could, sending the small creature bouncing across the ground back toward the slain adamantoise.

Over his shoulder, he shouted, "Run away!"

Nobody uttered a peep against him this time.


-o-
​

Jaune was the last to vault behind the rocky outcropping where everyone was hiding. This place made for a tight squeeze with six healthy people and a cat, but none of them complained, huddling in to minimize their bulk. Prompto laid at the very center of the group, carried here by his companions and dripping green goop from the healing potion that Escha had poured on him.

"Cats can talk…. Rabbits can kill…" Prompto chanted, rocking back and forth.

The miffed Escha whose medical advice had triggered a panic attack ignored Prompto to climb onto Jaune's shoulder, and they joined everybody still in fighting shape in poking their heads above the rocky outcropping to observe the bunny. It was a lot closer to them than Jaune would like, the time between him kicking it and its recovery having been too short for them to do anything but find the closest place to bunker down. Now puttering about near the adamantoise, the bunny would once in a while thump a foot against the fallen mountain as if kicking it in anger.

"What is that thing?" Gladiolus asked in a half-disbelieving voice.

"That, is the Beast of Caerbannog," said Jaune. "And I told you it was trouble. I told you."

If he sounded snide, forgive him. It had been quite a day.

"Perhaps it was an illusion," Ignis suggested, holding his chin.

Prompto awoke from his stupor. "It took a chunk out of my hand!"

"A very convincing illusion, then," Ignis allowed. "A defensive ability that allows it to waylay predators who would seek to do it harm. If we leave it alone, it might do the same in kind." The man sounded like he was trying to persuade himself.

Jaune coughed into his hand. "There's five hundred or so sets of skeletons in a cave that would beg to differ. That foul rodent reaps lives without discrimination."

"I still can't believe you were serious, boss. The rabbit's real."

"See, Bennett. I would never lie to you," Jaune lied. "I think it might be the reason why the adamantoise fell so easily, and the root cause of the earthquakes. It had been eating the turtle from the inside."

Shudders passed among the group as they each imagined the gruesome fate of the adamantoise, conjuring up visions of brain parasites and other such tales. Some acts went beyond the pale, and this nearly topped the list for most of the people present.

Prompto, still shaking, dared a look above the outcropping before hunching down again. "So, what now?" he whimpered. "Are we stuck here forever?"

"We can wait until nighttime," said Gladiolus. "Once it is asleep, escape will be a cinch."

"G-Good plan, Gladi-man. If you'd excuse me, gents, I'll be digging a hole to hide in."

Ignis chimed in. "You forget, we must arrange the harvesting of materials from the adamantoise. So long as the rabbit remains in the vicinity, anyone we send out here risks a bloody death."

That got an admiring nod from Jaune, whose thoughts went along the same lines. Leaving the rabbit alone was a poor proposition given the danger it posed to life.

"I'm going to take care of it," he said, drawing all eyes. "What, you worried about me? Let's just say…" A commotion broke out as he summoned a full suit of scaly armor to encase his form. "I have a few tricks up my sleeve that I haven't shown you yet."

"Ouch!"

"Watch it!"

"My spleen!"

Jaune grimaced as the spikes on the Rathalos hide continued to jab into the people huddled around him. "Oops. That looked a lot cooler in my head."

It was cool, the four locals agreed once the injuries he caused them stopped smarting. More inclined to believe him at this point, the mention of him fighting a dragon (technically a wyvern, but he preferred to call it a dragon) gained him a great measure of esteem in their eyes. The romance of dragon-slaying was one that crossed cultures and histories.

"I faced that rabbit twice already," Jaune informed them. "I know what it's capable of, and I've grown to the point where it isn't a threat to me. With all of you out of danger, I can confidently state that I got this covered."

Sharp teeth and a little hoppity hop. That made up the full arsenal of the rabbit, put to deadly use via its cunning mind. The Rathalos armor negated much of that, not to mention everything else he had amassed over the course of his journey since their last encounter. The enhanced durability imparted through the Adventurer Card, the Geo energy stemming from a trinket hanging off his belt, the… the…

Huh. Well, he had what he needed for these circumstances. That rabbit wouldn't know what hit it.

As he shifted position, ready to jump out of hiding, a hand landed on his shoulder. It belonged to Noctis, who pressed down signaling for him to wait.

"I have a better plan," the prince said. "I'm the fastest one here. A quick warp over there and we'll have rabbit stew to go with turtle soup, no chance for it to get away."

"Warp? That's your teleporting, right? Haha, no," Jaune replied. "You don't know what you're saying. That thing will kill you."

Yet, Noctis only chuckled with a confident air. The crown prince pushed off of the ground, and placed a foot over the rocks. He turned his head, giving a wink over his shoulder.

"No way I'll die here, not when I'm getting married soon."

For reasons Jaune could not adequately explain, a cold pit grew within his gut. However, he had no time to dissuade the royal fool or get him to stop long enough to unlock his Aura. In the blink of an eye, Noctis was behind the rabbit.

And in the blink of an eye, the rabbit was behind Noctis.

The prince stood too far to be heard, but the "Uhhh…" came through regardless due to his behavior, with Noctis looking around at the empty stretch of ground before him while carrying a lost expression.

"""Duck!"""" Jaune, Ignis, and Gladiolus shouted at the same time.

The rabbit's teeth snapped down on the empty spot that the prince's neck used to occupy. The creature landed on the ground, tilting its head in confusion for a moment before noticing the shadow that covered its form. Above, Noctis flailed in the air for balance, having teleported straight up rather than ducking as a non-teleporter might.

As gravity took hold, the prince turned the tip of his sword toward the ground, driving it down with both hands gripping the handle tight. Right before impact, Jaune managed a good look at what was happening with the rabbit. It curled up, seeming ready to spring. Except, it never jumped aside. A flicker, and Noctis's sword impaled deep into the dirt with the rabbit now several yards in front of its previous location, hunched in the same exact position. Another flicker, and it faced the complete opposite direction, glaring at Noctis. Now the rabbit sprang, bounding for him with its teeth glinting in the sunlight.

Noctis went to the left. The rabbit zapped to the left. He warped high. It followed suit.

"All of you are seeing this, correct?" Ignis said, quite weakly. "My eyesight has not gone completely blind, has it?"

Prompto answered, "If you mean the rabbit using Lucis royal magic, then yeah, I'm seeing it, too. I wish I didn't, but I do."

"This is not the time," Gladiolus chided them. "We have to help Noct!"

"How? We can't even keep up with them."

Numbly, Jaune nodded along. With the perspective of an outsider, he noted that the 'royal magic' was nothing but. It worked from different sources, discernible from how the prince created afterimages while the rabbit's was more of a puff of smoke. In practical terms, though, they were both teleporting.

That… That was new.

The chase between man and bunny continued with the two figures zipping back and forth in a frantic pace, sometimes moving onto the dead turtle to race across its massive head. Intermittent exchanges brought a lull where the prince's graceful swordplay would meet the rabbit's two front buckteeth. Contrary to every one of Jaune's expectations, Noctis came out on the losing side more often than not, with the rabbit using the momentum of its powerful leaps to the fullest to overwhelm the prince's attacks.

That it could directly match the strength of a grown man pointed to something strange happening here. Of course, Jaune arrived at a ready explanation for what it was. Like him, the rabbit had gained powers during their time apart.

"But how!?" Jaune cried, slamming a fist against the ground. "This isn't fair!"

With a final warp, the crown prince landed back in hiding among them. Covered in wounds, he slipped to the ground wheezing for breath as his companions caught him. Seeing that, Jaune immediately smashed one of Escha's healing potions to the side of his head, with Noctis shouting and the others trying to get between them until they recognized the green goop. The concoction slowly healed the injuries along with the swelling bump put there by the potion. A needle followed, summoned and stabbed into Noctis's bicep.

"Gah! Stop that!" Noctis yelped, slapping a hand over the spot on his arm.

"The stimpak will help keep that face in the boy band business," Jaune explained, vanishing the spent needle as he checked over the prince for more serious damage. "Anyway, good job."

Exhausted, the prince managed to halfheartedly cock an eyebrow. "Is that sarcasm? That monster beat me black and blue. Forget the turtle, because we're not getting it back. It's official. We are stuck in this desert forever."

"We're not quite done yet," Jaune assured him. "If you had given me time, I might have been able to change your loss to a win."

"Seriously? How?"

As his answer, Jaune slapped Noctis in the face.

"For it is in friendship that we change the—"

The prince smacked his hand away and slapped him right back. "What are you doing!?"

"Stop assaulting our prince!" his entourage cried.

"I'm helping!"

Unfortunately, his protests fell on deaf ears, with the prince inching away. The next minute saw him rushing through an explanation of Aura to much skepticism in an already poisoned well, while also fielding questions from Bennett and Escha on the rabbit's new abilities discovered via Noctis's sacrifice and what it meant for their strategy. No way, no how were they leaving something like that running around the Leide desert to eat Cindy's face off, which meant they had a murderous teleporting bunny looming in their near future.

"At the very least, it's territorial," Jaune said. "It's staying near the turtle for now, I think because it sees the adamantoise as its kill. That gives us a bit of leeway to set things up."

Escha gasped as an idea struck her. "You should set out bait! You're good at that!"

"Exactly," Jaune said, ruffling her fur. Behind the talking cat, an ongoing discussion between the prince and his retinue about whether they had been drugged by unknown hallucinogens went ignored. "The rabbit is an animal in the end. It doesn't possess the capacity for thought that you and I have. Our choice of bait is easy, anyway. We'll just have one of us stand out in the open. The challenge is the other half of the equation, how we will trap it. Bennett, thoughts?"

Bennett mulled it over, ultimately shaking his head. "I… I don't know. I'd need to study it for a while."

"Not a bad call," Jaune said, which perked Bennett up. "The biggest question on my mind is how its teleporting power works. That'd decide our approach."

Their immediate course determined, they poked their heads out of cover to observe their target.

"...Wait a minute, where did it go?"

A shadow fell over them.

From a higher outcropping, the rabbit stared down at the group with what Jaune could only call imperious disdain. The attitude of a higher being regarding its lessers, framed with the sun at its back. It snuffled, nose twitching.

"Scatter!" Ignis shouted, the quickest to regain his composure.

They parted like the tide, the prince going one way with his entourage shielding him using their bodies, Bennett and Escha heading the other direction. Jaune alone stayed, slamming down the visor of his helmet as he charged forward over the rocks. The rabbit thrived in chaos and panic. Give an inch, and it would leave bodies in its wake. Someone had to draw that creature's ire.

Crocea Mors leapt to his hand as the bunny launched off the outcropping, sharpened tip thrusting with lethal accuracy in order to skewer his opponent from end to end. Steel crashed against teeth.

Dust blew away in an intense shockwave, forcing Jaune to squint his eyes. Through his narrow vision, he beheld an impossible sight. He had witnessed the hardness of the rabbit's incisors, but… A blade once reforged in the flames of gods had encountered its match.

Golden Geo energy swirled into a sphere that encased him from all sides, pushing outward to knock the rabbit back. Between one moment and the next, the bunny teleported to bypass the shield altogether, upside-down with both feet aimed high. A rabbity double-kick sent Jaune's face snapping back, chin tilted up to expose his throat. Jaune choked out half a cry as big pointy teeth clamped onto him, crushing down with a dragon's strength.

He wasn't about to get his throat ripped out just yet, he reminded himself, fighting against the instinct to panic that every living thing, Aura or not, experienced when a predator had them in what should be a fatal position. Freeing his hands of sword and shield, he seized the rabbit and tore it away.

"Ha! I've got you"—the rabbit popped away in a puff of smoke—"now, crap, never mind."

Stupid teleporters.

It might be his eyes playing tricks on him, but he could have sworn he saw the word 'POOF' within the dissipating smoke, like a cartoon. There was no time to dwell on it, though. A hair-raising scream alerted him to the rabbit's change in victim.

Over the dry, cracked ground, four men shouted like little girls while desperately protecting their vitals as a flash of white bounced between them, ripping deep gashes wherever it sank its teeth. Noctis was in the best position to try and stick a blade in the rabbit, the attacks aimed at him intercepted by the others for the most part. The prince was less adept at fighting teleporters than being one, however, swiping his sword madly as he chased after the bunny.

"Noct, watch it!"

"I got him, I got him—WAIT, stop, don't swing, I don't got him!"

"We should regroup. Everyone form up!"

"To where, Ignis. To where? Ahhhh!"

They were doing pretty alright.

The tight quarters created by four people facing a tiny foe kept him from rushing in, though. This was a problem also felt by Bennett and Escha, armed yet not at all dangerous to the rabbit as they hesitated outside fighting range.

For a moment, Ruhm dropped into Jaune's hands, but he reconsidered the idea. Firing into an ongoing melee was how one caused a friendly-fire incident. Thinking fast, he swapped the firearm out for the glass jars filled with healing potion, slinging them in quick succession to render aid for the wounded combatants.

"Yes! I just cut a leg!" Noctis cheered.

A glass jar shattered.

"Oh gods, it's healed up again!"

Like he said, it thrived in chaos and panic. The rabbit was smarter than it appeared. It certainly had nothing to do with his misjudgment.

While he contemplated whether another healing potion would even up the odds or doom the crown prince of the kingdom, Escha screeched to a halt at his feet with Bennett on her heels. She spat out the boomerang gripped between her teeth, vibrating with nerves.

"Jaune, Jaune, what's the plan?"

"I don't have one."

"Weh?"

Oh shoot, he wasn't supposed to say that. This Jaune Arc always had a plan.

He snapped his fingers. A metal loop that had not been there a second earlier was now twirling around and around a knuckle.

"Do you know what this is?"

Both boy and cat looked closer at the thin band, with Bennett recognizing it first. "That's the collar that Miss Lisa likes to wear, isn't it? Uh, boss, I don't think she'll be happy if you bring home another girlfriend."

"What, no," Jaune spluttered. "Another girlfriend? I don't even—You know what, that's not important. Big fight going on, we need to focus. This is a choker and Lisa wears hers for medical reasons. It suppresses powers."

Escha gasped. "Like tele-potting."

Understanding dawned for Bennett.

"If we put it on the rabbit, it'll become helpless!"

Jaune made a so-so gesture, cutting that notion at the knees. "It stops the teleporting. No guarantees on anything else."

Even at baseline, the bunny constituted a menace. To society, and to life. Anybody who considered it helpless was asking to lose fingers.

"Get the rabbit's attention. Get this choker on it. Get it in containment," Jaune said, numbering his points one by one on a hand. It sounded simple, didn't it? Very confident? He was winging it, honestly.

The emboldened Bennett, in the midst of readying his blade, lowered his weapon and blinked a few times at him. "Don't you mean stab it with a sword?"

"If you see an opportunity, take it. Otherwise, so long as we have a chance, there's something I want to check on first. As for the how…"

He performed a mental rundown of the items in his Pocket, searching for one that would work. Funnily enough, cages and sedatives were not among the necessities to his trade, leaving him to settle for the closest equivalent he had on hand.

"I really have to thank Hu Tao."

Over by the rabbit, Noctis and company were in the middle of getting the tar beaten out of them. There one moment, gone the next, the bunny never allowed them more than a split second to react. With grit and teamwork, they held on.

And then Jaune came smashing through like a freight train.

Weathering stray shots and friendly fire, he wielded only a sword without shield or armor. The rabbit would be tempted by nothing less.

"Form up behind me!" he called out. "I'll draw its attention!"

As the others pulled back, he kicked out with a foot, blasting a gout of rocket fire for good measure. In response, the bunny went from the ground to perching on his leg with barely time in between, and raced up his body at a speed that defied belief.

A knife lanced past his throat, preventing the rabbit's teeth from catching hold. Its owner, Ignis, then ducked to avoid a faceful of fluffy death. A shadowy limb launched by Jaune passed above him to follow their diminutive opponent.

The rabbit twisted in the air to get its head around, biting through [Third Arm] and destroying the limb. Its little feet barely touched the dirt before its entire form blurred, zigzagging right back toward the group.

Jaune stomped the ground and beat his chest, presenting a loud and big target for the rabbit to focus on while everyone else waited in the wing. The moment it entered his range, he stabbed at it with Crocea Mors, whiffing air as the bunny vanished without a trace. A powerful impact then struck him from behind to send him stumbling.

His foe reappeared by his wrist, moving fast as a rocket. It clamped down on him in passing, pulling him off his feet entirely. Up became down, and down became up, with Jaune shouting in surprise as he swung a full circle to slam against the hard ground on his back, the air knocked out of him. Head spinning, he watched fluffy white death fall down on him from above.

Noctis met it in the sky, sword whipping out to gut the foul beast. The rabbit bypassed him, but found that the prince had anticipated the ploy, suffering the heel of a hard boot as Noctis kicked downward without looking. Squeaking, it hit the ground, bouncing off.

Escha tackled the rabbit, and they went down in a tangle of teeth and claws. Jaune rolled to his feet to the sight of a ferocious struggle, with Escha trying to scratch out the rabbit's eyes as it mauled her ear.

"Don't touch my friends!" Escha cried, meowing in pain as a mere few seconds facing off against the rabbit sent her Aura crashing, the pink glow around her already flickering.

The first to reach them was Gladiolus, his weapon of a greatsword left in the dirt so it would not slow him down. The man grabbed both cat and bunny to tug them apart, losing a strip of flesh from wrist to elbow in the process as the rabbit directed its anger his way. A healing potion smashed against his head.

"Fucking—Would you please stop doing that!?" the man roared while covered in green goop. The skin and flesh on his wounded arm pulled back together while he fended off the rabid bunny trying to chomp on his fingers.

"Pain is good for you," Jaune called back, sprinting over. "It shows you're alive!"

Their shouting seemed to confuse the rabbit, or at least gave it pause as it decided which of them it wanted to silence first. Ultimately, it went with the one already bleeding, sinking its fangs into the mending flesh. Gladiolus screamed through clenched teeth, fighting back the pain to desperately shake the rabbit off.

"Keep a hold of it," Jaune ordered him. Too late, for the rabbit had weighed the odds and cut its losses, releasing Gladiolus to poof away in a cloud of smoke.

The metal band appeared in Jaune's free hand. Where is it going to show up, he thought as his gaze flicked back and forth. A weight landed atop his head to answer that question.

Quick as a whip, he swung the open choker above him. The ends snapped close around empty air, the rabbit already gone. A shout of pain from Noctis told him where he was needed.

Looking that way, he quickly picked apart the scene. Noctis holding back the rabbit, with Prompto just turning around. The distance from here to there.

"Prompto!" he yelled, throwing the metal choker. "Put it on the bunny!"

Something seemed to click in Prompto's head at the commanding tone. The normally clumsy one among the four Lucians snatched the choker out of the air and dropped to a knee in one motion. The rabbit, sensing danger, vanished in a blink. Jaune did not even get the chance to figure out which way it had gone before Prompto threw the metal band.

"Ignis, it's your show," Prompto said.

And then it was Bennett's show, then Ignis again, then Escha. The metal band passed back and forth as an explanation of its function and Jaune's plan filtered out to the others. Division of roles began to take shape, with half of them serving as bait while the other half worried about neutralizing the rabbit's abilities.

Somehow, Noctis ended up alongside Jaune, Bennett, and Gladiolus on the front line. The amount of blood that spilled from the crown prince of the kingdom in the ensuing minutes would probably get Jaune the executioner's axe should news of it ever reach Lucis.

"I got this," the prince insisted, to all evidence of the contrary. "Like I'd die here, I still—"

Jaune slapped a hand over the young man's mouth, then with it pulled the prince by the face to get him out of the rabbit's path. Nasty big pointy teeth narrowly missed the royal jewels, drawing a collective breath of relief from the prince's entourage.

The rabbit landed in their midst, coming around for a second go at ending the Lucis line.

A soft click announced the next phase.

It had been Escha in the end, through a plot hatched with Prompto where she hung on his back and swung down like a monkey at a crucial moment. Suddenly, the rabbit had nowhere to go, surrounded on all sides. Jaune's foot met it an instant later, punting it against a rock.

"Escha, use [Feline Battlecry] on the rabbit!"

Escha answered him with a firm nod, and drew a breath. The resulting meow rang across the desert, loud and grating on the ears like a whole bunch of cats yowling at midnight. It attracted the attention of the rabbit, the people fighting said rabbit, plus all the wildlife that happened to be in the vicinity, because its effect wasn't actually to direct at a specific target or do anything except being very annoying. A distraction, and nothing more.

As the high, screeching note petered out, Jaune brought his hands together above his head. With a loud cry, he summoned his ultimate attack (Ver. II). A long wooden box appeared, standing on his palms. The lid swung open, and he slammed the box down with full force.

The rabbit, stripped of its new powers, could only leap aside on its own strength. A beat too late, it smacked against the inner wall of a meticulously lacquered coffin inlaid with the softest velvet padding. The edges struck the ground in the next moment to seal it inside.

The ensuing silence could have been appropriate for a funeral. Heart thundering, Jaune waited for something to go wrong. For a power-up out of the blue that would let the foul rodent turn the table.

None came.

Noctis broke the silence first. "Uhhh, why do you have a coffin on you?"

His retinue hemmed and hawed along the same line, each very concerned of a matter that was none of their business.

"I know a girl."

"That says nothing to us. Who is this girl? Does she have a screw loose?"

"She sounds dangerous, dude."

"Naw, she's a sweetheart. Think Cindy, but with a graveyard. I—whoa!"

The whole coffin with Jaune on it had shifted to one side, pushed from within. That froze everyone solid, until the coffin rattled again. Then, it became a full-on scramble to pile atop him and the coffin, adding weight to keep the box still.

"I told you," Jaune did not miss a chance to say again, casting his gaze from face to face. "I told you, but did you listen? Just a bunny, my foot."

"Give it a rest, man. We get it. Ugh, I don't know what that thing is, but it doesn't belong in this world," said Prompto, striking the nail on the head by accident.

Ignis held out a bleeding arm. "I'm more concerned with the fact that nobody will believe us. I will have to carry these nibble marks with me forever, hiding it from everybody who asks that I got it from a killer bunny."

"At least you have the turtle's carcass," Jaune said, which perked everybody right up.

The mood took a happier turn as it dawned on the prince and his friends that they were outright legends soon to be famous the world over, with guesses on just how much the adamantoise was worth. No matter how they sliced it, a big payout awaited them in the future. Not to mention the free food and drinks that they would likely get in every eatery from here to their destination for their story of today.

Jaune sensed it in the air, the end of an adventure. He kept quiet about it, letting everybody else enjoy the high of their success.

"Well then," said Ignis. "It's off to Galdin Quay, and from there Altissia. To get Noctis to his bride."

A rousing cheer greeted this proclamation, with many a slap on the prince's back for his upcoming marriage. Jaune wouldn't be present for the event, but he was happy about it nevertheless. He passed the groom a gift then and there, a bottle of the finest Spirytus to crack open at the wedding. Plus another bottle for this moment, with the cups to go along with it.

The sound of snapping wood cut short their celebration. All eyes turned to a small break on the coffin.

A rabbit's adorably twitching snout poked out of the hole, and an unholy screech echoed across the desert.

Six grown men and a cat screamed at the top of their lungs.


-o-
​

The tranquil afternoon dragged on and on, the hours spinning lazily toward the evening. A content yawn slipped out between Lisa's lips as she lounged on the couch of her rental home… base.

In her hand she held a tablet that was at once years ahead of what she knew yet familiar and intuitive in a way that something like Jaune's phone—wouldn't catch her dead calling it a scroll—never could be. A flick of her finger and headline after headline rolled by, not a one making mention of superpowered heroes, villains, accidents, 'accidents', Endbringers, or the Slaughterhouse Nine.

Little news for peaceful days, as she enjoyed the warm, insipid comfort of a world where everything went right for Lisa Wilbourn. Life had never gone so smoothly.

She wasn't certain if she liked it. It left her with this feeling of both utter calm and a yearning for something she could not adequately explain. Something… more?

It had been days since she put on her costume.

The portal on the wall flickered on, and Lisa found a big fox-like grin popping up on her face without meaning to. Life wouldn't be so peaceful anymore.

Her head tilted back to look behind the couch, just in time for Jaune to appear through the portal. Crossing within 4-6 seconds of activation. Ooh, he must be on a high.

"Did you have fun?" she chirped. "Bring back anything we can sell?"

A split second pause and a flick of his gaze told her that Jaune was clearly checking out her legs, which were dressed for the winter and for comfort in thick sweat pants. The soft sigh of disappointment was music to her ears.

The poor baby didn't get his eye candy. Sucks to suck.

It ceased to be amusing as she recalled one important detail, that some among the house's occupants had gotten more careless than her in the absence of boys. Her gaze drifted over to the other person hanging out in the room. Kiwi, who was in tank top and thong and didn't seem in any hurry to cover up. Give people an inch and they take a mile.

"Well, I got this," said Jaune, drawing her attention back to him. The goof turned around, grabbing a box carried by a triumphant Bennett and Escha over their heads like some sort of cartoon skit.

No, wait, that was not a simple box.

"Jaune, what are you doing with that coffin?"

Rather than replying, the boy walked over the dining table to slam the coffin on the surface where it shook and rattled, the noise leading Lisa and Kiwi to get up for a look. Lisa pushed past the furiously blushing Bennett trying to cover his eyes, scooting in next to Jaune as she put a little more effort into sussing out the details.

Something small, something angry.

"Heh. Something borrowed, something blue~"

"Hm?"

"Nothing. Just remembered a silly thing." She leaned down, pressing her ear to the wooden lid. "Now, what did you get me?"

She stopped grinning. Her face rapidly began to pale.

"Check the Company scroll I left with you for how much this is worth now." Jaune said above her. "Because I have a number in my head, and if it doesn't match up to that, I'm skewering this rabbit."

Oh, it was never boring with this fool around.
